El Fasher/Tawila, Sudan, July 31, 2026 - Months after the RSF seized El Fasher, Darfur remained the geographic core of mass-atrocity testimony, famine risk and constrained aid access even as Kordofan dominated late-July battlefield news.

Satellite-confirmed village burnings, sexual-violence documentation and overcrowded Tawila-linked sites kept western Sudan at the centre of genocide and crimes-against-humanity debates.

Humanitarian officials still describe Darfur as among the world’s gravest protection crises.

title: Aid Operations Face Drones, Extortion, Funding Gaps and Rainy-Season Collapse
excerpt: Khartoum, Sudan, July 31, 2026 - Humanitarian agencies reiterated that Sudan remains one of the world’s most dangerous operating environments, with drones hitting water points and infrastructure, armed checkpoints taxing truckers, parties obstructing access, and donor fatigue…
title_en: Aid Operations Face Drones, Extortion, Funding Gaps and Rainy-Season Collapse
excerpt_en: Khartoum, Sudan, July 31, 2026 - Humanitarian agencies reiterated that Sudan remains one of the world’s most dangerous operating environments, with drones hitting water points and infrastructure, armed checkpoints taxing truckers, parties obstructing access, and donor fatigue…
body_en:
Khartoum, Sudan, July 31, 2026 - Humanitarian agencies reiterated that Sudan remains one of the world’s most dangerous operating environments, with drones hitting water points and infrastructure, armed checkpoints taxing truckers, parties obstructing access, and donor fatigue colliding with needs above 20 million people.
Rainy-season flooding and mud further isolate communities as hunger peaks. Without protected corridors into El Obeid, Darfur and Blue Nile hotspots, agencies warn preventable deaths will continue to outpace attention paid to front-line vehicle counts.
Conclusion
The period from July 15 to July 31, 2026, marks a critical and volatile juncture in the Sudanese conflict, characterized by shifting battlefield dynamics, deepening humanitarian paralysis, and persistent diplomatic fragmentation. While the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and allied movements secured key operational breakthroughs by reclaiming critical transit corridors in North Kordofan, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) responded with asymmetric escalation, decentralized commander autonomy, and retaliatory strikes on strategic rear infrastructure. Consequently, key urban centers-most notably El Obeid-remain trapped under severe siege-like conditions, exposing hundreds of thousands of civilians to dual threats of militarized violence and weaponized resource scarcity.
On the economic and diplomatic fronts, structural divides continue to impede a viable path toward peace. International regulatory measures-such as targeted UK sanctions and EU commodity bans on gold-face severe enforcement bottlenecks within a hyper-informal conflict economy reliant on illegal transit routes and parallel extortion networks. Concurrently, political dialogue remains stalled: warring factions prioritize battlefield leverage over ceasefire compliance, while civilian political coalitions remain deeply fragmented over regional mediation formats.
As rainy-season logistics compound aid delivery blockades, systemic destruction of essential water, power, and healthcare networks is driving a severe escalation in cholera outbreaks, mass displacement, and famine-level food insecurity affecting over 20 million people. Moving forward, the trajectory of the crisis hinges entirely on whether international facilitators can establish enforceable, politically independent civilian protection mechanisms and secure unhindered humanitarian access across Darfur, Kordofan, and central Sudan. Without these structural safeguards, tactical military shifts will continue to yield only widespread destruction and escalating human suffering.
By Jeff Buleli

title_en: MPs Probe Shs25 Billion Uganda Railways Training Spend
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Parliament’s Physical Infrastructure Committee questioned Uganda Railway Corporation over about Shs25 billion spent on staff training under a Spanish- and EU-linked technical assistance programme, ordering CID-backed verification of participants.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Parliament’s Physical Infrastructure Committee questioned Uganda Railway Corporation over about Shs25 billion spent on staff training under a Spanish- and EU-linked technical assistance programme, ordering CID-backed verification of participants.

URC said the money covered 43 programmes for 1,150 employees nationwide, spanning technical, performance, finance and security courses. Committee chair Mwine Mpaka demanded full name and contact lists so investigators can check whether listed trainees were actually in Kampala on the claimed dates, and also summoned figures over disputed URC land.

Key points from the report: - Parliament’s Physical Infrastructure Committee questioned Uganda Railway Corporation over about Shs25 billion spent on staff training under a Spanish- and EU-linked technical assistance programme, ordering CID-backed verification of participants. - URC said the money covered 43 programmes for 1,150 employees nationwide, spanning technical, performance, finance and security courses. - Committee chair Mwine Mpaka demanded full name and contact lists so investigators can check whether listed trainees were actually in Kampala on the claimed dates, and also summoned figures over disputed URC land.

Hoima, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Authorities opened a Bunyoro regional migrant-workers support centre in Hoima City to offer information, data collection, rehabilitation and complaint-handling for Ugandans returning from foreign employment.

title_en: Eron Kiiza Says Besigye Trial Is Null and Void Over Imposed Lawyers
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Human-rights lawyer Eron Kiiza argued that treason proceedings before Justice Baguma are legally invalid, citing a report by court-appointed state-brief advocates that, he said, shows Besigye never accepted them.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Human-rights lawyer Eron Kiiza argued that treason proceedings before Justice Baguma are legally invalid, citing a report by court-appointed state-brief advocates that, he said, shows Besigye never accepted them.

Kiiza said no advocate may be imposed on an accused entitled to counsel of choice, and noted the appointed lawyers admitted they still awaited disclosure and the indictment-raising doubts about readiness.

The critique landed after Besigye’s collapse and the aborted follow-up hearing.

title_en: Researcher Says Congo “Lost Time” Grasping ADF’s Jihadist Mutation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Beni, July 31, 2026 - Researcher Claude Sengenya argued authorities and partners long misunderstood the ADF, which mutated after 2017 from a Uganda-focused politico-military refuge force into a jihadist threat documented by UN and independent reporting.
body_en:
Kinshasa/Beni, July 31, 2026 - Researcher Claude Sengenya argued authorities and partners long misunderstood the ADF, which mutated after 2017 from a Uganda-focused politico-military refuge force into a jihadist threat documented by UN and independent reporting.

He said delayed recognition cost lives as the group expanded across Ituri and North Kivu. Security debate increasingly focuses on ideology, recruitment and cross-border networks rather than treating the ADF only as a residual rebellion.

title_en: Muyaya Says Court Ruling Validates Referendum Framework Without Launching a Vote
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 31, 2026 - Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said the Constitutional Court’s clearance of the referendum organisation law validates a legal framework but does not itself mean a referendum has been organised or launched.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 31, 2026 - Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said the Constitutional Court’s clearance of the referendum organisation law validates a legal framework but does not itself mean a referendum has been organised or launched.

The clarification sought to cool speculation that the July 28 ruling automatically triggers a constitutional vote. Opposition critics still treat the law as a pathway to contested change; the presidential camp insists procedure and politics remain separate steps.

title_en: AUSSOM Summit Focuses on Somalia Threat and Post-UNSOS Sustainability

body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Military chiefs, defence ministers and heads of state meeting in Munyonyo reviewed Al-Shabaab threats, Somali security-force readiness and how African troop contributors can sustain AUSSOM after planned UNSOS closure.

Uganda, a long-standing contributor to Somali missions, used the chair’s platform to argue that African-led operations cannot depend indefinitely on shrinking UN logistics envelopes.

Recommendations from the summit are expected to shape contingency plans ranging from regional logistics frameworks to orderly handover scenarios.

title_en: Buwenge Buries Two Men Shot Dead During LC1 Polls

Jinja, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Mourners in Buwenge Town Council buried Latib Ikaali, 26, and Fred Kalulu, 19, allegedly shot by a police officer during LC1 elections in Kabi Zone, as residents demanded justice and electoral-security reforms.

Witnesses said voting was underway when gunfire erupted and Kalulu was found wounded at the scene. Local leaders said Buwenge has repeatedly seen election-day violence, putting pressure on police and the Electoral Commission to prevent further bloodshed in residual village contests.

Kinshasa, July 2026 - Nathanaël Onokomba was transferred to Makala prison after nearly seven months at Ndolo military prison, in a case that has also seen jurisdictional disputes between military and civilian justice.

Earlier procedural decisions included a finding of lack of competence by the Kinshasa/Gombe military garrison court and retransmission of the file toward higher military prosecution channels.

Rights advocates continue to track detention conditions and due-process guarantees.

body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC, July 31, 2026 - The Congolese government said Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) representatives had signed a protocol on disarmament, demobilisation, cantonment, monitoring and relocation through to dissolution, presenting the step as implementation of the U.S.-brokered Washington accord with Rwanda.

Regional Integration Minister Floribert Anzuluni said the document resulted from talks aimed at answering Kigali’s long-standing security concerns. Kinshasa argued five of six identified FDLR zones now lie under Rwanda/AFC-M23 rather than FARDC control, complicating unilateral Congolese enforcement.

title: Turkey: Rwandans celebrate 32 years of Rwanda's liberation through various games, 21 July 2026. Rwandans living in Turkey, joined their friends in celebrating 32 years of Rwanda's liberation, with participants being shown that the goal of the liberation struggle is not only to achieve victory, but also to preserve what has been achieved and continue to build on it.
excerpt: The event took place on 18 July 2026 in Ankara, the capital of Turkey. The event was marked by various games and talks on the journey of Rwanda's liberation as well as joy expressed in dance and songs, with a special emphasis on the role of the youth in preserving what has…
title_en: Turkey: Rwandans celebrate 32 years of Rwanda's liberation through various games, 21 July 2026. Rwandans living in Turkey, joined their friends in celebrating 32 years of Rwanda's liberation, with participants being shown that the goal of the liberation struggle is not only to achieve victory, but also to preserve what has been achieved and continue to build on it.
excerpt_en: The event took place on 18 July 2026 in Ankara, the capital of Turkey. The event was marked by various games and talks on the journey of Rwanda's liberation as well as joy expressed in dance and songs, with a special emphasis on the role of the youth in preserving what has…
body_en:
The event took place on 18 July 2026 in Ankara, the capital of Turkey.
The event was marked by various games and talks on the journey of Rwanda's liberation as well as joy expressed in dance and songs, with a special emphasis on the role of the youth in preserving what has been achieved.
Liberation Day is usually celebrated on July 4, but this year its activities in Turkey were postponed to July 18 due to various international conferences held in Ankara at that time, which caused the activities of many embassies to temporarily change dates.
The event included a cycling race, a walking race, a ping pong (table tennis) competition, discussions on the history of the Rwandan liberation struggle, and a concert featuring songs that characterized the liberation struggle.
The winners of some of the various competitions received various awards.
In the cycling race, Umut Akçaoğlu from Turkey came first, followed by Camille Niyonkuru who came second and Pascal Nshuti who came third.
In the running race, Lea Mujawimana came first, followed by Rulisa Briella and Laurence Uwonkunda Kayitare. In the table tennis match, the Rwandan Ambassador to Turkey, Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Charles Kayonga, won first place, followed by Nicole Cyuzuzo.
There was also a panel discussion moderated by the Rwandan Ambassador to Turkey, Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Charles Kayonga, together with the Military Attaché, Col. Jean Paul Rulisa, Capt. Claudette Nishimwe, and Murenzi Lucas, Commercial Affairs Officer at the Rwandan Embassy in Turkey, as well as Dr. Faustin Hategekimana.
The discussions focused on the journey of Rwanda’s liberation, emphasizing the courage and dedication of the young men and women who were members of the former RPA in the struggle to liberate the country and stop the Genocide against the Tutsi in 1994.
They also highlighted their role in rebuilding the country and the opportunities that today’s youth have enjoyed due to the leadership that promoted unity and reconciliation after the Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda.
Ambassador Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Charles Kayonga explained that the liberation struggle went through various stages, including the one that ended on July 4, 1994, when the RPA defeated the regime that had planned and implemented the Genocide against the Tutsi.
He stressed that although the armed conflict ended 32 years ago, Rwanda continues to struggle to rebuild the country, develop the economy and continue changes aimed at improving the quality of life and sustainable development.
Ambassador Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Charles Kayonga urged the participants of this ceremony to always remember the lessons of history that led Rwanda to the Genocide against the Tutsi, pointing out that politics based on any kind of discrimination can lead the country to disaster.
He recalled that the 2003 Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda abolished all forms of discrimination, including ethnic discrimination and divisive ideology.
He continued by saying that good governance has enabled today's youth to grow up in Rwanda in peace, unity and progress.
He urged them to strive to preserve what the country has achieved and to reject divisive ideologies that continue to create insecurity and violate the rights of citizens in some parts of the region.
Also during this ceremony, Rwandan students who completed their studies at various universities in Turkey were commended for their efforts and good academic performance.
They were encouraged to continue to be exemplary and use the knowledge they have gained to develop Rwanda. The youth were encouraged to continue to dedicate themselves and contribute to the development of the country.
The event concluded with a concert featuring songs and dances that hark back to the history of the liberation struggle, as part of the celebration of 32 years of Rwanda's liberation.

title: Kinshasa: Anglican Church insists AFC/M23 are ‘brothers’ who should not be excluded from talks, 22 July 2026. The leadership of the Anglican Church in the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced that Congolese fighters and members of the AFC/M23 movement should not be excluded from the peace talks being planned.
excerpt: This message was delivered by the Church’s Spokesperson, Pastor Eric Nsenga, after its and Catholic Church representatives met with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi on 17 July 2026, and he agreed to hold “informal talks” aimed at resolving the country’s problems. Following…
title_en: Kinshasa: Anglican Church insists AFC/M23 are ‘brothers’ who should not be excluded from talks, 22 July 2026. The leadership of the Anglican Church in the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced that Congolese fighters and members of the AFC/M23 movement should not be excluded from the peace talks being planned.
excerpt_en: This message was delivered by the Church’s Spokesperson, Pastor Eric Nsenga, after its and Catholic Church representatives met with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi on 17 July 2026, and he agreed to hold “informal talks” aimed at resolving the country’s problems. Following…
body_en:
This message was delivered by the Church’s Spokesperson, Pastor Eric Nsenga, after its and Catholic Church representatives met with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi on 17 July 2026, and he agreed to hold “informal talks” aimed at resolving the country’s problems.
Following these talks, DRC Government Spokesperson, Patrick Muyaya, signaled that the participants in the Congolese talks would not include those who had taken up arms and those who had not openly condemned what he called the provocations taking place in the east of their country.
The DRC government has repeatedly attacked AFC/M23 fighters, sometimes calling them foreigners, criminals and terrorists, and sometimes accusing them of being tools of foreign powers. This shows that it is not ready to join this group in the inter-Congolese talks.
Pastor Nsenga said that the Catholic and Anglican Churches cannot support the inclusion of the AFC/M23 led by Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo in the talks between the Congolese and the DRC government, and that this has been shown to them by Tshisekedi.
He said, “Can we now say that those who took up arms, the group of Corneille Nangaa, are not being listened to? No, that is not what we can say. That is why you saw us in Goma. At that time, we had a serious conversation with President Félix. I will tell you. The president said that there would be provocations.”
The pastor said that in February 2025, the Catholic and Anglican Churches told Tshisekedi that there may be a real provocation but that Goma is controlled by Congolese who have taken up arms and have a reason to fight.
He said, “Instead of dwelling on this issue of saying that an armed group is a provocation, let’s look at how we can solve the problems of the children of the country. That is why we went to Goma, we listened to those who are in Goma. They are our brothers. There are things they have said, we have heard them.”
Pastor Nsenga stressed that this is not the time to continue the issue, but that each side should be listened to. He explained that the AFC/M23 has a reason to fight and that the Catholic and Anglican Churches, as mediators, have no responsibility to undermine the reasons people give.

excerpt_en: The partnership will be implemented through Pakistan’s “Look Africa” development initiative. The agreement will be used to establish mechanisms to promote trade between the two countries, including the establishment of a joint Pakistan-Rwanda trade group, regular high-level…
body_en:
The partnership will be implemented through Pakistan’s “Look Africa” development initiative.
The agreement will be used to establish mechanisms to promote trade between the two countries, including the establishment of a joint Pakistan-Rwanda trade group, regular high-level dialogues and close cooperation with the business community in both countries.
Pakistan began sharing a draft of the bilateral trade agreement with Rwanda in July 2018.
After extensive discussions through diplomatic channels, inter-ministerial talks and virtual meetings between leaders of both countries, Pakistan and Rwanda agreed to replace the existing agreement with a more comprehensive and easier-to-implement one.
The decision by the Government of Pakistan has paved the way for the signing of the final agreement, which will provide for private sector cooperation, trade fairs and exhibitions, cooperation between business associations, the establishment of a Joint Business Council, promotion of joint projects, exchange of trade-related information and the removal of non-tariff barriers to trade.
Pakistan launched its “Look Africa Policy” in 2017, with the aim of increasing its exports, attracting investment and strengthening economic ties with African countries.
The program aims to help Pakistan expand its markets beyond its current markets through diplomatic efforts, trade agreements, private sector engagement and participation in regional trade fairs.
This is in line with Rwanda’s ambitions, especially as it has emerged as one of the fastest growing economies in Africa and is known as a hub for trade and investment in Africa, making it a key partner for Pakistan in expanding its trade activities in the region.
Rwanda and Pakistan share relations and cooperation in various fields including education, political consultations, diplomatic cooperation, cooperation between the Rwandan Armed Forces and Pakistani security agencies, trade and others.
In April 2026, it participated in the International Tourism Expo being held in Pakistan, where it showcased its unique tourism industry and its natural beauty to the participants.
In 2025, Rwanda opened its embassy in Pakistan, while this Asian country opened its embassy in Rwanda in 2021.
In the same year, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe, announced that Rwanda and Pakistan are in talks aimed at promoting trade and tourism between the two sides, so that in the future, non-stop flights between the two countries will be launched.
On July 15, 2024, Ambassador Fatou Harerimana presented credentials to the President of Pakistan, Asif Ali Zardari, authorizing her to represent Rwanda in that country.
Pakistan is among the top importers of some of Rwanda's products such as tea, coffee, avocados and other agricultural and livestock products.
Rwanda imports medical equipment, rice, clothing materials, agricultural technology and others.

The President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, announced that he would launch talks aimed at finding a solution to the political and security problems facing the country, indicating that he wants to create a broad community to fight the war in the east.
excerpt: Tshisekedi had put forward a project to change the Constitution; the idea was opposed by political opponents including Martin Fayulu, Delly Sesanga and Jean-Marc Kabund who founded the ‘C64’ coalition with the aim of challenging him. On 17 July 2026, the leaders of the main…
title_en: The context of the inter-Congolese talks announced by Tshisekedi, 22 July 2026. The President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, announced that he would launch talks aimed at finding a solution to the political and security problems facing the country, indicating that he wants to create a broad community to fight the war in the east.
excerpt_en: Tshisekedi had put forward a project to change the Constitution; the idea was opposed by political opponents including Martin Fayulu, Delly Sesanga and Jean-Marc Kabund who founded the ‘C64’ coalition with the aim of challenging him. On 17 July 2026, the leaders of the main…
body_en:
Tshisekedi had put forward a project to change the Constitution; the idea was opposed by political opponents including Martin Fayulu, Delly Sesanga and Jean-Marc Kabund who founded the ‘C64’ coalition with the aim of challenging him.
On 17 July 2026, the leaders of the main religious groups in the DRC met with President Tshisekedi to discuss ways to calm the simmering tensions. It was then that he decided to launch “permanent talks” to unite the inter-Congolese.
While Tshisekedi has said he wants to use the talks as a weapon to confront the AFC/M23 coalition that controls much of eastern DRC, his opponents say they have not yet received any details.
What is known about the talks
So far, not much is known about the talks, but analysts agree that Tshisekedi's announcement is a good step, as he has been asked to launch them for a long time but has not done so.
Preparations are underway to organize the talks, but the dates and venue have not yet been announced.
The Catholic Archbishop of Kinshasa, Cardinal Fridolin Ambongo, said that the conditions and the way the talks will proceed will become clearer as the days go by. He is one of those who met with Tshisekedi last week.
Jeune Afrique reported that President Tshisekedi is expected to sign a decree officially launching the program, and that a committee will be set up to prepare and oversee them.
Some opposition figures have called for the talks to be held outside the country, while others have called for confidence-building measures between the conflicting parties, such as the release of political prisoners. The government has confirmed that the talks will be held in Kinshasa.
The government is reportedly considering returning the passports of some of the opposition members, but has rejected a request to commute the sentences of some of the most prominent figures, including those accused of being members of armed groups.

title_en: President Kagame meets with Gen Muhoozi on regional security, 25 July 2026. President Kagame received the Chief of Defence Staff of Uganda, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, for discussions focused on the strong relationship between Rwanda and Uganda, peace and security in the region.
excerpt_en: The talks that brought together the two sides took place in Kigali on 25 July 2026, when Gen Muhoozi was on a working visit to Rwanda.
body_en:
The talks that brought together the two sides took place in Kigali on 25 July 2026, when Gen Muhoozi was on a working visit to Rwanda.

It is expected that during the two-day visit, Gen Muhoozi will discuss with senior Rwandan military leaders on strengthening military-to-military relations between the two countries.

A message posted on the X account of the Office of the Head of State Village Urugwiro reads: “President Kagame received the Chief of Defence Staff of Uganda, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba.

Their discussions focused on the strong relationship between Rwanda and Uganda, peace and security in the region.” Gen Muhoozi was last in Rwanda in March 2025.

At that time, he discussed with senior Rwandan military leaders on bilateral cooperation, and visited the Nyakinama Military Academy in Musanze District. At this academy, Gen Muhoozi delivered lectures on cooperation between African countries in maintaining peace and security.

excerpt: This message from President Kagame, Francis Gatare, was delivered to Julius Debrah, Director General of the Office of the President of Ghana, on 25 July 2026. The Rwandan Embassy in Ghana announced that during the talks, Gatare briefed Julius Debrah on the activities of the…
title_en: President Kagame sends message to Ghanaian counterpart, 26 July 2026. President Paul Kagame sent a message to his Ghanaian counterpart, John Dramani Mahama, through the President of the African School of Governance (ASG), Francis Gatare, who was on a working visit to Accra.
excerpt_en: This message from President Kagame, Francis Gatare, was delivered to Julius Debrah, Director General of the Office of the President of Ghana, on 25 July 2026. The Rwandan Embassy in Ghana announced that during the talks, Gatare briefed Julius Debrah on the activities of the…
body_en:
This message from President Kagame, Francis Gatare, was delivered to Julius Debrah, Director General of the Office of the President of Ghana, on 25 July 2026.
The Rwandan Embassy in Ghana announced that during the talks, Gatare briefed Julius Debrah on the activities of the school of governance in Kigali, where it has made progress in promoting research and education in the field of governance.
Gatare was accompanied by the Rwandan Ambassador to Ghana, Rosemary Mbabazi, who participated in the talks that focused on the relationship between the two countries and the ongoing expansion of cooperation between Rwanda and Ghana.
During their discussions, they also discussed the African School of Governance’s partnership with the Accra Reset initiative, as well as how Rwanda and Ghana can continue to work together to promote cooperation and integration in Africa.
Accra Reset is an initiative that aims to bring together leaders, scholars, investors and other stakeholders to discuss how Africa can rethink its development and find new solutions to the challenges facing the continent.
It is a forum based on ideas for reforming governance, economics, technology and cooperation between African countries, with the aim of promoting solutions that come from within Africa rather than relying heavily on aid or solutions from outside it.
The African School of Governance is a school that aims to contribute to building future leaders through education, research and the provision of knowledge in the fields of public policy and governance.
Francis Gatare's visit to Ghana comes as the two countries continue to develop relations and cooperation in various fields, with the aim of maintaining a partnership that benefits their peoples and the African continent as a whole.

title: Minister Bizimana's response to Belgian journalist who mocked Rwandans over the death of King Rudahigwa, 26 July 2026. The Minister of Rwandan Unity and Civic Engagement, Dr Jean Damascène Bizimana, responded to Belgian journalist Peter Verlinden, who criticized him after writing about the death of King Mutara III Rudahigwa, saying that what he had said was a "distortion of history" and that there was no evidence that the King had been assassinated.
excerpt: The controversy began after Minister Bizimana posted on the X website on 25 July 2026, returning to the death of King Mutara III Rudahigwa, saying that his death was one of the most important and sad dates in Rwandan history that should not be forgotten. In his message,…
title_en: Minister Bizimana's response to Belgian journalist who mocked Rwandans over the death of King Rudahigwa, 26 July 2026. The Minister of Rwandan Unity and Civic Engagement, Dr Jean Damascène Bizimana, responded to Belgian journalist Peter Verlinden, who criticized him after writing about the death of King Mutara III Rudahigwa, saying that what he had said was a "distortion of history" and that there was no evidence that the King had been assassinated.
excerpt_en: The controversy began after Minister Bizimana posted on the X website on 25 July 2026, returning to the death of King Mutara III Rudahigwa, saying that his death was one of the most important and sad dates in Rwandan history that should not be forgotten. In his message,…
body_en:
The controversy began after Minister Bizimana posted on the X website on 25 July 2026, returning to the death of King Mutara III Rudahigwa, saying that his death was one of the most important and sad dates in Rwandan history that should not be forgotten.
In his message, Minister Bizimana said that on Saturday, July 25, 1959, shortly after 5:30 p.m., King of Rwanda Mutara III Rudahigwa, who was born in Nyanza in March 1911, passed away at the Prince Regent Hospital in Bujumbura.
He said that the death of Mutara III Rudahigwa was the result of an injection administered by a Belgian doctor named Dr. Vyncke, emphasizing that this was a political crime, and that it led Rwanda to a period of discrimination and persecution against the Tutsi from November 1959 until the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
Following the message, Peter Verlinden, a Belgian journalist and author, responded by saying that what Minister Bizimana said was a change of history.
Verlinden said that King Rudahigwa was not killed, so the idea that he was killed for political reasons is baseless.
Later, Verlinden reiterated that the fact that a Minister of State accuses another country of political killings is a serious problem, saying that this is a distortion of history.
Minister Bizimana asked him not to interfere in Rwandan history
In response, Minister Bizimana said that what he wrote was the history of his country and that he could not allow people outside Rwanda to change it or try to erase its evidence.
He said: “This is the history of my country, and I want to remind you. What gives you the right to interfere in the life of a country that is not yours and does not concern you?”
Minister Bizimana continued by saying that his presentation of the truth about Rwandan history should not be called distortion, but rather a confrontation with those who want parts of history to be forgotten.
He said, “Because I reveal things that you want to hide and erase, you call me a distorter of history to support your colonialist ideas and denial of history.”
Minister Bizimana also said that many years after Rudahigwa was killed, in 1994, Belgium expelled Queen Gicanda Rosalie who had gone to this country for medical treatment, knowing full well that she would be killed in the Genocide.

title: Rwanda and Tanzania in talks to strengthen ties, 27 July 2026. The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, Olivier Nduhungirehe, visited Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, where he held talks with his counterpart, Amb. Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Tanzania, aimed at strengthening relations between the two countries.
excerpt: The talks between the two leaders took place on Sunday, 26 July 2026. In addition to Nduhungirehe, on the Rwandan side were also attended by Gisa Teta, Head of Africa at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Gen. Patrick Nyamvumba, Rwandan Ambassador to Tanzania. The Rwandan…
title_en: Rwanda and Tanzania in talks to strengthen ties, 27 July 2026. The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, Olivier Nduhungirehe, visited Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, where he held talks with his counterpart, Amb. Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Tanzania, aimed at strengthening relations between the two countries.
excerpt_en: The talks between the two leaders took place on Sunday, 26 July 2026. In addition to Nduhungirehe, on the Rwandan side were also attended by Gisa Teta, Head of Africa at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Gen. Patrick Nyamvumba, Rwandan Ambassador to Tanzania. The Rwandan…
body_en:
The talks between the two leaders took place on Sunday, 26 July 2026. In addition to Nduhungirehe, on the Rwandan side were also attended by Gisa Teta, Head of Africa at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Gen. Patrick Nyamvumba, Rwandan Ambassador to Tanzania.
The Rwandan Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that their talks focused on “strengthening relations between the two countries”.
Minister Nduhungirehe's visit comes as Rwanda and Tanzania continue to work to further enhance cooperation in various fields, based on the bilateral relationship and the fact that they are members of the East African Community.
This relationship has also been marked by visits by senior leaders of both countries.
In May 2026, President Paul Kagame visited Tanzania, where he held talks with President Samia Suluhu Hassan.
During the visit, the two leaders discussed issues related to further developing relations between Rwanda and Tanzania, as well as strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.
At that time, President Kagame identified Tanzania as a key partner.
He said, “Tanzania is a key partner of Rwanda. Over the years, we have developed cooperation in various sectors, especially trade and transport, to facilitate Rwanda’s access to the international market. The President and I discussed how we can build on that foundation, to ensure that our cooperation model can increase investment and trade between our countries.”
He continued by saying, “We are proud of the progress that has been made, and we look forward to the implementation of our joint projects.”
This visit by President Kagame was followed by that of his counterpart, President Suluhu, to Kigali in May 2026.
Rwanda and Tanzania already have strong relations based on the fact that they are neighboring countries, united in the East African Community.
They have cooperation agreements in the areas of promoting trade, transport, investment and other development activities.

title: Rwanda has granted citizenship to over 100 people, mostly Burundians and Congolese, 28 July 2026. Rwanda has granted citizenship to 105 people born in 27 countries, mostly Burundians and the Democratic Republic of Congo.
excerpt: A statement released by the country's immigration authority shows that among those granted citizenship, 26 were born in Burundi, 20 were born in the DRC, nine were born in Uganda and eight were born in the United States. They include six born in Belgium, five born in…
title_en: Rwanda has granted citizenship to over 100 people, mostly Burundians and Congolese, 28 July 2026. Rwanda has granted citizenship to 105 people born in 27 countries, mostly Burundians and the Democratic Republic of Congo.
excerpt_en: A statement released by the country's immigration authority shows that among those granted citizenship, 26 were born in Burundi, 20 were born in the DRC, nine were born in Uganda and eight were born in the United States.
body_en:
A statement released by the country's immigration authority shows that among those granted citizenship, 26 were born in Burundi, 20 were born in the DRC, nine were born in Uganda and eight were born in the United States.

They include six born in Belgium, five born in Cameroon, four born in Kenya and three born in Rwanda to parents of foreign origin. Canada, the Netherlands, the Republic of Congo, Switzerland and Tanzania each have two people born in their country who have been granted Rwandan citizenship.

About 60% of those granted Rwandan citizenship are between 30 and 49 years of age, who appear to have the potential to contribute to the country's development. The next largest group are those aged between 50 and 64, those over 65, and youth under 30.

The youngest is 5 years old, the oldest is 81 years old. Rwandan citizenship came into effect on July 24, 2026, according to the official gazette in which the announcement was published.

title: Rwanda and Belarus to expand cooperation, 29 July 2026. Rwanda and Belarus have expressed their willingness to further develop relations and cooperation in sectors including trade, agriculture, technology, education and security.
excerpt: This was revealed on 28 July 2026 when Ambassador Gen Maj Joseph Nzabamwita presented credentials to the President of Belarus, Aleksandr Lukashenko, authorizing him to represent Rwanda in Belarus. Belarus has an economy based largely on industry, agriculture, technology and…
title_en: Rwanda and Belarus to expand cooperation, 29 July 2026. Rwanda and Belarus have expressed their willingness to further develop relations and cooperation in sectors including trade, agriculture, technology, education and security.
excerpt_en: This was revealed on 28 July 2026 when Ambassador Gen Maj Joseph Nzabamwita presented credentials to the President of Belarus, Aleksandr Lukashenko, authorizing him to represent Rwanda in Belarus. Belarus has an economy based largely on industry, agriculture, technology and…
body_en:
This was revealed on 28 July 2026 when Ambassador Gen Maj Joseph Nzabamwita presented credentials to the President of Belarus, Aleksandr Lukashenko, authorizing him to represent Rwanda in Belarus.
Belarus has an economy based largely on industry, agriculture, technology and trade, and is well known for manufacturing agricultural machinery, industrial equipment and other technological equipment.
Belarus gained independence in 1991 after the collapse of the Soviet Union. It shares borders with other countries including Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.
President Lukashenko said that Belarus wants to increase economic cooperation with Rwanda, describing it as a foundation for the development of bilateral political relations.
He said, “Belarus wants to expand its relations with Rwanda. We attach special importance to economic cooperation as a foundation for building political relations.”
Lukashenko called for the strengthening of trade between the two countries, and for the establishment of a joint commission that would play a role in promoting cooperation projects in key sectors.
Ambassador Nzabamwita said that he was happy with the new role of representing Rwanda in Belarus, indicating that he would do everything possible to promote Rwanda’s interests and strengthen relations between the two countries.
He said, “It is a great honor to represent my country and its leadership as the non-resident Ambassador to Belarus. I will strive to promote Rwanda’s interests and cooperation between our countries.”
Cooperation between Rwanda and Belarus has been discussed on various occasions, with both countries expressing their willingness to work together in the fields of agriculture, industry, information technology, education and security.
Belarus has also expressed its willingness to assist Rwanda in acquiring agricultural machinery and providing maintenance services.
In August 2025, Ambassador Nzabamwita, who also represents Rwanda in Russia, discussed with the Belarusian Ambassador to Russia, Aleksandr Rogozhnik, how the two countries could further enhance cooperation in these areas.
This step comes as Rwanda continues to expand its relations with various countries around the world, seeking new opportunities in trade, investment and the development of various sectors.
Economy and Tech.

title: Rwanda to start producing its own lightning rods, 23 July 2026. The Ministry of Emergency Situations (MINEMA) has announced that Rwanda has a plan to start producing its own lightning rods in order to find affordable lightning rods for every Rwandan who needs to have a lightning rod in their home.
excerpt: The Director General in charge of monitoring disaster-prone areas at MINEMA, Niyotwambaza Christine, made the announcement in Karongi District, on 23 July 2026, during the official handover of powerful lightning rods installed at GS Musango and Musango Power Station. The…
title_en: Rwanda to start producing its own lightning rods, 23 July 2026. The Ministry of Emergency Situations (MINEMA) has announced that Rwanda has a plan to start producing its own lightning rods in order to find affordable lightning rods for every Rwandan who needs to have a lightning rod in their home.
excerpt_en: The Director General in charge of monitoring disaster-prone areas at MINEMA, Niyotwambaza Christine, made the announcement in Karongi District, on 23 July 2026, during the official handover of powerful lightning rods installed at GS Musango and Musango Power Station. The…
body_en:
The Director General in charge of monitoring disaster-prone areas at MINEMA, Niyotwambaza Christine, made the announcement in Karongi District, on 23 July 2026, during the official handover of powerful lightning rods installed at GS Musango and Musango Power Station.
The power station and the facility are located in Rwankuba Sector, one of the five sectors in Karongi that are often struck by lightning.
Dushimimana John from Rwankuba Sector told IGIHE that Rwankuba is often struck by lightning, killing residents, livestock and electrical equipment.
He said, “I know of more than seven people in Rwankuba Sector who have died after being struck by lightning. The reason is that we don’t have lightning rods in our houses. We don’t know where to buy them, we don’t even know how much they cost.”
The Deputy Mayor of Karongi District, in charge of economic development, Ntakirutimana Julienne, said that the districts most frequently affected by lightning are Rwankuba, Gitesi, Ruganda and Rugabano because they are located in a series of high mountains that make up the Congo-Nile Basin. Lightning strikes are common in high mountains.
The Director General of MINEMA, Niyotwambaza Christine, said that the reason why many residents do not have lightning rods in their houses is because they are expensive.
He said, “Lightning rods are very expensive, you cannot find a lightning rod that costs less than 3 million Rwf.”
Niyotwambaza said that in collaboration with MIMENA, RP Karongi College, the Rwanda Standards Board (RSB), and the National Center for Research, Technology, and Innovation (NCST), they will next week evaluate the lightning rod being manufactured in Rwanda.
He said, “At the national level, we do not have the capacity to certify it, we will export it, if those who have the knowledge and experience to manufacture lightning rods tell us that it has lightning protection capabilities, we will have reached another stage of starting to manufacture it in Rwanda. When we start manufacturing it in Rwanda, we will take another step to find a way to make it cheap so that the citizen can buy it and install it in his house.”
MINEMA figures show that in the past four years, lightning has killed 287 people and left more than 950 permanently disabled.
Mugarura Amiri, who works at the Ottawa Lightning Protection Center in Rwanda, said that installing concrete in houses and wearing plastic shoes reduces the risk of being struck by lightning by 85%.
This innovative lightning protection system installed in Musango was built by the United Nations Office for Migration (IOM) with funding from the Government of Japan.
Takashi Ujikawa, an IOM official who is supporting Rwanda’s lightning protection program, said that the reason they support disaster prevention programs is because they are one of the reasons why people move from their homes to become migrants.

title: Modern farming expertise to cost Rwanda $5 million, 24 July 2026. The Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MINAGRI), in collaboration with the Rwanda Agricultural Research Institute (RICA), is involved in a project that will see farmers cultivating 600,000 hectares of land across the country practicing soil conservation agriculture in a project that will cost $5 million.
excerpt: It is a project that aims to expand and integrate soil conservation agriculture into agricultural extension programs, which began by providing training to various categories of workers in the agricultural sector close to the people. Those trained will then teach the people…
title_en: Modern farming expertise to cost Rwanda $5 million, 24 July 2026. The Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MINAGRI), in collaboration with the Rwanda Agricultural Research Institute (RICA), is involved in a project that will see farmers cultivating 600,000 hectares of land across the country practicing soil conservation agriculture in a project that will cost $5 million.
excerpt_en: It is a project that aims to expand and integrate soil conservation agriculture into agricultural extension programs, which began by providing training to various categories of workers in the agricultural sector close to the people. Those trained will then teach the people…
body_en:
It is a project that aims to expand and integrate soil conservation agriculture into agricultural extension programs, which began by providing training to various categories of workers in the agricultural sector close to the people.
Those trained will then teach the people how to practice soil conservation agriculture where the project will be implemented for four years.
This project will be implemented in all districts where land consolidation agriculture is practiced, starting with 100,000 hectares in the next cropping season, then 150,000 hectares until 2029, reaching 600,000 hectares.
So far, 168 people have been trained, including district agricultural officers and agricultural extension officers in RAB.
On July 22, another two-day training course began at RICA in Bugesera, which will be given to 52 agricultural interns in all districts.
This is while the total number of people who will be trained in this project is 889 before the start of the 2027 A (Autumn) cropping season.
The Director of Agricultural Extension and Livestock in RICA, Dr. Harelimana Léonce, said that the project aims to create a sustainable agriculture in Rwanda and increase production.
He said, “We want sustainable agriculture to ensure that the land is not bare, so that even our rivers are filled with soil due to erosion. Another is to increase production because the land will have recovered.”
Dr. Harelimana explained that in conventional agriculture, there are some things that people do wrong that damage production, including over-cultivating the field, which makes the soil soft and easily eroded.
There is also the practice of burning the field to remove all the grass residues and using chemical fertilizers at once, which makes the plants unable to use it all and the remaining ones harm the environment, as well as not mulching.
In mixed farming, the soil must be covered, not plowed too much, and the fertilizer must be applied in stages and close to the plants so that it does not die in vain.
In terms of production, the land is taken care of and maintained, for a maize crop grown on good seeds, seven tons can be obtained per hectare, while on unmanaged land, less than two tons per hectare.
For beans, the yield per hectare on managed land ranges from 1.6 tons to more, but on unmanaged land it does not exceed 500 kilograms.
The coordinator of this project at MINAGRI, Dr. Nkurunziza Christian, said that what they want to solve is the problem of land that clearly needs attention in order to continue to produce significant yields.
He said, “Today, the land is not increasing, but we want it to produce as much as possible. If we do not maintain it, it will lose its originality because, as in the past, there were fields, but now this is no longer possible, it requires cultivation every season. There have been efforts such as cutting terraces, but they did not produce enough, so we decided to bring this project.”
Trainee Eric, who is among the trainees working in Ruhango District, said he learned that crop rotation helps reduce crop diseases, and that soil conservation methods reduce the number of wastes in agriculture in general, which is knowledge he is going to share with farmers.

title: Harvesting 18 tons of potatoes per hectare: Highlights of the agricultural exhibition in Kigali, 24 July 2026. More than 200 farmers and livestock producers supported by six projects under the Rwanda Agricultural Board-SPIU (RAB-SPIU) are set to showcase their work at the 10-day agricultural exhibition in Kigali.
excerpt: The annual exhibition is organized by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, and this year it was attended by more than 600 exhibitors, including individuals, companies and groups. Among those who will be showcasing their work are those supported by six projects operating…
title_en: Harvesting 18 tons of potatoes per hectare: Highlights of the agricultural exhibition in Kigali, 24 July 2026. More than 200 farmers and livestock producers supported by six projects under the Rwanda Agricultural Board-SPIU (RAB-SPIU) are set to showcase their work at the 10-day agricultural exhibition in Kigali.
excerpt_en: The annual exhibition is organized by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, and this year it was attended by more than 600 exhibitors, including individuals, companies and groups. Among those who will be showcasing their work are those supported by six projects operating…
body_en:
The annual exhibition is organized by the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, and this year it was attended by more than 600 exhibitors, including individuals, companies and groups.
Among those who will be showcasing their work are those supported by six projects operating under RAB, namely SAIP, CDAT, KIWIIP, SAPMP, RDDP and PRISM.
All these projects have worked with farmers or herders to help them improve their practices and the results they have achieved show that their efforts have made positive progress.
Iyakaremye Wenceslas, who is part of the Kowabimuru Cooperative, which grows potatoes in the Karongi and Rutsiro districts, said that they started as self-help groups but later came together to form a cooperative in 2018 when they came across the SAIP project.
This project has helped them to farm better, and they have been able to increase their production from less than seven tons of potatoes per hectare to more than 18 tons per hectare.
In particular, SAIP provided them with six irrigation machines, carts for transporting produce, and equipment for spraying pesticides, among other things, which allowed them to expand their cultivated area from 161 hectares to more than 200 hectares.
He added, “Personally, I have reached a point where I can work with financial institutions. I recently took out a loan of 12 million Frw and I am also growing two or three hectares of my own and getting good yields.”
Uzamukunda Yikunda, who heads an agricultural and livestock cooperative in Muhanga District, said that they started working in 2007 but that they had no tangible activities until they started receiving support from the CDAT project. Now, they have a sugarcane factory and export products abroad, which is further developing them.
Rukera Christine, founder and head of CF Premium, a pepper farming company in Kicukiro District, said that the SAIP project played a major role in this because it helped her make a profit.
She revealed that she used to grow pepper on 22 hectares and produce less than eight tons, but SAIP helped her grow it with irrigation and increased the area she grows to 30 hectares, and now she produces 14 tons per hectare.
Mugisha Eric, head of a fruit growing cooperative in Kayonza District, said that the KIWIIP project was what enabled them to start operations in 2021 and now they have received about 300 million Rwf, and they are now able to export avocados abroad and they are also making progress.
He said, “All the members brought was land, and before they used to grow sorghum and other crops, they earned no more than 200,000 Rwf per hectare, but now they earn about 2 million Rwf in one season.”
These farmers and livestock producers, apart from the obvious attractions they had to exhibit in Kigali, agree that this exhibition helps them find new markets and learn from others and improve their practices.
The Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Dr. Ndabamenye Telesphore, said that promoting agricultural and livestock activities is very important in building partnerships and collaborations that enable timely solutions to be found.
He said, “This shows that agricultural and livestock production cannot be achieved without innovation or collaboration in solving the problems facing agriculture and livestock in Rwanda.”
The Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock indicates that agriculture and livestock constitute about 19% of the country’s gross domestic product, and 70% of industries in Rwanda process agricultural products.
Under the Fifth Five-Year Agricultural Transformation Plan (PSTA5), Rwanda will spend $5.4 billion to develop this sector.

title: Ruti Joel helped Rwandans living in Indonesia to celebrate 32 years since the liberation of Rwanda, 22 July 2026. Rwandans living in Indonesia celebrated 32 years since the liberation of Rwanda, showing how culture can also be a bridge that strengthens relations between countries.
excerpt: It is a ceremony marked by various activities that took place from 17 to 18 July 2026 in Jakarta. It was attended by representatives of the Government of Indonesia, representatives of their countries in this country, international organizations, Rwandans living in Indonesia…
title_en: Ruti Joel helped Rwandans living in Indonesia to celebrate 32 years since the liberation of Rwanda, 22 July 2026. Rwandans living in Indonesia celebrated 32 years since the liberation of Rwanda, showing how culture can also be a bridge that strengthens relations between countries.
excerpt_en: It is a ceremony marked by various activities that took place from 17 to 18 July 2026 in Jakarta. It was attended by representatives of the Government of Indonesia, representatives of their countries in this country, international organizations, Rwandans living in Indonesia…
body_en:
It is a ceremony marked by various activities that took place from 17 to 18 July 2026 in Jakarta.
It was attended by representatives of the Government of Indonesia, representatives of their countries in this country, international organizations, Rwandans living in Indonesia and friends of Rwanda.
Today was celebrated on the theme of showing how Rwanda's progress in development continues.
It has been pointed out that liberation is a great day in the history of Rwanda that shows the journey to rebuild the country after the Genocide against the Tutsis in 1994 that left it in shambles.
The participants of this event were also shown that the celebration of Rwanda's liberation day reflects the integrity of Rwandans, strengthening unity and reconciliation and the country's efforts to build a better future based on peace and development.
The Ambassador of Rwanda to Indonesia, Sheikh Abdul Karim Harelimana, said that what Rwanda has achieved today is based on visionary management, the loyalty of Rwandans and the common will to rebuild the country.
He pointed out how Rwanda is now recognized internationally due to the progress it has made in good governance, security, equality, innovation, environmental protection, health, education and economic development.
He said, "It reminds us that liberating the country is not a historical event, but an ongoing responsibility. Rwanda's journey continues through unity, loyalty and trust as we continue to strive to build a better future for our descendants."
Santo Darmosumarto, the Director General for Africa and Asia Pacific in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, who represented the Government of Indonesia in this event, said that Rwanda's trip was a lesson for many countries including Indonesia, because of the strength of unity and willingness to rebuild the country.
He said: "On behalf of the Government and the people of Indonesia, I express the respect and solidarity we owe to Rwandans. The extraordinary journey of Rwanda has given many countries the strength to believe in the ability of unity and reconstruction. Peace, reconciliation and development must go hand in hand."
In this song, Ruti Joel expressed the uniqueness of Nyarwanda culture through his songs and conveyed it to the youth through modern methods.

title: July saw above-normal temperatures in Rwanda, 24 July 2026. Rwanda's temperatures in the second half of July 2026 were above normal, with temperatures exceeding the average for that period.
excerpt: A report by the National Meteorological Institute (Meteo Rwanda) for farmers and ranchers indicates that from 11 to 20 July 2026, temperatures were above normal compared to the past 30 years. The Meteo Rwanda report indicates that during those ten days, rainfall was higher in…
title_en: July saw above-normal temperatures in Rwanda, 24 July 2026. Rwanda's temperatures in the second half of July 2026 were above normal, with temperatures exceeding the average for that period.
excerpt_en: A report by the National Meteorological Institute (Meteo Rwanda) for farmers and ranchers indicates that from 11 to 20 July 2026, temperatures were above normal compared to the past 30 years. The Meteo Rwanda report indicates that during those ten days, rainfall was higher in…
body_en:
A report by the National Meteorological Institute (Meteo Rwanda) for farmers and ranchers indicates that from 11 to 20 July 2026, temperatures were above normal compared to the past 30 years.
The Meteo Rwanda report indicates that during those ten days, rainfall was higher in many parts of the country compared to the average rainfall for those dates over the past several years.
However, there were areas where rainfall decreased, including most of Kigali City, some parts of the Southern and Northern Provinces, as well as the districts of Kayonza, Nyagatare and Nyamasheke.
Meteo Rwanda said that where rainfall was observed, it fell for between one and five days. The heaviest rainfall was observed in some parts of the districts of Nyamasheke, Nyaruguru, Musanze and Nyabihu.
At the Busogo ISAE station in Musanze District, 40.9 millimeters of rain were measured, falling in two days. According to Ntendezi in Nyamasheke District, 37.7 millimeters were measured, falling in five days, while according to Kibeho in Nyaruguru District, 31.2 millimeters were measured, falling in one day.
During that period, some parts of Kigali City, Eastern Province, Southern Province and Northern Province did not receive rain.
Temperatures above normal
Meteo Rwanda indicated that in many parts of the country, temperatures were above the normal average between July 11 and 20.
The lowest temperature was recorded at Kinigi in Musanze District, where it was 20.7°C. The highest temperature was recorded at Bugarama in Rusizi District, where it reached 32.1°C.
In general, Meteo Rwanda said that Rusizi District, especially the Bugarama Valley, recorded the highest temperature in the country during that period.
The report also shows that the minimum temperature in most parts of the country was above the average minimum temperature observed between July 11 and 20.
The lowest temperature was recorded at Busogo in Musanze District, where it was 12°C, while the highest temperature was recorded at Bugarama in Rusizi District, where it was 19.9°C.
Meteo Rwanda indicated that Musanze, Burera and Nyabihu Districts were the coldest areas in the country during that period.
Meteo Rwanda advised farmers to continue to consult with their local agricultural advisors and carry out activities related to the C growing season, including planting in swamps and irrigating where possible.
Farmers were also asked to prepare for the 2027 A season, while livestock farmers were asked to contact veterinarians for advice on how to care for their livestock based on the expected weather and summer conditions.
Meteo Rwanda urged the population to continue monitoring weather forecast information and use it in planning agricultural and livestock activities.

title_en: 360,000 families appeal to the Mutual Fund contribution authorities, 26 July 2026. The Director of the Department of Social Welfare in the Ministry of Local Government, Kayigana Godfrey, said that there is a problem that has not been resolved by the financial institution that determines the Mutual Fund contribution that they must pay, with more than 360,000 people appealing.
excerpt_en: He said this in an interview on Royal FM that was about the new mutual health insurance contributions that came into effect in the 2026/27 financial year. The inclusion of residents in the financial institutions is done using the MINALOC Social Security System. However, when…
body_en:
He said this in an interview on Royal FM that was about the new mutual health insurance contributions that came into effect in the 2026/27 financial year.
The inclusion of residents in the financial institutions is done using the MINALOC Social Security System. However, when it began to be used to determine the Mutual Fund contribution that members will pay, it was discovered that there were errors.
Kayigana said, "When you start something, mistakes are inevitable. The fact that more than 360,000 households have already appealed means that there are problems with this technology. All of this will help MINALOC and RSSB to improve it so that in the coming years everyone is in the category they deserve to be in."
Of the 360,000 households that appealed, about 340,000 have already been answered.
The director explained that the information entered into the Social System website is based on a person's social information, especially their activities and income, but that more can be added.
He said that in the next three years, this system, which is still in its first year, will contain a lot of personal information, including money flowing through their accounts and their phone.
In general, the new contributions paid are divided into five categories based on the level of the population's finances. Among these institutions, there are three where residents pay the entire contribution themselves, while those in the other two are subsidized by the government.
The Director of Mobilization and Registration of Mutual Insurance Members at the National Social Security Board (RSSB), Ntigurirwa Deogratias, announced that Rwandans are paying contributions to the mutual health insurance, which has decreased by 12% this year compared to the previous year.
He indicated that since the beginning of this year, they have received contributions equivalent to 51% of all those who are required to pay and that they have put a lot of effort into mobilization, although it has not yet yielded sufficient results.
He said that the reason is that there is still a problem of residents who still have the attitude of being hesitant in paying the increased Mutual Insurance contribution, even though some of them are capable of it.
He said, "Many people were used to giving 3,000 Frw, and those who gave 7,000 Frw were few. So telling someone who used to give 3,000 Frw that today they should give 8,000 Frw, even if they have the means, is somewhat difficult and requires a lot of explaining. Today we are at 51%, and last year at this time we were at 63%. This means that there is a gap between where we were last year and where we are today."

title: Ebola outbreak in DRC: Cases surpass 3,200, deaths reach 1,405, 27 July 2026. The Ebola outbreak continues to escalate in the Democratic Republic of Congo, DRC, where as of 25 July 2026, 3,200 people had been infected, while 1,405 had died.
excerpt: Ministry of Health figures show that 773 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, while 571 have recovered. The mortality rate from the epidemic has reached 43.9%, while people who came into contact with infected people are being followed up at a rate of 77.8%. The Ministry…
title_en: Ebola outbreak in DRC: Cases surpass 3,200, deaths reach 1,405, 27 July 2026. The Ebola outbreak continues to escalate in the Democratic Republic of Congo, DRC, where as of 25 July 2026, 3,200 people had been infected, while 1,405 had died.
excerpt_en: Ministry of Health figures show that 773 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, while 571 have recovered. The mortality rate from the epidemic has reached 43.9%, while people who came into contact with infected people are being followed up at a rate of 77.8%. The Ministry…
body_en:
Ministry of Health figures show that 773 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, while 571 have recovered. The mortality rate from the epidemic has reached 43.9%, while people who came into contact with infected people are being followed up at a rate of 77.8%.
The Ministry of Health in the DRC says that Ebola response measures are being stepped up in the five provinces where the outbreak has been detected: Ituri, Haut-Uélé, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo.
Doctors and other health workers are continuing to identify those with symptoms, test suspected cases, treat patients and trace contacts.
Ituri remains the hardest hit. In this province, the number of teams monitoring the outbreak, laboratory capacity and clinics have been increased.
In Ituri, a campaign is also being carried out to explain the seriousness of Ebola to the population, monitor those entering and leaving the affected areas and provide equipment to workers who will be dealing with the outbreak.
The World Health Organization (WHO) reported that as of July 15, Ituri had accounted for nearly 90% of the total number of cases, mainly in Bunia, Mongbwalu, Nizi and Nyankunde.
The Ebola outbreak is caused by a strain of the virus known as Bundibugyo. The outbreak, which was declared in Ituri on May 15, 2026, is the 17th to hit the DRC since the Ebola virus was first identified in 1976.
On May 17, the WHO declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, requiring international cooperation to contain it.
The WHO had reported that on July 15, the DRC had 2,124 Ebola cases and 828 deaths. In the following 10 days, the number of infected people increased by 1,076, and the number of deaths increased by 577.
The fight against the epidemic remains difficult due to challenges including insecurity, population displacement, and people refusing to go to health facilities, choosing to get sick at home.
There is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo Ebola, but trials of drugs containing MBP134 and remdesivir have begun in the DRC, which are expected to reduce deaths and the severity of the epidemic.
Justice and Rights

title: Gen Tshiwewe asked to be released on parole because he kept important secrets, 21 July 2026, Gen Christian Tshiwewe Songesha, who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, asked the military court to release him temporarily because he kept important secrets.
excerpt: This soldier, who was also the head of the army in charge of protecting senior officials and adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi on military affairs, was arrested on July 9, 2025. He is accused of crimes including treason, encouraging soldiers to commit illegal acts and…
title_en: Gen Tshiwewe asked to be released on parole because he kept important secrets, 21 July 2026, Gen Christian Tshiwewe Songesha, who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, asked the military court to release him temporarily because he kept important secrets.
excerpt_en: This soldier, who was also the head of the army in charge of protecting senior officials and adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi on military affairs, was arrested on July 9, 2025. He is accused of crimes including treason, encouraging soldiers to commit illegal acts and…
body_en:
This soldier, who was also the head of the army in charge of protecting senior officials and adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi on military affairs, was arrested on July 9, 2025.
He is accused of crimes including treason, encouraging soldiers to commit illegal acts and illegal possession of weapons. It is all related to the plan to remove Tshisekedi's regime.
Gen Tshiwewe is competing with others including Maj Gen Maurice Nyembo, Brig Gen John Ngoy Kabila, Brig Gen John Sangwa Muhemedi, Col Guy Mukombozi Zahinda, Col Pathy Sangwa Lumbu and Col Christophe Tshibangu Kenge.
Gen John Numbi who headed the RDC Police and the Inspector General of the country's military and Brig Gen Chinyabuuma Pascal Kamukinde and civilian Pascal Nyembo were also among the defendants in this case but they escaped.
After the commencement of their trial on June 4, 2026, where the court examined their profiles, Gen Tshiwewe used his lawyer, Me Parfait Kanyanga, to request their release.
On July 21, Me Kanyanga pointed out that Gen Tshiwewe has been released on bail, he cannot escape justice, so the court should not be worried.
Mr. Kanyanga also said that in relation to the fact that his client has done important work in the military, the Ndolo military prison where he is being held is not the place he should be because he is keeping important secrets.
This lawyer pointed out that the way Gen Tshiwewe was prosecuted was against the law, because he was not subjected to a preliminary investigation after his arrest.
He explained that there were no concrete reasons to show that Gen Tshiwewe may have committed the crimes he is accused of, so that they would have been based on sending him to Ndolo prison.
Others in this file who were detained in Ndolo military prison also pointed out that the way they were prosecuted was against the law, they asked the military court to release them on bail, and they tried them outside.

title: Major Ntabakuze, who recently appeared for questioning, again requested his early release, 22 July 2026. Major Aloys Ntabakuze, who was the Commander of a commando battalion in the defeated Rwandan Armed Forces (Ex-FAR), has again requested the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) for his early release.
excerpt: The soldier submitted this request on 29 June 2026 after the President of the IRMCT, Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected his previous request on the grounds that the request exceeded the word limit on 26 June. The IRMCT states that a request should not exceed 3000 words, but on…
title_en: Major Ntabakuze, who recently appeared for questioning, again requested his early release, 22 July 2026. Major Aloys Ntabakuze, who was the Commander of a commando battalion in the defeated Rwandan Armed Forces (Ex-FAR), has again requested the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) for his early release.
excerpt_en: The soldier submitted this request on 29 June 2026 after the President of the IRMCT, Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected his previous request on the grounds that the request exceeded the word limit on 26 June. The IRMCT states that a request should not exceed 3000 words, but on…
body_en:
The soldier submitted this request on 29 June 2026 after the President of the IRMCT, Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected his previous request on the grounds that the request exceeded the word limit on 26 June.
The IRMCT states that a request should not exceed 3000 words, but on 22 June, Ntabakuze's lawyer, Me Sandrine Gaillot, had written 4636 words. Graciela allowed him to submit another request that complied with the guidelines.
After Maj Ntabakuze and his lawyer requested that the second request be kept confidential, on July 21, Graciela reminded them that all events at the IRMCT must be public unless special reasons are shown for confidentiality.
The judge noted that a convicted person represented by a lawyer, when requesting early release, must submit a document addressed to this institution along with another document containing the information to be disclosed.
Graciela explained that Maj Ntabakuze was reminded that he must submit another document containing the information to be disclosed but that he did not comply.
The judge asked Maj Ntabakuze to prepare another document containing the information to be disclosed and submit it within 14 days so that his request can be considered.
Maj Ntabakuze was the commander of the Ex-FAR para-commando battalion from June 1988 to July 1994.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) had convicted him of ordering para-commandos to kill Tutsis on Nyanza Hill in Kicukiro on 11 April 1994 and at the former IAMSEA college in Remera on 15 April 1994.
The former IAMSEA (African and Mauritian Institute of Statistics and Economics) was the site of the KIE after the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, which later became a department of the University of Rwanda.
The ICTR Trial Chamber convicted Maj Ntabakuze of genocide, extermination and persecution as crimes against humanity and sentenced him to life imprisonment, but he appealed and was sentenced to 35 years in prison on 8 May 2012.
After his conviction, Maj Ntabakuze was transferred to a prison in Benin under an extradition agreement between that country and the United Nations.
Maj Ntabakuze is requesting early release on the grounds that he has served two-thirds of his sentence, a percentage determined by the IRMCT.

The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) had convicted him of ordering para-commandos to kill Tutsis on Nyanza Hill in Kicukiro on 11 April 1994 and at the former IAMSEA college in Remera on 15 April 1994.
The former IAMSEA (African and Mauritian Institute of Statistics and Economics) was the site of the KIE after the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, which later became a department of the University of Rwanda.
The ICTR Trial Chamber convicted Maj Ntabakuze of genocide, extermination and persecution as crimes against humanity and sentenced him to life imprisonment, but he appealed and was sentenced to 35 years in prison on 8 May 2012.
After his conviction, Maj Ntabakuze was transferred to a prison in Benin under an extradition agreement between that country and the United Nations.
Maj Ntabakuze is requesting early release on the grounds that he has served two-thirds of his sentence, a percentage determined by the IRMCT.
