Mathayo Ngirumpatse, who was convicted of genocide and crimes against humanity and sentenced to life imprisonment, requested the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) to release him on grounds of ill health and retirement.
excerpt: Ngirumpatse was the President of the MRND party that ruled Rwanda from 1975 to 1994. After the death of Juvenal Habyarimana, he played a key role in establishing the Interim Government that implemented the Genocide against the Tutsi, led by Théodore Sindikubwabo. The…
title_en: Mathayo Ngirumpatse, sentenced to life imprisonment, requested release on 23 July 2026. Mathayo Ngirumpatse, who was convicted of genocide and crimes against humanity and sentenced to life imprisonment, requested the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) to release him on grounds of ill health and retirement.
excerpt_en: Ngirumpatse was the President of the MRND party that ruled Rwanda from 1975 to 1994. After the death of Juvenal Habyarimana, he played a key role in establishing the Interim Government that implemented the Genocide against the Tutsi, led by Théodore Sindikubwabo. The…
body_en:
Ngirumpatse was the President of the MRND party that ruled Rwanda from 1975 to 1994. After the death of Juvenal Habyarimana, he played a key role in establishing the Interim Government that implemented the Genocide against the Tutsi, led by Théodore Sindikubwabo.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) convicted Ngirumpatse of participating in the planning of the Genocide, inciting the Interahamwe to commit Genocide, and inciting the Inrerahamwe to rape Tutsi women and girls, and sentenced him to life imprisonment on 2 February 2012.
Judge Denis Bryon, who presided over the trial, stated that based on the gravity of the crimes Ngirumpatse was convicted of and the manner in which they were committed, the entire panel of judges found him to be worthy of life imprisonment.
Ngirumpatse was not satisfied with this verdict. He appealed, requesting an acquittal, but on 29 September 2014, the ICTR Appeals Chamber upheld the charges against him in the original trial, upholding his life sentence.
In December 2017, Ngirumpatse, who was being held in Arusha at the ICTR, was transferred to Sébikhotane prison in Senegal to serve the rest of his life sentence.
On July 23, 2026, Ngirumpatse's lawyer, Me Frédéric Weyl, wrote to the President of the IRMCT, Graciela Gatti Santana, asking her to either release his client from prison or release him early.
Me Weyl indicated that since 1999, his client, who had been in detention for a year, had begun to suffer from health problems including worsening diabetes, Hepatitis C, high blood pressure, stroke and eye disease.
The lawyer explained to Graciela that due to the stroke, Ngirumpatse cannot stand for long periods of time, so in order to avoid falling down, as happened four times while he was in the shower, he walks with a cane.
He said, "He can no longer bathe himself. Since his stroke, a fellow prisoner has brought him water, cleaned his cell, changed his bedding, and managed to do simple things including washing his clothes. This problem has been going on for over a year."
Ngirumpatse says that since Senegal has decided not to imprison people over 70 years of age, even if they are in good health, he also believes that he should be released because he is 86 years old.
Among the reasons that the IRMCT bases its early release on those it has imprisoned, include that they have completed two-thirds of their sentence. For those sentenced to life imprisonment, this is equivalent to 45 years.
Me Weyl believes that based on this principle, Ngirumpatse should wait to apply for release on June 4, 2028, when he will have served 30 years in prison, at the age of 89. He says that it would be difficult for him to be alive at that time and still be living the life he has been living.
Ngirumpatse points out that the principle of completing two-thirds of a sentence regardless of age makes the sentence a death sentence.
The lawyer requested that Senegalese law be considered, because if a prisoner behaves well in prison, 25 years is considered two-thirds of a life sentence, as each year is reduced by three months.
Although Ngirumpatse is requesting release, he continues to maintain his innocence, even though he respects the conclusion of his trial in the ICTR Appeals Chamber. He says that he was convicted solely for having been President of the MRND.
In 2024, Ngirumpatse had also requested the IRMCT to release him early, but this body rejected it because he had not served 30 years, which is considered two-thirds of a life sentence.

The retreat was attended by a large number of RCS executive board members who also formed the decision-making council.

title_en: RCS leaders discuss how prisoners can return home with confidence and the ability to avoid crime, 23 July 2026. RCS Commissioner General, CG Evaritse Murenzi, inaugurated a three-day retreat for staff of the Rwanda Correctional Service, RCS. The retreat was attended by a large number of RCS executive board members who also formed the decision-making council.
excerpt_en: The retreat is being held at the Gako Military Academy in Bugesera District. The retreat, which began on 23 July, saw RCS staff and invited partners learn together about the progress of the Rwanda Correctional Service in implementing its core mission of rehabilitating…
body_en:
The retreat is being held at the Gako Military Academy in Bugesera District.
The retreat, which began on 23 July, saw RCS staff and invited partners learn together about the progress of the Rwanda Correctional Service in implementing its core mission of rehabilitating offenders who are punished by the courts, and preparing them to return to Rwandan society as productive members of their families and Rwandan society at large.
CG Evariste Murenzi, opening the retreat, reminded the staff of their own responsibilities and those of RCS, including that RCS has a strong responsibility to reform through prison management and providing quality services, protecting the rights of prisoners, and preparing them well to return to normal life with confidence and the ability to prevent crime and contribute to the development of the country.
He affirmed that RCS has a responsibility to change the mindset and behavior of prisoners, to train them in nation-building values, and to help them rebuild themselves in a proper manner. All these responsibilities are aimed at building a new citizen, with values, knowledge and proper behavior, so that the country has lasting security.
CG Murenzi reminded the participants of this retreat that in order to fulfill these responsibilities, they are required to be professional in everything they do and to work together, each one knowing their responsibilities. He said that this retreat is a solution because RCS staff and its stakeholders will share ideas aimed at developing it so that it reaches the level they desire.
He said, “To accomplish these important tasks, we need to work together, plan for what is needed and take joint measures to improve our responsibilities, each with a clear understanding of their contribution.”
“This retreat comes as one of the solutions, where RCS staff in collaboration with experienced partners will provide discussions on topics including various national policies, technology, security management, public financial management, productivity, mental health, and corrections with the aim of increasing our knowledge and skills that will help us achieve the RCS we desire.”
The three-day retreat, which is comprised of leaders of various farms from across the country, heads of various departments in RCS and others from the Rwanda Revenue Authority Headquarters, is scheduled to be concluded by the Minister of Internal Security, Dr. Vincent Biruta, on July 25 this year.

excerpt: The ceremony to induct the commandos into AFC/M23 was led by senior leaders of the coalition at the military level, including its Commander-in-Chief, Gen Maj Sultani Makenga, on 20 July 2026. Gen Maj Makenga announced that the DRC government is killing civilians, in…
title_en: AFC/M23 has more than 9,300 new commandos, 22 July 2026. The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo announced that it has gained 9,318 new commandos who have been training for many months at the Tchanzu military camp in North Kivu Province.
excerpt_en: The ceremony to induct the commandos into AFC/M23 was led by senior leaders of the coalition at the military level, including its Commander-in-Chief, Gen Maj Sultani Makenga, on 20 July 2026. Gen Maj Makenga announced that the DRC government is killing civilians, in…
body_en:
The ceremony to induct the commandos into AFC/M23 was led by senior leaders of the coalition at the military level, including its Commander-in-Chief, Gen Maj Sultani Makenga, on 20 July 2026.
Gen Maj Makenga announced that the DRC government is killing civilians, in collaboration with armed groups including Burundi, the FDLR terrorist group and the Wazalendo coalition, and the AFC/M23 is fighting to stop this killing.
He asked the new commandos who joined the AFC/M23 to join their comrades on the battlefield to defend the people and restore peace and security so that those who fled can return to their homes; and to prosper.
This fighter explained to the commandos that their operations must be different from that of the DRC army, which is accustomed to stealing, raping and killing innocent citizens, and that they must have good morals.
Gen Maj Makenga said, “Let us start with our relatives, let us start with our country, let us start with our family. If you do that, it will make you proud because you will be liberating your country, liberating your brothers, liberating the Congolese in general.”
He explained to them that the main goal of the AFC/M23 is to remove bad government and replace it with good, and that to achieve this, they must have good morals, respect themselves and the people.
In September 2025, the AFC/M23 also gained 7,437 new commandos and another 9,350 joined in October of that year. These included former civilians, former DRC soldiers, and Wazalendo who agreed to join this forum.

Habarurema Theophile, who was among those who returned, said that he arrived in Rwanda and found it peaceful because they were being harassed by armed groups there.

body_en:
The Rwandans who were welcomed included 11 men, 27 women and 70 children.
Habarurema Theophile, who returned from the DRC, told RBA that since 1994 he has continued to stay in this country because if he returns he will be killed or mistreated.
He said that the FDLR and some elders who have similar views have always persuaded them that they should not return.
He said, “It was bad, especially since they hated us because we didn’t speak the same language and persecuted us. Then the Wazalendo regime came and they treated us even worse…and to make the decision to return home, I spoke to one Kinangufu and told him about my district of origin and he told me that they heard on the radio that there was no problem and I immediately made plans to return home.”
The man said that he saw Rwanda very differently from the DRC because in the 32 years he had been there, it was the first time in two hours that he had not seen a fighter with a gun.
He said, “You don’t live in a country with guns and say you are safe when you are not a gunman. I am curious to go to where I came from and see if it is the same there as it is here.”
He said that none of his children have been able to go to school but he is ready to start them.
The mayor of Rusizi District, Sindayiheba Phanuel, said that they were grateful for their decision to return to Rwanda.
He said, “We congratulate them for making the right decision to return to their homeland, especially since there are many children who were not born in this country, who were born in exile and do not know Rwanda. It is a great opportunity for them to grow up in a country like Rwanda.”
Mayor Sindayiheba said that there was false information these residents were given about Rwanda, telling them that if they returned they would be killed, that there was no security, but that the information they were told by their friends who returned made them decide to return and they found it to be safe.
He said that the administration is assisting those who returned with health issues, returning to their families, helping children return to school, and so on.

title: Rwanda receives over 400 hostages held by FDLR, 23 July 2026. On 22 July 2026, Rwanda received 421 Rwandans who were held hostage by the FDLR terrorist group operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
excerpt: The Rwandans who returned were received at the Grande Barrière border in Rubavu District, including 43 men, 115 women and 263 children from 136 families. Mwemezi Dusabe, who is among the Rwandans who returned from Kanyabayonga, said that her husband was killed by five…
title_en: Rwanda receives over 400 hostages held by FDLR, 23 July 2026. On 22 July 2026, Rwanda received 421 Rwandans who were held hostage by the FDLR terrorist group operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
excerpt_en: The Rwandans who returned were received at the Grande Barrière border in Rubavu District, including 43 men, 115 women and 263 children from 136 families. Mwemezi Dusabe, who is among the Rwandans who returned from Kanyabayonga, said that her husband was killed by five…
body_en:
The Rwandans who returned were received at the Grande Barrière border in Rubavu District, including 43 men, 115 women and 263 children from 136 families.
Mwemezi Dusabe, who is among the Rwandans who returned from Kanyabayonga, said that her husband was killed by five children, and she managed to bring back four children who survived the war.
Ndayambaje Sebutozi, who returned from the Rutongo area, in Rutshuru Territory, said that he fled in 1998, but finding a way to return was a problem because the FDLR knew that anyone who wanted to return was killed.
Sebutozi says that since M23 captured Rutshuru, security has returned, which is why he decided to return home.
He also confirmed that he arrived in Rwanda and found it peaceful because he was well received and that he asked his comrades who remained in the forests of the DRC to return home.
The mayor of Rubavu District, Mulindwa Prosper, said that Rwandans who were held hostage by the FDLR will be given all the necessary documents, and will even get the opportunities they did not have.
He said, "We thank them for being explained and knowing the truth, and being able to free themselves from the shackles that prevented them from returning. They will continue to receive assistance like other Rwandans based on Rwanda's policy of changing the welfare of the population. There are programs to help people get out of poverty like Girinka and other opportunities that will be linked to it."
What they will receive includes basic money to help them start their lives, with returnees over the age of 18 receiving $188, those under 18 receiving $113, and each person receiving basic food worth 45,000 Rwf.

title: Gen Maj Alex Kagame lauds China’s role in enhancing RDF capabilities, 23 July 2026. The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Maj Alex Kagame, has lauded Rwanda’s military cooperation with China, saying it has played a significant role in enhancing the capabilities and professionalism of the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF).
excerpt: He reiterated this on the evening of 22 July 2026, at a ceremony organized by the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda to celebrate the 99th anniversary of the founding of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA). At the ceremony, which was attended by security officials, diplomats…
title_en: Gen Maj Alex Kagame lauds China’s role in enhancing RDF capabilities, 23 July 2026. The Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Maj Alex Kagame, has lauded Rwanda’s military cooperation with China, saying it has played a significant role in enhancing the capabilities and professionalism of the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF).
excerpt_en: He reiterated this on the evening of 22 July 2026, at a ceremony organized by the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda to celebrate the 99th anniversary of the founding of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA). At the ceremony, which was attended by security officials, diplomats…
body_en:
He reiterated this on the evening of 22 July 2026, at a ceremony organized by the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda to celebrate the 99th anniversary of the founding of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA).
At the ceremony, which was attended by security officials, diplomats and other guests, Gen Maj Alex Kagame represented the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Mubarakh Muganga.
In his speech, Gen Maj Alex Kagame thanked the Chinese Armed Forces for their journey over the past century, saying that they have become a highly capable force that has contributed to safeguarding China’s security and maintaining international peace and security.
He expressed that Rwanda values ​​its long-standing relationship with China, noting that this relationship continues to expand in various areas, including military and security cooperation.
He said, “Rwanda values ​​its long-standing friendship with China. The bilateral relationship continues to expand in many areas, including military cooperation.”
Gen Maj Alex Kagame said that the cooperation between the Rwandan Armed Forces and the Chinese Armed Forces has already yielded tangible results, especially in terms of developing military capabilities, training and enhancing the skills of soldiers.
He said that China’s support in professional training and specialized knowledge has contributed to maintaining the professionalism and capability of the RDF in fulfilling its missions.
He said, “The cooperation between the Chinese Armed Forces and the Rwandan Armed Forces continues to yield tangible results. China’s assistance in military education and specialized training has made a significant contribution to the ongoing development of the RDF’s capabilities.”
Gen Maj Alex Kagame also said that as the global security landscape continues to change, the militaries of countries need reliable cooperation to enhance capabilities, promote professionalism and work together to maintain peace and security.
He added that Rwanda is ready to continue working with China in promoting peace and security in the region and internationally.
China to further enhance cooperation with RDF
Senior Captain (Navy) Li Dayi, the military attaché at the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda, said that the relationship between the Rwandan Armed Forces and the Chinese Armed Forces continues to develop through training, knowledge exchange and capacity building.
He said that the cooperation between the two militaries is an important part of the overall Rwanda-China relationship, and that it has already yielded results in developing the capabilities of both institutions.
Li Dayi said that China is willing to continue to develop military-to-military relations with Rwanda, based on mutual respect and common interests, with a view to contributing to maintaining peace and security.
He noted that China and Rwanda have a long history of cooperation, with military cooperation being one of the areas that have strengthened the friendship between the two countries.
Li Dayi said that China is ready to work with Rwanda to further develop the bilateral military-to-military relations, with the aim of contributing to regional peace and security and promoting common development.
The anniversary celebrations came as Rwanda and China continue to develop relations in various fields, with military cooperation remaining one of the key pillars of this relationship.
body_fr:

At the ceremony, which was attended by security officials, diplomats and other guests, Gen Maj Alex Kagame represented the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen Mubarakh Muganga.
In his speech, Gen Maj Alex Kagame thanked the Chinese Armed Forces for their journey over the past century, saying that they have become a highly capable force that has contributed to safeguarding China’s security and maintaining international peace and security.
He expressed that Rwanda values ​​its long-standing relationship with China, noting that this relationship continues to expand in various areas, including military and security cooperation.
He said, “Rwanda values ​​its long-standing friendship with China. The bilateral relationship continues to expand in many areas, including military cooperation.”
Gen Maj Alex Kagame said that the cooperation between the Rwandan Armed Forces and the Chinese Armed Forces has already yielded tangible results, especially in terms of developing military capabilities, training and enhancing the skills of soldiers.
He said that China’s support in professional training and specialized knowledge has contributed to maintaining the professionalism and capability of the RDF in fulfilling its missions.
He said, “The cooperation between the Chinese Armed Forces and the Rwandan Armed Forces continues to yield tangible results. China’s assistance in military education and specialized training has made a significant contribution to the ongoing development of the RDF’s capabilities.”
Gen Maj Alex Kagame also said that as the global security landscape continues to change, the militaries of countries need reliable cooperation to enhance capabilities, promote professionalism and work together to maintain peace and security.

Li Dayi said that China is willing to continue to develop military-to-military relations with Rwanda, based on mutual respect and common interests, with a view to contributing to maintaining peace and security.

The training, which concluded on Thursday, was organized in collaboration with the Rwanda National Police and a special unit in the Qatari security forces known as Lekhwiya. It was attended by 209 police officers.
It lasted six weeks at the Counter-Terrorism Training Center (CTTC) located in Mayange, Bugesera District.

The training focused on topics including how to protect dignitaries, deal with acts of terrorism in urban areas, quell protests and restore calm in the event of security incidents.
At the conclusion of the training, CP Vincent Sano commended the organizers and participants for their efforts, noting that enhancing the capacity of the police is essential in addressing new security challenges.
The Rwanda National Police continues to enhance the skills of police officers through various training courses aimed at enhancing their capacity to protect national security and confront acts that could undermine it.

The leader of the AFC/M23 alliance, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, said that Joseph Kabila, who led the Democratic Republic of Congo from 2001 to 2019, is a key figure who should be used to solve the country's problems because of his experience in governance and history.

title_en: Nangaa sees Joseph Kabila as key to solving DRC's problems, 23 July 2026. The leader of the AFC/M23 alliance, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, said that Joseph Kabila, who led the Democratic Republic of Congo from 2001 to 2019, is a key figure who should be used to solve the country's problems because of his experience in governance and history.
excerpt_en: Nangaa said this in an interview on the Grand Lacs News YouTube channel, when asked about his relationship with Kabila, who now lives in the area controlled by AFC/M23, and the role he can play in the political problems the DRC is facing. He said that in other countries,…
body_en:
Nangaa said this in an interview on the Grand Lacs News YouTube channel, when asked about his relationship with Kabila, who now lives in the area controlled by AFC/M23, and the role he can play in the political problems the DRC is facing.
He said that in other countries, former heads of state are considered people who are still useful, and are used to build the country, instead of being sidelined after leaving power.
He said, "In other countries, a former head of state is an asset. In Kenya, you see how they treat former heads of state. In Ghana, you see how they are treated, even in South Africa, they are assets of their countries."
Nangaa said that the DRC has a problem of not capitalizing on the experience of previous leaders, and that Kabila is one of the people with a history who can contribute to solving the country's problems.
He pointed out that sometimes countries ask former heads of state to help them solve problems, ignoring experienced former leaders who know how to solve them.
He said, "When it comes to mediation, it is former heads of state who are brought in to solve our problems, and yet they do not know the problems you have. But you have someone. So why are you using him?"
Regarding his relationship with Joseph Kabila, Nangaa said that he is in good standing, portraying him as a former leader who deserves respect.
"We have a very good relationship. Our leader, a former Head of State, a former President, deserves respect."
Nangaa also said that Kabila still has a say in DRC politics, saying, "Does he still have a say? The answer is yes."
The politician continued to say that Kabila's long leadership of the DRC gives him a responsibility in the country's journey, expressing his desire for him to participate in the efforts aimed at saving the country.
Regarding the AFC/M23, which was once suspected of instigating a bad atmosphere, Nangaa said that the conflict is between fighters or members of this group, indicating that M23 and AFC are the same entity.
He said, "M23 or AFC are not two different things."
Corneille Nangaa gave this message when in September 2025, the DRC's High Military Court convicted Kabila of involvement in the war in the east of the country, where it sentenced him to death.
Currently, President Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC is preparing for "indefinite talks" to unite the Congolese people. He reportedly does not want representatives of the AFC/M23 and Kabila to attend.

title_en: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba in Kigali, 25 July 2026. The Chief of Staff of the Ugandan Armed Forces and Special Adviser to President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni on Military Operations, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has arrived in Rwanda.
excerpt_en: Upon his arrival at Kigali International Airport on 25 July 2026, Gen Muhoozi was received by the Chief of Staff of the Rwandan Armed Forces, Gen Mubarakh Muganga.
body_en:
Upon his arrival at Kigali International Airport on 25 July 2026, Gen Muhoozi was received by the Chief of Staff of the Rwandan Armed Forces, Gen Mubarakh Muganga.

Other officials who received Gen Muhoozi included the Commander of the Rwandan Armed Forces' Security Corps, Gen Maj Willy Rwagasana, and the Military Adviser at the Ugandan Embassy, ​​Col Ezekiel Matsiko.

During the two-day visit, Gen Muhoozi is expected to discuss with senior Rwandan military leaders on strengthening military ties between the two countries, and will also hold talks with President Paul Kagame.

Gen Muhoozi was last in Rwanda in March 2025. At that time, he discussed with senior Rwandan military leaders on bilateral cooperation, and visited the Nyakinama Military Academy in Musanze District.

At the academy, Gen Muhoozi delivered lectures on African cooperation in maintaining peace and security. The soldier indicated that when the Ugandan and Rwandan Armed Forces have the same capabilities, no problem can overcome them.

title: AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho continue to expand their bases, 27 July 2026. The four-and-a-half-year war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo continues to change its face, with the AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho alliances continuing to expand their bases in various parts of North Kivu and South Kivu.
excerpt: The Critical Threats report, which collects and analyzes security information in various countries, shows that as of 24 July 2026, AFC/M23 continued to fight in Masisi Territory, Walikale and the South Kivu highlands. Last week, the alliance said it had trained and recruited…
title_en: AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho continue to expand their bases, 27 July 2026. The four-and-a-half-year war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo continues to change its face, with the AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho alliances continuing to expand their bases in various parts of North Kivu and South Kivu.
excerpt_en: The Critical Threats report, which collects and analyzes security information in various countries, shows that as of 24 July 2026, AFC/M23 continued to fight in Masisi Territory, Walikale and the South Kivu highlands. Last week, the alliance said it had trained and recruited…
body_en:
The Critical Threats report, which collects and analyzes security information in various countries, shows that as of 24 July 2026, AFC/M23 continued to fight in Masisi Territory, Walikale and the South Kivu highlands.
Last week, the alliance said it had trained and recruited more than 9,318 new fighters, in addition to the more than 30,000 it had previously identified, as confirmed by United Nations experts.
The Commander-in-Chief of the AFC/M23, Gen Maj Sultani Makenga, informed the fighters who were being trained at the Tshanzu military base in North Kivu that their comrades who joined the group last year had played a key role in capturing parts of the highlands.
Gen Maj Makenga gave the fighters a mission to help their comrades liberate other parts of the country to free the country from the grip of President Félix Tshisekedi, who he accuses of mismanagement.
On July 20, Gen Maj Makenga said, “Let us liberate our brothers, let us liberate our country, let us liberate our community. If you do this, it will make you proud because you will be liberating your country, liberating your brothers, liberating the Congolese people in general.”
Last week, the DRC government forces launched attacks to retake parts of the highlands in South Kivu, including Minembwe and Point-Zéro, but were repelled by MRDP-Twirwaneho, which is allied with AFC/M23.
On July 25, 2026, Twirwaneho spokesman Col Kamasa Ndakize Welcome announced that their fighters had captured the Kipupu center in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga Territory.
In a video message, Col Kamasa said, “Here we are in Gipupu in the sector, in fact, the Gipupu center.”
On July 26, Col Fidèle Rugabo, one of Twirwaneho’s senior officers, was also seen in Gipupu, planning that the entire Itombwe sector would soon be captured.
Fighting also pitted AFC/M23 against Wazalendo groups in Masisi and Walikale, as both sides sought to control key routes linking North and South Kivu.
Wazalendo, backed by DRC government forces, has long attempted to wrest back territory it seized from AFC/M23 in Masisi and Walikale, but has been repeatedly pushed back, sometimes losing ground.

title: Are FDLR fighters injured in the DRC being treated in Burundi?, 28 July 2026. One of the stories that continues to dominate events in Burundi and the Great Lakes region in general is how the country's army and allied groups continue to suffer from the fighting in South Kivu Province in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
excerpt: However, there is a part of this story that has been kept top secret but is being revealed by some concerned Burundians, including security officials, doctors and the human rights activist who founded the FOCODE organization, Pacifique Nininahazwe. Nininahazwe announced that…
title_en: Are FDLR fighters injured in the DRC being treated in Burundi?, 28 July 2026. One of the stories that continues to dominate events in Burundi and the Great Lakes region in general is how the country's army and allied groups continue to suffer from the fighting in South Kivu Province in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
excerpt_en: However, there is a part of this story that has been kept top secret but is being revealed by some concerned Burundians, including security officials, doctors and the human rights activist who founded the FOCODE organization, Pacifique Nininahazwe. Nininahazwe announced that…
body_en:
However, there is a part of this story that has been kept top secret but is being revealed by some concerned Burundians, including security officials, doctors and the human rights activist who founded the FOCODE organization, Pacifique Nininahazwe.
Nininahazwe announced that the wounded from the war in the DRC, including Wazalendo and those suspected of being members of the FDLR terrorist group, are being treated in private and expensive hospitals in Bujumbura, including the Tanganyika Care Polyclinic.
He said that for the first time, this information was received by Burundians who went to the hospital branch located in Nyabugete in the Muha zone, after finding that the security there was compromised by soldiers, where wounded people were being treated, including those who spoke Lingala, Swahili, French and Kinyarwanda.
As he explained, residents told him that they had received information that these wounded people, who call themselves Wazalendo, told them that they were brought to this hospital by one of the leaders of the Imbonerakure group called Willy Habarishize known as ‘Brig Gen Kanyisha’.
He said, “They say that he is in command of two Imbonerakure battalions that were sent to fight in Wazalendo. He also gives himself ranks, now he is said to be a Brigade General, and when they show him in photos, you can see that he is wearing military uniform.”
He continued, “So that’s the one who brought Wazalendo who said they were injured in the recent war in Congo, others who said they had a car accident, and they said they were targeted by M23.”
Nininahazwe explained that this information prompted him to start investigating to find out if these hospitals are actually treating Wazalendo and FDLR wounded, and he spoke to doctors, who told him that the fact that there are Kinyarwanda speakers does not mean that these are Rwandans.
He said, “Some of those who approached the hospital’s leaders came to us. When they came to us, the first thing they said was, ‘The story you said that there were Congolese fighters who were being treated here is true. 80% of the patients there are now those fighters. Even though they are fighters, there is no proof that they are FDLR, you should not continue to say that.”
The Burundian explained that for the third time, he spoke to the hospital authorities, who admitted to him that there were many fighters being treated in their branch in Nyabugete but that there were also others at their headquarters who were seriously ill.
Nininahazwe said that he had received further reports of the great resentment of the Burundian soldiers being treated in these hospitals, admitting that they were with the fighters who were wounded in the DRC but that what hurt them most and surprised them was that these fighters were treated better than them.
He received further serious information from soldiers who visited the hospital in Nyabugete, who explained to him that they had found that a Rwandan who had been rumored to be an FDLR fighter for many years was frequently visiting the wounded there and providing them with assistance.
He said, “Some of the soldiers said, ‘We went to Nyabugete and looked at it, we saw the sick there. We also found out that there is a well-known person in Burundi who has been there for several years, a Rwandan man from the Netherlands who many say is a well-known FDLR member. He is the one who comes to see them in Nyabugete, and you see that he helps them.’”
Nininahazwe indicated that the story of this Rwandan visiting these wounded and who is said to be an FDLR fighter led him to begin to believe that among those being treated in these hospitals are members of this group that aims to destabilize Rwanda.
The Burundian government has been rumored to be working with the FDLR terrorist group for many years. One of the most serious signs that has recently emerged is the way it received its fighters in military camps when they fled in early December 2025 after the AFC/M23 coalition captured the town of Uvira.

One of the most serious signs that has recently emerged is the way it received its fighters in military camps when they fled in early December 2025 after the AFC/M23 coalition captured the town of Uvira.

title: Fuel Escorts and Interior Aid Runs Define Civil-Military Stabilisation Push
excerpt: Bamako and regions, July 31, 2026 - Across July, FAMa escorts for hydrocarbon convoys and deliveries of food and medicine to enclave communities became twin pillars of the government’s claim to restore both security and basic services. Ministers linked tanker success to road…
title_en: Fuel Escorts and Interior Aid Runs Define Civil-Military Stabilisation Push
excerpt_en: Bamako and regions, July 31, 2026 - Across July, FAMa escorts for hydrocarbon convoys and deliveries of food and medicine to enclave communities became twin pillars of the government’s claim to restore both security and basic services. Ministers linked tanker success to road…
body_en:
Bamako and regions, July 31, 2026 - Across July, FAMa escorts for hydrocarbon convoys and deliveries of food and medicine to enclave communities became twin pillars of the government’s claim to restore both security and basic services.
Ministers linked tanker success to road maintenance and force protection, while Russia-WFP food tonnage and presidency donations filled some household gaps. Sustaining interior supply beyond Bamako remains the stated next test after the 850-tanker arrival.
Conclusion
The events of July 2026 illustrate a pivotal moment for Mali as the transitional government simultaneously navigates severe economic pressures, complex security dynamics, and a major geopolitical realignment. The successful late-July arrival of major hydrocarbon convoys and the rebuilding of strategic fuel stocks provided much-needed relief to Bamako's supply chain. However, extending this logistics and economic recovery into interior regions such as Koutiala and Bandiagara remains a critical next test for long-term stability.
On the security front, the operational embedding of Russian Africa Corps logistics alongside FAMa counter-terrorism campaigns-demonstrated by high-tempo operations in Tessalit, Anéfis, and central Mali-underscores the government's aggressive approach to reclaiming territorial sovereignty. Parallel to military action, the push to operationalize the 18,000-troop Alliance of Sahel States (AES) unified force and establish sovereign confederation media channels signals an increasingly consolidated regional strategy away from traditional ECOWAS frameworks.
Diplomatically, Mali's foreign policy has proven both adaptive and strategic. While deepening ties with non-Western partners like Russia and China, Bamako successfully executed pragmatic engagements with regional neighbours. The diplomatic thaw with Algeria, alongside President Faye’s solidarity visit representing ECOWAS leadership, indicates that vital trade, security, and corridor partnerships are being maintained despite broader geopolitical shifts.
Ultimately, Mali’s short- to medium-term trajectory depends on balancing these sweeping security and geopolitical shifts with internal stability. Securing fuel and food distribution to vulnerable interior populations, managing judicial and press freedom concerns, and delivering on economic promises like local industrial cotton processing and municipal modernization will be key to sustaining domestic cohesion and operational momentum in the months ahead.
By Jeff Buleli

Rubanda, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - District councillors urged the Ministry of Works and Transport to terminate Samcrete Egypt Engineers and Contractors over the deteriorating Kabale-Lake Bunyonyi tourism road.

United Nations, July 31, 2026 - The Security Council began selecting the next United Nations secretary-general with a first straw poll among the seven declared candidates, including Uganda’s Olara Otunnu.

title_en: Medical Waste Dumping Alarms Bidibidi Residents
excerpt_en: Yumbe, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Residents of Bidibidi settlement raised alarm over alleged open dumping of syringes and other medical waste at Twajiji Health Centre III, saying maternity, outpatient and pharmacy refuse was left in open areas instead of treated disposal systems.
body_en:
Yumbe, Uganda, July 31, 2026 - Residents of Bidibidi settlement raised alarm over alleged open dumping of syringes and other medical waste at Twajiji Health Centre III, saying maternity, outpatient and pharmacy refuse was left in open areas instead of treated disposal systems.

Local leaders said children had been seen picking and playing with discarded items and warned of infection risks including HIV and hepatitis. Community representatives said repeated complaints to facility managers had produced no corrective action.

title_en: Investigation Places Start of Ebola Outbreak in January, Before Official Alert
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 31, 2026 - An inquiry concluded that the Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak began in January, well before the official public alert and May confirmation in Ituri.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 31, 2026 - An inquiry concluded that the Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak began in January, well before the official public alert and May confirmation in Ituri.

Earlier undetected circulation helps explain why the epidemic had already seeded multiple provinces by the time national and international surge capacity fully mobilised.

Health authorities face questions about surveillance gaps in mining and conflict zones.

Key points from the report: - An inquiry concluded that the Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak began in January, well before the official public alert and May confirmation in Ituri. - Earlier undetected circulation helps explain why the epidemic had already seeded multiple provinces by the time national and international surge capacity fully mobilised. - Health authorities face questions about surveillance gaps in mining and conflict zones.

title: Night Attacks Kill Two in Nyiragongo Territory
excerpt: Nyiragongo, North Kivu, July 30, 2026 - At least two people were killed in overnight armed raids in Nyiragongo Territory north of Goma, with looting reported and attackers still unidentified. Around 11 p.m. on July 29, gunmen hit a shop in Bugamba 1 (Mudja grouping) and shot…
title_en: Night Attacks Kill Two in Nyiragongo Territory
excerpt_en: Nyiragongo, North Kivu, July 30, 2026 - At least two people were killed in overnight armed raids in Nyiragongo Territory north of Goma, with looting reported and attackers still unidentified.
body_en:
Nyiragongo, North Kivu, July 30, 2026 - At least two people were killed in overnight armed raids in Nyiragongo Territory north of Goma, with looting reported and attackers still unidentified.

Around 11 p.m. on July 29, gunmen hit a shop in Bugamba 1 (Mudja grouping) and shot dead the young owner after stealing goods. About 1 a.m., assailants stormed a home in Kiziba 1 (“9 Portes”), fatally wounding the woman owner; other injuries were reported.

Some residents said attackers wore military-style clothing. The area, under AFC/M23 control, had seen relative calm for months.

Families decried weak judicial mechanisms and called for stronger protection as banditry multiplies.

Nyala, Sudan, July 30, 2026 - RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, told fighters to prepare for an offensive aimed at capturing Khartoum following army and allied advances in North Kordofan.

excerpt: Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Staff at the Congolese Posts and Telecommunications Company (SCPT) remained on strike, demanding payment of 17 consecutive months of salary arrears and the departure of Director-General Sandra Tshibonge Mbiye, whom they accuse of mismanagement. Union…
title_en: SCPT Workers Strike Over 17 Months of Unpaid Salaries
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Staff at the Congolese Posts and Telecommunications Company (SCPT) remained on strike, demanding payment of 17 consecutive months of salary arrears and the departure of Director-General Sandra Tshibonge Mbiye, whom they accuse of mismanagement.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Staff at the Congolese Posts and Telecommunications Company (SCPT) remained on strike, demanding payment of 17 consecutive months of salary arrears and the departure of Director-General Sandra Tshibonge Mbiye, whom they accuse of mismanagement.

Union vice-president Jean Makayanga Kalukula said workers claim more than $300 million and want the state to treat SCPT like other public enterprises. Strikers also said more than seven tonnes of parcels remained blocked at the post office.

The walkout, launched June 22, had still not produced a settlement.

The developments were reported in the DRC briefing covering mid-to-late July 2026. The account centers on: SCPT Workers Strike Over 17 Months of Unpaid Salaries. Taken together, the available details outline both the immediate incident and the broader situation described by officials and witnesses in the source report.

excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Justice David Matovu dismissed a bail application by city lawyer and Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago, ruling it had been overtaken by his July 16 committal to the High Court on a charge of misprision of treason. The application related to Makindye…
title_en: High Court Dismisses Lukwago Bail Bid After Committal for Trial
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Justice David Matovu dismissed a bail application by city lawyer and Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago, ruling it had been overtaken by his July 16 committal to the High Court on a charge of misprision of treason.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Justice David Matovu dismissed a bail application by city lawyer and Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago, ruling it had been overtaken by his July 16 committal to the High Court on a charge of misprision of treason.

The application related to Makindye Chief Magistrate’s Court Case No. 0762 of 2026, which ceased to exist after committal. The court directed the criminal division’s deputy registrar to expedite allocation to a trial judge.

Lukwago, who had been among Besigye’s defence lawyers, was charged on June 17 with failing to report alleged treason plots involving opposition figures between 2021 and November 2024-an offence under Section 25 of the Penal Code that he denies.

Matovu separately held that a Mulago consultants’ report recommending specialised spinal care in India was insufficient without Uganda Prisons medical certification that the condition could not be managed in custody-the decisive barrier to medical bail.

title_en: Kinshasa Rejects AFC/M23 Role in National Dialogue
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Congolese authorities again rejected participation by the AFC/M23 coalition in the proposed national dialogue, framing inclusion of the armed movement as equivalent to bringing Rwanda into talks among Congolese.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Congolese authorities again rejected participation by the AFC/M23 coalition in the proposed national dialogue, framing inclusion of the armed movement as equivalent to bringing Rwanda into talks among Congolese.

The position restates a longstanding government red line: dialogue among Congolese political and social actors must not legitimise an armed group Kinshasa links to foreign aggression in the east.

The stance contrasts with some church and opposition voices that have argued armed Congolese actors with grievances should not be excluded from conflict-resolution talks.

title_en: Government Says Five of Six Identified FDLR Zones Are Outside Army Control
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Anzuluni said the parties to the Washington follow-up mechanism identified six zones hosting FDLR fighters in North and South Kivu, and that five of them are under Rwanda/AFC-M23 control rather than FARDC authority.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Anzuluni said the parties to the Washington follow-up mechanism identified six zones hosting FDLR fighters in North and South Kivu, and that five of them are under Rwanda/AFC-M23 control rather than FARDC authority.

Only the Walikale area, he said, remains under Congolese control among the identified zones, explaining why military deployment focused there. Four of the contested zones are in North Kivu and one in the South Kivu high plateaus, according to the minister.

The claim is intended to undercut arguments that Kinshasa alone can immediately eliminate the FDLR threat everywhere it has been mapped, while keeping pressure on Kigali over territorial control in the east.

Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Reporting on environmental and mining compliance said a cobalt mine linked to Chinese group CMOC had exceeded legal uranium thresholds for years, raising questions about monitoring of radioactive by-products in industrial mining operations.

Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Defence and Veteran Affairs Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka told AUSSOM defence ministers that military pressure alone cannot deliver lasting peace in Somalia while Al-Shabaab still strikes forces, institutions and civilians.

Uganda framed African-led logistics and broader political, economic and institutional measures as essential to protect gains made under AMISOM, ATMIS and AUSSOM.

body_en:
Kinshasa, July 30, 2026 - Moïse Katumbi intervened to calm an internal dispute inside Ensemble pour la République after public speculation over differences between cabinet director and spokesperson Olivier Kamitatu and senator Salomon Idi Kalonda.

In a joint statement dated July 29, Kamitatu and Kalonda said they had spoken at length at Katumbi’s request and that misunderstandings between them had been resolved.

The episode came as Ensemble, a C64 member, navigates positioning around the national dialogue and the coming political calendar. Party militants had worried that the reported rift could weaken opposition cohesion at a sensitive moment.

The joint communiqué sought to project restored unity around Katumbi’s leadership.

title_en: Nation Media Group Wins Clearance to Resume After Month-Long Shutdown
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Nation Media Group Uganda began a phased return after the Uganda Communications Commission conveyed President Museveni’s clearance to reopen, ending restrictions that followed a June 28 security shutdown of the group’s newspaper, television...
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Nation Media Group Uganda began a phased return after the Uganda Communications Commission conveyed President Museveni’s clearance to reopen, ending restrictions that followed a June 28 security shutdown of the group’s newspaper, television and radio outlets.

UCC told Managing Director Susan Nsibirwa that the president had authorised the businesses to resume. NMG started with digital publishing while engineers assessed broadcast and printing infrastructure sealed since the blockade of Namuwongo and Serena Hotel facilities.

Group leaders, including Rostam Aziz and Joe Muganda, thanked Museveni and acknowledged Gen. Muhoozi’s role in engagements leading to the decision.

The company pledged to rebuild audience trust and continue regional investment across East Africa.

excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - The Uganda Medical Association told Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara that accountability for corruption, absenteeism and poor care is necessary, but that televised or camera-led public questioning of health workers before…
title_en: Doctors Warn Against Public Shaming During Health Inspections
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - The Uganda Medical Association told Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara that accountability for corruption, absenteeism and poor care is necessary, but that televised or camera-led public questioning of health workers before...
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - The Uganda Medical Association told Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara that accountability for corruption, absenteeism and poor care is necessary, but that televised or camera-led public questioning of health workers before investigations finish can violate due process and patient rights.

UMA President Prof. Frank Asiimwe said proven misconduct deserves punishment, yet inspection teams arriving with security and media risk prejudging staff.

The letter added tension to a government drive to clean up public facilities.

Key points from the report: - The Uganda Medical Association told Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara that accountability for corruption, absenteeism and poor care is necessary, but that televised or camera-led public questioning of health workers before investigations finish can violate due process and patient rights. - UMA President Prof. - Frank Asiimwe said proven misconduct deserves punishment, yet inspection teams arriving with security and media risk prejudging staff. - The letter added tension to a government drive to clean up public facilities.

Gaborone, Botswana, July 30, 2026 - AU facilitators adopted a six-month roadmap and operational action plan covering July-December 2026 after high-level talks in Gaborone on July 25-26 with SADC and Botswana hosting.

Priorities include political analysis, military-security tracks, humanitarian access, armed-group dialogue, regional economic and natural-resource issues, and reconciliation.

Former Nigerian president Olusegun Obasanjo, chairing the AU facilitators’ group, pressed for tighter coordination among African mediation architectures.

title_en: Government Extends Northern Cattle Restocking Horizon to 10 Years
excerpt_en: Gulu, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Authorities said the Northern Uganda cattle restocking programme would be extended across a 10-year horizon, reinforcing a multi-year recovery plan for Acholi, Lango and Teso households that lost livestock to conflict and raids.
body_en:
Gulu, Uganda, July 30, 2026 - Authorities said the Northern Uganda cattle restocking programme would be extended across a 10-year horizon, reinforcing a multi-year recovery plan for Acholi, Lango and Teso households that lost livestock to conflict and raids.

Current phases have disbursed large cash grants-about Shs5 million per verified household-toward productive assets. Officials cite tens of billions already paid to more than 12,000 households, with Shs100 billion earmarked in the next financial year, while acknowledging long-term need far exceeds the first cohorts.

Social and Health.

body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, July 30, 2026 - A precarious calm settled over parts of southern Masisi after nearly a week of fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo fighters that began on July 24.

Clashes with heavy and light weapons concentrated in Kibabi I, Kibabi II and Ufamandu I. Civilians fled Kasoko, Mushebere and surrounding villages, with many seeking refuge in Ngungu.

Residents remain fearful of renewed hostilities despite the relative lull.

El Obeid, Sudan, July 30, 2026 - Despite eastern breakthroughs, El Obeid stayed under partial siege pressure, with RSF forces still able to threaten approaches and strike infrastructure by drone.

UN rights chief Volker Türk’s earlier “red alert” that catastrophe was unfolding around the city continued to frame international messaging through late July, alongside warnings that a full RSF capture could echo El Fasher’s mass atrocities.

excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Chief of Defence Forces Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba told the 2nd Extraordinary Summit of AUSSOM troop-contributing countries at Speke Resort Munyonyo that the mission needs alternative support arrangements as the United Nations Support Office in…
title_en: Muhoozi Warns AUSSOM Must Find New Funding as UN Support Shrinks
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Chief of Defence Forces Gen.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Chief of Defence Forces Gen.

Muhoozi Kainerugaba told the 2nd Extraordinary Summit of AUSSOM troop-contributing countries at Speke Resort Munyonyo that the mission needs alternative support arrangements as the United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) prepares to wind down by December.

He said UNSOS had already cut support to AUSSOM and the UN Guard Unit by 25%, forcing operational adjustments and weakening effectiveness in some areas. Muhoozi added that the United States had indicated it would not back renewing AUSSOM’s Security Council mandate if it continued to include UNSOS support.

The three-day meeting brought together military and political representatives from Uganda, Somalia, Burundi, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Egypt and Kenya under the theme of sustaining Somalia’s stabilisation.

Delegates reviewed Somali force readiness, deployments, air assets and options for African-led financing after UNSOS closes.

The developments were reported in the UGANDA briefing covering mid-to-late July 2026. The account centers on: Muhoozi Warns AUSSOM Must Find New Funding as UN Support Shrinks. title: Rwanda Returns 39 Congolese to DRC After Screening
excerpt: RUBAVU, Rwanda, July 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Demobilization and Reintegration Commission returned 39 Congolese nationals to DR Congo after an assessment found they did not meet the criteria for Rwanda’s ex-soldiers rehabilitation programme. The commission said the transfer…
title_en: Rwanda Returns 39 Congolese to DRC After Screening
excerpt_en: RUBAVU, Rwanda, July 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Demobilization and Reintegration Commission returned 39 Congolese nationals to DR Congo after an assessment found they did not meet the criteria for Rwanda’s ex-soldiers rehabilitation programme. The commission said the transfer…
body_en:
RUBAVU, Rwanda, July 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Demobilization and Reintegration Commission returned 39 Congolese nationals to DR Congo after an assessment found they did not meet the criteria for Rwanda’s ex-soldiers rehabilitation programme.
The commission said the transfer occurred with MONUSCO officials present and followed findings that the individuals had falsely presented themselves as former FDLR fighters. AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka alleged the DRC government was recruiting people to pose as FDLR members, an allegation not independently verified.
Conclusion
The period from July 16 to July 30, 2026, highlights Rwanda’s active engagement across international diplomacy, economic expansion, and regional stability:
Diplomatic & Global Outreach: Rwanda continues to strengthen its international footprint. From diaspora-led Liberation Day commemorations in Turkey and Indonesia to new diplomatic, trade, and economic agreements with Poland, Pakistan, and Belarus, the nation is actively solidifying its global partnerships and trade pathways.
Economic & Infrastructure Advancement: Significant progress was demonstrated in local infrastructure and public investments, including the commissioning of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System, cost optimization for the Bugesera Nuclear Research Centre, and large-scale agricultural soil-conservation initiatives. Furthermore, the establishment of a dedicated national parks conservation agency underscores a commitment to sustainable tourism and ecological management.
Health & Technological Integration: High-profile engagements-such as visits from global health leaders-emphasize Rwanda's rapid adoption of AI-enabled health systems, paperless clinical workflows, and telemedicine aimed at reducing maternal and child mortality.
Security & Humanitarian Operations: The country remains a central actor in regional dynamics. While internal security forces advance their capabilities through international partnerships, Rwandan authorities continue to facilitate the peaceful return, screening, and reintegration of returnees and former combatants amidst ongoing political and armed tensions in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo.
Overall, the report reflects a country focused on long-term socio-economic modernization and strategic diplomacy, even as it navigates complex regional security dynamics in East Africa.
By Jeff Buleli

title_en: Maniema PDL-145T Workers Demand 22 Months of Wage Arrears
excerpt_en: Kindu, July 29, 2026 - More than 60 engineers, site supervisors and agents who worked on the Local Development Programme for 145 Territories (PDL-145T) in Maniema submitted a memorandum seeking payment of over 22 months of unpaid wages.
body_en:
Kindu, July 29, 2026 - More than 60 engineers, site supervisors and agents who worked on the Local Development Programme for 145 Territories (PDL-145T) in Maniema submitted a memorandum seeking payment of over 22 months of unpaid wages.

They accused contractor SAFRICAS of abandoning them after they fulfilled their duties. A SAFRICAS representative in Maniema, Alain Kabongo, said the firm contracted ITM for human-resources recruitment and redirected claims to that company, leaving workers caught between subcontracting layers.

title_en: About 100 Community Ebola Deaths in One Week at Mambasa PK51
excerpt_en: Mambasa, July 29, 2026 - Health officials reported about 100 community deaths linked to Ebola in one week at kilometre point 51 (PK51) in Mambasa Territory, with 10 to 15 deaths a day cited by the Niania health-zone chief.
body_en:
Mambasa, July 29, 2026 - Health officials reported about 100 community deaths linked to Ebola in one week at kilometre point 51 (PK51) in Mambasa Territory, with 10 to 15 deaths a day cited by the Niania health-zone chief.

More than 40 of roughly 50 local health facilities had closed after the Ebola treatment centre was wrecked on June 30 by residents contesting the epidemic’s existence; many health workers fled to Niania.

Patients often arrive only at a late stage, raising fatality risk. Authorities said measures were being prepared to contain spread from the mining settlement.

Key points from the report: - Health officials reported about 100 community deaths linked to Ebola in one week at kilometre point 51 (PK51) in Mambasa Territory, with 10 to 15 deaths a day cited by the Niania health-zone chief. - More than 40 of roughly 50 local health facilities had closed after the Ebola treatment centre was wrecked on June 30 by residents contesting the epidemic’s existence; many health workers fled to Niania. - Patients often arrive only at a late stage, raising fatality risk. - Authorities said measures were being prepared to contain spread from the mining settlement.

excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Besigye, 70, collapsed and lost consciousness during his High Court treason hearing while protesting continuation of the trial without lawyers of his choosing, after Lukwago’s detention and related defence disruptions. Witnesses said he…
title_en: Besigye Collapses in Court and Is Taken to Intensive Care
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Besigye, 70, collapsed and lost consciousness during his High Court treason hearing while protesting continuation of the trial without lawyers of his choosing, after Lukwago’s detention and related defence disruptions.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Besigye, 70, collapsed and lost consciousness during his High Court treason hearing while protesting continuation of the trial without lawyers of his choosing, after Lukwago’s detention and related defence disruptions.

Witnesses said he repeatedly shouted “stop” before falling in the dock. He was taken to Mulago National Referral Hospital’s intensive-care unit under heavy security.

Wife Winnie Byanyima said he was unconscious and unresponsive; family members reported difficulty securing preferred medical care. Son Adam Ampa appealed to Museveni and Gen.

Muhoozi for humanitarian release. Exiled opposition figure Bobi Wine called forcing an ill detainee into court a rights violation.

Besigye has been held since a November 2024 abduction in Kenya and return to face treason charges with aide Obeid Lutale.

Key points from the report: - Besigye, 70, collapsed and lost consciousness during his High Court treason hearing while protesting continuation of the trial without lawyers of his choosing, after Lukwago’s detention and related defence disruptions. - Witnesses said he repeatedly shouted “stop” before falling in the dock. - He was taken to Mulago National Referral Hospital’s intensive-care unit under heavy security. - Wife Winnie Byanyima said he was unconscious and unresponsive; family members reported difficulty securing preferred medical care. - Son Adam Ampa appealed to Museveni and Gen. - Muhoozi for humanitarian release.

title_en: Uganda Eyes Green Hydrogen Production Powered by Karuma
excerpt_en: Kiryandongo, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Uganda moved deeper into the global green-hydrogen race with plans for a Karuma facility drawing about 100 megawatts from Karuma Hydropower Station for electrolysis.
body_en:
Kiryandongo, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - Uganda moved deeper into the global green-hydrogen race with plans for a Karuma facility drawing about 100 megawatts from Karuma Hydropower Station for electrolysis.

Backers present hydrogen as a way to convert surplus renewable power into a higher-value export and industrial feedstock, potentially supporting fertiliser production and new skills.

Analysts cautioned that electrolysers, transmission, storage and secure offtake markets will determine whether policy ambition becomes a bankable industry.

excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - State Minister for Health Charles Ayume said Uganda has moved from containing domestic outbreaks to exporting response capacity, with Ugandan doctors and health workers running two Ebola treatment centres in the Democratic Republic of Congo.…
title_en: Uganda Exports Ebola Expertise to Eastern Congo
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - State Minister for Health Charles Ayume said Uganda has moved from containing domestic outbreaks to exporting response capacity, with Ugandan doctors and health workers running two Ebola treatment centres in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - State Minister for Health Charles Ayume said Uganda has moved from containing domestic outbreaks to exporting response capacity, with Ugandan doctors and health workers running two Ebola treatment centres in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

He linked the deployment to lessons from repeated Ugandan outbreaks and said national protocols are increasingly referenced by international partners. Officials present the assistance as both solidarity and self-defence while the virus circulates across the border.

Key points from the report: - State Minister for Health Charles Ayume said Uganda has moved from containing domestic outbreaks to exporting response capacity, with Ugandan doctors and health workers running two Ebola treatment centres in the Democratic Republic of Congo. - He linked the deployment to lessons from repeated Ugandan outbreaks and said national protocols are increasingly referenced by international partners. - Officials present the assistance as both solidarity and self-defence while the virus circulates across the border.

title_en: Bamako Commune VI High Court Opens First Criminal Session
excerpt_en: Bamako, Mali, July 29, 2026 - The Tribunal de Grande Instance of Bamako’s Commune VI opened its first criminal session, taking up cases including rape, assassination and child sexual abuse under newly transferred jurisdiction.

Bamako, Mali, July 29, 2026 - The Tribunal de Grande Instance of Bamako’s Commune VI opened its first criminal session, taking up cases including rape, assassination and child sexual abuse under newly transferred jurisdiction.

The prosecutor said moving major crimes to TGIs should accelerate dockets and reduce backlog. Reformers present the sessions as a test of judicial reorganisation after years of congestion at older venues.

excerpt: Kinshasa, July 29, 2026 - The C64 coalition rejected the Constitutional Court’s clearance of the referendum organisation law as null and void, accusing the court of “judicial rebellion” and complicity in what it called a plot against constitutional order. Ensemble…
title_en: C64 Calls Constitutional Court Ruling a “Judicial Rebellion”
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 29, 2026 - The C64 coalition rejected the Constitutional Court’s clearance of the referendum organisation law as null and void, accusing the court of “judicial rebellion” and complicity in what it called a plot against constitutional order.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 29, 2026 - The C64 coalition rejected the Constitutional Court’s clearance of the referendum organisation law as null and void, accusing the court of “judicial rebellion” and complicity in what it called a plot against constitutional order.

Ensemble secretary-general Dieudonné Bolengetenge read a joint declaration saying the ruling opens the way to Balkanisation and exposes those involved to high-treason sanctions under Congolese law.

C64 listed four red lines it said Congolese should not accept: circumvention of the Constitution, personalisation of institutions, constitutional change, and a third presidential term.

The statement hardened opposition messaging even as the same coalition had suspended street protests to give dialogue until August 15 a chance.

Key points from the report: - The C64 coalition rejected the Constitutional Court’s clearance of the referendum organisation law as null and void, accusing the court of “judicial rebellion” and complicity in what it called a plot against constitutional order. - Ensemble secretary-general Dieudonné Bolengetenge read a joint declaration saying the ruling opens the way to Balkanisation and exposes those involved to high-treason sanctions under Congolese law. - C64 listed four red lines it said Congolese should not accept: circumvention of the Constitution, personalisation of institutions, constitutional change, and a third presidential term. - The statement hardened opposition messaging even as the same coalition had suspended street protests to give dialogue until August 15 a chance.

The developments were reported in the DRC briefing covering mid-to-late July 2026. The account centers on: C64 Calls Constitutional Court Ruling a “Judicial Rebellion”. Taken together, the available details outline both the immediate incident and the broader situation described by officials and witnesses in the source report.

title_en: Thousands Flee to Bush in Fizi and Mwenga After Reported Drone Strikes
excerpt_en: Fizi/Mwenga, South Kivu, July 29, 2026 - National deputy Nyamangyoku Ishibwela raised an SOS for thousands of civilians from Mulima, Point Zéro and Rugezi in Fizi, and Kipupu, Mikenge and Kiseke in Mwenga, who fled into the bush without shelter or aid after July 24.
body_en:
Fizi/Mwenga, South Kivu, July 29, 2026 - National deputy Nyamangyoku Ishibwela raised an SOS for thousands of civilians from Mulima, Point Zéro and Rugezi in Fizi, and Kipupu, Mikenge and Kiseke in Mwenga, who fled into the bush without shelter or aid after July 24.

He attributed the flight to kamikaze-drone bombardments he said originated from Rwanda and were continuing, leaving wounded people without care and children exposed to hunger and disease.

He urged the FARDC to protect civilians and the government to deliver urgent assistance. Attribution of responsibility remains contested in the wider regional information war.

The developments were reported in the DRC briefing covering mid-to-late July 2026. The account centers on: Thousands Flee to Bush in Fizi and Mwenga After Reported Drone Strikes. title_en: Retreating RSF Units Launch Reprisal Raids on North Kordofan Civilians
excerpt_en: El Obeid, Sudan, July 29, 2026 - Large RSF contingents retreating from Um Qurfa and related losses launched reprisal attacks on civilians in Um Badr, Sodari, Abu Zaima, Hamrat al-Sheikh and El Malha areas, according to local reports.
body_en:
El Obeid, Sudan, July 29, 2026 - Large RSF contingents retreating from Um Qurfa and related losses launched reprisal attacks on civilians in Um Badr, Sodari, Abu Zaima, Hamrat al-Sheikh and El Malha areas, according to local reports.

The raids fitted a wartime pattern in which battlefield setbacks are followed by collective punishment of nearby communities. Protection actors said such cycles drive fresh displacement into already overcrowded camps.

title: Kinshasa Announces FDLR Demilitarisation Protocol Under Washington Framework
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 29, 2026 - Regional Integration Minister Floribert Anzuluni said the FDLR had signed a protocol on demilitarisation, demobilisation and cantoning, describing it as a major step in implementing the CONOPS attached to the Washington peace agreement with Rwanda.…
title_en: Kinshasa Announces FDLR Demilitarisation Protocol Under Washington Framework
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 29, 2026 - Regional Integration Minister Floribert Anzuluni said the FDLR had signed a protocol on demilitarisation, demobilisation and cantoning, describing it as a major step in implementing the CONOPS attached to the Washington peace agreement with Rwanda.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 29, 2026 - Regional Integration Minister Floribert Anzuluni said the FDLR had signed a protocol on demilitarisation, demobilisation and cantoning, describing it as a major step in implementing the CONOPS attached to the Washington peace agreement with Rwanda.

Anzuluni said Kinshasa’s obligations include neutralising the FDLR, while Rwanda committed to withdraw forces it presents as defensive measures. He argued Kigali has long used the FDLR issue as a pretext for presence and resource predation in eastern Congo, while insisting the DRC would still fulfil its commitments through sensitisation and, if needed, force.

He said community outreach with MONUSCO support began in October 2025, followed by deployment of two battalions around Walikale after limited results by March, after which FDLR political and military leaders contacted the government on surrender modalities.

title_en: Rwanda Returns 39 People Once Sent Through MONUSCO DDRRR Channel
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC, July 29, 2026 - Thirty-nine people were sent back into the DRC via the Grande Barrière crossing from Gisenyi after time at Rwanda’s Mutobo centre; returnees said they had earlier been transferred to Rwanda under MONUSCO’s DDRRR programme as alleged FDLR members-an...
body_en:
Goma, DRC, July 29, 2026 - Thirty-nine people were sent back into the DRC via the Grande Barrière crossing from Gisenyi after time at Rwanda’s Mutobo centre; returnees said they had earlier been transferred to Rwanda under MONUSCO’s DDRRR programme as alleged FDLR members-an affiliation they disputed.

MONUSCO said the next day it played no role in the July 29 transfer and was not present when the group re-entered Congo. Rwanda has said some returnees did not meet criteria for its rehabilitation programme.

The episode feeds mutual propaganda among Kinshasa, Kigali and AFC/M23 over who manipulates demobilisation caseloads.

title_en: Muwanga Kivumbi Resurfaces at Nateete Police After 19-Day Search
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - National Unity Platform Buganda deputy president Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi resurfaced at Nateete Police Station after about 19 days of uncertainty, conflicting security accounts and a pending High Court habeas corpus application.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 29, 2026 - National Unity Platform Buganda deputy president Muhammad Muwanga Kivumbi resurfaced at Nateete Police Station after about 19 days of uncertainty, conflicting security accounts and a pending High Court habeas corpus application.

He was later taken under tight security to Butambala Chief Magistrate’s Court. Party leaders said the appearance came as they pursued court orders to produce him, framing the episode as incommunicado detention ended only under legal pressure.

title_en: Five Arrested Over Kassanda Double Murder and Coffee Robbery

title_en: Kasai-Central Orders Immediate Removal of Illegal Road Barriers
excerpt_en: Kananga, July 29, 2026 - Kasai-Central’s provincial interior minister, Kamayi Méroé, ordered the immediate suppression of illegal barriers and fake tax posts after bicycle transporters known as Bayanda denounced repeated roadside shakedowns.
body_en:
Kananga, July 29, 2026 - Kasai-Central’s provincial interior minister, Kamayi Méroé, ordered the immediate suppression of illegal barriers and fake tax posts after bicycle transporters known as Bayanda denounced repeated roadside shakedowns.

Territory administrators and sector chiefs were instructed to enforce the measure without delay, with sanctions threatened against any service that erects unauthorised barriers.

Transporters said they previously had to stop and pay at multiple points on each trip and asked for sustained enforcement.

The Rwandan Commission for the Rehabilitation of Ex-Soldiers, RDRC, announced that it has returned to the Democratic Republic of Congo 39 Congolese ex-FDLR fighters who were falsely accused of being former members of the terrorist group.
excerpt: The commission explained that the operation took place on July 29, 2026, in the presence of the media and officials from the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the DRC (MONUSCO). It said: "The RDRC returned the 39 Congolese ex-FDLR fighters on July 19, 2026, after an…
title_en: Rwanda sends 39 Congolese ex-FDLR fighters to DRC, July 29, 2026. The Rwandan Commission for the Rehabilitation of Ex-Soldiers, RDRC, announced that it has returned to the Democratic Republic of Congo 39 Congolese ex-FDLR fighters who were falsely accused of being former members of the terrorist group.
excerpt_en: The commission explained that the operation took place on July 29, 2026, in the presence of the media and officials from the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the DRC (MONUSCO). It said: "The RDRC returned the 39 Congolese ex-FDLR fighters on July 19, 2026, after an…
body_en:
The commission explained that the operation took place on July 29, 2026, in the presence of the media and officials from the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the DRC (MONUSCO).
It said: "The RDRC returned the 39 Congolese ex-FDLR fighters on July 19, 2026, after an assessment confirmed that they had falsely claimed to be former FDLR fighters, and therefore did not meet the requirements of Rwanda's ex-soldiers' rehabilitation program."
On July 29, 2026, AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka announced that the DRC government is recruiting people to pose as FDLR fighters and offer them money.
Kanyuka explained that after being offered money, the Congolese would be integrated into a democratic reintegration (DDR) program led and implemented by MONUSCO.
The forum explained that these activities are aimed at hiding the real FDLR fighters; a group that the DRC government is required to dismantle under the peace agreement it signed with Rwanda last year, with the assistance of the United States.
Kanyuka accused the DRC government of continuing to give the FDLR a place in the country's security forces, saying that some members of the group have been integrated into government forces and Wazalendo armed groups.
He said, “Kinshasa uses the FDLR as an important part of its security apparatus. Members of this group are included in the FARDC, in the Wazalendo groups and in the state security apparatus.”
He continued by saying that there are also FDLR fighters used in the unit responsible for protecting senior government officials (GR) and other important people.
AFC/M23 called for an end to the activities of asking citizens to identify themselves as FDLR fighters, stating that they are intended to mislead the people of the DRC and the international community.
By Jeff Buleli
