title_en: Kigali Dismisses Congolese FDLR Protocol as a “Non-Event”
excerpt_en: Kigali, July 29, 2026 - Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe rejected Kinshasa’s announced FDLR disarmament protocol, saying it has no basis in the Washington accords and calling the move a non-event.
body_en:
Kigali, July 29, 2026 - Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe rejected Kinshasa’s announced FDLR disarmament protocol, saying it has no basis in the Washington accords and calling the move a non-event.

Nduhungirehe said the FDLR are the object of the agreement, not a party to it, and accused Kinshasa of trying to circumvent security obligations under CONOPS and related operational orders, including measures expected within 90 days.

The exchange deepened the gap between Congolese claims of progress and Rwandan insistence that neutralisation commitments remain unmet.

body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, July 28-29, 2026 - Intra-wazalendo clashes between Uhuru RDC factions at Kilambo in Bafuna grouping paralysed traffic between Ntoto and Ngora, while tensions between commanders Shukuru Bulenda and Boaz over Malembe headquarters drove residents of Malembe and Mumba to flee on July 28.

The fragmentation of supposedly allied self-defence groups continued to generate civilian displacement even where AFC/M23 was not the immediate opponent. Road closures deepen isolation of communities already caught among FARDC, AFC/M23 and local armed groups.

title_en: Central Bank Data Show Security Spending More Than Doubled in 2025
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC, July 28, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo’s monetary-policy report said security spending more than doubled in 2025 to about 8,599 billion Congolese francs (roughly $3.9 billion), up 119% from 2024.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC, July 28, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo’s monetary-policy report said security spending more than doubled in 2025 to about 8,599 billion Congolese francs (roughly $3.9 billion), up 119% from 2024.

The surge, tied to eastern military operations including against the M23, widened the state’s cash deficit. Economists note that higher budgets have not yet translated into durable civilian safety in Beni, Masisi or Ituri.

title: First Human Dose Given in Global Bundibugyo Ebola Vaccine Trial
excerpt: Oxford/Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - Oxford Vaccine Group announced the first volunteer had received ChAdOx1 BDBV in the BD-Ebov Phase 1 trial, the first clinical study of a vaccine designed for Bundibugyo Ebola. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called the launch…
title_en: First Human Dose Given in Global Bundibugyo Ebola Vaccine Trial
excerpt_en: Oxford/Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - Oxford Vaccine Group announced the first volunteer had received ChAdOx1 BDBV in the BD-Ebov Phase 1 trial, the first clinical study of a vaccine designed for Bundibugyo Ebola.
body_en:
Oxford/Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - Oxford Vaccine Group announced the first volunteer had received ChAdOx1 BDBV in the BD-Ebov Phase 1 trial, the first clinical study of a vaccine designed for Bundibugyo Ebola.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called the launch an important step and said data would guide next development stages. The candidate uses the same viral-vector platform as the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine; CEPI is funding an $8.6 million programme with Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, which produced a stockpile of about 620,000 doses and supplied trial vials.

Further studies are being prepared with partners in Uganda if early results are favourable. Unlike Zaire-strain Ebola, Bundibugyo still lacks a licensed vaccine or specific treatment, leaving the DRC’s 17th outbreak dependent on classic containment tools.

title_en: FARDC Drone Strikes and Explosion Rock AFC/M23 Positions at Nyabiondo
excerpt_en: Nyabiondo, Masisi, July 28-29, 2026 - On July 28 a military drone dropped two bombs on an AFC/M23 position near the local Catholic church around 08:00, triggering panic and suspending daytime activity for hours in Osso Banyungu sector.
body_en:
Nyabiondo, Masisi, July 28-29, 2026 - On July 28 a military drone dropped two bombs on an AFC/M23 position near the local Catholic church around 08:00, triggering panic and suspending daytime activity for hours in Osso Banyungu sector.

A strong explosion on an AFC/M23 position the following day again sowed panic; precise casualties and the weapon used in the second blast were not clearly established in initial reports.

The incidents fit a pattern of aerial and blast pressure alongside ground contests across Masisi-Walikale axes.

title: Government Begins Paying Risk Bonuses to Ebola Response Workers
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - Authorities said they had begun paying risk bonuses owed to front-line workers fighting the 17th Ebola epidemic across five affected provinces, after strikes over arrears disrupted parts of the response, especially in Ituri. The Incident Manager’s…
title_en: Government Begins Paying Risk Bonuses to Ebola Response Workers
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - Authorities said they had begun paying risk bonuses owed to front-line workers fighting the 17th Ebola epidemic across five affected provinces, after strikes over arrears disrupted parts of the response, especially in Ituri.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - Authorities said they had begun paying risk bonuses owed to front-line workers fighting the 17th Ebola epidemic across five affected provinces, after strikes over arrears disrupted parts of the response, especially in Ituri.

The Incident Manager’s office said President Tshisekedi is closely following the response and noted Suminwa’s recent field visits. More than 12,000 providers in Ituri alone-about 80% of responders-are concerned, spanning clinicians, epidemiologists, hygienists, laboratory staff, logisticians and community relays.

Payments started with teams at the Elikya treatment centre in Bunia, with file cleaning continuing to resolve disputes. Officials urged teams to maintain operations until the outbreak is controlled, while insecurity and even attacks on some treatment centres continue to complicate the fight.

body_en:
Beni, July 28, 2026 - Local rights organisation Badilika said nearly 200 civilians were killed between April and June 2026 across Beni, Rutshuru, Masisi and Walikale, with Beni alone accounting for 199 deaths, mainly in ADF attacks despite joint Shujaa operations with Uganda.

The group also reported arbitrary arrests by AFC/M23 of youths accused of FDLR links in Rutshuru, and abuses by some Wazalendo factions in Masisi and Walikale, including looting, kidnapping and illegal detention.

Fighting around the Rubaya mining hub continues to disrupt livelihoods and deepen humanitarian need. Badilika called for more effective civilian-protection strategies from Congolese authorities and partners.

title_en: OPM Refugee Commissioner Charged With Abuse of Office
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - The Office of the Prime Minister’s Refugee Commissioner was charged with abuse of office and remanded, in a case watched closely by humanitarian partners in one of Africa’s largest refugee-hosting operations.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - The Office of the Prime Minister’s Refugee Commissioner was charged with abuse of office and remanded, in a case watched closely by humanitarian partners in one of Africa’s largest refugee-hosting operations.

excerpt: Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - The Constitutional Court ruled that the bill setting conditions for organising a referendum is constitutional, subject to reservations on articles including 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23 and 43. The decision allows President Tshisekedi to…
title_en: Constitutional Court Clears Referendum Law With Multiple Reservations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - The Constitutional Court ruled that the bill setting conditions for organising a referendum is constitutional, subject to reservations on articles including 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23 and 43.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 28, 2026 - The Constitutional Court ruled that the bill setting conditions for organising a referendum is constitutional, subject to reservations on articles including 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 19, 21, 23 and 43.

The decision allows President Tshisekedi to promulgate the text after its adoption by the National Assembly and Senate, provided the court’s reservations are annexed when the law is published in the Official Journal.

Tshisekedi had referred the bill to the court under Article 160 of the Constitution after defending Parliament’s right to legislate during Independence Day remarks on June 30.

Opposition groups accuse the majority of using the referendum framework to prepare constitutional change that could loosen presidential term limits-an allegation rejected by the presidential camp, which says the reform is about institutional functioning.

The ruling landed as C64 and other opponents had suspended field actions in favour of the announced dialogue.

title: Uganda Declared Ebola-Free After 42-Day Surveillance Window
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi declared Uganda officially Ebola-free after completing the mandatory 42-day monitoring period that began when the last Ugandan national patient was discharged on June 16. He said nationwide intensified…
title_en: Uganda Declared Ebola-Free After 42-Day Surveillance Window
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi declared Uganda officially Ebola-free after completing the mandatory 42-day monitoring period that began when the last Ugandan national patient was discharged on June 16.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi declared Uganda officially Ebola-free after completing the mandatory 42-day monitoring period that began when the last Ugandan national patient was discharged on June 16.

He said nationwide intensified surveillance found no new cases and no unexplained community transmission. The outbreak recorded 20 confirmed infections-including Congolese nationals, health workers and a driver-with two deaths, both among patients from the DRC, and a case fatality rate near 10%.

Baryomunsi stressed that the 2026 flare was a documented importation with fully mapped transmission chains and quarantined contacts. He urged continued vigilance along the West Nile-Kisoro belt because the epidemic remains active in eastern Congo.

title: Uganda Continues Large-Scale Refugee Hosting Amid Aid Strain
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - Refugee-management briefings during the period again underlined funding gaps facing settlements and host communities, even as DRDIP II and related livelihood projects prepare new phases. Commissioner-level legal trouble added political noise…
title_en: Uganda Continues Large-Scale Refugee Hosting Amid Aid Strain
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - Refugee-management briefings during the period again underlined funding gaps facing settlements and host communities, even as DRDIP II and related livelihood projects prepare new phases. Commissioner-level legal trouble added political noise…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 28, 2026 - Refugee-management briefings during the period again underlined funding gaps facing settlements and host communities, even as DRDIP II and related livelihood projects prepare new phases.
Commissioner-level legal trouble added political noise to an already stressed system. Humanitarian agencies warn that without sustained donor support, services for refugees and hosts will thin further.
Medical-waste complaints in Bidibidi further illustrated how weak facility hygiene can compound risks inside large settlements.
Conclusion
Between July 16 and July 31, 2026, Uganda navigated a complex interplay of international diplomacy, high-stakes political friction, economic initiatives, and critical public health milestones.
Diplomacy & Security: Uganda positioned itself prominently on the world stage by formally nominating Olara Otunnu for United Nations Secretary-General and Rosette Muzigo-Morrison for the International Criminal Court. Concurrently, Kampala hosted the AUSSOM Extraordinary Summit, taking a lead role in urging alternative, sustainable financing models for African-led peacekeeping as UN support in Somalia winds down.
Domestic Politics & Legal Controversies: Tensions surrounding opposition trials reached a flashpoint with the courtroom collapse and subsequent intensive care admission of Dr. Kizza Besigye, sparking severe criticism from rights advocates regarding trial conditions and legal representation. In contrast, a press freedom milestone was achieved with President Museveni authorizing the reopening of the Nation Media Group.
Public Health Successes & Challenges: Uganda marked a major victory by officially declaring an end to its domestic Ebola outbreak while exporting medical expertise to assist the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. However, local public health infrastructure faced criticism over medical waste management in Bidibidi refugee settlement and post-Cleaning Day waste disposal struggles.
Economic Momentum & Innovation: Economic developments demonstrated strong forward momentum through expanded export earnings, Tyms’ landmark partnership with OpenAI, and long-term infrastructure and green-energy projects like the Karuma green hydrogen initiative. Nevertheless, contractor delays on vital road projects and financial losses at Dfcu Bank highlighted ongoing operational and economic hurdles.
Overall, this fortnight highlights Uganda’s growing influence in regional and global governance alongside persistent internal pressures surrounding rule of law, political governance, and infrastructure execution.
By Jeff Buleli

title_en: Rwanda Grants Citizenship to 105 Applicants From 27 Countries

body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda, July 28, 2026 - Rwanda granted citizenship to 105 people born in 27 countries, with the largest groups born in Burundi and the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the official gazette.

The group included 26 people born in Burundi, 20 in the DRC, nine in Uganda and eight in the United States, as well as applicants born in Belgium, Cameroon, Kenya and Rwanda to foreign parents.

About 60% were aged 30 to 49; the youngest was five and the oldest 81. The citizenship decisions took effect on July 24.

excerpt_en: MINSK, Belarus, July 28, 2026 - Ambassador Gen.
body_en:
MINSK, Belarus, July 28, 2026 - Ambassador Gen.

Maj. Joseph Nzabamwita presented credentials to President Aleksandr Lukashenko as Rwanda’s non-resident ambassador to Belarus, where both sides said they sought wider cooperation in trade, agriculture, technology, education and security.

title_en: Mutamba Walks Out of FRIVAO Hearing at Court of Cassation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 27, 2026 - Former justice minister Constant Mutamba left a Court of Cassation hearing in the FRIVAO case in protest, accusing court clerks of inserting false mentions in his summons and saying he was denied the chance to raise preliminary objections.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 27, 2026 - Former justice minister Constant Mutamba left a Court of Cassation hearing in the FRIVAO case in protest, accusing court clerks of inserting false mentions in his summons and saying he was denied the chance to raise preliminary objections.

Mutamba had demanded live RTNC broadcast and a public courtroom, citing constitutional provisions on open justice. He is pursued alongside former FRIVAO coordinator Chancard Bukolela over contested disbursements, including a $14.3 million payment to Congo Energy.

He said he would rather “drink hemlock like Socrates” than accept what he called an irregular procedure. At an earlier July 13 appearance he had already disputed proper service and access to the case file.

title_en: Deminers Neutralise Seven Explosive Devices at Mutwanga
excerpt_en: Mutwanga, Beni, July 27, 2026 - UNMAS, AFRILAM and Civil Protection destroyed seven explosive devices at Mutwanga, including one inside Saints-Pierre-et-Paul Catholic parish and six at the SICOVIR concession in Nzenga.
body_en:

title: Uganda Nominates Olara Otunnu for United Nations Secretary-General
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 26, 2026 - The government formally seconded Ambassador Olara Otunnu as its candidate for United Nations Secretary-General, urging member states to support a diplomat with more than four decades in international service. A Foreign Affairs statement signed…
title_en: Uganda Nominates Olara Otunnu for United Nations Secretary-General
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 26, 2026 - The government formally seconded Ambassador Olara Otunnu as its candidate for United Nations Secretary-General, urging member states to support a diplomat with more than four decades in international service.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 26, 2026 - The government formally seconded Ambassador Olara Otunnu as its candidate for United Nations Secretary-General, urging member states to support a diplomat with more than four decades in international service.

A Foreign Affairs statement signed by Permanent Secretary Vincent Waiswa Bagiire described Otunnu as a distinguished statesman and former Under-Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict who also served as Uganda’s UN permanent representative in the 1980s.

Officials said Kampala would campaign for him among Security Council members, while Otunnu noted travel complications linked to regional Ebola formalities had slowed his early New York outreach.

Other declared contenders include Michelle Bachelet, María Fernanda Espinosa, Rafael Grossi, Rebeca Grynspan, Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and Macky Sall. The next secretary-general is expected to take office on January 1, 2027.

Kampala, Uganda, July 26, 2026 - Alongside the UN secretary-general race, Uganda presented international human-rights lawyer Rosette Muzigo-Morrison as its candidate for a seat on the International Criminal Court bench.

Officials said the twin nominations underline Kampala’s effort to place Ugandans in senior multilateral justice and diplomatic roles. Campaigning for both posts is expected to intensify through the second half of 2026.

DAR ES SALAAM, Tanzania, July 26, 2026 - Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe met Tanzania’s Foreign Minister Mahmoud Thabit Kombo to review ways of strengthening bilateral relations.

title_en: Tracep Cargo Plane Crashes in Walikale; MONUSCO Helps Recover Survivors
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, July 26-31, 2026 - A Tracep Congo Aviation LET L-410 cargo flight from Beni toward Shabunda territory crashed near Buruko/Kamaninge in Walikale after an engine failure and lost radio contact while trying to divert.
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, July 26-31, 2026 - A Tracep Congo Aviation LET L-410 cargo flight from Beni toward Shabunda territory crashed near Buruko/Kamaninge in Walikale after an engine failure and lost radio contact while trying to divert.

The aircraft carried two crew and about two tonnes of cargo. Search teams found the wreckage days later; one crew member survived and the captain died.

By July 31, MONUSCO peacekeepers were reported assisting recovery of crash survivors as investigations continued.

excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 26, 2026 - Rwandan and Kenyan tourism officials and businesses opened consultations to increase visitor flows and develop a shared East African tourism vision. More than 50 participants, including travel operators, hotel investors and government…
title_en: Rwanda and Kenya Open Tourism Cooperation Talks
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 26, 2026 - Rwandan and Kenyan tourism officials and businesses opened consultations to increase visitor flows and develop a shared East African tourism vision.
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda, July 26, 2026 - Rwandan and Kenyan tourism officials and businesses opened consultations to increase visitor flows and develop a shared East African tourism vision.

More than 50 participants, including travel operators, hotel investors and government representatives, met in Kigali under a partnership involving the Kenya Tourism Board, RwandAir and sector stakeholders.

Kenyan Embassy counsellor Esther Magiti cited wildlife, coastal, cultural and heritage tourism, MICE travel and investment as areas for collaboration. The talks follow a June 29 agreement on use of Kenyan infrastructure for Rwanda’s petroleum imports.

title_en: DR Congo Ebola Caseload Passes 3,200
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 25, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo recorded 3,200 Ebola cases and 1,405 deaths, with 773 people isolated or hospitalized and 571 recovered, health authorities said.
body_en:
KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 25, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo recorded 3,200 Ebola cases and 1,405 deaths, with 773 people isolated or hospitalized and 571 recovered, health authorities said.

The outbreak, declared in Ituri on May 15, involves the Bundibugyo strain and has spread to Ituri, Haut-Uélé, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo. The mortality rate was 43.9%, while 77.8% of contacts were being followed.

WHO said Ituri accounted for nearly 90% of cases as of July 15. Justice and Rights.

KIGALI, Rwanda, July 25, 2026 - President Paul Kagame received Uganda’s Chief of Defence Staff, Gen.

Muhoozi Kainerugaba, for talks on Rwanda-Uganda relations and regional peace and security during Muhoozi’s two-day working visit. Gen.

title: Bizimana and Verlinden Clash Over Account of King Rudahigwa’s Death
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 25, 2026 - Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement Dr. Jean Damascène Bizimana and Belgian journalist Peter Verlinden publicly disputed the circumstances of King Mutara III Rudahigwa’s death in Bujumbura on July 25, 1959. Bizimana said Rudahigwa…
title_en: Bizimana and Verlinden Clash Over Account of King Rudahigwa’s Death
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 25, 2026 - Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement Dr.
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda, July 25, 2026 - Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement Dr.

Jean Damascène Bizimana and Belgian journalist Peter Verlinden publicly disputed the circumstances of King Mutara III Rudahigwa’s death in Bujumbura on July 25, 1959.

Bizimana said Rudahigwa died after an injection administered by Belgian doctor Dr. Vyncke and characterized the death as a political crime that preceded decades of discrimination and persecution of Tutsi.

Verlinden challenged that account, saying there was no evidence of an assassination. Bizimana rejected the criticism as an attempt by outsiders to alter or erase Rwanda’s history.

Key points from the report: - Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement Dr. - Jean Damascène Bizimana and Belgian journalist Peter Verlinden publicly disputed the circumstances of King Mutara III Rudahigwa’s death in Bujumbura on July 25, 1959. - Bizimana said Rudahigwa died after an injection administered by Belgian doctor Dr. - Vyncke and characterized the death as a political crime that preceded decades of discrimination and persecution of Tutsi. - Verlinden challenged that account, saying there was no evidence of an assassination. - Bizimana rejected the criticism as an attempt by outsiders to alter or erase Rwanda’s history.

The developments were reported in the RWANDA briefing covering mid-to-late July 2026. The account centers on: Bizimana and Verlinden Clash Over Account of King Rudahigwa’s Death. title_en: Army and Allies Recapture Bara and Nearby North Kordofan Towns
excerpt_en: Bara, Sudan, July 25, 2026 - Sudanese Armed Forces units, the Joint Force of armed movements, Qashan forces and supporting troops recaptured Bara, Al-Baraka, Um Sayala, Um Qurfa and Jabrat Al-Sheikh after heavy clashes with the RSF.
body_en:
Bara, Sudan, July 25, 2026 - Sudanese Armed Forces units, the Joint Force of armed movements, Qashan forces and supporting troops recaptured Bara, Al-Baraka, Um Sayala, Um Qurfa and Jabrat Al-Sheikh after heavy clashes with the RSF.

Military officials claimed dozens of RSF vehicles destroyed and numerous fighters killed. Bara, about 40-50 kilometres from El Obeid on the corridor toward Omdurman, has changed hands repeatedly; its loss again reopened an eastern approach to the besieged state capital.

Geneva/Kinshasa, July 25, 2026 - WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that insecurity and conflict are obstructing the Ebola response and called for stronger community engagement plus political action toward a ceasefire to improve humanitarian access.

Priorities remain cutting transmission in Ituri through surveillance, clinical care, safe burials and community involvement. Tedros said the Congolese people cannot confront the epidemic alone and need sustained international support and peace.

title_en: Congolese Analyst Remains Detained in Burundi
excerpt_en: BUJUMBURA, Burundi, July 25, 2026 - Congolese analyst and aid worker Benjamin Babunga remained detained after his May 27 arrest on allegations including terrorism, treason and endangering national security, accusations he denies.
body_en:
BUJUMBURA, Burundi, July 25, 2026 - Congolese analyst and aid worker Benjamin Babunga remained detained after his May 27 arrest on allegations including terrorism, treason and endangering national security, accusations he denies.

The prosecution relied on social-media posts, including comments on conditions in Bukavu and a drone attack at Kisangani airport. His lawyers said the posts contained no threats or criminal conduct and that he was being prosecuted for commentary.

A court ordered bail on July 15, but he had not been released pending a prosecution response. Security and Humanitarian Affairs.

title_en: Kagame Sends Message to Ghana as Governance Partnership Expands

body_en:
ACCRA, Ghana, July 25, 2026 - Francis Gatare, president of the African School of Governance, delivered a message from President Kagame to Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama through the head of Ghana’s presidential office, Julius Debrah.

Gatare, accompanied by Rwanda’s ambassador to Ghana, Rosemary Mbabazi, briefed Debrah on the Kigali-based school’s work in governance research and education. Their discussions covered Rwanda-Ghana relations, the school’s partnership with the Accra Reset initiative and African cooperation and integration.

title_en: Otunnu Says Museveni Photo Moment in Gulu Was Unplanned
excerpt_en: Gulu, Uganda, July 25, 2026 - Former UPC leader Olara Otunnu said a public handshake and photograph with President Yoweri Museveni at Kaunda Grounds during homecoming celebrations for Chief Justice Emeritus Alfonse Owiny-Dollo was spontaneous rather than choreographed.
body_en:
Gulu, Uganda, July 25, 2026 - Former UPC leader Olara Otunnu said a public handshake and photograph with President Yoweri Museveni at Kaunda Grounds during homecoming celebrations for Chief Justice Emeritus Alfonse Owiny-Dollo was spontaneous rather than choreographed.

Residents applauded as the longtime critic briefly joined Museveni and Owiny-Dollo on the podium after local leaders persuaded him to return for the picture. Otunnu later said he and Museveni had shaken hands before, but that the three-way photo had not been arranged in advance-an image widely read as a symbol of political thaw ahead of his UN candidacy.

title: Writing that Bukavu is among the prisoners of Benjamin Babunga in Burundi, July 25, 2026. A Congolese known for analyzing the history of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Great Lakes region in general, Benjamin Babunga, is still imprisoned in Burundi since May 27, 2026 when he was arrested in Bujumbura.
excerpt: Babunga was arrested while working for a Dutch non-governmental organization called ZAO, which was responsible for monitoring its projects in Burundi and other countries in the region. The Burundian government accuses him of crimes including terrorism, treason and endangering…
title_en: Writing that Bukavu is among the prisoners of Benjamin Babunga in Burundi, July 25, 2026. A Congolese known for analyzing the history of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Great Lakes region in general, Benjamin Babunga, is still imprisoned in Burundi since May 27, 2026 when he was arrested in Bujumbura.
excerpt_en: Babunga was arrested while working for a Dutch non-governmental organization called ZAO, which was responsible for monitoring its projects in Burundi and other countries in the region. The Burundian government accuses him of crimes including terrorism, treason and endangering…
body_en:
Babunga was arrested while working for a Dutch non-governmental organization called ZAO, which was responsible for monitoring its projects in Burundi and other countries in the region.
The Burundian government accuses him of crimes including terrorism, treason and endangering national security. He denies the allegations, saying his social media posts are within his right to free speech.
In the first hearing that took place in the High Court of Mukaza on July 13, the Burundi Prosecutor's Office presented the records of the messages he published on social media as evidence.
His lawyers said that none of the posts he posted on social media contained threats, criminal activities or hints of foreign nationalism.
The lawyers said their client was being prosecuted for his comments and discussions on social media, rather than for his criminal activities.
Among the documents that caused controversy in the court was the one he put on X on May 11, 2026, where he mentioned that the city of Bukavu in South Kivu Province is cleaner than it was before it was captured by the AFC/M23 coalition in February 2025.
Babunga's message also said that today's Bukavu is calm and everything is in order, rules and regulations are respected, so this good should continue for a long time.
Another controversial document is the one on May 25 about the drone attack on the Kisangani airport. At that time, he said that the fact that AFC/M23 was able to reach this place where there is a strong base of the RDC forces is a sign of a major change in the war.
The Burundian Prosecutor's Office interpreted this message as an expression of support for the AFC/M23; the coalition considers Burundi as a very strong enemy that it joins forces with the RDC in fighting it.
The Burundian authorities also analyzed Babunga's relationship with some of the suspected supporters of AFC/M23 such as journalist Rodriguez Katsuva, questioned him, and looked at the conversations they had.
The names of journalist Steve Wembi and Adrien Kimanuka were also mentioned among the people Babunga is accused of having a private relationship with.
Members of Babunga's family said that the talks he had with Kimanuka about the success of AFC/M23 were only for delay, so they have nothing to do with political activities.
When he was arrested, his phone and computer were seized. His family says that the intelligence agencies in Burundi have lost evidence that he is working with the leaders of AFC/M23 or those in the state of Rwamda.
His lawyers insist that he is not a politician, but an aid worker and historical commentator.
In order to refute allegations that he has a special relationship with Rwanda, his lawyers showed a document he published in 2020 about the massacre in Kasika, where he criticized the country's army accused of being involved.
At that time, Vincent Karega, who was the Ambassador of Rwanda to the RDC, condemned Wembi's message, stating that it was a propaganda campaign.
On July 15, the court ordered that Babunga be released on bail only and was not released because the Prosecution had not commented on this decision.
On July 6, President Evariste Ndayishimiye of Burundi hosted politicians who are opposed to the RDC regime to discuss the bad atmosphere that was still prevailing in Kinshasa.
Although what took them to Burundi was mainly to discuss the Tshisekedi government's plan to change the Constitution, they also told Ndayizimye that Babunga should be released but he was in the air.

title_en: Ituri Military Governor Orders Dismantling of Illegal Roadblocks
excerpt_en: Bunia, July 25, 2026 - Ituri’s military governor ordered military, police and administrative authorities to dismantle illegal barriers on main roads after widespread racketeering of motorists and motorcycle taxis.
body_en:
Bunia, July 25, 2026 - Ituri’s military governor ordered military, police and administrative authorities to dismantle illegal barriers on main roads after widespread racketeering of motorists and motorcycle taxis.

Checkpoints on axes including Bunia-Kasenyi, Nyakunde, Komanda, Mahagi and Aru had been extracting 500 to 1,000 Congolese francs, sometimes every five kilometres.

In Mahagi, youths tore down several barriers before police dispersed them, and civil society organised a “ville morte” that shut shops and transport until the order and promised investigations restored activity.

The instruction was later extended province-wide.

body_en:
Walikale/Masisi, July 24, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels reinforced positions with men and ammunition at Ihula in Walikale and Malemo in Masisi, according to local security sources, in what was described as preparation for a renewed offensive toward Mpety and Mindjendje in Banakindi/Kisimba.

title: The government has established a new agency that will manage the Ibirunga and Gishwati-Mukura National Parks, 25 July 2026. The Cabinet meeting approved the establishment of a national agency for the conservation of the Biological Network in the care of wildlife in Rwanda, including the management of the Gishwati-Mukura National Park and the Ibirunga National Park.
excerpt: It was a decision made in the Cabinet meeting on July 24, 2026, led by President Paul Kagame in Village Urugwiro. The government of Rwanda explained that this new center will take care of wildlife through ecosystem conservation, research, innovation and building…
title_en: The government has established a new agency that will manage the Ibirunga and Gishwati-Mukura National Parks, 25 July 2026. The Cabinet meeting approved the establishment of a national agency for the conservation of the Biological Network in the care of wildlife in Rwanda, including the management of the Gishwati-Mukura National Park and the Ibirunga National Park.
excerpt_en: It was a decision made in the Cabinet meeting on July 24, 2026, led by President Paul Kagame in Village Urugwiro. The government of Rwanda explained that this new center will take care of wildlife through ecosystem conservation, research, innovation and building…
body_en:
It was a decision made in the Cabinet meeting on July 24, 2026, led by President Paul Kagame in Village Urugwiro.
The government of Rwanda explained that this new center will take care of wildlife through ecosystem conservation, research, innovation and building sustainability in environmental care.
He explained that improving the management of National Parks will continue to promote sustainable tourism, protect services based on environmental protection and improve the economy and well-being of the people who live in these parks.
In February 2016, the Gishwati-Mukura forest, located in the Congo-Nile mountain range, was recognized as Rwanda's fourth National Park.
This park is located in Rutsiro and Ngororero Districts in the Western Province of the country, with an area of 3,558 hectares, including the Gishwati area with an area of 1,570 hectares and the Mukura area with an area of 1,988 hectares.
It is home to more than 60 species of trees including table and bamboo. This park is known for housing a variety of animals, including 20 species of chimpanzees, golden monkeys, birds and other small animals.
Volcanoes National Park is also a must-see in this center which is known to be home to the rarest volcanic geese in the world.
Some of them are found in East Africa, especially in Rwanda, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In 2010, 480 geese were counted, but in 2019, they reached 604. In the world that year, they reached 1,063.
It is located in the mountain range of Karisimbi, Muhabura, Bisoke and the lake above, Sabyinyo and Gahinga.
Apart from mountain geese, there are more than 200 species of birds and cattle.
Rwanda also has Akagera National Park and Nyungwe National Park, both of which have unique wildlife habitats and attract new tourists every year.
The 2025 activity report of the Rwanda Development Agency, RDB, shows that tourism revenue in 2025 is $685 million, from $647 million in 2024, which represents an increase of 6%.
The number of visitors to Rwanda also increased by 9% to 1.49 million people. Many of these visit Volcanoes National Park, which is popular for its geese, as well as other parks.
Rwanda expects that in 2029, the tourism sector will earn the country $1.1 billion.
Currently, 10% of the revenue generated by each park is distributed to the people who live near the park through providing them with infrastructure and programs aimed at their development.

title: UN Rights Office Flags Sharp Rise in Violations Concentrated in the East
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 24, 2026 - The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) said its May monthly report, released July 24, documented a sharp deterioration, with more than 1,200 people affected by human-rights violations and 59 conflict-related sexual-violence cases. Violations and…
title_en: UN Rights Office Flags Sharp Rise in Violations Concentrated in the East
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 24, 2026 - The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) said its May monthly report, released July 24, documented a sharp deterioration, with more than 1,200 people affected by human-rights violations and 59 conflict-related sexual-violence cases.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 24, 2026 - The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) said its May monthly report, released July 24, documented a sharp deterioration, with more than 1,200 people affected by human-rights violations and 59 conflict-related sexual-violence cases.

Violations and victims rose about 26% and 20% respectively in a month, and more than 80% of abuses were concentrated in Ituri and the two Kivus, linked mainly to ADF, M23 and LRA attacks.

State actors, chiefly FARDC soldiers, were identified as responsible for nearly half of conflict-related sexual-violence cases recorded, even as overall sexual-violence figures fell versus April.

The office also noted 66 judicial proceedings against soldiers, police and civilians during the month, producing nearly 50 convictions for serious violence. Security and Humanitarian Affairs.

title_en: ICRC Urges Parties to Respect IHL Amid Explosive Weapons Use
excerpt_en: Geneva/Goma, July 24, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross called on all parties to respect international humanitarian law in light of explosive weapons affecting civilians in eastern Congo.
body_en:
Geneva/Goma, July 24, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross called on all parties to respect international humanitarian law in light of explosive weapons affecting civilians in eastern Congo.

excerpt: Bunia, July 24, 2026 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa visited Ebola treatment and response sites in Rwampara and Mongbwalu, the epicentre of the country’s 17th Ebola outbreak, to show state support for patients, communities and front-line teams. At Rwampara, she observed…
title_en: Suminwa Visits Rwampara and Mongbwalu as Ebola Epicentre Response Continues
excerpt_en: Bunia, July 24, 2026 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa visited Ebola treatment and response sites in Rwampara and Mongbwalu, the epicentre of the country’s 17th Ebola outbreak, to show state support for patients, communities and front-line teams.
body_en:
Bunia, July 24, 2026 - Prime Minister Judith Suminwa visited Ebola treatment and response sites in Rwampara and Mongbwalu, the epicentre of the country’s 17th Ebola outbreak, to show state support for patients, communities and front-line teams.

At Rwampara, she observed biosecurity procedures and patient care; authorities highlighted recoveries including a 15-month-old infant and mother, described as the first baby officially cured in the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak.

In Mongbwalu, responders listed shortages of electricity and drinking water, insecurity, continuing mining activity, community resistance and weak support for community relays.

Suminwa handed over 10 off-road vehicles to provincial response coordinator Prof. Steve Ahuka and said partner financing now allows a focus on logistics, ambulances, oxygen and safe burial equipment.

Five provinces-Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo and Haut-Uele-are affected.

title: Rwanda and Poland signed an agreement to make it easier for embassy staff to find work, 24 July 2026. Rwanda and Poland signed an agreement to help embassy staff to find work and make it easier to work in those countries.
excerpt: It is an agreement signed on July 24, 2026, in the capital of Poland, Warsaw. The Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland, Wojciech Zajaczkowski, and the outgoing Ambassador of Rwanda in that country, Prof. Shyaka Anastase, signed the agreement between…
title_en: Rwanda and Poland signed an agreement to make it easier for embassy staff to find work, 24 July 2026. Rwanda and Poland signed an agreement to help embassy staff to find work and make it easier to work in those countries.
excerpt_en: It is an agreement signed on July 24, 2026, in the capital of Poland, Warsaw. The Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland, Wojciech Zajaczkowski, and the outgoing Ambassador of Rwanda in that country, Prof. Shyaka Anastase, signed the agreement between…
body_en:
It is an agreement signed on July 24, 2026, in the capital of Poland, Warsaw.
The Secretary of State in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland, Wojciech Zajaczkowski, and the outgoing Ambassador of Rwanda in that country, Prof. Shyaka Anastase, signed the agreement between the two countries that allows them to carry out beneficial activities for members of the families of diplomats and other embassies of the two countries.
ZajaczKowski, who has Africa in his responsibilities, praised the progress that has been made, pointing out that Rwanda is the first country to sign such an agreement in Africa.
He said, "We are proud of the relationship we have with Rwanda and how it is growing...Rwanda is the first country where we have signed such an agreement, on the African continent".
Amb Prof Shyaka, also thanked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Government of Poland, for the way they value good relations and cooperation with Rwanda.
He said, "Rwanda is proud of the good cooperation with Poland, as we treat you as one of our best friends".
The relationship between Rwanda and Poland has been going on for over 61 years, but the last five years have been a special part of the partnership between the two countries.
Some of the achievements include the fact that both countries have established permanent embassies and Poland has become one of Rwanda's major economic partners.
The two countries also have cooperation agreements in various sectors aimed at the development of their people.

title_en: Government Tests Path Toward Locally Made Lightning Protection
excerpt_en: KARONGI, Rwanda, July 23, 2026 - The Ministry in charge of emergency management said Rwanda was preparing to assess a locally manufactured lightning rod, aiming to make protection more accessible in high-risk communities.
body_en:
KARONGI, Rwanda, July 23, 2026 - The Ministry in charge of emergency management said Rwanda was preparing to assess a locally manufactured lightning rod, aiming to make protection more accessible in high-risk communities.

The announcement accompanied installation of lightning protection at GS Musango and Musango Power Station in Rwankuba Sector. MINEMA official Christine Niyotwambaza said imported systems cost no less than Rwf3 million.

In the past four years, lightning killed 287 people and left more than 950 permanently disabled, authorities said.

title_en: Radio Technician Found Dead After ADF Abduction at Mangina
excerpt_en: Mangina, Beni, July 23, 2026 - A radio technician abducted by ADF fighters was found dead, adding to a string of civilian targeting cases along the Beni-Lubero belt.
body_en:

title_en: Dfcu Bank Slips Into First-Half Loss as Costs Jump
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 22, 2026 - Dfcu reported a pre-tax loss of about Shs26.3 billion for the first half of 2026, reversing a Shs39.7 billion pre-tax profit a year earlier, after operating expenses rose to about Shs230 billion from Shs150.4 billion.
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 22, 2026 - Dfcu reported a pre-tax loss of about Shs26.3 billion for the first half of 2026, reversing a Shs39.7 billion pre-tax profit a year earlier, after operating expenses rose to about Shs230 billion from Shs150.4 billion.

The roughly 53% cost increase outpaced income growth, underlining pressure on mid-tier lenders amid higher operating and compliance burdens. Markets watched whether management would cut costs or rebuild fee and interest income in the second half.

excerpt: BUGESERA, Rwanda, July 22, 2026 - The Agriculture Ministry and Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture launched training under a $5 million programme to put 600,000 hectares under soil-conservation farming by 2029. The four-year project begins with 100,000 hectares next…
title_en: Soil Conservation Programme Targets 600,000 Hectares
excerpt_en: BUGESERA, Rwanda, July 22, 2026 - The Agriculture Ministry and Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture launched training under a $5 million programme to put 600,000 hectares under soil-conservation farming by 2029.
body_en:
BUGESERA, Rwanda, July 22, 2026 - The Agriculture Ministry and Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture launched training under a $5 million programme to put 600,000 hectares under soil-conservation farming by 2029.

The four-year project begins with 100,000 hectares next season, then 150,000 hectares annually. It plans to train 889 personnel before the 2027A season; 168 had already been trained, and 52 district agricultural interns began a two-day course on July 22.

Officials said improved soil cover, reduced tillage, crop rotation and staged fertilizer use would protect productivity.

excerpt: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 22, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi announced plans for permanent inter-Congolese talks intended to address political and security pressures, but key details, including dates, venue and participants, remained unsettled. The initiative followed a…
title_en: Tshisekedi’s Dialogue Plan Emerges Amid Uncertainty Over Participation
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 22, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi announced plans for permanent inter-Congolese talks intended to address political and security pressures, but key details, including dates, venue and participants, remained unsettled.
body_en:
KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 22, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi announced plans for permanent inter-Congolese talks intended to address political and security pressures, but key details, including dates, venue and participants, remained unsettled.

The initiative followed a July 17 meeting with leaders of major religious groups. It comes after opposition to Tshisekedi’s proposed constitutional changes, including from Martin Fayulu, Delly Sesanga, Jean-Marc Kabund and the C64 coalition, and amid conflict in the east.

The government has said the talks will be held in Kinshasa. Some opposition figures have called for an external venue and confidence-building measures such as freeing political prisoners.

Authorities were considering restoring some opposition passports but had rejected sentence commutations for certain prominent detainees.

excerpt: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 22, 2026 - Anglican Church leaders said the AFC/M23 coalition should not be excluded from proposed inter-Congolese dialogue, arguing that the country’s armed actors must be heard in efforts to resolve its political and security crisis. Church…
title_en: Church Leaders Urge Inclusive Approach to Proposed Congolese Dialogue
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 22, 2026 - Anglican Church leaders said the AFC/M23 coalition should not be excluded from proposed inter-Congolese dialogue, arguing that the country’s armed actors must be heard in efforts to resolve its political and security crisis.
body_en:
KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 22, 2026 - Anglican Church leaders said the AFC/M23 coalition should not be excluded from proposed inter-Congolese dialogue, arguing that the country’s armed actors must be heard in efforts to resolve its political and security crisis.

Church spokesperson Pastor Eric Nsenga spoke after Catholic and Anglican representatives met President Félix Tshisekedi on July 17, when the president agreed to informal talks.

Nsenga said the churches’ contacts in Goma had made clear that AFC/M23 members are Congolese with grievances that mediators should hear, rather than dismiss as a “provocation.” The position differs from the government’s stated approach.

Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya indicated that participants would not include those who had taken up arms or had not condemned developments in the east. The timing, participation rules and venue for the broader talks had not been announced.

title: UR to invest Rwf4.4 billion awarded by Mastercard Foundation in scholarships, July 22, 2026. The University of Rwanda (UR) announced that it will use the $3 million award from the Mastercard Foundation to enhance the capacity of its medical education, provide scholarships to more students and purchase equipment for its existing laboratory.
excerpt: The announcement was made by UR’s Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs and Research, Dr. Ndikumana Raymond, after the university was named one of the top five African universities to receive the Africa Higher Education for Transformation (AHEFT) Prize. The award, presented by…
title_en: UR to invest Rwf4.4 billion awarded by Mastercard Foundation in scholarships, July 22, 2026. The University of Rwanda (UR) announced that it will use the $3 million award from the Mastercard Foundation to enhance the capacity of its medical education, provide scholarships to more students and purchase equipment for its existing laboratory.
excerpt_en: The announcement was made by UR’s Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs and Research, Dr. Ndikumana Raymond, after the university was named one of the top five African universities to receive the Africa Higher Education for Transformation (AHEFT) Prize. The award, presented by…
body_en:
The announcement was made by UR’s Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs and Research, Dr. Ndikumana Raymond, after the university was named one of the top five African universities to receive the Africa Higher Education for Transformation (AHEFT) Prize.
The award, presented by the Mastercard Foundation, aims to recognize universities that demonstrate exceptional contributions to advancing education and youth development in Africa.
UR won in the ‘Excellence in Health’ category, for its role in advancing education and capacity in the health sector in Rwanda.
Dr. Ndikumana said that the money will not only be used in the medical field, but will also help publicize the many activities carried out by UR.
He said, “This award will help us to better demonstrate what we do, because it is not only in medicine. We do a lot in agriculture, in construction, in environmental issues and in various other sectors.”
He explained that one of the efforts that will be made in using the money is to increase the capacity of medical schools.
He said, “We are going to invest this money in teaching medical subjects. We have many students but we want to have more. We will provide scholarships and the main goal is to increase the number of students who can study these subjects and study them well, because we will increase laboratory equipment where we did not have it.”
Returning to the reasons why they were awarded the award in the health subjects category, Dr. Ndikumana said that especially since the Genocide against the Tutsi, UR has made a significant contribution to training medical personnel.
In 2013, when various public universities were merged to form the University of Rwanda, Dr. Ndikumana highlighted that this was one of the factors that increased the university's performance and development, allowing it to do many things, including improving the quality of health courses.
He said that last year, more than 1,000 research papers were published, most of which were in the field of medicine, as there were 477.
He stressed that UR's being the first university in Rwanda, especially in the field of medicine, was not something that just happened, as it has educated more than 26,000 people in the field of health, has many departments related to medicine, and has a lot of infrastructure.
The universities that won these awards, which were contested for the first time, will be presented at the International Conference on the Contribution of Universities to Development to be held in Ghana on September 22, 2026, and the awards will continue for 10 years, with a total of $500 million.

title_en: DRC Uses Security Council Presidency to Link Natural Resources and Peace
excerpt_en: New York, July 22, 2026 - During its July presidency of the UN Security Council, the DRC convened a high-level debate on natural-resource governance as a foundation for peace, security and prosperity, following earlier sessions on conflict-related sexual violence and an...
body_en:
New York, July 22, 2026 - During its July presidency of the UN Security Council, the DRC convened a high-level debate on natural-resource governance as a foundation for peace, security and prosperity, following earlier sessions on conflict-related sexual violence and an Arria-formula meeting on resources and conflict.

Congolese officials argued that permanent sovereignty over natural resources must be exercised so that wealth serves populations rather than armed groups and illicit networks.

Kinshasa said existing tools on mineral traceability, corporate due diligence and conflict financing remain fragmented and insufficiently coordinated. The diplomatic push reflects the country’s dual position as a major source of critical minerals and a theatre where illegal extraction continues to feed insecurity, especially in the east.

title_en: Pakistan Ratifies Framework for Expanded Trade With Rwanda
excerpt_en: ISLAMABAD, Pakistan, July 22, 2026 - Pakistan ratified a memorandum of understanding with Rwanda on trade cooperation under its Look Africa initiative, opening the way for a more comprehensive bilateral arrangement.
body_en:
ISLAMABAD, Pakistan, July 22, 2026 - Pakistan ratified a memorandum of understanding with Rwanda on trade cooperation under its Look Africa initiative, opening the way for a more comprehensive bilateral arrangement.

The framework provides for a joint trade group, regular high-level dialogue, business-community cooperation, trade fairs, a Joint Business Council, joint projects, information exchange and work to remove non-tariff barriers.

Pakistan began circulating a draft bilateral trade agreement in 2018. Rwanda opened an embassy in Pakistan in 2025, while Pakistan opened one in Rwanda in 2021.

The two countries already cooperate in education, political consultations, defence and security, and trade; Pakistan imports Rwandan tea, coffee, avocados and other agricultural products, while Rwanda imports medical equipment, rice, textiles and agricultural technology.

title: President Trump appoints US Ambassador to Rwanda July 22, 2026. President Donald Trump has appointed a well-known diplomat in Africa, Nicholas 'Nick' Checker, to the position of US Ambassador to Rwanda.
excerpt: The announcement released by the Office of the President of the United States on July 21, 2026, shows that Nicholas Checker from the State of Wisconsin, is among the people appointed by the President to go to various positions of the State, but they must first be approved by…
title_en: President Trump appoints US Ambassador to Rwanda July 22, 2026. President Donald Trump has appointed a well-known diplomat in Africa, Nicholas 'Nick' Checker, to the position of US Ambassador to Rwanda.
excerpt_en: The announcement released by the Office of the President of the United States on July 21, 2026, shows that Nicholas Checker from the State of Wisconsin, is among the people appointed by the President to go to various positions of the State, but they must first be approved by…
body_en:
The announcement released by the Office of the President of the United States on July 21, 2026, shows that Nicholas Checker from the State of Wisconsin, is among the people appointed by the President to go to various positions of the State, but they must first be approved by the Senate.
Among those presented to the Senate, Nicholas Checker was asked to be the Ambassador representing the United States of America in Rwanda.
While the US Senate will confirm him, Checker will be given the task of representing his country in Kigali, where he will be responsible for continuing to develop relations between Rwanda and the United States of America.
Normally, the US Ambassador to another country is appointed by the President of the United States, but must first be confirmed by the Senate before starting his duties.
Checker was previously the US State Department Director of Cooperation with South Africa and Foreign Aid.
From June 1 to July 18, 2026, he was the Director General of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in charge of cooperation with Africa.
He served as Deputy Executive Secretary of the United States Security Council; He became a CIA agent from 2014 to 2025, where he oversaw security in the Middle East and the Horn of Africa.
When Rwandans began commemorating the 32nd Genocide against the Tutsis, on April 7, 2026, Checker was the first American leader to use the appropriate title of this history.
At that time, he said, "I myself visited Rwanda, and I saw with my own eyes the places where the Genocide took place, in Nyamata and Ntarama, where the churches used to be, where thousands of Tutsis were brutally killed by extremists."
Ambassador Checker said that he stood in front of the altars of those churches, overcome by the gravity of what happened.
He said, "On the altar where the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass is offered, where the blood of Jesus is shown as the salvation of the world, the blood of innocent people in the Genocide against the Tutsis is mixed."
This diplomat pointed out that in order for the world not to experience Genocide again, countries are required to give justice to the survivors by prosecuting those who participated, and that the United States will continue to work with Rwanda to achieve this.
Ambassador Checker will replace Eric Kneedler who left Rwanda in January 2026. For the past six months, the US Embassy in Kigali was headed by Chargé d'Affaires John Armiger.

title: What Bill Gates saw at the Mwulire Health Center On July 21, 2026, American financier Bill Gates, founder and Chairman of the Board of the Gates Foundation, visited the health facilities in Rwamagana District, praising the way Rwanda uses medical technology and the way pregnant mothers are monitored.
excerpt: Bill Gates arrived in Rwamagana District on Monday with the Minister of Health, Dr Sabin Nsanzimana, the Governor of Eastern Province, Pudence Rubingisa, the Mayor of Rwamagana District, Mbonyumuvunyi Radjab and various others. It is a visit he made with the aim of seeing the…
title_en: What Bill Gates saw at the Mwulire Health Center On July 21, 2026, American financier Bill Gates, founder and Chairman of the Board of the Gates Foundation, visited the health facilities in Rwamagana District, praising the way Rwanda uses medical technology and the way pregnant mothers are monitored.
excerpt_en: Bill Gates arrived in Rwamagana District on Monday with the Minister of Health, Dr Sabin Nsanzimana, the Governor of Eastern Province, Pudence Rubingisa, the Mayor of Rwamagana District, Mbonyumuvunyi Radjab and various others. It is a visit he made with the aim of seeing the…
body_en:
Bill Gates arrived in Rwamagana District on Monday with the Minister of Health, Dr Sabin Nsanzimana, the Governor of Eastern Province, Pudence Rubingisa, the Mayor of Rwamagana District, Mbonyumuvunyi Radjab and various others.
It is a visit he made with the aim of seeing the progress Rwanda has made in improving health. He visited a factory that manufactures needles that are exported to several African countries, and visited the Mwulire Health Center and met with health advisors.
The director of Mwulire Health Center, Ingabire Mediatrice, told IGIHE that the businessman said that he was first told about the history of Mwulire Health Center, the service it provides and the people who receive it.
He said that they visit the technology that they use to treat them, from the reception point of the patient to the health center, they show him how to enter the technology using the ID, and he is sent to the service that brought him.
He said, "After we showed him the service where we start medication for a person who has already been treated, he was explained how we get the medication from a treated person and how we give it to him. We then went to the laboratory and showed him where we take the tests."
Ingabire went on to say that they took her to a place where pregnant women are examined, it is shown how the child is monitored from the first month where the mother is examined eight times until she gives birth.
He said, "He appreciated how clean our health center is, he appreciated the way we use technology in medicine, every service he went to asked the doctors what is the point of not using paper anymore but using technology for everything. He was happy about it and praised Rwanda for using technology in medicine and how it helps to speed up services.''
Mwulire Health Center started in 2014 as a primary health center and in 2023 many buildings were built so that the primary health center became a health center. Every day they receive at least 90 patients while in a month they have more than 2240 patients from Mwulire Sector.
Bill Gates is shown Rwanda's progress in using AI in healthcare, July 21, 2026. Billionaire Bill Gates, who is in Rwanda on a visit to see the progress made in health promotion activities, visited the National Health Information Center (NHIC), where he was shown how the data collected continues to improve the healthcare sector across the country.
Bill Gates visited the center on July 21, 2026, and was received by the Minister of Health, Dr. Nsanzimana Sabin and the Minister of Technology and Innovation, Ingabire Paula, who showed him how data is collected in the health sector from the village level and while continuing to improve the healthcare sector across the country.
Since the center was launched last year, it has brought together all the country's health-related data, helping to transform health policies into practical actions to deliver the necessary results and quickly.
Bill Gates was shown how this technology has reduced the time patients spent waiting in lines to receive medical services.
This technology helps to manage and track emergency medical services dispatched to health emergencies in a timely manner.
Among other things, this technology has strengthened the ability to monitor and prevent epidemics.
NHIC's partnership with the Gates Foundation will further enable this institution to continue to expand its operations and capabilities in providing early warning information on epidemics, on issues that require urgent attention and prevent health problems before they escalate.
Other benefits include the effective use of modern technology and the integration of information at the national level of health.
Bill Gates has been in Rwanda since July 20, 2026, on a visit aimed at reviewing the progress made in health promotion activities.
He first visited a syringe factory located in Rwamagana District. He visited the Mwulire Health Center and one of the health consultants to understand the functioning of the health sector from the village level.
The projects Gates visited in Rwanda are among those that the Gates Foundation, of which he is the Chairman of the Board, already supports.

title: Construction of Kivu Belt Water Supply System Completed On July 21, 2026, the Ministry of Infrastructure announced that the construction of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System has been completed and has begun supplying water to residents in Bwishyura and Rubengera Sectors in Karongi District.
excerpt: Mininfra announced that the completion of the plant will help provide clean water to various parts of the Western Province. The plant has a water treatment capacity of 13,000 cubic meters. The completed part of the plant is the first phase of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System…
title_en: Construction of Kivu Belt Water Supply System Completed On July 21, 2026, the Ministry of Infrastructure announced that the construction of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System has been completed and has begun supplying water to residents in Bwishyura and Rubengera Sectors in Karongi District.
excerpt_en: Mininfra announced that the completion of the plant will help provide clean water to various parts of the Western Province. The plant has a water treatment capacity of 13,000 cubic meters. The completed part of the plant is the first phase of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System…
body_en:
Mininfra announced that the completion of the plant will help provide clean water to various parts of the Western Province.
The plant has a water treatment capacity of 13,000 cubic meters.
The completed part of the plant is the first phase of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System project that will, when completed, provide clean water to over 130,000 residents.
The message reads: “In addition to providing clean water to households, the project will improve service delivery to health facilities, schools, hotels, commercial centers, and other government institutions, in line with supporting public health and economic development.”
Rwanda says it is committed to providing safe water to Rwandans and ensuring sustainable access to clean water, sanitation and hygiene for all Rwandans.
The Rwandan government recently announced that in a move to address the problem of insufficient clean water reaching the population, 688,000 metric tons of clean water will be processed by 2029.
WASAC indicates that at least 1,234 metric tons of wastewater are processed daily by existing plants but are not available due to aging plants.
Among the efforts being made are the expansion and rehabilitation of infrastructure and water pipes, with the aim of reducing water leakage before it reaches the population to 25% by 2029 from the current 35%.

title: The cost of building the Rwanda Nuclear Research Center has been reduced by $300 million, July 22, 2026. The Director General of the Rwanda Atomic Energy Agency, Dr. Fidel Ndahayo, said that the cost of building the Center for Nuclear Science and Technology (CNST) has been reduced from $800 million to $500 million after various analyses.
excerpt: He reiterated this on July 21, 2026, when members of the IAEA’s Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review Mission for Research Reactors (INIR-RR) concluded their visit to Rwanda. The INIR-RR mission aims to assess Rwanda’s progress in developing infrastructure for research…
title_en: The cost of building the Rwanda Nuclear Research Center has been reduced by $300 million, July 22, 2026. The Director General of the Rwanda Atomic Energy Agency, Dr. Fidel Ndahayo, said that the cost of building the Center for Nuclear Science and Technology (CNST) has been reduced from $800 million to $500 million after various analyses.
excerpt_en: He reiterated this on July 21, 2026, when members of the IAEA’s Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review Mission for Research Reactors (INIR-RR) concluded their visit to Rwanda. The INIR-RR mission aims to assess Rwanda’s progress in developing infrastructure for research…
body_en:
He reiterated this on July 21, 2026, when members of the IAEA’s Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review Mission for Research Reactors (INIR-RR) concluded their visit to Rwanda.
The INIR-RR mission aims to assess Rwanda’s progress in developing infrastructure for research based on nuclear technology.
From July 13 to 21, 2026, IAEA experts conducted an inspection to determine whether Rwanda met the requirements to build a nuclear research and development center.
The Director General of RAEB, Dr. Fidele Ndahayo, said that the inspection was successful because they found that Rwanda met the requirements to build this center.
He said, “They found that we met the requirements in the first phase of building the research center.”
He continued by saying that the second phase that will follow is about signing agreements with other research centers, universities and others to complete it with experts to work there.
He said that once this is completed, the construction of this center will begin because the site has been found, but he did not announce when construction work will begin.
On October 30, 2024, Rwanda approved a study worth $800 million to build this facility, which will be located in the Eastern Province, Bugesera District.
Dr. Ndahayo said that after approving the study, they conducted research and analysis on the construction of this facility and found that it would cost a lot of money, and ended up cutting it by $300 million.
He said, “After discussing and conducting various analyses, looking at similar facilities that have been built, we found that the costs could be reduced to $500 million.”

This ‘reactor’ will have the capacity to generate 400 kilowatts of energy. This energy produces radiation that makes research more effective.

This center will also include a pharmaceutical factory that will help diagnose and treat many diseases that previously required medical treatment outside the country, and another part of the laboratories that will be used for various activities.
There will also be a section dedicated to training, where those who will receive it will be prepared to work in another center to be built, which will generate electricity from nuclear energy

excerpt: The awarding ceremony took place at the Presidential Palace in Bangui, on July 21, 2026. It was attended by senior officials in the Central African Government, the Rwandan Ambassador to the Central African Republic, Olivier Kayumba, senior military officials, and Rwandans…
title_en: President Touadéra awards medals to Rwandan soldiers July 22, 2026, the President of the Central African Republic, Faustin Archange Touadéra, awarded medals of commendation to Rwandan soldiers of the RWANBATT-15 team, after completing a year in the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Central African Republic.
excerpt_en: The awarding ceremony took place at the Presidential Palace in Bangui, on July 21, 2026. It was attended by senior officials in the Central African Government, the Rwandan Ambassador to the Central African Republic, Olivier Kayumba, senior military officials, and Rwandans…
body_en:
The awarding ceremony took place at the Presidential Palace in Bangui, on July 21, 2026. It was attended by senior officials in the Central African Government, the Rwandan Ambassador to the Central African Republic, Olivier Kayumba, senior military officials, and Rwandans living in the country.
The Rwandan Ministry of Defense announced that the medals were awarded to these soldiers in recognition of their dedication, professionalism, and successful fulfillment of their duties while serving in the MINUSCA mission in the Central African Republic.
During their time on the mission, RWANBATT-15 soldiers played a significant role in protecting civilians and promoting peace, security and stability in the Central African Republic.
The award, known as the Presidential Medal of Appreciation, is a token of appreciation from President Touadéra for the work Rwandan soldiers have done in peacekeeping operations and assisting the people of the Central African Republic.
The Commander of the 15th Battalion, Lt Col Paul Gasasira, thanked the President of the Central African Republic for the continued support he has given to the Battalion in carrying out its missions. He also praised the professionalism, good conduct and dedication of the RWANBATT-15 soldiers throughout their time on the mission.
Rwanda has been collaborating with the United Nations in peacekeeping operations in the Central African Republic for years, through the mission called MINUSCA (United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic) to help restore peace, security and stability in the country.

title: AI to be used in the treatment of pregnant mothers in Rwanda, 22 July 2026. The Ministry of Health has launched the use of ‘Telemedicine’ technology that uses artificial intelligence ‘AI’ in order to reduce maternal and newborn deaths and improve medical services.
excerpt: On July 21, 2026, this technology was launched at Nemba Hospital located in Gakenke District and is expected to be extended to different parts of the country. This technology will be used when a pregnant mother has a problem that may require her to go to a higher hospital for…
title_en: AI to be used in the treatment of pregnant mothers in Rwanda, 22 July 2026. The Ministry of Health has launched the use of ‘Telemedicine’ technology that uses artificial intelligence ‘AI’ in order to reduce maternal and newborn deaths and improve medical services.
excerpt_en: On July 21, 2026, this technology was launched at Nemba Hospital located in Gakenke District and is expected to be extended to different parts of the country. This technology will be used when a pregnant mother has a problem that may require her to go to a higher hospital for…
body_en:
On July 21, 2026, this technology was launched at Nemba Hospital located in Gakenke District and is expected to be extended to different parts of the country.
This technology will be used when a pregnant mother has a problem that may require her to go to a higher hospital for treatment.
In this case, the obstetrician treating her will use this ‘Telemedicine’ technology to communicate with a specialist doctor to explain the patient’s problem and then tell him how to care for him without requiring the patient to be referred to other hospitals.
A doctor at Nemba Hospital, Uwacu Mudusa Ghislain, explained how the technology works and what it will help them with.
He said, “I will wear a ‘camera’ so that I can tell it what I want to do and it will do it. This ‘camera’ will connect with a specialist doctor at the Ministry of Health so that he can help me with any problems I may have while treating a patient.” It will help us reduce the number of patients being referred to hospitals in Kigali to seek specialists.”
Ingabire Josiane told RBA that she went to the hospital with a stomach problem and they gave her basic treatment but it did not help and she continued to suffer. Later, with the help of this new method, she recovered.
He said, “They spoke to the specialists using technology and they helped me recover from my stomach. We are grateful to the Rwandan government for promoting technology because people get fast services and because we are treated by specialists, we trust that they are helping us.”
The Ministry of Health says the technology will be deployed in hospitals with high rates of maternal and neonatal mortality.
In Rwanda, statistics show that the hospital birth rate is 95%, maternal mortality is 203 per 100,000 women, and neonatal mortality is 19 per 1,000 children, under-five mortality is 45 per 1,000 children, and infant mortality is 33 per 1,000 live births.
body_fr:
On July 21, 2026, this technology was launched at Nemba Hospital located in Gakenke District and is expected to be extended to different parts of the country.
This technology will be used when a pregnant mother has a problem that may require her to go to a higher hospital for treatment.
In this case, the obstetrician treating her will use this ‘Telemedicine’ technology to communicate with a specialist doctor to explain the patient’s problem and then tell him how to care for him without requiring the patient to be referred to other hospitals.
A doctor at Nemba Hospital, Uwacu Mudusa Ghislain, explained how the technology works and what it will help them with.
He said, “I will wear a ‘camera’ so that I can tell it what I want to do and it will do it. This ‘camera’ will connect with a specialist doctor at the Ministry of Health so that he can help me with any problems I may have while treating a patient.” It will help us reduce the number of patients being referred to hospitals in Kigali to seek specialists.”
Ingabire Josiane told RBA that she went to the hospital with a stomach problem and they gave her basic treatment but it did not help and she continued to suffer. Later, with the help of this new method, she recovered.
He said, “They spoke to the specialists using technology and they helped me recover from my stomach. We are grateful to the Rwandan government for promoting technology because people get fast services and because we are treated by specialists, we trust that they are helping us.”
The Ministry of Health says the technology will be deployed in hospitals with high rates of maternal and neonatal mortality.
In Rwanda, statistics show that the hospital birth rate is 95%, maternal mortality is 203 per 100,000 women, and neonatal mortality is 19 per 1,000 children, under-five mortality is 45 per 1,000 children, and infant mortality is 33 per 1,000 live births.

KARONGI, Rwanda, July 21, 2026 - The first phase of the Kivu Belt Water Supply System was completed and began supplying Bwishyura and Rubengera sectors in Karongi District, the Ministry of Infrastructure said.

The plant has a treatment capacity of 13,000 cubic metres. Once the wider project is complete, it is expected to serve more than 130,000 residents as well as health facilities, schools, hotels, commercial centres and public institutions.

Authorities aim to reduce network leakage from about 35% to 25% by 2029.

title_en: Fear After Nyakunde Clashes Continues to Slow Ebola Response

body_en:
Nyakunde, July 20, 2026 - Six days after armed clashes around Nyakunde, about 45 kilometres southwest of Bunia, economic and health activities were gradually restarting, but Ebola treatment-centre attendance remained low and some medical staff had not returned.

Fighting on July 15 between soldiers and FPIC militia after the death of the militia’s chief displaced residents and disrupted response work in Irumu Territory.

UNADI said four escaped Ebola patients were brought back by families, while FPIC reaffirmed commitment to the Aru II accords. Civil society later welcomed a gradual return of humanitarian actors to Nyakunde as essential to slowing the outbreak’s advance.
