title: Opposition Suspends Kinshasa March and Sets August 15 Dialogue Deadline
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 20, 2026 - The C64 opposition coalition postponed its planned July 22 demonstration in Kinshasa after appeals from CENCO and the ECC, while demanding that President Tshisekedi formally convene the national dialogue before August 15. Failing that deadline, the…
title_en: Opposition Suspends Kinshasa March and Sets August 15 Dialogue Deadline
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 20, 2026 - The C64 opposition coalition postponed its planned July 22 demonstration in Kinshasa after appeals from CENCO and the ECC, while demanding that President Tshisekedi formally convene the national dialogue before August 15.
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 20, 2026 - The C64 opposition coalition postponed its planned July 22 demonstration in Kinshasa after appeals from CENCO and the ECC, while demanding that President Tshisekedi formally convene the national dialogue before August 15.

Failing that deadline, the coalition said it would resume street action. Religious mediators told opposition interlocutors that no subject should be excluded in advance and that participants should help define the agenda.

Government messaging continued to refer to a presidential ordinance setting organisational rules, while church representatives emphasised a hybrid format mixing elements of the presidency’s earlier proposal and CENCO’s approach.

ECC spokesperson Éric Nsenga said no actor should be placed in a posture of exclusion, though contacts with some platforms, including Sauvons la RDC, had not yet taken place.

title: Rwandans in Turkey Mark Liberation Anniversary Through Sport and Dialogue
excerpt: ANKARA, Turkey, July 18, 2026 - Rwandans in Turkey, joined by friends and partners, marked the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda’s liberation with sport, discussion and cultural performances, emphasizing the responsibility to preserve national gains and continue development. The…
title_en: Rwandans in Turkey Mark Liberation Anniversary Through Sport and Dialogue
excerpt_en: ANKARA, Turkey, July 18, 2026 - Rwandans in Turkey, joined by friends and partners, marked the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda’s liberation with sport, discussion and cultural performances, emphasizing the responsibility to preserve national gains and continue development. The…
body_en:
ANKARA, Turkey, July 18, 2026 - Rwandans in Turkey, joined by friends and partners, marked the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda’s liberation with sport, discussion and cultural performances, emphasizing the responsibility to preserve national gains and continue development.
The programme, postponed from July 4 because international conferences disrupted embassy programming in Ankara, included cycling, walking and table-tennis contests. Umut Akçaoğlu won the cycling race, ahead of Camille Niyonkuru and Pascal Nshuti; Lea Mujawimana won the running race, ahead of Rulisa Briella and Laurence Uwonkunda Kayitare; and Ambassador Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Charles Kayonga won the table-tennis contest, followed by Nicole Cyuzuzo.
Kayonga moderated a discussion with Military Attaché Col. Jean Paul Rulisa, Capt. Claudette Nishimwe, Commercial Affairs Officer Murenzi Lucas and Dr. Faustin Hategekimana. He said the RPA’s July 4, 1994 victory ended the regime that planned and carried out the Genocide against the Tutsi, while reconstruction, economic development and improvements in living standards remain continuing work. Students graduating from Turkish universities were recognized and urged to use their skills for Rwanda’s development.

Ambassador Sheikh Abdul Karim Harelimana said Rwanda’s progress rested on leadership, unity and the collective will to rebuild after the Genocide against the Tutsi.

title: Tayebwa Calls on OACPS States to Prioritise Value Addition and End Raw Mineral Exports
excerpt: BRUSSELS, July 17, 2026 - Uganda’s Deputy Speaker of Parliament and President of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS) Parliamentary Assembly, Thomas Tayebwa, has urged member states to place trade, industrialisation, and value addition at the…
title_en: Tayebwa Calls on OACPS States to Prioritise Value Addition and End Raw Mineral Exports
excerpt_en: BRUSSELS, July 17, 2026 - Uganda’s Deputy Speaker of Parliament and President of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS) Parliamentary Assembly, Thomas Tayebwa, has urged member states to place trade, industrialisation, and value addition at the…
body_en:
BRUSSELS, July 17, 2026 - Uganda’s Deputy Speaker of Parliament and President of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS) Parliamentary Assembly, Thomas Tayebwa, has urged member states to place trade, industrialisation, and value addition at the centre of their development strategies.
Addressing the 121st OACPS Council of Ministers at the Egmont Palace in Brussels, Tayebwa said the organisation’s future relevance would depend on its ability to advance practical economic policies that improve citizens’ livelihoods, create jobs, strengthen industries, and help countries benefit more from their natural resources.
He identified the continued export of unprocessed minerals as one of the biggest challenges facing Africa and other developing regions, arguing that countries must move away from exporting raw materials while importing finished products.
Tayebwa said the issue, which has also been repeatedly highlighted by President Yoweri Museveni, requires urgent action to ensure African countries capture more value from their resources.
“I think at the level of the Council of Ministers, we need to start tackling the hard questions relevant to our people. One of them is... the issue of Africa and the developing world exporting unprocessed minerals as raw materials,” Tayebwa said.
He noted that Africa possesses an estimated US$29.5 trillion in mineral wealth, representing about 20 percent of global mineral resources, yet continues to lose significant economic opportunities because much of its minerals are exported in raw or minimally processed form.
According to Tayebwa, the current model allows external economies to benefit more from Africa’s resources by processing raw materials into higher-value products, while African countries miss out on industrial growth, employment opportunities, and increased revenues.
He cited the Democratic Republic of Congo’s cobalt sector as an example of how domestic processing can increase economic returns, saying the experience demonstrates the importance of mineral beneficiation and industrial development.
Tayebwa also highlighted the coffee value chain as another example of the imbalance between producers and global markets. He referenced President Museveni’s argument that commodity-producing countries often receive only a small share of the final value generated from their products.
“I remember my President gave us some feedback... the coffee market was worth around US$465 billion and out of that only US$25 billion was going to the coffee-producing countries, with Africa taking only 3%,” Tayebwa said.
He warned that unless OACPS countries focus on issues directly affecting ordinary citizens, the organisation risks losing its relevance.
“If we don't tackle such issues, then the organisation will not be relevant to our people... We should look at topics that do speak to the hearts of our people, that do speak to the transformation of our people,” he said.
The OACPS brings together 79 countries from Africa, the Caribbean, and the Pacific to promote cooperation in trade, sustainable development, and political dialogue.
Tayebwa said the bloc should use its collective influence to promote policies that encourage value addition, industrialisation, and regional integration, enabling member states to create jobs, increase revenues, and accelerate economic transformation.
Economy and Tech.

PARIS, July 17, 2026 - The appeal of Eugène Rwamucyo, sentenced to 27 years for complicity in genocide and crimes against humanity, concluded after hearings from June 8 to July 17, confirming the October 30, 2024 judgment.

Civil-parties lawyer André Martin Karongozi said disruptions, threats and online allegations against lawyers marked the proceedings. He said supporters interrupted survivor testimony, prompting a temporary suspension and later tighter security.

Rwamucyo was convicted for crimes in Ngoma, Gishamvu, Ndora and Huye in the former Butare Prefecture.

title: Museveni Grants Official Burial to Former North West Tooro MP Kosia Mudabi Ngirisi
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - President Yoweri Museveni has granted an official burial to former North West Tooro Member of Parliament Kosia Mudabi Ngirisi in recognition of his decades of service as a legislator, civil servant, and local government leader. The decision was…
title_en: Museveni Grants Official Burial to Former North West Tooro MP Kosia Mudabi Ngirisi
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - President Yoweri Museveni has granted an official burial to former North West Tooro Member of Parliament Kosia Mudabi Ngirisi in recognition of his decades of service as a legislator, civil servant, and local government leader. The decision was…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - President Yoweri Museveni has granted an official burial to former North West Tooro Member of Parliament Kosia Mudabi Ngirisi in recognition of his decades of service as a legislator, civil servant, and local government leader.
The decision was announced by Minister for the Presidency Milly Babirye Babalanda, who said Ngirisi passed away on July 10 at Buhinga Hospital in Fort Portal City.
Babalanda said President Museveni approved the official burial in accordance with Article 99 of the 1995 Constitution of Uganda, which grants executive authority to the President.
“His Excellency Yoweri Kaguta Museveni, in accordance with Article 99 of the Constitution of the Republic of Uganda (1995) as amended, has directed that the late Hon. Kosia Mudabi Ngirisi be accorded an official burial,” Babalanda said.
Born on March 15, 1933, in Hakitengya Parish, Tokwe Sub County, Bundibugyo District, Ngirisi entered Parliament in 1962 as the representative for North West Tooro Constituency.
He served in Uganda’s Second Parliament until 1971, when the government of President Milton Obote was overthrown by Idi Amin.
Before joining Parliament, Ngirisi worked as a Cooperative Assistant with the Bwamba-Rwenzori Cooperative Union and served on the Tooro District Council.

title: Government to Brief Parliament on Treaties, Roads and Electricity Access Progress
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The government is set to present three key statements to Parliament next week covering Uganda’s international treaty commitments, the state of the country’s road network, and progress in expanding electricity access through the Electricity Access…
title_en: Government to Brief Parliament on Treaties, Roads and Electricity Access Progress
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The government is set to present three key statements to Parliament next week covering Uganda’s international treaty commitments, the state of the country’s road network, and progress in expanding electricity access through the Electricity Access…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The government is set to present three key statements to Parliament next week covering Uganda’s international treaty commitments, the state of the country’s road network, and progress in expanding electricity access through the Electricity Access Scale-up Project (EASP).
The updates will be presented during parliamentary sittings scheduled for July 21 to 23, 2026, following a communication from Prime Minister Robinah Nabbanja in her capacity as Leader of Government Business.
In a letter dated July 16, Nabbanja outlined the government’s planned business for the upcoming parliamentary week, in line with parliamentary procedures requiring updates on government agenda and activities.
The Minister of Foreign Affairs is expected to table a report detailing treaties, protocols, and international agreements ratified or acceded to by Uganda between 2021 and 2025.
The Minister of Works and Transport will also present a comprehensive statement on the condition of roads across the country, providing lawmakers with an update on ongoing infrastructure development and challenges affecting the transport sector.
Meanwhile, the Minister of Energy and Mineral Development will brief Parliament on the implementation progress of the Electricity Access Scale-up Project, which aims to increase electricity connectivity and improve access to power across Uganda.
The ministerial statements are expected to give Members of Parliament an opportunity to assess government performance in key sectors, including infrastructure development, energy access, and international cooperation.
Following the presentations, lawmakers will scrutinise the reports, debate the issues raised, and make recommendations on areas requiring further government action.

title: Museveni Links Uganda’s Industrial Growth to Reliable Markets and Local Production
excerpt: KISOZI, July 16, 2026 — President Yoweri Museveni has said guaranteed markets are essential for expanding production and accelerating Uganda’s industrial growth, arguing that farmers can supply agro-processing industries if they are assured of stable demand. Speaking during…
title_en: Museveni Links Uganda’s Industrial Growth to Reliable Markets and Local Production
excerpt_en: KISOZI, July 16, 2026 — President Yoweri Museveni has said guaranteed markets are essential for expanding production and accelerating Uganda’s industrial growth, arguing that farmers can supply agro-processing industries if they are assured of stable demand. Speaking during…
body_en:
KISOZI, July 16, 2026 — President Yoweri Museveni has said guaranteed markets are essential for expanding production and accelerating Uganda’s industrial growth, arguing that farmers can supply agro-processing industries if they are assured of stable demand.
Speaking during the commissioning of the National Enterprise Corporation (NEC) Meat and Beans Processing Plant in Kisozi, Gomba District, Museveni described the facility as a major step in Uganda’s industrialisation agenda, promoting value addition and strategic self-reliance.
The plant, established through a partnership between NEC and businessman Francis Ragwa, will process canned beef and beans for domestic consumption and export markets.
Museveni said Uganda already possesses the production capacity needed to support the facility but noted that the key challenge has been organising farmers and creating reliable markets for their products.
He pointed to the growth of the coffee and dairy sectors as examples of how market-driven production can transform industries and improve economic opportunities.
“Once I am sure about the market, I can mobilise Ugandans to produce because the economics are correct. The stimulus for production is the market,” Museveni said.
The President highlighted Uganda’s expanding cattle population, which has grown from about three million in 1986 to more than 16 million, as evidence of the country’s ability to support a thriving meat-processing industry through both commercial and small-scale farmers.
He urged stakeholders to develop effective production models that ensure farmers directly benefit from value addition opportunities.
Museveni also praised NEC and its partners for completing the project despite challenges, including delays linked to the Covid-19 pandemic.
Minister of Defence and Veteran Affairs Kiryowa Kiwanuka described the facility as an important milestone in Uganda’s pursuit of industrialisation and self-sufficiency. He said the country has historically relied on imported operational rations, including canned beef and beans, but the new plant would help reduce that dependence.
“With this plant, the UPDF is transitioning towards self-sufficiency,” Kiwanuka said, adding that the ministry would prioritise procurement from the facility and encourage other government institutions to support locally manufactured products.
NEC Managing Director Lt Gen James Mugira said the project was initiated in 2019 with the goal of establishing a beef and beans processing plant alongside a tin can manufacturing facility.
He said the factory would support import substitution by producing canned food products locally, reducing government spending on imported rations for the Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF), Uganda Police Force, and Uganda Prisons Service.
Mugira added that local production would strengthen national food security and reduce risks associated with global supply chain disruptions.
Francis Ragwa, Managing Director of NEC Meat and Beans Processing Plant, said extensive research and international benchmarking guided the development of the facility. He called for Uganda’s Ankole cattle to be positioned as a premium global brand by moving beyond selling beef as a basic commodity.
“We can no longer sell beef simply as a commodity. We must tell our story and market the uniqueness of Uganda’s cattle heritage,” Ragwa said.

title: Uganda Parliament Orders Restoration of MPs’ Reserved Parking Spaces
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Uganda’s Parliament is set to restore designated parking spaces reserved for Members of Parliament after concerns were raised over the conversion of some parking bays into storage areas, causing congestion and limiting access to the parliamentary…
title_en: Uganda Parliament Orders Restoration of MPs’ Reserved Parking Spaces
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Uganda’s Parliament is set to restore designated parking spaces reserved for Members of Parliament after concerns were raised over the conversion of some parking bays into storage areas, causing congestion and limiting access to the parliamentary…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Uganda’s Parliament is set to restore designated parking spaces reserved for Members of Parliament after concerns were raised over the conversion of some parking bays into storage areas, causing congestion and limiting access to the parliamentary precincts.
The directive was issued by Speaker Jacob Marksons Oboth Oboth during a plenary sitting after Kalungu West MP Joseph Gonzaga Ssewungu informed the House that several parking spaces allocated to legislators had been repurposed for storage.
Ssewungu told Parliament that the changes had created difficulties for lawmakers seeking parking facilities within the parliamentary premises, affecting convenience and access to the House.
In response, Speaker Oboth Oboth instructed the Clerk to Parliament to take immediate action to restore the affected parking spaces to their original purpose.
“Let’s go back to what those parking spaces were meant for,” the Speaker said, emphasizing that the bays were specifically designated to support Members of Parliament and should not be used for storage or other activities.
Parliamentary staff have since been directed to remove stored items from the affected areas and relocate them to approved storage facilities within the parliamentary premises.
The decision was welcomed by several legislators, who said restoring the reserved parking spaces would help reduce congestion, improve accessibility, and strengthen order and security within Parliament.

title: Uganda Seeks to Host 2027 OACPS-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Uganda has formally expressed interest in hosting the 2027 Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States-European Union (OACPS-EU) Joint Parliamentary Assembly, as the country moves to strengthen parliamentary diplomacy and cooperation with…
title_en: Uganda Seeks to Host 2027 OACPS-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Uganda has formally expressed interest in hosting the 2027 Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States-European Union (OACPS-EU) Joint Parliamentary Assembly, as the country moves to strengthen parliamentary diplomacy and cooperation with…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Uganda has formally expressed interest in hosting the 2027 Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States-European Union (OACPS-EU) Joint Parliamentary Assembly, as the country moves to strengthen parliamentary diplomacy and cooperation with international partners.
The proposal was presented by Deputy Speaker of Parliament Thomas Tayebwa during a bilateral meeting with Francisco Assis, his co-president of the OACPS-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly, at the Egmont Palace in Brussels, Belgium.
During the meeting, Tayebwa invited Assis to visit the East African region and proposed Uganda as the venue for the 2027 session of the joint assembly.
The two leaders also discussed the ratification and implementation of the Samoa Agreement, a 20-year framework governing relations between the European Union and the 79 member states of the OACPS.
The agreement provides a platform for cooperation in areas including trade, human rights, climate action, migration, sustainable development, and economic partnerships.
“As Co-Presidents, we pledged to continue working together and exchanged views on strengthening cooperation between the European Union and the nations of Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific from a parliamentary perspective,” Tayebwa said.
Tayebwa was accompanied by Uganda’s Ambassador to the European Union, Mirjam Blaak.
The OACPS-EU Joint Parliamentary Assembly brings together lawmakers from EU member states and OACPS countries to discuss political, economic, social, and development issues affecting the two regions.
Uganda’s bid to host the 2027 assembly highlights its growing emphasis on parliamentary diplomacy and its efforts to deepen engagement with European and ACP partners.
If selected, hosting the meeting would give Uganda an opportunity to showcase its role in regional and international parliamentary cooperation while providing a platform for dialogue on shared priorities between the EU and OACPS member states.

title: High Court Orders Production of Erias Lukwago for Treason-Related Trial
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 — The High Court in Kampala has ordered authorities at Luzira Upper Prison to produce former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago in court next week as he faces charges of misprision of treason. A production warrant issued by the High Court Criminal…
title_en: High Court Orders Production of Erias Lukwago for Treason-Related Trial
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 — The High Court in Kampala has ordered authorities at Luzira Upper Prison to produce former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago in court next week as he faces charges of misprision of treason. A production warrant issued by the High Court Criminal…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 — The High Court in Kampala has ordered authorities at Luzira Upper Prison to produce former Kampala Lord Mayor Erias Lukwago in court next week as he faces charges of misprision of treason.
A production warrant issued by the High Court Criminal Division on July 16 directs Luzira Upper Prison authorities to present Lukwago before Justice David Matovu on July 24, 2026, at 10:00am.
The warrant was issued in Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. HCT-00-CR-CM-0261-2026, where Lukwago is listed as the applicant and the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) as the respondent.
The Officer in Charge of Luzira Upper Prison has been instructed to ensure Lukwago’s attendance before the court on the scheduled date.
The development followed a decision by Makindye Chief Magistrate Sarah Basemera to commit Lukwago to the High Court for trial over charges of misprision of treason.
Prosecution alleges that Lukwago, who also leads the People’s Front for Freedom (PFF), failed to report information about an alleged plan to overthrow the government by force of arms despite allegedly being aware of the plot.
The state claims the alleged offence occurred between January and June 2026.
Lukwago has denied the allegations, maintaining his innocence.
The case will now proceed before the High Court, where further guidance on the trial process is expected during the July 24 hearing.

title: Salam TV Chief Pays Tribute to Qatar’s Late Father Amir at Kampala Embassy
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Salam TV Managing Director Hajji Karim Kaliisa has joined Ugandan leaders and members of the public in mourning Qatar’s late Father Amir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, following his death. Hajji Kaliisa paid his respects during a condolence…
title_en: Salam TV Chief Pays Tribute to Qatar’s Late Father Amir at Kampala Embassy
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Salam TV Managing Director Hajji Karim Kaliisa has joined Ugandan leaders and members of the public in mourning Qatar’s late Father Amir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, following his death. Hajji Kaliisa paid his respects during a condolence…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Salam TV Managing Director Hajji Karim Kaliisa has joined Ugandan leaders and members of the public in mourning Qatar’s late Father Amir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, following his death.
Hajji Kaliisa paid his respects during a condolence session held at the Qatar Embassy in Kampala, where he signed the official condolence book and conveyed his sympathies to the Qatari leadership, embassy staff, and the people of Qatar.
The session, held at Kampala Serena Hotel, followed the passing of Sheikh Hamad on July 12, 2026, at the age of 74. Hajji Kaliisa was received by Abdallah Al Jofairi, Chargé d’Affaires at the Qatar Embassy in Uganda, who represented Qatar’s Ambassador to Uganda, H.E. Ahmed bin Mohammed Alzowaidi.
In his condolence message, Hajji Kaliisa described Sheikh Hamad as a respected statesman whose leadership and contributions to Qatar’s development and the broader Muslim world would remain remembered.
He also offered prayers for the late Father Amir, asking Allah to grant him mercy, forgiveness, and a place in Jannah.
The Qatar Embassy in Kampala opened the condolence book to provide an opportunity for government officials, institutional leaders, and members of the public to pay their respects following Sheikh Hamad’s death.

The session, held at Kampala Serena Hotel, followed the passing of Sheikh Hamad on July 12, 2026, at the age of 74. Hajji Kaliisa was received by Abdallah Al Jofairi, Chargé d’Affaires at the Qatar Embassy in Uganda, who represented Qatar’s Ambassador to Uganda, H.E. Ahmed bin Mohammed Alzowaidi.

title: Mufti Mubaje Commits to Stronger Partnership Between UMSC and IUEA
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The Mufti of Uganda, Sheikh Shaban Ramadhan Mubaje, has pledged to strengthen cooperation between the Uganda Muslim Supreme Council (UMSC) and the International University of East Africa (IUEA), highlighting the importance of science, technology, and…
title_en: Mufti Mubaje Commits to Stronger Partnership Between UMSC and IUEA
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The Mufti of Uganda, Sheikh Shaban Ramadhan Mubaje, has pledged to strengthen cooperation between the Uganda Muslim Supreme Council (UMSC) and the International University of East Africa (IUEA), highlighting the importance of science, technology, and…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The Mufti of Uganda, Sheikh Shaban Ramadhan Mubaje, has pledged to strengthen cooperation between the Uganda Muslim Supreme Council (UMSC) and the International University of East Africa (IUEA), highlighting the importance of science, technology, and innovation in driving Uganda’s socio-economic transformation.
Speaking during a courtesy visit to the IUEA main campus in Kansanga, Kampala, Mubaje praised the university’s focus on practical education in fields including engineering, petroleum studies, mining, and electric motorcycle technology.
He said the partnership between UMSC and IUEA, which has supported scholarship opportunities for students, would be expanded to create more educational opportunities and promote skills development.
“I am delighted to return and find that what was once a place of recreation has become a centre of knowledge shaping the future of young people,” Mubaje said, referring to the campus site’s former use as Didi’s World amusement park.
The Mufti also commended the university’s multicultural environment, describing diversity as an important factor in promoting unity, mutual respect, and knowledge exchange among students from different backgrounds.
“Diversity is a blessing. I encourage students to embrace one another regardless of their backgrounds because education thrives where people learn from each other’s experiences,” he said.
Mubaje was accompanied by Deputy Mufti of Uganda Sheikh Muhammad Ali Waiswa and other senior officials from the Uganda Muslim Supreme Council.
The delegation was received by IUEA Vice Chancellor Prof. Emeka Akaezuwa and the university’s Resident Director, Ambassador Hassan Alwi.
Prof. Akaezuwa described IUEA as a technology-focused institution committed to producing graduates with practical and industry-relevant skills capable of meeting the demands of the modern labour market.
He said the university continues to build international partnerships aimed at strengthening teaching, research, and innovation while preparing students for global competitiveness.
During the visit, Mubaje toured the university’s lecture halls, laboratories, and library, where he interacted with students and staff to learn more about the institution’s academic programmes and learning environment.
The visit concluded with an exchange of commemorative gifts between UMSC and IUEA, followed by a luncheon hosted by the university management.
The renewed commitment to collaboration is expected to enhance educational opportunities for students while supporting Uganda’s broader efforts to develop expertise in science, technology, and innovation.

title: Egypt Restarts Scholarships for Ugandan Students After Years-Long Suspension
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Egypt has resumed its scholarship programme for Ugandan students after several years of suspension, with 23 students selected to pursue studies at the renowned Al-Azhar University in Cairo as the two countries strengthen cooperation in Islamic…
title_en: Egypt Restarts Scholarships for Ugandan Students After Years-Long Suspension
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Egypt has resumed its scholarship programme for Ugandan students after several years of suspension, with 23 students selected to pursue studies at the renowned Al-Azhar University in Cairo as the two countries strengthen cooperation in Islamic…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Egypt has resumed its scholarship programme for Ugandan students after several years of suspension, with 23 students selected to pursue studies at the renowned Al-Azhar University in Cairo as the two countries strengthen cooperation in Islamic education.
The announcement was made by Egypt’s Ambassador to Uganda, Monzer Selim, during a meeting with Uganda Muslim Supreme Council (UMSC) leadership at the council’s headquarters in Kampala.
Selim said the renewed scholarship programme represents a new phase of cooperation between Egypt and UMSC, adding that the first group of beneficiaries is expected to travel to Cairo on July 26, 2026, while another group will depart in September.
“The Egyptian Government has resumed offering scholarships to Ugandan students, and 23 students have already been selected to benefit from the programme,” the ambassador said.
The envoy also requested the Mufti of Uganda, Sheikh Shaban Ramadhan Mubaje, to nominate five imams from major mosques across the country for a refresher training programme at Al-Azhar University aimed at enhancing religious knowledge and leadership skills.
In addition, Selim invited Mubaje to attend an upcoming international Islamic conference in Egypt.
The ambassador also sought the Mufti’s support in resolving a land dispute affecting Kimanya Noor Islamic Learning Centre in Masaka District, an institution established in 1998 with Egyptian assistance and affiliated with Al-Azhar University.
Selim said the dispute emerged after the death of the original land donor, with some family members claiming ownership of the property. He noted that the disagreement has affected the institution’s operations and prevented Egyptian teachers from continuing their work.
Mubaje welcomed the return of the scholarship programme and expressed appreciation for Egypt’s continued support towards Islamic education in Uganda.
He described the relationship between UMSC and Egyptian institutions, particularly Al-Azhar University, as a long-standing partnership built on mutual benefit and cooperation.
Regarding the Kimanya Noor Islamic Learning Centre dispute, the Mufti directed the UMSC Education Secretary to organise a stakeholders’ meeting within two weeks to find an amicable and lasting solution.
“The meeting will seek an amicable and lasting solution to the ownership dispute and ensure the institution resumes normal operations,” Mubaje said.
The meeting was attended by Deputy Mufti Sheikh Muhammad Ali Waiswa, UMSC Secretary General Hajji Abbas Muluubya Ssekyanzi, UMSC Education Secretary Sheikh Juma Bakhit Cucu, and other senior officials.

title: Malian Military Delegation Hails Ugandan Pharmaceutical Plant as Model for Africa’s Self-Reliance
excerpt: MATUGGA, July 16, 2026 - A high-level military delegation from nine African countries has praised Uganda’s Dei BioPharma Ltd pharmaceutical manufacturing facility as a model for the continent’s pursuit of medicine and vaccine self-reliance. The delegation, composed of…
title_en: Malian Military Delegation Hails Ugandan Pharmaceutical Plant as Model for Africa’s Self-Reliance
excerpt_en: MATUGGA, July 16, 2026 - A high-level military delegation from nine African countries has praised Uganda’s Dei BioPharma Ltd pharmaceutical manufacturing facility as a model for the continent’s pursuit of medicine and vaccine self-reliance. The delegation, composed of…
body_en:
MATUGGA, July 16, 2026 - A high-level military delegation from nine African countries has praised Uganda’s Dei BioPharma Ltd pharmaceutical manufacturing facility as a model for the continent’s pursuit of medicine and vaccine self-reliance.
The delegation, composed of officers attending training at the Malian Army War College, visited the company’s drugs and vaccines manufacturing campus in Matugga on Wednesday as part of a strategic study tour hosted by the Uganda Peoples’ Defence Forces (UPDF) from July 13 to 17.
The visit was led by Brig. Gen. Moussa Yoro Kante, Director of Education of the Mali Defence Forces, who was accompanied by Mali’s Defence Attaché to Uganda, Col. Diallo Belco.
The 36-member delegation included military officers from Mali, Guinea Conakry, Burkina Faso, Niger, Morocco, Togo, Chad, Senegal, and Cameroon.
Speaking after the tour, Gen. Kante expressed appreciation for the scale and ambition of Dei BioPharma’s operations, describing the facility as an inspiring example of Africa’s capacity to develop advanced pharmaceutical industries.
“The visit this evening allowed us to see beautiful things. I would like to congratulate Dr. Magoola for everything he is doing in the field of biotechnology,” Gen. Kante said.
He added that the experience would be shared with the participating officers’ home countries as an example of Africa’s potential in pharmaceutical manufacturing.
“I hope that each of these trainees, upon returning home, will be able to bear witness to what we have seen here at Dei BioPharma,” he said.
Gen. Kante also invited Dr. Matthias Magoola, founder and Managing Director of Dei BioPharma, to explore opportunities to expand the company’s work across Africa.
Responding to the delegation’s remarks, Dr. Magoola said the visit demonstrated the growing importance of Uganda’s investment in biotechnology and pharmaceutical production.
He said many of the visiting officers had never encountered a facility of such scale on the continent, highlighting the strategic importance of developing local manufacturing capacity.
“This is not surprising, as only a few countries, such as Morocco and Egypt, have attempted to move into manufacturing. Some of the students are from those regions, yet you heard them say they have not seen anything like this elsewhere,” Magoola said.
Dr. Magoola also linked Uganda’s willingness to share pharmaceutical technology with other African countries to President Yoweri Museveni’s Pan-African vision.
He said African countries should work together to reduce dependence on imported medicines and vaccines.
“Africa does not need to depend on others for vaccine and drug manufacturing. I am operating in that spirit of Pan-Africanism that our president consistently emphasizes,” he said.
Addressing Africa’s continued reliance on imported medicines, Magoola identified limited technological capacity as the main challenge preventing local production.
“The problem is a lack of technology. Africa currently imports 85 percent of its medicine,” he said, adding that Dei BioPharma had developed its own innovations, secured patents in the United States, and built the capacity to manufacture vaccines and medicines locally.
He argued that expanding pharmaceutical production could transform Africa’s economy by improving access to affordable healthcare products while creating industrial opportunities.
“Our ultimate vision is to make these biological drugs, which 90 percent of our population currently cannot afford, accessible and affordable,” Magoola said.
Dei BioPharma Chief Executive Officer Dr. Chetna Jain said the visit reflected growing continental recognition of the company’s achievements.
“It shows that what we are doing here is being recognized across Africa. People are aware of Dei BioPharma, and they are willing to come here and collaborate with us after seeing what we have developed,” she said.
Established in 2014 by Ugandan scientist Dr. Matthias Magoola, Dei BioPharma operates one of Africa’s largest pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturing complexes. The facility was inaugurated in July 2021 by President Museveni and former Kenyan Deputy President William Ruto.
Located on more than 250 acres in Matugga, the campus includes multiple manufacturing units focused on biotechnology, injectables, generic medicines, nutraceuticals, oncology products, and vaccines.
The facility is designed to produce treatments for diseases including malaria, HIV, and cancer, as well as insulin, monoclonal antibodies, and mRNA-based therapeutics.
The National Drug Authority licensed Dei BioPharma in May 2024 to manufacture medicines, including non-beta-lactam tablets and hard gelatin capsules.
The company holds more than 100 patents filed with the United States Patent and Trademark Office and is preparing for large-scale mRNA vaccine production in line with international standards.
The facility is projected to create more than 40,000 professional jobs and has been identified by Ugandan authorities as a potential driver of industrial growth and reduced dependence on imported medicines.
The pharmaceutical tour formed part of wider military engagements between Uganda and Mali. During the visit, Ugandan defence officials highlighted ongoing cooperation between the two countries under a military training agreement, which has so far supported the training of 58 Malian officer cadets.
Gen. Kante also announced that Mali had offered Uganda 23 training opportunities, including a slot at the Mali War College, further strengthening defence cooperation between the two nations.

title: Uganda Suspends Land Deal Roles for Campaigning LC I Chairpersons
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development has temporarily restricted Local Council I (LC I) chairpersons seeking re-election from participating in land transactions until the conclusion of the upcoming village elections. The directive aims…
title_en: Uganda Suspends Land Deal Roles for Campaigning LC I Chairpersons
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development has temporarily restricted Local Council I (LC I) chairpersons seeking re-election from participating in land transactions until the conclusion of the upcoming village elections. The directive aims…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - The Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development has temporarily restricted Local Council I (LC I) chairpersons seeking re-election from participating in land transactions until the conclusion of the upcoming village elections.
The directive aims to prevent possible fraud, disputes, and irregularities during the campaign period ahead of the July 28 LC I chairperson elections.
In a public notice issued on Thursday, the ministry instructed campaigning LC I chairpersons to stop witnessing, endorsing, recommending, or overseeing land-related transactions until the electoral process is completed.
“The advisory has been issued as a precautionary measure to safeguard the integrity of land transactions during this transition period and to minimise the risk of disputes, fraud, or other irregularities that may arise,” the ministry stated.
The ministry advised members of the public against seeking land transaction services from LC I chairpersons who are actively campaigning, including verification of ownership, witnessing land sale agreements, resolving boundary disputes, or handling other administrative land matters.
Those with urgent land issues were encouraged to seek assistance from qualified legal practitioners or follow alternative lawful procedures until the elections are concluded.
The ministry said the temporary measure was intended to protect the interests of all parties involved and prevent costly mistakes during the transition period.
Land disputes remain a major source of conflict in Uganda, with local leaders often playing an important role in verifying ownership, confirming identities of sellers, identifying boundaries, and witnessing agreements at community level.
Although LC I chairpersons do not have the authority to transfer land ownership or issue official land titles, they are frequently relied upon because of their knowledge of local communities and land histories.
Legal experts have previously warned that LC I endorsements only provide community-level verification and do not replace formal legal procedures required under Uganda’s land laws. Buyers are still expected to conduct proper due diligence before completing land purchases.
According to the Electoral Commission roadmap, elections for Village (LC I) chairpersons will take place on July 28 across Uganda’s 71,214 villages, followed by Parish (LC II) chairperson elections on August 10.
The Ministry of Lands said LC I chairpersons will resume their normal role in land-related matters once the electoral process is concluded.

title: Speaker Oboth Promises Equal Support for Parliamentary Committees, Restricts Foreign Trips
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Speaker of Parliament Jacob Oboth-Oboth has pledged equal facilitation for all parliamentary committees and introduced new limits on foreign travel delegations as part of efforts to improve efficiency and control spending in the 12th Parliament. The…
title_en: Speaker Oboth Promises Equal Support for Parliamentary Committees, Restricts Foreign Trips
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Speaker of Parliament Jacob Oboth-Oboth has pledged equal facilitation for all parliamentary committees and introduced new limits on foreign travel delegations as part of efforts to improve efficiency and control spending in the 12th Parliament. The…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 16, 2026 - Speaker of Parliament Jacob Oboth-Oboth has pledged equal facilitation for all parliamentary committees and introduced new limits on foreign travel delegations as part of efforts to improve efficiency and control spending in the 12th Parliament.
The Speaker assured legislators that every parliamentary committee would receive equal support to effectively carry out its legislative, oversight, and accountability responsibilities.
The assurance came after concerns were raised by some Members of Parliament who complained about being assigned to committees they considered less prominent and lacking adequate resources.
“I have gotten complaints from some legislators on designating them to committees where their competencies don’t lie,” Speaker Oboth said during Thursday’s plenary sitting.
Oboth urged MPs to embrace their committee assignments, regardless of whether the roles directly match their areas of expertise, stressing that every committee contributes to Parliament’s work.
“All committees are equal and all will be facilitated equally to perform their work,” he said.
The Speaker emphasized that no committee should be viewed as more important than another and said Parliament’s administration would ensure consistent support across all committees.
During the sitting, logistical challenges affecting committee operations were also raised, with Local Government Accounts Committee Chairperson Betty Nambooze citing difficulties in accessing meeting rooms.
“We are failing to get rooms where to hold meetings,” Nambooze said.
In a separate announcement, Speaker Oboth introduced new restrictions on parliamentary foreign travel, reducing the size of delegations participating in international engagements.
He said that, with immediate effect, foreign trips would be limited to a maximum of six Members of Parliament and two staff members per delegation.
“All foreign trips have now been limited to only six MPs and two staff per trip. This has been done to cut on the costs Parliament has been spending on foreign trips,” Oboth said.
The Speaker said the measures are aimed at reducing expenditure while ensuring parliamentary committees receive sufficient resources to perform their oversight, legislative, and accountability duties effectively.

excerpt: Kinshasa, July 15, 2026 - The lawyers representing Senator and Deputy Quaestor of the Congolese Senate, Omana Bitika Pascal, have filed a legal complaint against journalist Gauthier Sey of Netic Television over reports alleging the senator’s involvement in a mining-related…
title_en: Senator Omana Bitika’s Legal Team Files Complaint Against Journalist Over Alleged Defamation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 15, 2026 - The lawyers representing Senator and Deputy Quaestor of the Congolese Senate, Omana Bitika Pascal, have filed a legal complaint against journalist Gauthier Sey of Netic Television over reports alleging the senator’s involvement in a mining-related…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 15, 2026 - The lawyers representing Senator and Deputy Quaestor of the Congolese Senate, Omana Bitika Pascal, have filed a legal complaint against journalist Gauthier Sey of Netic Television over reports alleging the senator’s involvement in a mining-related fraud case.
The complaint, submitted on Wednesday, July 15, was filed with the Office of the Attorney General at the Kinshasa Court of Appeal.
Led by lawyer Alexis Bangabanga, the senator’s defense team rejected allegations linking their client to an alleged $600,000 fraud case involving the Mandumbwila mining site. The lawyers stated that Omana Bitika has no connection to the accusations and denied any involvement in the matter.
According to the defense, the journalist’s publications constitute defamatory statements that harm the reputation, dignity, and public image of the Senate official.
The legal team announced that it has initiated judicial proceedings to obtain legal remedies and protect the rights and reputation of their client. It also indicated that additional complaints could be filed before other competent courts.
The case now moves into the judicial process, where the parties will have the opportunity to present their arguments before the relevant authorities.
Security and Humanitarian Affairs

title: Campaign Launched to Provide Sanitary Pads to One Million Ugandan Girls
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - A nationwide menstrual health campaign has been launched to distribute one million packs of sanitary pads to vulnerable schoolgirls across Uganda in an effort to address period poverty and prevent menstruation from disrupting girls’ education.…
title_en: Campaign Launched to Provide Sanitary Pads to One Million Ugandan Girls
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - A nationwide menstrual health campaign has been launched to distribute one million packs of sanitary pads to vulnerable schoolgirls across Uganda in an effort to address period poverty and prevent menstruation from disrupting girls’ education.…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - A nationwide menstrual health campaign has been launched to distribute one million packs of sanitary pads to vulnerable schoolgirls across Uganda in an effort to address period poverty and prevent menstruation from disrupting girls’ education.
The initiative, known as “1 Million Pads for 1 Million Girls,” was launched by the Union Transport Alliance (UNION) in partnership with The Mental Health Awareness Initiative (TMHAI) under the KILI CLEAR Campaign.
The campaign aims to bring together government agencies, schools, development partners, private companies, civil society organisations, and individuals to support girls who cannot afford menstrual hygiene products.
Organisers said the initiative is designed not only to improve access to affordable sanitary products but also to ensure that girls from vulnerable communities receive consistent support throughout the year.
Union Transport Alliance officials said a sanitary pad production facility is being developed to guarantee a reliable supply as the campaign expands across the country.
The initiative has already partnered with several schools and plans to increase its reach through a nationwide community network, with organisers calling on individuals and organisations to contribute towards keeping girls in school.
Campaign supporters said menstrual health remains a major education and public health concern, as many girls miss classes or face social challenges due to limited access to sanitary products.
The Ministry of Health welcomed the initiative, noting that menstrual hygiene is closely linked to school attendance, adolescent health, and girls’ dignity. Officials said inadequate access to menstrual products remains one of the factors contributing to absenteeism and school dropout among some girls.
Authorities also highlighted ongoing efforts to improve menstrual health education and sanitation facilities in schools, including better changing spaces and safe disposal systems for menstrual products.
Youth leaders supporting the campaign called for broader involvement from government, communities, private sector actors, and individuals to reduce stigma and ensure girls can manage menstruation with confidence.
Organisers said the programme aligns with Uganda’s menstrual health goals by expanding access to hygiene products, promoting awareness, and supporting better educational outcomes for girls.
Through nationwide mobilisation and distribution efforts, the campaign aims to ensure that menstruation no longer becomes a barrier to education, health, dignity, and future opportunities for girls.

excerpt: Mpigi, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Residents of Bukasa-Lwamikoma Village in Kituntu Sub-county, Mpigi District, have appealed to security authorities to increase police presence and conduct night patrols following growing concerns over robbery, theft, and harassment allegedly…
title_en: Mpigi Residents Demand Security Action Over Rising Youth Crime Fears
excerpt_en: Mpigi, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Residents of Bukasa-Lwamikoma Village in Kituntu Sub-county, Mpigi District, have appealed to security authorities to increase police presence and conduct night patrols following growing concerns over robbery, theft, and harassment allegedly…
body_en:
Mpigi, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Residents of Bukasa-Lwamikoma Village in Kituntu Sub-county, Mpigi District, have appealed to security authorities to increase police presence and conduct night patrols following growing concerns over robbery, theft, and harassment allegedly linked to local youth.
Community leaders said the situation has created fear among residents, with many people avoiding movement after dark due to concerns over attacks and theft.
The LC I Chairperson of Bukasa-Lwamikoma, Fredrick Sempereza, said suspected offenders are mainly young people from the same community rather than outsiders. He said repeated efforts by village leaders and parents to address the problem through dialogue have failed to stop the alleged criminal activities.
Residents reported that some people, particularly women returning home at night, have been targeted in incidents involving stolen phones, handbags, and money. Many community members said they now adjust their routines to avoid travelling after nightfall.
Local leaders have appealed to the Mpigi District Security Committee and the Uganda Police Force to strengthen security measures, including increased patrols and action against individuals suspected of criminal activities.
Authorities have been urged to intervene before the situation worsens, as Bukasa-Lwamikoma continues to grow as a trading centre with an increasing population.
Residents say improved security is needed to protect lives, property, and economic activities in the area.

title: Uganda Ministry Orders Assessment of Tororo Market Challenges Amid Trader Concerns
excerpt: Tororo, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Ministry of Local Government has pledged to send engineers to assess structural and operational challenges affecting Tororo Central Market after municipal leaders raised concerns over the facility’s design, electricity supply, and…
title_en: Uganda Ministry Orders Assessment of Tororo Market Challenges Amid Trader Concerns
excerpt_en: Tororo, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Ministry of Local Government has pledged to send engineers to assess structural and operational challenges affecting Tororo Central Market after municipal leaders raised concerns over the facility’s design, electricity supply, and…
body_en:
Tororo, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Ministry of Local Government has pledged to send engineers to assess structural and operational challenges affecting Tororo Central Market after municipal leaders raised concerns over the facility’s design, electricity supply, and management issues.
The commitment followed a meeting between Local Government Minister Balaam Barugahara Ateenyi and a delegation from Tororo Municipality, which presented concerns affecting traders and the market’s operations.
Municipal leaders highlighted problems including alleged design flaws, unreliable electricity, governance challenges, and accountability concerns, saying the issues have affected traders’ willingness to operate from the facility.
The ministry agreed to deploy engineers to conduct a technical assessment and provide recommendations on possible solutions. The minister also pledged to visit Tororo to engage with local leaders and stakeholders on the way forward.
Local authorities had requested temporary permission for traders to continue operating outside the market while improvements were being made. However, the proposal was rejected, with officials insisting that traders must comply with government directives requiring businesses to operate from designated marketplaces rather than streets and road reserves.
The intervention comes as authorities continue enforcing measures aimed at restoring order in urban trading areas across the country.
Leaders also raised concerns over unreliable electricity supply at the market, saying frequent disruptions have affected business activities and limited the facility’s potential as a commercial centre.
The meeting further addressed governance and accountability concerns within the municipality, including allegations of corruption. The minister warned that anti-corruption operations would expand to the Bukedi sub-region after ongoing inspections in Bugisu are completed.
He also cautioned individuals accused of taking money in exchange for government jobs to refund the funds or face legal action.
The planned technical assessment and the minister’s upcoming visit are expected to provide recommendations for improving Tororo Central Market and enhancing services for traders and residents.

N’Djamena, July 15, 2026 - President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo arrived in N’Djamena on Wednesday to participate in the African Water and Energy Forum, a high-level continental meeting focused on accelerating investments in water security, energy access, and climate resilience.
Held from July 15 to 16 in the Chadian capital, the forum brings together African heads of state and government, international financial institutions, development partners, regional organizations, and private-sector representatives to address major infrastructure and sustainability challenges facing the continent.
The participation of the Congolese Head of State follows an official invitation from Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno, delivered during a meeting in Kinshasa with a delegation led by Chad’s Minister of Water and Energy, Passalé Kanabé Marcelin.
During discussions with President Tshisekedi, the Chadian delegation emphasized the importance of the forum as a platform to mobilize financing, strengthen partnerships, and accelerate strategic projects aimed at improving access to clean water and reliable energy across Africa.
With its vast freshwater reserves and major hydropower potential, the Democratic Republic of Congo is expected to play a key role in discussions on sustainable management of water resources and climate adaptation.
“President Tshisekedi will represent the DRC, a country with immense water resources, in the search for sustainable solutions to climate change and water-security challenges,” according to the Congolese presidency. The Minister of Water Resources and Electricity, along with the Director General of the national water distribution company Regideso, are accompanying the president during the forum.
The meeting aims to advance the implementation of the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Plus (WASH+) Investment Roadmap and encourage stronger political commitment and financial mobilization to improve water access across the continent.
Beyond drinking water and sanitation, discussions will focus on integrating water management with agriculture, energy development, and climate resilience strategies. The forum also seeks to strengthen cooperation among countries sharing major transboundary river basins and promote coordinated management of Africa’s water resources.
Co-chaired by President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno and Anna Bjerde, Managing Director of Operations at the World Bank Group, the forum is designed to move beyond political declarations by translating commitments into concrete projects.
Key priorities include improving coordination between public policies, institutions, and financing mechanisms, developing national and regional water management agreements, and identifying investment opportunities capable of attracting both public and private capital.
The gathering also provides a platform for governments, financial institutions, and businesses to build partnerships and transform continental water and energy priorities into sustainable development projects.
For the DRC, participation in the N’Djamena forum represents an opportunity to highlight its strategic role in Africa’s water and energy future while seeking new partnerships to support infrastructure development and climate adaptation efforts.
Economy and Tech.

title: Uganda Religious Leaders Appeal for Release of South Korean Faith Leader Lee Man-hee
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Inter-Religious Council of Uganda (IRCU) has appealed to South Korean authorities to release Shincheonji Church of Jesus Chairman Lee Man-hee, arguing that his continued detention should be addressed through principles of fairness,…
title_en: Uganda Religious Leaders Appeal for Release of South Korean Faith Leader Lee Man-hee
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Inter-Religious Council of Uganda (IRCU) has appealed to South Korean authorities to release Shincheonji Church of Jesus Chairman Lee Man-hee, arguing that his continued detention should be addressed through principles of fairness,…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Inter-Religious Council of Uganda (IRCU) has appealed to South Korean authorities to release Shincheonji Church of Jesus Chairman Lee Man-hee, arguing that his continued detention should be addressed through principles of fairness, justice, and due process.
In a letter sent to the South Korean government, IRCU Secretary General Joshua Kitakule called for Lee’s case to be handled through a transparent and impartial legal process, while expressing concern that prolonged detention could undermine confidence in judicial procedures.
Kitakule acknowledged that Lee was arrested in relation to election-related allegations but said any concerns regarding his conduct should be resolved through established legal channels rather than measures that could be perceived as excessive or politically influenced.
He described Lee as an international religious figure known for peace initiatives and efforts to promote dialogue among communities across cultural and religious boundaries. According to Kitakule, Lee’s detention affects not only his personal freedom but also his ability to continue his peace-building activities.
The IRCU official urged South Korean authorities to uphold human rights standards and ensure that justice is administered with fairness and dignity, especially given Lee’s advanced age.
The appeal emphasized the importance of protecting democratic values and transparent judicial processes, while calling for a resolution that respects both legal principles and humanitarian considerations.
The statement comes as legal proceedings involving Lee Man-hee continue in South Korea, with Ugandan religious leaders expressing hope that the matter will be resolved in accordance with the rule of law.

title: WFP Launches Food Assistance for 7,525 Households in Ituri to Help Contain Ebola Spread
excerpt: Mongbwalu, Ituri, July 15, 2026 - The World Food Programme (WFP) has begun distributing food assistance to 7,525 households in Mongbwalu, Djugu Territory, as part of an emergency operation aimed at supporting vulnerable families while helping reduce the risk of Ebola…
title_en: WFP Launches Food Assistance for 7,525 Households in Ituri to Help Contain Ebola Spread
excerpt_en: Mongbwalu, Ituri, July 15, 2026 - The World Food Programme (WFP) has begun distributing food assistance to 7,525 households in Mongbwalu, Djugu Territory, as part of an emergency operation aimed at supporting vulnerable families while helping reduce the risk of Ebola…
body_en:
Mongbwalu, Ituri, July 15, 2026 - The World Food Programme (WFP) has begun distributing food assistance to 7,525 households in Mongbwalu, Djugu Territory, as part of an emergency operation aimed at supporting vulnerable families while helping reduce the risk of Ebola transmission.
The food distribution, which began on July 14, comes as Mongbwalu remains one of the main areas affected by the Democratic Republic of Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak. The locality is also classified as IPC Phase 3+, indicating a severe food security crisis.
According to the WFP, the assistance is intended not only to address immediate food needs but also to reduce population movements by enabling households to remain in their communities instead of traveling in search of food or income, thereby lowering the risk of exposure to the Ebola virus.
Each household is receiving a 30-day food ration designed to meet basic nutritional requirements. The package includes 72 kilograms of rice, 21.6 kilograms of beans, 5.4 liters of cooking oil, and 0.9 kilograms of salt, based on assessments of local dietary habits and nutritional needs.
Beneficiaries welcomed the assistance, saying it would help families cope with both food shortages and the impact of the ongoing health emergency. Many residents noted that the support allows them to feed their children while reducing the need to undertake activities that could increase their exposure to the disease.
To avoid overcrowding at distribution sites, the operation is being conducted in phases. An initial group of 1,000 households has already received assistance, with the remaining beneficiaries expected to be served in successive waves.
The WFP said beneficiary households were identified through field assessments and noted that the entire Mongbwalu community is considered to be living in an area at high risk due to the active circulation of the Ebola virus.
The organization added that the food assistance program could be extended next month, subject to the availability of funding and operational resources, as humanitarian efforts continue to address both the health and food security challenges facing the affected population.

title: Akena Urges Uganda to Build Multi-Airport Export Network to Expand Global Trade
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda People’s Congress (UPC) President Jimmy Akena has called on the government to develop cargo infrastructure across multiple airports in the country, saying a wider export network would help farmers and producers access international…
title_en: Akena Urges Uganda to Build Multi-Airport Export Network to Expand Global Trade
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda People’s Congress (UPC) President Jimmy Akena has called on the government to develop cargo infrastructure across multiple airports in the country, saying a wider export network would help farmers and producers access international…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda People’s Congress (UPC) President Jimmy Akena has called on the government to develop cargo infrastructure across multiple airports in the country, saying a wider export network would help farmers and producers access international markets.
Akena argued that Uganda should move beyond concentrating export activities around a single airport and instead establish a nationwide cargo strategy supported by modern handling facilities, cold storage systems, and efficient transport networks.
Speaking in Kampala, Akena said Uganda has an opportunity to expand its international trade by positioning regional airports as export hubs serving agricultural producers and other industries.
He said he had previously submitted policy proposals to President Yoweri Museveni aimed at helping Uganda benefit from emerging trade opportunities linking markets in South America, China, Europe, and the Middle East.
According to Akena, increased air cargo activity associated with global investment projects could create opportunities for Uganda to export products such as agricultural goods and farmed fish if the country develops the necessary infrastructure.
He emphasized that attracting cargo aircraft alone would not be sufficient without supporting facilities such as cold storage, export processing systems, and efficient logistics networks.
Akena proposed expanding cargo capacity at airports including Entebbe, Gulu, and other regional facilities, arguing that multiple export hubs would benefit farmers, exporters, and communities across the country.
He said improved export capacity could increase household incomes, strengthen food security, and contribute to addressing challenges such as child malnutrition by creating more economic opportunities.
The UPC leader also called for greater cooperation among political actors, saying national development requires practical solutions beyond political differences.
Akena said he remains committed to sharing policy ideas aimed at creating jobs, expanding Uganda’s export base, and improving livelihoods despite differences with the current administration.

title: SODE 2026 to Explore Uganda’s Next Phase of Digital Economy Growth
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda’s technology leaders, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and innovators are set to gather for the third edition of the State of the Digital Economy (SODE 2026) conference, focusing on how the country can transform digital expansion into jobs,…
title_en: SODE 2026 to Explore Uganda’s Next Phase of Digital Economy Growth
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda’s technology leaders, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and innovators are set to gather for the third edition of the State of the Digital Economy (SODE 2026) conference, focusing on how the country can transform digital expansion into jobs,…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda’s technology leaders, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and innovators are set to gather for the third edition of the State of the Digital Economy (SODE 2026) conference, focusing on how the country can transform digital expansion into jobs, innovation, and inclusive economic growth.
The conference, scheduled for July 24 at the Next Conference Center, will be held under the theme “Beyond Connectivity: Turning Access into Opportunity”, as Uganda shifts attention from expanding digital access to maximising its economic benefits.
Organised by NextCom, the communications agency under Next Media, SODE 2026 will bring together government officials, regulators, investors, technology companies, academics, content creators, and innovators to discuss strategies for strengthening Uganda’s digital economy.
The conference will examine how increasing internet access, smartphone adoption, and digital services can translate into employment opportunities, entrepreneurship, and sustainable economic development.
Discussions will focus on four major areas: Human Capital, Policy, Infrastructure, and Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity.
Participants will explore ways to improve digital skills, develop resilient technology infrastructure, create supportive policies, and prepare businesses and citizens for an increasingly digital economy.
Beyond keynote speeches and panel discussions, the event will feature innovation exhibitions, fintech showcases, GovTech demonstrations, creator economy sessions, and interactive masterclasses highlighting technology-driven solutions.
A major highlight will be the Vibe Hackathon, which will bring together young innovators and experienced developers to create practical solutions using emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Organisers said the hackathon aims to showcase Uganda’s growing technology ecosystem while encouraging innovations that address real-world challenges.
The conference will also provide a platform for dialogue between government, private sector players, regulators, and technology innovators on policies and investments needed to strengthen digital transformation.
Although Uganda has expanded mobile connectivity, digital payments, and online services in recent years, previous discussions under SODE have highlighted challenges including limited digital skills, cybersecurity concerns, regulatory gaps, and unequal participation in the digital economy.
SODE 2026 is expected to attract policymakers, developers, entrepreneurs, educators, students, and technology enthusiasts from across Uganda as stakeholders seek solutions to move the country’s digital agenda beyond connectivity.
The conference aims to redefine Uganda’s digital future by focusing on how technology can create practical opportunities for citizens, businesses, and the wider economy.

title: Uganda Launches New Cybersecurity Framework to Protect Digital Government Systems
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda has launched the Updated National Information Security Framework (NISF) 2026, a new cybersecurity framework aimed at strengthening protection of government systems, safeguarding public data, and building a more secure digital…
title_en: Uganda Launches New Cybersecurity Framework to Protect Digital Government Systems
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda has launched the Updated National Information Security Framework (NISF) 2026, a new cybersecurity framework aimed at strengthening protection of government systems, safeguarding public data, and building a more secure digital…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda has launched the Updated National Information Security Framework (NISF) 2026, a new cybersecurity framework aimed at strengthening protection of government systems, safeguarding public data, and building a more secure digital environment.
The framework was unveiled during an event in Kampala organised by the National Information Technology Authority-Uganda (NITA-U) under the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project-Government Network programme.
Minister of ICT and National Guidance Justine Kasule Lumumba said information security has become a national priority beyond a technical issue, as government services increasingly rely on digital platforms.
She emphasized that protecting information systems and citizens’ data is essential for national security, economic development, public service delivery, and maintaining public trust.
The updated framework replaces the earlier version introduced in 2014 and responds to major technological changes and emerging cyber threats over the past decade. It provides guidance on cybersecurity governance, risk assessments, security controls, and institutional resilience against digital attacks.
The minister urged government institutions to treat cybersecurity risks as institutional responsibilities, warning that cyber incidents could disrupt public services, expose sensitive information, cause financial losses, and damage public confidence.
She called on ministries, departments, and agencies to work closely with NITA-U by conducting regular security assessments, addressing vulnerabilities, and strengthening their cybersecurity capabilities.
Private sector operators managing critical infrastructure, including banking, telecommunications, energy, transport, and health services, were also encouraged to collaborate with government to protect Uganda’s interconnected digital ecosystem.
NITA-U Executive Director Dr. Hatwib Mugasa described the framework as a major step in Uganda’s cybersecurity development, saying it provides institutions with practical tools to assess their security capacity and improve resilience against evolving threats.
He said the focus would now shift from awareness creation to measurable implementation, with NITA-U supporting institutions in improving compliance and adopting minimum cybersecurity standards.
The framework is built around seven key principles, including leadership accountability, collective responsibility, individual responsibility, risk management, secure information sharing, trusted personnel, and organisational resilience.
Authorities said implementation of the NISF 2026 is expected to strengthen protection of national information assets, improve government digital services, and increase public confidence as Uganda continues its digital transformation agenda.

title: Uganda Electoral Commission Launches 2026 Election Review, Plans Reforms Ahead of Future Polls
excerpt: Masaka, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda’s Electoral Commission has begun a nationwide assessment of the 2026 General Elections, engaging stakeholders to identify challenges and develop reforms aimed at improving future electoral processes. During a consultation meeting in…
title_en: Uganda Electoral Commission Launches 2026 Election Review, Plans Reforms Ahead of Future Polls
excerpt_en: Masaka, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda’s Electoral Commission has begun a nationwide assessment of the 2026 General Elections, engaging stakeholders to identify challenges and develop reforms aimed at improving future electoral processes. During a consultation meeting in…
body_en:
Masaka, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Uganda’s Electoral Commission has begun a nationwide assessment of the 2026 General Elections, engaging stakeholders to identify challenges and develop reforms aimed at improving future electoral processes.
During a consultation meeting in Masaka, Electoral Commission officials said the review seeks to examine what worked well during the elections, identify shortcomings, and collect recommendations on strengthening election management and public confidence.
One of the key concerns raised during the consultations was inadequate voter education. The Commission said it would review its voter education programmes and improve efforts to ensure citizens receive sufficient information before future elections.
The Commission also defended the role of security agencies during elections, saying their involvement is intended to maintain law and order and protect citizens rather than interfere with the electoral process.
Officials said the electoral roadmap is guided by legal requirements and acknowledged concerns raised by stakeholders over issues such as election timelines and the management of results at tally centres. These concerns will be reviewed as part of preparations for future polls.
The Commission also addressed criticism regarding the independence of its members, stating that commissioners undergo parliamentary vetting and approval before assuming office.
According to the Commission, some election-related challenges, including violence, voter bribery, and disputes among candidates, are linked to the conduct of political actors rather than the electoral body itself.
Ahead of the upcoming Local Council I (LC1) elections, authorities urged candidates and voters to maintain peace, emphasizing that grassroots elections involve communities where competitors and voters continue to live together after polling.
The Commission said approximately Shs53 billion has been allocated to support LC1 election activities, including payments for officials involved in voter register updates, nominations, and polling operations across more than 70,000 villages.
The post-election consultations are part of a broader assessment aimed at improving electoral transparency, strengthening voter education, and addressing concerns raised by stakeholders before Uganda’s next electoral cycle.

title_en: ICC Prosecutor Seeks to Drop War-Crimes Case Against Abdallah Banda
excerpt_en: The Hague, Netherlands, July 15, 2026 - The International Criminal Court prosecutor asked Trial Chamber IV for leave to withdraw war-crimes charges against Darfur rebel leader Abdallah Banda, saying evidence and witness conditions no longer supported proceeding.
body_en:
The Hague, Netherlands, July 15, 2026 - The International Criminal Court prosecutor asked Trial Chamber IV for leave to withdraw war-crimes charges against Darfur rebel leader Abdallah Banda, saying evidence and witness conditions no longer supported proceeding.

The request, made public in court filings, reopened debate over accountability gaps for older Darfur cases even as new atrocity files from El Fasher and El Geneina dominate diplomacy.

Victims’ advocates warned that withdrawals without clear alternative justice deepen impunity perceptions.
