title: UNBS Warns Ugandans Against Buying Fuel from Roadside Sellers
excerpt: Masaka, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) has warned the public against purchasing fuel from unlicensed roadside sellers, citing risks including fire hazards, environmental damage, and financial losses caused by poor-quality petroleum…
title_en: UNBS Warns Ugandans Against Buying Fuel from Roadside Sellers
excerpt_en: Masaka, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) has warned the public against purchasing fuel from unlicensed roadside sellers, citing risks including fire hazards, environmental damage, and financial losses caused by poor-quality petroleum…
body_en:
Masaka, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) has warned the public against purchasing fuel from unlicensed roadside sellers, citing risks including fire hazards, environmental damage, and financial losses caused by poor-quality petroleum products.
The warning was issued during a stakeholders’ meeting in Masaka involving UNBS officials, the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development, fuel station operators, and local leaders. The discussions focused on fuel quality standards, consumer protection, and safe handling of petroleum products.
Authorities said fuel sold in jerrycans and plastic containers along roadsides is often handled under unsafe conditions and may not meet required quality standards. The public was encouraged to purchase petroleum products only from licensed filling stations and to report suspected cases of fuel adulteration.
UNBS officials said regular inspections and testing are conducted on imported petroleum products and fuel sold at authorised stations to ensure compliance with national standards. However, they emphasized that public cooperation remains essential in identifying illegal fuel sales and protecting consumers.
Motorcycle riders and generator owners also raised concerns over losses linked to suspected substandard fuel, with some consumers reporting damage to equipment after purchasing poor-quality products from unreliable suppliers.
Meanwhile, energy officials encouraged households to adopt cleaner cooking alternatives, including liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), as part of efforts to reduce dependence on charcoal and firewood and address environmental degradation.
Authorities urged beneficiaries of government-supported LPG programmes to use the provided equipment for its intended purpose and avoid selling the supplied cylinders.
The engagement was part of broader efforts to improve fuel quality control, strengthen consumer safety, and promote cleaner energy solutions across Uganda.

title: Ibanda Electoral Officer Removed from LC1 Polls Over Alleged Guidelines Violation
excerpt: Ibanda, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - An electoral officer assigned to supervise the upcoming Local Council I (LC1) elections in Kigando Trading Centre Cell, Bugarama Ward, Bisheshe Division, has been barred from conducting the exercise following allegations of breaching Electoral…
title_en: Ibanda Electoral Officer Removed from LC1 Polls Over Alleged Guidelines Violation
excerpt_en: Ibanda, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - An electoral officer assigned to supervise the upcoming Local Council I (LC1) elections in Kigando Trading Centre Cell, Bugarama Ward, Bisheshe Division, has been barred from conducting the exercise following allegations of breaching Electoral…
body_en:
Ibanda, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - An electoral officer assigned to supervise the upcoming Local Council I (LC1) elections in Kigando Trading Centre Cell, Bugarama Ward, Bisheshe Division, has been barred from conducting the exercise following allegations of breaching Electoral Commission guidelines.
The decision to remove Emmanuel Byamukama was reached during a harmonisation meeting chaired by Ibanda District Deputy Resident District Commissioner Suleiman Walugembe, after stakeholders raised concerns over his conduct during the voter registration process.
Complainants alleged that Byamukama irregularly included names of individuals who were not physically present during voter registration, contrary to Electoral Commission procedures requiring eligible voters to appear in person at designated registration centres.
NRM LC1 flag bearer Lawrence Muhwezi claimed that some individuals who had not lived in the village for the required period were also included on the voter register, raising concerns about the credibility of the process.
Muhwezi further accused Byamukama of having a conflict of interest, alleging that the electoral officer was related to the incumbent LC1 chairperson and had been supporting his re-election campaign.
The petitioners cited Electoral Commission guidelines requiring voters to personally appear during registration and to have lived in the village for at least six months before qualifying to participate in the election.
Following the meeting, Bisheshe Division Electoral Commission Returning Officer John-Patrick Tumuhumwire confirmed that Byamukama would no longer oversee the LC1 elections in Kigando Trading Centre.
He said the Electoral Commission remains committed to ensuring a free, fair, and credible electoral process.
Ibanda Deputy RDC Suleiman Walugembe urged all election officials to strictly follow EC guidelines, warning that any actions that undermine the integrity of the process would not be tolerated.
The Electoral Commission roadmap indicates that LC1 chairperson elections are scheduled for July 28, 2026, marking the first nationwide village leadership elections since 2018.
The polls are expected to bring in new village leaders as political parties and independent candidates compete for grassroots positions across Uganda.

title: Bunyoro Businesses Raise Concerns Over Taxes, Bureaucracy and Limited Access to Government Funds
excerpt: Hoima, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Business owners in the Bunyoro sub-region have raised concerns over high taxes, bureaucratic procedures, and difficulties accessing government financing programmes, saying the challenges continue to limit the growth of small enterprises. The…
title_en: Bunyoro Businesses Raise Concerns Over Taxes, Bureaucracy and Limited Access to Government Funds
excerpt_en: Hoima, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Business owners in the Bunyoro sub-region have raised concerns over high taxes, bureaucratic procedures, and difficulties accessing government financing programmes, saying the challenges continue to limit the growth of small enterprises. The…
body_en:
Hoima, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Business owners in the Bunyoro sub-region have raised concerns over high taxes, bureaucratic procedures, and difficulties accessing government financing programmes, saying the challenges continue to limit the growth of small enterprises.
The concerns were raised during a Regional Post-National Budget Dialogue organised by the Private Sector Foundation Uganda (PSFU) in Hoima City, where entrepreneurs discussed opportunities under the 2026/27 National Budget and challenges affecting private sector development.
Participants highlighted difficulties accessing government-backed financing programmes, including the Small Business Fund (SBF), Agricultural Credit Facility (ACF), GROW Project, and Emyooga, despite the initiatives being designed to support small businesses and agricultural enterprises.
Business owners said lengthy approval processes, complex application requirements, and limited communication from responsible institutions have prevented many eligible entrepreneurs from benefiting from the programmes.
Some participants said they had applied for funding several years ago without receiving clear feedback, leading to growing frustration and declining confidence in government support initiatives.
Entrepreneurs also called for increased financial literacy training, saying many small businesses require support in areas such as record keeping, taxation, business management, and formal registration to improve their chances of accessing financing.
The Private Sector Foundation Uganda said it would continue engaging government agencies and financial institutions to address barriers preventing businesses from accessing available funding opportunities.
Business leaders further raised concerns over the rising cost of doing business, particularly the burden of taxation, calling for reforms that would create a more supportive environment for private enterprises.
Officials from the Bank of Uganda said government has established several financing mechanisms to support businesses and agriculture, with funds channelled through commercial banks, SACCOs, and other approved financial institutions.
However, they acknowledged that some entrepreneurs fail to qualify because of weak business practices, including poor financial records, lack of formal registration, and limited use of formal banking systems.
Officials explained that under the Agricultural Credit Facility, businesses can access financing of up to Shs500 million at an annual interest rate of 10 percent, with repayment periods depending on the size and nature of the investment.
Entrepreneurs were also advised to avoid excessive borrowing from multiple lenders, as high levels of debt can reduce their chances of qualifying for additional financing.
Stakeholders agreed that improving financial literacy, simplifying access procedures, and reducing operational costs will be essential to ensuring that government financing programmes effectively support small businesses and economic growth in Bunyoro.

title: UNDP Strengthens Ebola Preparedness in Uganda’s Transport Sector
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has provided infection prevention and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) equipment to Uganda’s transport sector as part of efforts to strengthen preparedness against Ebola Virus Disease and…
title_en: UNDP Strengthens Ebola Preparedness in Uganda’s Transport Sector
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has provided infection prevention and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) equipment to Uganda’s transport sector as part of efforts to strengthen preparedness against Ebola Virus Disease and…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has provided infection prevention and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) equipment to Uganda’s transport sector as part of efforts to strengthen preparedness against Ebola Virus Disease and other public health threats.
The equipment was handed over at Nateete Transport Terminal through the Uganda Professional Drivers’ Network (UPDN) and is intended to support bus operators, taxi park workers, truck drivers, and other transport stakeholders who interact with thousands of travellers every day.
The supplies include infrared temperature guns, handwashing facilities, water container stands, liquid soap, hand sanitisers, and disposable gloves aimed at improving hygiene standards and infection prevention practices at public transport facilities.
UPDN said the intervention recognises the transport sector as a critical frontline in disease surveillance due to the high movement of passengers and cargo within Uganda and across regional borders.
The organisation noted that public transport workers are often among the first points of contact for travellers moving between districts and neighbouring countries, making their role essential in detecting and preventing the spread of infectious diseases.
Thousands of passengers, buses, and long-distance trucks travel daily along routes connecting Uganda to neighbouring countries, including the Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing the importance of strengthening health measures within transport networks.
Beyond the distribution of equipment, the programme will support risk communication, community engagement, public awareness campaigns, surveillance activities, and behaviour change initiatives among transport operators and surrounding communities.
UPDN said improved infection prevention measures among long-distance truck drivers and other transport workers will also contribute to protecting regional trade routes.
The organisation pledged continued cooperation with the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Works and Transport, Kampala Capital City Authority, transport associations, and development partners to enhance public health preparedness across Uganda’s transport system.

title_en: RSF Accepts Humanitarian Truce but Rejects Withdrawal Terms
excerpt_en: Khartoum, Sudan, July 15, 2026 - The Rapid Support Forces submitted their reply to U.S. peace proposals, accepting an unconditional three-month humanitarian truce under United Nations supervision in Darfur, Kordofan, Ed Damazin and the Nuba Mountains while rejecting demands...
body_en:
Khartoum, Sudan, July 15, 2026 - The Rapid Support Forces submitted their reply to U.S. peace proposals, accepting an unconditional three-month humanitarian truce under United Nations supervision in Darfur, Kordofan, Ed Damazin and the Nuba Mountains while rejecting demands to withdraw from captured territories.

An RSF official said the package also covered security arrangements, restructuring of state institutions, transitional justice and political dialogue toward a transitional government.

Sudan’s Security and Defence Council, chaired by Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, had separately submitted its own response days earlier.

U.S. Senior Advisor Massad Boulos cautioned against claims of a breakthrough, saying multiple substantive issues remained unresolved or rejected and that only a formal announcement would confirm any deal.

title_en: Kibaale Residents Raise Land Corruption Concerns as Government Moves to Issue Titles
excerpt_en: Kibaale, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Residents of Kibaale District have raised concerns over alleged corruption and delays in land title processing, saying the challenges have increased uncertainty over ownership and contributed to land-related disputes. The concerns were raised…
body_en:
Kibaale, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - Residents of Kibaale District have raised concerns over alleged corruption and delays in land title processing, saying the challenges have increased uncertainty over ownership and contributed to land-related disputes.
The concerns were raised during a community sensitisation meeting organised by the Uganda Land Commission (ULC) on the Systematic Land Adjudication and Certification (SLAC) programme, ahead of the planned issuance of more than 2,000 land titles covering land acquired by the government for beneficiary communities.
The land, located in Buyanga Sub-county, covers several villages including Kasambya, Kineka A, Kikonge, and Kidukuule. The Uganda Land Commission said it remains committed to addressing challenges affecting land certification and ensuring that communities benefit from secure land ownership.
Authorities said preparations for the latest land title distribution exercise have been completed, with previous programmes already resulting in the issuance of thousands of titles across different areas of the district.

title: Uganda Energy Ministry Launches Reforms to Drive $500 Billion Economy Vision by 2040
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 – The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development has launched a leadership retreat aimed at transforming the energy and minerals sector into a major engine of industrialisation, job creation, and economic growth as Uganda pursues its target of a…
title_en: Uganda Energy Ministry Launches Reforms to Drive $500 Billion Economy Vision by 2040
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 – The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development has launched a leadership retreat aimed at transforming the energy and minerals sector into a major engine of industrialisation, job creation, and economic growth as Uganda pursues its target of a…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 – The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development has launched a leadership retreat aimed at transforming the energy and minerals sector into a major engine of industrialisation, job creation, and economic growth as Uganda pursues its target of a US$500 billion economy by 2040.
The five-day retreat, held in Kampala, brings together senior ministry officials, government agencies, state corporations, and technical experts to develop reforms focused on expanding energy access, promoting mineral value addition, strengthening industrial capacity, and improving coordination across the sector.
Energy and Mineral Development Minister Dr Monica Musenero urged ministry leaders to move beyond routine administration and reposition the sector as a strategic driver of national transformation.
She introduced the One MEMD Doctrine, an institutional framework designed to align departments and agencies under a common vision focused on using energy, minerals, and natural resources to create wealth and support industrial development.
Musenero said Uganda must shift from exporting raw materials to building domestic processing industries that increase value, create jobs, and strengthen national revenues.
She emphasized that natural resources should not only be viewed as commodities for extraction but as foundations for innovation, manufacturing, and long-term economic growth.
The government estimates Uganda’s economy at more than US$60 billion and aims to expand it to US$500 billion by 2040 through industrialisation, science, technology, innovation, and increased private sector participation.
The energy and minerals sector is expected to play a central role in achieving this ambition through developments in oil production, mineral exploitation, electricity generation, and expansion of energy infrastructure.
Uganda currently has electricity generation capacity exceeding 2,000 megawatts, while ongoing investments in transmission networks, renewable energy, and oil-related infrastructure are expected to improve reliability and support industrial expansion.
During the retreat, officials are reviewing sector value chains, assessing institutional performance, and identifying reforms needed to improve collaboration among ministry departments and affiliated agencies.
The discussions are also aimed at replacing fragmented decision-making with integrated planning and strategic management under the One MEMD framework.
At the conclusion of the retreat, ministry leaders are expected to adopt a transformation roadmap to guide implementation of reforms and accelerate Uganda’s transition towards a modern industrial economy by 2040.

title: Buganda Kingdom Calls for Continuous Efforts to Expand Africa’s Coffee Markets
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Buganda Kingdom has called on coffee stakeholders across Africa to strengthen year-round market engagement in order to attract global buyers, increase investment, and improve incomes for farmers. The call was made during the launch of the…
title_en: Buganda Kingdom Calls for Continuous Efforts to Expand Africa’s Coffee Markets
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Buganda Kingdom has called on coffee stakeholders across Africa to strengthen year-round market engagement in order to attract global buyers, increase investment, and improve incomes for farmers. The call was made during the launch of the…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The Buganda Kingdom has called on coffee stakeholders across Africa to strengthen year-round market engagement in order to attract global buyers, increase investment, and improve incomes for farmers.
The call was made during the launch of the 23rd African Fine Coffees Conference and Exhibition and the 4th African Coffee Week at Speke Resort Munyonyo, where industry leaders, farmers, exporters, buyers, and policymakers gathered to discuss the future of Africa’s coffee sector.
The Second Deputy Katikkiro and Buganda Kingdom Treasurer, Owek. Robert Waggwa Nsibirwa, said Africa’s coffee industry should move beyond relying on annual conferences and exhibitions by creating permanent platforms that connect farmers, exporters, investors, and international buyers throughout the year.
He urged industry bodies to develop digital systems that allow stakeholders to build business relationships before major events, ensuring conferences focus on finalising partnerships and trade opportunities.
Nsibirwa said increasing coffee production alone is not enough, emphasizing the need to maintain quality standards, strengthen farmer support systems, and improve value chain management.
He highlighted the impact of the Buganda Kingdom’s Mwanyi Terimba programme, which promotes coffee growing and farmer support, saying the initiative has contributed to increased production, with annual output exceeding four million bags.
The Kingdom official stressed that coffee quality begins at the farm level through proper crop management, technical support, and continuous monitoring of plantations.
He also highlighted the programme’s contribution to empowering women and youth in coffee-growing communities, saying more women are now participating in agricultural decision-making and gaining ownership of productive assets.
According to Nsibirwa, young people are increasingly joining the coffee sector through activities such as certified seedling production, technology-based coffee traceability, and agricultural entrepreneurship.
He said improved participation in coffee production has enabled many households to increase financial independence, invest in property, support education, and improve access to healthcare.
The conference brings together stakeholders from across Africa and beyond to explore opportunities for strengthening the continent’s coffee value chain, expanding markets, and improving the livelihoods of coffee-growing communities.

title: Govt Considers UPDF Recruitment for Skilled Ugandan Returnees From South Africa
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The government is exploring the possibility of recruiting skilled Ugandans recently repatriated from South Africa into the Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) as part of efforts to support their reintegration and utilise their professional…
title_en: Govt Considers UPDF Recruitment for Skilled Ugandan Returnees From South Africa
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The government is exploring the possibility of recruiting skilled Ugandans recently repatriated from South Africa into the Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) as part of efforts to support their reintegration and utilise their professional…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 15, 2026 - The government is exploring the possibility of recruiting skilled Ugandans recently repatriated from South Africa into the Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF) as part of efforts to support their reintegration and utilise their professional expertise.
Minister for Gender, Labour and Social Development Lt Gen Henry Tumukunde said he would engage the Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, on the possibility of absorbing qualified returnees who have expressed interest in joining the military.
Tumukunde made the remarks while addressing more than 1,000 returnees undergoing rehabilitation and ideological orientation at the National Leadership Institute (NALI) Kyankwanzi.
Several returnees reportedly expressed interest in serving in the UPDF, citing skills in professional driving, forensic work, and other technical fields acquired while living abroad.
The minister said the country could benefit from their expertise, particularly those who worked in specialised occupations in South Africa, including transport, engineering, and technical services.
He described the 1,030 Ugandans currently at Kyankwanzi, including 331 children, as a valuable pool of skilled citizens capable of contributing to national development.
According to Tumukunde, the returnees include plumbers, refrigeration and cooling system technicians, machine operators, dog handlers, drivers, and other professionals.
He said the government initially anticipated challenges in reintegrating the returnees but found instead a group of disciplined and skilled individuals who could support economic growth.
The minister said authorities plan to identify highly skilled returnees and support them to train other Ugandans, establish businesses, and provide services through organised pools of skilled workers.
He highlighted existing government programmes, including the GROW Project, Youth Livelihood Programme, and Emyooga, as potential avenues to support entrepreneurship and economic reintegration.
Tumukunde also urged the returnees to respect Ugandan laws and avoid criminal behaviour as they rebuild their lives after returning home.
The minister said Uganda remains open to receiving citizens abroad who wish to return, describing the returnees as an opportunity rather than a burden.
The government estimates that about one million Ugandans live in South Africa, although only about 1,000 have returned under the first phase of the voluntary repatriation exercise.
Meanwhile, NRM Chapter Chairperson in South Africa Luzige Isma encouraged Ugandans still living in South Africa who wish to return home to remain patient and follow official government communication.
The rehabilitation and orientation programme at NALI Kyankwanzi is being coordinated by the National Secretariat for Patriotism Corps and includes sessions on citizenship, personal security, crime prevention, and responsible use of social media.
The returnees are expected to complete the programme on July 17, 2026, during a pass-out ceremony expected to be presided over by President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.
The initiative aims to support the returnees’ reintegration while connecting them with employment opportunities, skills development programmes, and government-backed enterprise initiatives.
Conclusion
Uganda’s coffee export performance in May 2026 highlights both the resilience and vulnerability of one of the country’s most important economic sectors. While short-term earnings were affected by declining international prices and reduced export volumes, the sector continues to demonstrate strong underlying growth, supported by increased production, expanding cultivation areas and sustained global demand.
The decline in monthly revenues underscores the need for greater resilience against global commodity price fluctuations, which remain beyond Uganda’s control. Strengthening value addition, improving market diversification and investing in productivity and quality enhancement will be critical to ensuring farmers and exporters capture greater value from the coffee value chain.
With annual export earnings exceeding $2 billion, coffee remains a strategic pillar of Uganda’s economy and a major source of foreign exchange. The challenge ahead will be converting production growth into long-term income stability for farmers and stronger competitiveness in international markets.
By Jeff Buleli

title: Seven Killed in Suspected ADF Attack on Outskirts of Beni
excerpt: Beni, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 – At least seven people, including four civilians and three soldiers, were killed in a predawn attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on the outskirts of Beni city in North Kivu, marking another deadly episode in the region's…
title_en: Seven Killed in Suspected ADF Attack on Outskirts of Beni
excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 – At least seven people, including four civilians and three soldiers, were killed in a predawn attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on the outskirts of Beni city in North Kivu, marking another deadly episode in the region's…
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 – At least seven people, including four civilians and three soldiers, were killed in a predawn attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on the outskirts of Beni city in North Kivu, marking another deadly episode in the region's ongoing insecurity.
The assault targeted the neighborhoods of Sayo and Matembo in Mulekera Commune during the early hours of Tuesday. According to local reports, four civilians were killed in the Mbutaba and Vuthala areas, where the attackers reportedly used bladed weapons during the assault. Several other civilians sustained injuries and were taken to nearby health facilities for treatment.
Local volunteers recovered the victims' bodies, which were later transferred to the morgue pending burial.
Community representatives credited the intervention of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) with preventing an even higher death toll, while urging residents to remain vigilant despite the heightened security response.
The attack also targeted security forces. According to security sources, government troops were caught in an ambush during the operation, resulting in the deaths of at least three soldiers.
The latest violence has triggered widespread panic across Sayo and neighboring communities. Fearing further attacks, many residents fled their homes, abandoning their belongings as they sought refuge in central Beni and other areas considered safer.
The incident highlights the persistent security challenges facing the Beni region, where repeated attacks by armed groups continue to cause civilian casualties, population displacement, and heightened humanitarian concerns.

title: Walikale Civil Society Urges Immediate FARDC Deployment After AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Ikobo
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 - Civil society leaders in Walikale Territory have called on the Congolese government to urgently deploy the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) to several villages in the Ikobo area following the announced withdrawal…
title_en: Walikale Civil Society Urges Immediate FARDC Deployment After AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Ikobo
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 - Civil society leaders in Walikale Territory have called on the Congolese government to urgently deploy the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) to several villages in the Ikobo area following the announced withdrawal…
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, July 14, 2026 - Civil society leaders in Walikale Territory have called on the Congolese government to urgently deploy the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) to several villages in the Ikobo area following the announced withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters, warning that the move could represent a tactical repositioning rather than a genuine retreat.
The appeal concerns the villages of Buleusa, Kateku, Bukumbirwa, and Rusamambu, where local civil society believes a rapid military deployment is necessary to secure the area and facilitate the safe return of thousands of displaced families who fled the fighting.
Despite reports that AFC/M23 forces have withdrawn from parts of Ikobo, civil society leaders remain skeptical about the rebels' intentions. They argue that the withdrawal may be part of a broader strategy to regroup and reinforce positions ahead of future military operations elsewhere in North and South Kivu.
Local representatives warned against allowing a security vacuum to emerge, stressing that the absence of government forces could enable armed groups to reoccupy the abandoned areas or allow other militias to establish a presence.
Civil society also urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report any suspicious movements, emphasizing that community cooperation remains essential while security conditions remain uncertain.
The call comes just days after AFC/M23 fighters reportedly pulled back from several localities in the Ikobo area. Although the development has raised hopes for the gradual return of displaced populations, local leaders maintain that lasting security can only be achieved through a sustained FARDC presence capable of preventing renewed violence.
As authorities consider their response, thousands of displaced residents continue to await conditions that would allow them to return safely to their communities, while local civil society organizations continue to advocate for stronger security measures to stabilize this part of Walikale Territory.

title_en: Uganda Breweries Contributes Shs1.127 Trillion to National Economy
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 14, 2026 - Uganda Breweries Limited (UBL) contributed an estimated Shs1.127 trillion to Uganda’s economy in 2024 through its operations, supply chain activities and wider business network, according to a new economic assessment. The report shows that the…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 14, 2026 - Uganda Breweries Limited (UBL) contributed an estimated Shs1.127 trillion to Uganda’s economy in 2024 through its operations, supply chain activities and wider business network, according to a new economic assessment.

title: Analyst Christian Moleka Says Military Performance Remains DRC's Main Challenge in Eastern Conflict
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - Congolese political analyst Christian Moleka has argued that the Democratic Republic of Congo's greatest challenge in the conflict in the east remains military rather than diplomatic, despite recent international support for Kinshasa's position.…
title_en: Analyst Christian Moleka Says Military Performance Remains DRC's Main Challenge in Eastern Conflict
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - Congolese political analyst Christian Moleka has argued that the Democratic Republic of Congo's greatest challenge in the conflict in the east remains military rather than diplomatic, despite recent international support for Kinshasa's position.…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - Congolese political analyst Christian Moleka has argued that the Democratic Republic of Congo's greatest challenge in the conflict in the east remains military rather than diplomatic, despite recent international support for Kinshasa's position.
Speaking during an online discussion hosted by journalist Stanis Bujakera Tshiamala, Moleka assessed the government's military and diplomatic strategies in response to the conflict involving the AFC/M23.
He noted that between 2022 and 2025, the DRC allocated approximately US$4.5 billion to defense under its military programming law. However, he said the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have been unable to regain the strategic initiative since the capture of Bunagana in 2022, describing the operational results as falling short of expectations.
While acknowledging significant diplomatic achievements, Moleka pointed to what he described as a disconnect between international support and developments on the battlefield. He cited measures including European sanctions against Rwanda, growing international recognition of the conflict, and the unanimous adoption of a United Nations Security Council resolution addressing the crisis.
Despite these diplomatic gains, he argued that they have yet to produce decisive changes on the ground. Referring to recent assessments of the conflict, Moleka noted that AFC/M23 has continued to expand the territory under its control since the Doha agreements, illustrating what he described as the limited practical impact of diplomatic efforts alone.
According to the analyst, military capacity remains the decisive factor in strengthening the country's diplomatic position. He compared diplomacy and military operations to two complementary elements that must work together, arguing that international negotiations require credible military leverage to achieve lasting results.
Moleka warned that diplomatic momentum could lose its effectiveness if it is not supported by stronger military performance, emphasizing that battlefield realities continue to shape political negotiations.
Looking beyond the immediate situation, he characterized the conflict as a prolonged war of attrition that has evolved over nearly three decades. In his view, the central challenge is no longer the intensity of individual military engagements but the ability of both the state and its institutions to sustain a long-term strategy combining military resilience with diplomatic engagement.

title: Stable Congolese Franc Offers Economic Relief and Strengthens Confidence in Local Markets
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The relative stability of the Congolese franc against foreign currencies is increasingly becoming a key factor influencing the daily economic realities of households, businesses, and consumers across the Democratic Republic of Congo. Although…
title_en: Stable Congolese Franc Offers Economic Relief and Strengthens Confidence in Local Markets
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The relative stability of the Congolese franc against foreign currencies is increasingly becoming a key factor influencing the daily economic realities of households, businesses, and consumers across the Democratic Republic of Congo. Although…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The relative stability of the Congolese franc against foreign currencies is increasingly becoming a key factor influencing the daily economic realities of households, businesses, and consumers across the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Although exchange rate figures published daily by the Central Bank of Congo (BCC) may appear to be technical data reserved for economists and financial institutions, they directly affect the prices of goods, household purchasing power, and business decisions.
The latest indicative exchange rates published by the BCC show that the Congolese franc is operating in a more stable monetary environment, a development that authorities and economic observers consider important for controlling inflation and improving economic predictability.
A stable exchange rate matters because a significant portion of goods consumed in the country depend on imports or foreign currency transactions. Fuel, medicines, construction materials, spare parts, industrial equipment, electronic products, and some food items are often affected by movements in the dollar exchange rate.
When the dollar rises sharply against the Congolese franc, import costs increase, and businesses frequently pass these additional expenses on to consumers through higher prices. Conversely, greater exchange rate stability allows companies to better anticipate costs and avoid frequent price adjustments.
The role of the Central Bank is not to impose a fixed exchange rate but to maintain an orderly market through monetary policy tools. These include managing liquidity in circulation, adjusting interest rates, intervening in the foreign exchange market when necessary, and managing foreign exchange reserves.
The objective is to limit excessive fluctuations that could destabilize economic activity while maintaining confidence among households, investors, and businesses.
The daily publication of indicative exchange rates also contributes to greater transparency in the currency market. While banks and authorized exchange offices may apply slightly different rates, the official benchmark provides citizens and economic operators with a reference point for comparing offers and making better-informed decisions.
This transparency helps reduce information gaps between market participants and encourages healthier competition among foreign exchange operators. With a publicly available reference rate, excessive margins become easier to identify, pushing financial institutions and exchange bureaus to offer more competitive conditions.
For businesses, currency stability provides greater visibility when planning investments, importing goods, signing contracts, or managing operational costs. Predictable exchange conditions reduce uncertainty and allow companies to develop longer-term strategies.
Economists also emphasize the importance of expectations in maintaining monetary stability. When businesses and households believe that a currency will lose value rapidly, they may rush to purchase foreign currency, contributing to additional pressure on the exchange rate.
By contrast, confidence in the ability of monetary authorities to preserve stability can reduce speculative behavior and reinforce market confidence.
The benefits of a stable Congolese franc extend across the economy. For households, it helps preserve purchasing power and improve visibility over daily expenses. For traders, it facilitates stock management and pricing decisions. For companies, it supports investment planning. For financial institutions and public authorities, it contributes to a more predictable economic environment.
However, maintaining this stability will depend on the continuation of consistent macroeconomic policies and the confidence of economic actors in the national currency.
Beyond exchange rate figures, the stability of the Congolese franc reflects a broader economic challenge: building lasting trust between citizens, businesses, and institutions. A currency gains strength not only through monetary policies but also through the confidence placed in it by the society it serves.
Social and Health

title: DRC Lawmaker Calls for Greater Military Support to End ADF Violence in Beni
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - National Assembly member Enock Batsotsi Nyamwisi has called for increased financial and logistical support for the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), arguing that sustained resources are essential to defeating the Allied…
title_en: DRC Lawmaker Calls for Greater Military Support to End ADF Violence in Beni
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - National Assembly member Enock Batsotsi Nyamwisi has called for increased financial and logistical support for the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), arguing that sustained resources are essential to defeating the Allied…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - National Assembly member Enock Batsotsi Nyamwisi has called for increased financial and logistical support for the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), arguing that sustained resources are essential to defeating the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and ending the persistent violence in Beni and surrounding areas.
The appeal came during a meeting in Kinshasa with General Jacques Ychaligonza Nduru, Deputy Chief of Staff of the FARDC in charge of operations and intelligence. The discussions focused on ongoing military operations against the ADF, whose attacks continue to cause civilian casualties and insecurity in North Kivu.
Representing Beni Territory, Batsotsi conveyed the concerns of local communities affected by repeated attacks and urged the government to ensure that military operations are backed by adequate funding, logistics, and infrastructure.
He stressed that military campaigns cannot succeed without sufficient operational resources, expressing confidence that the government would provide the army with the support needed to sustain operations on the ground.
During the meeting, General Ychaligonza reportedly outlined the implementation of an integrated interprovincial operational plan designed to strengthen coordination among security forces across provinces affected by ADF activities. The strategy aims to improve joint military operations and enhance efforts to neutralize the armed group.
According to the lawmaker, the senior military officer also reaffirmed the General Staff's commitment, under the leadership of President Félix Tshisekedi, to restoring the country's territorial integrity and addressing ongoing security threats.
Batsotsi further emphasized the importance of strengthening cooperation between civilians and the military, describing public support as a key element in efforts to combat both the ADF insurgency and broader security challenges in eastern DRC.
He also called for stricter military discipline, criticizing the existence of illegal checkpoints allegedly established by some soldiers in operational areas. Such practices, he argued, restrict civilian movement and undermine public confidence in the armed forces, stressing that professionalism and discipline remain essential to the success of military operations against armed groups.
Conclusion
The first half of July 2026 underscores the complex and multifaceted challenges confronting the Democratic Republic of Congo, revealing a persistent gap between notable diplomatic advances, institutional reforms, and the difficult realities unfolding on the ground.
On the international stage, the DRC continued to strengthen its diplomatic positioning by leveraging its rotating presidency of the United Nations Security Council to advance discussions on conflict-related sexual violence and promote natural resource governance as a key pillar of sustainable peace. At the national level, Kinshasa pursued institutional consolidation through reforms aimed at strengthening anti-corruption mechanisms, enhancing financial transparency with CENAREF’s strategic integration into the Egmont Group, and promoting economic participation through the implementation of the Local Content Law.
Nevertheless, these political and diplomatic achievements remain overshadowed by the worsening security and humanitarian situation in eastern DRC. Despite ongoing mediation efforts, including the Doha peace process and the Washington Agreement framework, armed violence continues to intensify, with the AFC/M23 maintaining territorial influence through external support and benefiting from illicit mineral networks operating across borders. Internal tensions within the movement, combined with the continued activity of other armed groups such as the ADF, further complicate efforts to restore stability, while civilians remain exposed to displacement, human rights violations, and public health emergencies, including the ongoing Ebola outbreak.
At the same time, the DRC has continued to reinforce its image as a strategic actor in global climate and resource governance, highlighting its role as a “solution country” through initiatives focused on forest conservation, sustainable mining, and energy development. However, translating this international recognition into lasting domestic transformation remains the central challenge.
Ultimately, the first half of July demonstrates that the DRC’s future trajectory will depend on its ability to bridge the gap between diplomatic commitments and realities on the ground. Sustainable peace and development will require not only stronger security capabilities and effective enforcement of state authority, but also deeper reforms in governance, responsible management of natural resources, and renewed confidence between institutions, communities, and international partners.
By Jeff Buleli

title: Universities Put Under Spotlight as Uganda Steps Up HIV Prevention Drive Ahead of 2030 Goal
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - Universities are facing renewed scrutiny over their role in preventing HIV infections among young people as Uganda intensifies efforts to end HIV/AIDS as a public health threat by 2030. With five years remaining to meet the national target,…
title_en: Universities Put Under Spotlight as Uganda Steps Up HIV Prevention Drive Ahead of 2030 Goal
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - Universities are facing renewed scrutiny over their role in preventing HIV infections among young people as Uganda intensifies efforts to end HIV/AIDS as a public health threat by 2030. With five years remaining to meet the national target,…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - Universities are facing renewed scrutiny over their role in preventing HIV infections among young people as Uganda intensifies efforts to end HIV/AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
With five years remaining to meet the national target, health officials have urged higher education institutions to strengthen student-focused HIV prevention programmes, warning that young people remain vulnerable due to risky sexual behaviour, limited access to prevention services, and gaps in awareness.
A major concern raised by health authorities is whether universities are complying with the national HIV policy requirement to allocate 0.1 percent of their budgets towards HIV prevention initiatives targeting students, staff, and surrounding communities.
Health officials say institutions that fail to provide funding for HIV programmes are not fully implementing national guidelines.
At Kyambogo University, student leaders said the institution has introduced initiatives including medical camps offering HIV testing services and distributing preventive materials.
Kyambogo University Guild President Edward Agaba acknowledged that while prevention efforts are ongoing, some students continue to engage in behaviours that increase their risk of infection.
He encouraged students to practise safer sexual behaviours and regularly know their HIV status.
At Makerere University, student leaders said they are working with the university hospital to expand HIV awareness campaigns, including plans for a health week offering free testing services and prevention materials.
Makerere University Guild Health Minister Ebenezer Wamezaya said the institution is also promoting peer education programmes to encourage open discussions on sexual and reproductive health among students.
Health organisations have also increased engagement with young people through awareness campaigns and youth-led platforms.
The Executive Director of Reproductive Health Uganda, Jackson Chekweko, said involving young people directly in HIV prevention discussions is essential for improving access to accurate information and changing behaviours.
He said youth-led platforms, including online health programmes and inter-university dialogues, provide spaces where students can openly discuss sexual and reproductive health challenges.
The Uganda AIDS Commission has called on universities to take greater responsibility by establishing effective prevention programmes before seeking external support.
Dr Daniel Byamukama, Head of HIV Prevention at the commission, said institutions must first put in place measures that educate students about HIV prevention and encourage responsible choices.
A 2024 Uganda AIDS Commission report indicated that more than 5,000 new HIV infections occurred among young people aged between 15 and 24 years.
Byamukama said the commission remains ready to support universities but stressed that institutions must comply with national requirements, including allocating resources for HIV prevention activities.
As Uganda approaches its 2030 HIV elimination target, health experts say sustained prevention efforts among university students will be critical in reducing new infections and HIV-related deaths.
They are urging young people to take greater responsibility for their health by knowing their HIV status, practising safer sex, or choosing abstinence.

title: Mutamba’s Defense Challenges Trial Procedure and Raises Rights Concerns Before Court of Cassation
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The trial involving former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba opened before the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa, with his defense immediately challenging what it described as several procedural irregularities and violations of defense rights. The first…
title_en: Mutamba’s Defense Challenges Trial Procedure and Raises Rights Concerns Before Court of Cassation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The trial involving former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba opened before the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa, with his defense immediately challenging what it described as several procedural irregularities and violations of defense rights. The first…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The trial involving former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba opened before the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa, with his defense immediately challenging what it described as several procedural irregularities and violations of defense rights.
The first hearing, held on Monday, July 13, concerns Constant Mutamba and Chancard Bolukola, former interim coordinating director of the Fund for the Reparation and Compensation of Victims of Illegal Activities in Uganda (FRIVAO), who is currently detained at Makala Central Prison and facing separate proceedings before the Kinshasa/Gombe Court of Appeal.
According to the prosecution, the two defendants are considered accomplices in a case involving alleged irregularities in the management of FRIVAO funds. The charges focus notably on several financial operations, including a payment of $14.3 million to Congo Energy linked to a contested public contract.
Other transactions cited by prosecutors include $4 million allocated to the Congolese Institute for Nature Conservation (ICCN), $200,000 transferred to the Tshopo Provincial Assembly, more than $1 million paid to Divo SARL for documentary production, and over $700,000 directed to Tropic Architecture.
Following the hearing, lawyer Emiphe Munganga, representing Constant Mutamba, criticized the conduct of the proceedings and accused the judicial process of failing to fully respect the rights of the defense.
The lawyer claimed that several attorneys were initially prevented from entering the courthouse, arguing that this situation affected the proper preparation and participation of the defense team from the beginning of the hearing.
He also stated that the defense had raised several preliminary objections, including concerns over the notification process, but that these arguments were not taken into consideration by the Court.
According to Munganga, Constant Mutamba was never formally summoned by the prosecution before the case reached the Court of Cassation and only became aware of the proceedings through public information circulating on social media.
The defense further contested the investigation process, arguing that the former minister had not been questioned by prosecutors despite legal requirements that a defendant be heard before proceedings advance.
Another objection raised concerned the participation of a civil party before the Court of Cassation. The defense argued that legal provisions governing the high court do not allow such participation and said the issue was not sufficiently addressed during the hearing.
While refusing to comment on the substance of the accusations, the lawyer emphasized that his criticism focused exclusively on procedural matters and the need to ensure a fair judicial process.
The Court adjourned the case for two weeks. The defense expressed concern that this timeframe would not allow sufficient preparation, given the volume of documents involved in the proceedings.
According to Munganga, the case files from both the Court of Cassation and the Court of Appeal contain thousands of documents, potentially exceeding 5,000 pages. The defense had requested a one-month delay to study the files but said the request was rejected.
Despite these concerns, the defense indicated that it would continue participating in the proceedings while awaiting future developments.
The current case comes after Constant Mutamba was previously convicted by the Court of Cassation in September 2025 in a separate case involving funds intended for the construction of a prison facility in Kisangani. He was sentenced to three years of hard labor and received a five-year ban from holding public office.
During that previous trial, prosecutors had requested a heavier sentence, including ten years of hard labor and additional restrictions on political rights. The former minister has continued to contest aspects of the judicial process surrounding the cases against him.

Another objection raised concerned the participation of a civil party before the Court of Cassation. The defense argued that legal provisions governing the high court do not allow such participation and said the issue was not sufficiently addressed during the hearing.
While refusing to comment on the substance of the accusations, the lawyer emphasized that his criticism focused exclusively on procedural matters and the need to ensure a fair judicial process.
The Court adjourned the case for two weeks. The defense expressed concern that this timeframe would not allow sufficient preparation, given the volume of documents involved in the proceedings.
According to Munganga, the case files from both the Court of Cassation and the Court of Appeal contain thousands of documents, potentially exceeding 5,000 pages. The defense had requested a one-month delay to study the files but said the request was rejected.
Despite these concerns, the defense indicated that it would continue participating in the proceedings while awaiting future developments.
The current case comes after Constant Mutamba was previously convicted by the Court of Cassation in September 2025 in a separate case involving funds intended for the construction of a prison facility in Kisangani. He was sentenced to three years of hard labor and received a five-year ban from holding public office.
During that previous trial, prosecutors had requested a heavier sentence, including ten years of hard labor and additional restrictions on political rights. The former minister has continued to contest aspects of the judicial process surrounding the cases against him.

title: Kinshasa Deploys Officers to Goma to Support Ceasefire Monitoring Mission

title_en: Kinshasa Deploys Officers to Goma to Support Ceasefire Monitoring Mission
excerpt_en: GOMA, July 14, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has deployed three military officers to Goma to participate in efforts to monitor the ceasefire in the country’s eastern region, as part of a new international verification mechanism. The officers - Lt.…
body_en:
GOMA, July 14, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has deployed three military officers to Goma to participate in efforts to monitor the ceasefire in the country’s eastern region, as part of a new international verification mechanism.
The officers - Lt. Col. Ben Epule Cosmas, who heads the delegation, Maj. Lokuli Bofanda Fredy, and Maj. Kitoko Dimonekene André - arrived in Goma on July 13 aboard a United Nations peacekeeping mission aircraft. They were accompanied by Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Deputy Head of MONUSCO.
The deployment follows discussions held on July 2 between Defense Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita and MONUSCO Head James Swan on establishing mechanisms to strengthen monitoring of the ceasefire in eastern DRC.
The three Congolese representatives will join the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), a new body created through commitments reached during the Doha peace talks between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, as well as the Washington peace agreement.
Operating from Goma, the EJVM+ is tasked with monitoring civilian protection, supporting security sector reforms, and overseeing compliance with ceasefire commitments agreed under the Doha and Washington frameworks.
The mechanism is led by Zambian Brig. Gen. Charles Simuyuni Nakeempaa, appointed to head the body, with Angolan Col. Arlindo Sebastião Vandunem Fernandes serving as deputy.
Under the agreement establishing the EJVM+, signed in Montreux, Switzerland, on April 14, 2026, the DRC government and AFC/M23 are each expected to appoint three representatives, while additional members will come from international organizations.
MONUSCO, which remains responsible for operational security support in eastern DRC, will provide logistical assistance to the mechanism, including transportation support through its aircraft to facilitate field operations in areas where monitoring activities are required.

title: Tanganyika Governor Pledges Tough Response to Alleged AFC/M23 Infiltration
excerpt: Kalemie, Tanganyika, July 14, 2026 - Tanganyika Governor Christian Kitungwa Muteba has reaffirmed his administration's commitment to preventing any infiltration by the AFC/M23 rebellion following a security operation in Kalemie that resulted in the arrest of several military…
title_en: Tanganyika Governor Pledges Tough Response to Alleged AFC/M23 Infiltration
excerpt_en: Kalemie, Tanganyika, July 14, 2026 - Tanganyika Governor Christian Kitungwa Muteba has reaffirmed his administration's commitment to preventing any infiltration by the AFC/M23 rebellion following a security operation in Kalemie that resulted in the arrest of several military…
body_en:
Kalemie, Tanganyika, July 14, 2026 - Tanganyika Governor Christian Kitungwa Muteba has reaffirmed his administration's commitment to preventing any infiltration by the AFC/M23 rebellion following a security operation in Kalemie that resulted in the arrest of several military deserters and individuals suspected of posing security risks.
Speaking upon his return to Kalemie, the governor sought to reassure residents amid heightened security concerns, insisting that Tanganyika would not become a base of operations for AFC/M23 or its alleged supporters.
His remarks came after the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out a large-scale security operation across several neighborhoods of the provincial capital. According to the military, the operation led to the arrest of military deserters as well as individuals suspected of engaging in activities considered detrimental to public security.
The detained individuals were transferred to Kalemie Central Prison, where they remain in custody pending judicial review.
Governor Kitungwa warned that provincial authorities were closely monitoring alleged attempts to infiltrate the province and stated that security services would continue to identify and apprehend anyone suspected of threatening Tanganyika's stability.
The operation follows growing concerns over possible armed infiltration, which have contributed to increased anxiety among local residents.
Tanganyika's heightened security posture reflects broader efforts by the Congolese authorities to prevent the conflict affecting eastern DRC from spreading beyond North and South Kivu, where AFC/M23 continues to operate in several areas. Bordering South Kivu, Tanganyika has become an important focus of preventive security measures aimed at detecting and deterring potential incursions by armed groups.
Provincial authorities have continued to encourage residents to cooperate with defense and security services by reporting suspicious activities while emphasizing that maintaining public vigilance remains an essential component of the province's security strategy.
Through these measures and public assurances, the provincial government aims to reinforce confidence in the ability of the FARDC and security services to preserve stability and protect the territorial integrity of Tanganyika Province.

title: Parliament Calls for Review of University District Quota Sponsorship Scheme
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - Parliament has adopted a motion urging the government to review the university district quota sponsorship scheme, with legislators arguing that the current allocation formula does not adequately address inequalities in access to higher…
title_en: Parliament Calls for Review of University District Quota Sponsorship Scheme
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - Parliament has adopted a motion urging the government to review the university district quota sponsorship scheme, with legislators arguing that the current allocation formula does not adequately address inequalities in access to higher…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - Parliament has adopted a motion urging the government to review the university district quota sponsorship scheme, with legislators arguing that the current allocation formula does not adequately address inequalities in access to higher education.
The motion, tabled by Bardege-Layibi MP Martin Ojara Mapenduzi, seeks reforms to increase opportunities for students from poor, rural, and underserved districts seeking government-sponsored university education.
Mapenduzi argued that the district quota scheme, introduced in 2004 to promote equitable access to higher education, has lost part of its original purpose because allocations are largely determined by district population size.
He said smaller rural districts continue to receive fewer government sponsorship slots despite facing greater educational challenges, limiting opportunities for disadvantaged students.
Under the current government sponsorship arrangement, about 4,000 students are admitted annually to public universities.
Of these, 3,000 slots, representing 75 percent, are allocated through the national merit scheme, while 896 slots are reserved for the district quota system.
The remaining positions are shared between the sports scheme, which receives 40 slots, and the special needs scheme, which receives 64 slots.
State Minister for Higher Education John Chrysostom Muyingo told Parliament that the number of students benefiting through the district quota system is higher than the figures presented in the motion.
He said that under the Higher Education Students’ Financing Scheme, 1,228 out of 2,048 students selected in the current academic year were admitted through the district quota arrangement.
Despite the clarification, legislators supported the proposed review, maintaining that the current formula continues to disadvantage students from rural and marginalised communities.
The motion was adopted with amendments after Muyingo assured Parliament that government would consider and implement the recommendations, depending on available resources.
The review is expected to focus on creating a more equitable sponsorship model that better supports students from disadvantaged backgrounds and strengthens access to university education across Uganda.

title: AFD Reinforces Partnership with Kinshasa to Protect Congo Basin Forests and Fight Climate Change
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and France are strengthening their cooperation on environmental protection and climate action, with a renewed focus on preserving the Congo Basin forests and involving local communities in sustainable resource…
title_en: AFD Reinforces Partnership with Kinshasa to Protect Congo Basin Forests and Fight Climate Change
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and France are strengthening their cooperation on environmental protection and climate action, with a renewed focus on preserving the Congo Basin forests and involving local communities in sustainable resource…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 14, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and France are strengthening their cooperation on environmental protection and climate action, with a renewed focus on preserving the Congo Basin forests and involving local communities in sustainable resource management.
The Minister of Environment, Sustainable Development and New Climate Economy, Marie Nyange Ndambo, met in Kinshasa with Christophe Lecourtier, Director General of the French Development Agency (AFD) Group, during his first official visit to the DRC.
The discussions focused on strengthening Franco-Congolese cooperation in key areas, including forest conservation, climate initiatives, and support for strategic institutions such as the National Institute of Biomedical Research (INRB).
Christophe Lecourtier praised the environmental commitments undertaken by the Congolese government and reaffirmed France’s support for the DRC’s climate ambitions. He emphasized that protecting forests remains one of the AFD Group’s major priorities, given the global importance of the Congo Basin ecosystem.
“Forests are at the forefront of our priorities, and the challenge is to move from commitments to concrete actions,” he said, highlighting the need for practical solutions capable of producing measurable results.
The AFD chief also welcomed the role assigned to the DRC under the Belém Appeal framework, which places the country at the center of global efforts to preserve the Congo Basin forests. He expressed France’s willingness to support Congolese initiatives ahead of the next United Nations Climate Conference (COP), scheduled to take place in Turkey.
A major focus of the discussions was the Z3D pilot project, an initiative designed to directly involve local communities in reducing deforestation through financial incentives. The project aims to ensure that communities living near forest areas become key actors in conservation efforts while benefiting economically from environmental protection.
According to Christophe Lecourtier, the initiative could serve as a model beyond the DRC by demonstrating how local populations can be integrated into climate solutions through direct support mechanisms.
The AFD Director General also highlighted the global importance of Congolese forests and peatlands, stressing that their protection has consequences far beyond national borders. These ecosystems play a crucial role in carbon storage and climate regulation, affecting both African and global climate stability.
He warned that increasing climate disruptions, including extreme heat events affecting Europe and other regions, demonstrate the urgency of stronger international cooperation.
“Global warming can only be contained through partnerships with countries such as the DRC, which possess essential natural assets for slowing climate change,” he emphasized.
The visit reflects the strategic importance of the DRC within France’s development cooperation priorities. With more than €731 million allocated across 35 ongoing projects, the country remains one of the French Development Agency Group’s major areas of intervention in Central Africa.
Through its various entities, including AFD for public-sector financing, Proparco for private-sector support, and Expertise France for technical cooperation, the AFD Group continues to support projects aligned with sustainable development goals, including climate protection, biodiversity preservation, health-system strengthening, economic development, and social resilience.
As the DRC seeks to position itself as a global environmental actor, the strengthened partnership with France aims to transform the country’s vast forest resources into a foundation for sustainable development and international climate action.

title: Uganda Coffee Export Earnings Drop as Global Prices Weaken
excerpt: KAMPALA, July 14, 2026 - Uganda’s coffee export revenues declined sharply in May 2026 as falling international prices and reduced shipment volumes affected monthly earnings, despite strong growth recorded over the past year. Coffee export earnings fell to $151.7 million in…
title_en: Uganda Coffee Export Earnings Drop as Global Prices Weaken
excerpt_en: KAMPALA, July 14, 2026 - Uganda’s coffee export revenues declined sharply in May 2026 as falling international prices and reduced shipment volumes affected monthly earnings, despite strong growth recorded over the past year. Coffee export earnings fell to $151.7 million in…
body_en:
KAMPALA, July 14, 2026 - Uganda’s coffee export revenues declined sharply in May 2026 as falling international prices and reduced shipment volumes affected monthly earnings, despite strong growth recorded over the past year.
Coffee export earnings fell to $151.7 million in May 2026, compared with $242.5 million recorded during the same month in 2025.
Export volumes also decreased by 21.6 per cent, dropping from 788,115 bags to 617,491 60-kilogram bags during the period.
The decline was linked to weaker global coffee prices, driven by expectations of increased supply from major producing countries, particularly Brazil, where forecasts pointed to a stronger upcoming harvest.
The average price of Ugandan coffee exports declined to $4.10 per kilogram in May, compared with $5.10 per kilogram during the same period a year earlier.
Despite the monthly decline, Uganda’s coffee sector maintained strong annual performance, with exports reaching 8.6 million bags worth $2.3 billion over the 12 months ending May 2026.
The annual figures represented growth in both export volumes and earnings, supported by increased production, expansion of coffee-growing areas and efforts to improve quality and competitiveness.
Italy remained Uganda’s largest coffee export destination during May, accounting for more than a quarter of total exports, reflecting continued demand for Ugandan coffee in European markets.
Coffee remains one of Uganda’s most important sources of foreign exchange and supports millions of households involved in farming, processing and trade.
However, the latest decline highlights the sector’s exposure to global commodity market changes, with prices affected by weather conditions, production forecasts and international demand.
Industry players are expected to continue monitoring global supply trends, especially developments in major producing countries, as Uganda seeks to maintain growth in its coffee export sector.

title: Buganda Kingdom and Health Ministry Begin Distribution of 4.7 Million Mosquito Nets to Fight Malaria
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - The Buganda Kingdom, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, has launched a campaign to distribute more than 4.7 million insecticide-treated mosquito nets across Buganda as part of efforts to reduce malaria infections. The distribution…
title_en: Buganda Kingdom and Health Ministry Begin Distribution of 4.7 Million Mosquito Nets to Fight Malaria
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - The Buganda Kingdom, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, has launched a campaign to distribute more than 4.7 million insecticide-treated mosquito nets across Buganda as part of efforts to reduce malaria infections. The distribution…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 14, 2026 - The Buganda Kingdom, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, has launched a campaign to distribute more than 4.7 million insecticide-treated mosquito nets across Buganda as part of efforts to reduce malaria infections.
The distribution campaign was launched at Bulange, where Buganda Kingdom leaders urged communities to strengthen malaria prevention measures and ensure proper use of the mosquito nets.
Buganda’s Second Deputy Katikkiro and Kingdom Treasurer Robert Waggwa Nsibirwa encouraged residents to eliminate mosquito breeding sites by draining stagnant water, clearing bushes around homes, and seeking medical advice from qualified health professionals.
He cautioned the public against self-medication and relying on unverified health information from social media, urging people to seek treatment from trained healthcare providers.
Nsibirwa also reminded beneficiaries that the mosquito nets are intended strictly for malaria prevention and should be used every night while sleeping.
He warned against misuse of the nets for activities such as fishing, making clothing, or other purposes, saying their primary goal is to protect families from malaria.
The Kingdom leader called on Buganda chiefs and local leaders to mobilise communities to collect and properly use the mosquito nets, while encouraging parents to ensure their children receive malaria vaccinations where the programme is available.
Ministry of Health Commissioner Dr Richard Kabanda thanked the Buganda Kingdom for supporting public health initiatives and urged communities to follow guidance from health workers.
He said the current campaign marks the fourth round of mosquito net distribution and stressed the importance of consistent malaria prevention practices.
Buganda Minister for Social Development and Health Choltilda Nakate Kikomeko reaffirmed the Kingdom’s commitment to improving healthcare outcomes among its people, describing prevention as a key foundation for community productivity.
Health officials said malaria remains a major public health challenge in Uganda, with available figures indicating that about 16 people die from malaria every day and the country remains among the nations with the highest malaria burden globally.
Authorities warned that malaria-related deaths continue to place a heavy social and economic burden on families and communities.
The campaign is expected to strengthen malaria prevention efforts across Buganda by increasing access to protective mosquito nets and promoting community awareness.

Kinshasa, July 13, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo is seeking to deepen its integration into international electrotechnical standards through a high-level working visit by François Yapo Ahoti, Regional Director for Africa of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), held from July 13 to 14 in Kinshasa.
The meeting, organized by the National Electrotechnical Committee of the DRC (IEC-DRC), brought together key stakeholders from the country’s energy and quality-control sectors, including representatives of the Congolese Control Office (OCC), the National Electricity Company (SNEL), and the IEC.
The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation between the IEC, OCC, and SNEL, with the objective of increasing the DRC’s participation in international standard-setting processes and promoting the adoption of global electrotechnical standards to support the development of a modern and sustainable electricity sector.
Representatives from the Congolese Control Office highlighted the strategic importance of international standards in improving the reliability, safety, and competitiveness of electrical infrastructure. The OCC reaffirmed its commitment, as the secretariat of the National Electrotechnical Committee, to advancing technical capacities, promoting compliance with IEC standards, and supporting the transformation of the country’s energy sector.
The visit was also presented as part of the government’s broader modernization agenda. Officials emphasized the role of national reforms and institutional cooperation in creating a stronger industrial environment and improving technical governance in key sectors.
For his part, François Yapo Ahoti praised the progress made by the DRC in promoting electrotechnical standardization and encouraged the country to continue strengthening its national committee. He stressed that international standards represent a critical tool for industrialization, electrical safety, technological innovation, and the global energy transition.
Highlighting the DRC’s significant energy and mineral potential, the IEC representative encouraged Kinshasa to pursue full membership within the International Electrotechnical Commission. Such membership would allow the country to play a greater role in developing international standards, attract more investment, and accelerate industrial and technological growth.
The first day of activities concluded with technical visits to SNEL’s laboratories and the OCC’s Technical Control Laboratory. The IEC delegation assessed the capabilities of both institutions in quality control, conformity assessment, and electrotechnical standardization.
The visit marks another step in the DRC’s efforts to strengthen technical cooperation, improve energy-sector governance, and position itself as a more competitive player in Africa’s industrial and technological development.
