title: Tadjourah Launches Initiative to Empower Young Entrepreneurs
excerpt: Tadjourah, July 6, 2026 - Djibouti's Tadjourah region has launched a new initiative to strengthen youth entrepreneurship, bringing together local authorities, development partners, and aspiring business owners in a bid to promote innovation, job creation, and sustainable…
title_en: Tadjourah Launches Initiative to Empower Young Entrepreneurs
excerpt_en: Tadjourah, July 6, 2026 - Djibouti's Tadjourah region has launched a new initiative to strengthen youth entrepreneurship, bringing together local authorities, development partners, and aspiring business owners in a bid to promote innovation, job creation, and sustainable…
body_en:
Tadjourah, July 6, 2026 - Djibouti's Tadjourah region has launched a new initiative to strengthen youth entrepreneurship, bringing together local authorities, development partners, and aspiring business owners in a bid to promote innovation, job creation, and sustainable economic growth.
The entrepreneurship awareness day, organized by the Club des Jeunes Entrepreneurs de Tadjourah (CJET), marked the beginning of a broader effort to build a stronger entrepreneurial ecosystem by equipping young people with the skills, knowledge, and support needed to turn business ideas into viable enterprises.
Held at the Regional Council headquarters, the event attracted entrepreneurs, students, job seekers, and project leaders, reflecting growing interest among the region's youth in entrepreneurship as a pathway to economic opportunity and self-employment.
Discussions focused on the realities of launching and managing businesses, the challenges facing young entrepreneurs, and the economic opportunities available in promising sectors across the region. Participants also explored the role of entrepreneurship in addressing youth unemployment while fostering local innovation and private sector development.
Local officials, representatives of development organizations, and experienced entrepreneurs participated in the event, sharing their professional experiences and encouraging young people to pursue their business ambitions through perseverance, innovation, and strategic planning. Speakers emphasized that successful enterprises are built on clear vision, adaptability, and sustained commitment.
The program also introduced participants to the key stages of business creation, available support mechanisms, and practical approaches for transforming innovative ideas into financially sustainable ventures. CJET presented its mentoring and coaching program, which aims to identify promising entrepreneurs and provide guidance throughout the development of their projects.
The initiative is supported by several national and international partners, including the European Union, the World Bank, the Center for Leadership and Entrepreneurship (CLE), and the Ministry Delegate for Innovation and the Digital Economy. Their collaboration is intended to strengthen entrepreneurial capacity and encourage the emergence of a new generation of business leaders capable of contributing to Djibouti's economic development.
Beyond the awareness campaign, organizers announced a series of follow-up activities that will provide selected participants with specialized training in entrepreneurial leadership, accounting, financial management, communication, and marketing. Participants will also receive technical support to refine their business plans ahead of the Tadjourah Regional Entrepreneurship Forum, scheduled for November, where they will have the opportunity to present their projects to investors and development partners.
The initiative reflects Tadjourah's broader commitment to promoting entrepreneurship as a driver of inclusive economic growth. By investing in youth skills, encouraging innovation, and expanding opportunities for business creation, the region aims to lay the foundation for a more resilient and diversified local economy.

title_en: Tanzanian Police Arrest Suspects Over Alleged Plot to Attack Officials
excerpt_en: DAR ES SALAAM, Tanzania, July 6, 2026 - Tanzanian police say they have arrested several suspects in connection with an alleged plot to organize unlawful protests and carry out violent attacks targeting government officials and public institutions. Police spokesperson David…
body_en:
DAR ES SALAAM, Tanzania, July 6, 2026 - Tanzanian police say they have arrested several suspects in connection with an alleged plot to organize unlawful protests and carry out violent attacks targeting government officials and public institutions.
Police spokesperson David Misime announced the arrests during a press briefing in Dar es Salaam, stating that security agencies had uncovered plans involving the use of social media and online groups to encourage acts of violence and public disorder.
According to police, the alleged plans included attacks on government officials, destruction of public and private property, arson targeting schools, and assaults on security personnel with the intention of seizing their weapons. Authorities said investigations are ongoing and that additional suspects remain under surveillance, although the number of those arrested has not been disclosed.
Police maintained that the country's security situation remains stable and urged the public to continue their daily activities while cooperating with law enforcement by reporting information that could help prevent criminal acts. Authorities said security agencies remain on alert to safeguard public order and national security.

title_en: Djibouti and France Expand Partnership on Vocational Training and Youth Employment
excerpt_en: Djibouti City, July 6, 2026 - Djibouti and France have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in vocational training and youth employment following a working meeting between Minister of Labor in charge of Formalization and Social Protection Yonis Ali Guedi…
body_en:
Djibouti City, July 6, 2026 - Djibouti and France have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in vocational training and youth employment following a working meeting between Minister of Labor in charge of Formalization and Social Protection Yonis Ali Guedi and French Ambassador Jérôme Bresson.
The discussions focused on reinforcing the long-standing partnership between the two countries while exploring new initiatives aimed at improving the employability of young people, strengthening the capacities of national institutions, and supporting ongoing reforms in Djibouti's vocational training sector.
Both sides reviewed the progress of the Skills program, now in its third year of implementation, highlighting its contribution to workforce development and discussing prospects for its future expansion.
The meeting also examined a new European Union-funded initiative designed to complement existing programs by promoting skills development and facilitating the professional integration of young people into the labor market.
The exchange underscored the shared objective of equipping Djibouti's workforce with the competencies needed to meet evolving economic demands while creating greater employment opportunities for the country's youth.
Concluding the meeting, the Djiboutian minister and the French ambassador reaffirmed the strength of bilateral relations and expressed their commitment to continuing cooperation in support of vocational training, employment creation, and the long-term social and economic integration of young people.

excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 1,561 confirmed Ebola cases and 506 deaths, as health authorities continue efforts to contain the outbreak in several parts of the country.
body_en:
KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 6, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 1,561 confirmed Ebola cases and 506 deaths, as health authorities continue efforts to contain the outbreak in several parts of the country.

The latest figures, released by the government on Sunday, indicate that the outbreak remains a major public health challenge, particularly in eastern regions where Ebola has historically been most prevalent.

Health authorities said response measures remain underway, including patient testing, treatment, contact tracing, and community awareness campaigns aimed at limiting further transmission of the virus.

Officials have urged the public to remain vigilant by avoiding contact with suspected Ebola cases and promptly reporting symptoms to health facilities to support early detection and containment efforts.

title_en: Rwanda and Israel Sign Cooperation Agreements on Education, Science and Research
excerpt_en: JERUSALEM, Israel, July 6, 2026 - Rwanda and Israel have signed new cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening collaboration in education, science, technology, higher education, and scientific research, as both countries reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral…
body_en:
JERUSALEM, Israel, July 6, 2026 - Rwanda and Israel have signed new cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening collaboration in education, science, technology, higher education, and scientific research, as both countries reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral relations.
The agreements were signed in Jerusalem by Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, and Israel's Foreign Minister, Gideon Moshe Sa'ar. Rwanda's Centre for International Cooperation (RCI) and Israel's Agency for International Development Cooperation (MASHAV) also concluded a partnership agreement to support development cooperation.
During the signing ceremony, the two ministers emphasized the historical ties between Rwanda and Israel, noting that both countries have rebuilt after periods of profound national tragedy and continue to prioritize resilience, innovation, and development. They said the new agreements would promote knowledge sharing, capacity building, academic exchanges, and joint initiatives in education and research.
Rwandan officials described the agreements as another step in deepening bilateral cooperation, while Israeli officials highlighted the partnership as an example of how countries can transform historical challenges into opportunities for growth and innovation. During the visit, Minister Nduhungirehe also toured several sites in Jerusalem, including the Western Wall and the Yad Vashem Holocaust Memorial.

title_en: Woman Arrested for Allegedly Defrauding Ugandan MP of Shs60 Million in Fake Government Scheme
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 6, 2026 - Ugandan authorities have arrested a 53-year-old businesswoman accused of defrauding a Member of Parliament of Shs60 million after allegedly posing as an official from the Office of the President. Investigators allege that the suspect convinced…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 6, 2026 - Ugandan authorities have arrested a 53-year-old businesswoman accused of defrauding a Member of Parliament of Shs60 million after allegedly posing as an official from the Office of the President.
Investigators allege that the suspect convinced the legislator she could facilitate access to government programmes and services for the MP's constituency, claiming to have influence within the presidency. Believing the promises, the MP reportedly transferred the funds in several instalments over a period beginning in June 2025.
The alleged scheme came to light after the legislator reported the matter to authorities, leading to the suspect's arrest.
Investigators are now examining whether the suspect used the same method to target other victims, raising concerns that the fraud may have extended beyond a single case.
Authorities have urged public officials and citizens to verify the identity and authority of individuals claiming to represent government institutions before making financial transactions or responding to requests involving public programmes.
The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine the full scope of the alleged fraud.

title: Sudan Finance Minister Rejects Claims of Foreign Deposit Behind Currency Stabilization
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 5, 2026 - Sudan’s Finance and Economic Planning Minister Gibril Ibrahim has denied reports that a foreign financial deposit was responsible for strengthening the Sudanese pound, saying government measures and economic policies helped stabilize the exchange rate…
title_en: Sudan Finance Minister Rejects Claims of Foreign Deposit Behind Currency Stabilization
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 5, 2026 - Sudan’s Finance and Economic Planning Minister Gibril Ibrahim has denied reports that a foreign financial deposit was responsible for strengthening the Sudanese pound, saying government measures and economic policies helped stabilize the exchange rate…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 5, 2026 - Sudan’s Finance and Economic Planning Minister Gibril Ibrahim has denied reports that a foreign financial deposit was responsible for strengthening the Sudanese pound, saying government measures and economic policies helped stabilize the exchange rate against major foreign currencies.
The minister said Sudan continues to face severe economic challenges caused by the ongoing war, which has disrupted production, increased demand for foreign currency, and placed additional pressure on citizens. He acknowledged the hardships faced by the population but said authorities were working to improve living conditions and develop solutions to support the economy.
Ibrahim said he had previously expected the US dollar to rise to around 10,000 Sudanese pounds in 2025 due to production shutdowns and economic disruptions. However, he argued that government interventions helped contain the currency’s decline and predicted further stabilization of the exchange rate on the parallel market.
Despite the improvement in the exchange rate, the minister admitted that lower currency rates have not yet translated into reduced prices for consumers.
He said the long-term solution to Sudan’s economic crisis depends on increasing domestic production and adding value to local goods rather than exporting raw materials.
Ibrahim also revealed that the government spends approximately 50 billion Sudanese pounds each month to support the electricity sector, covering maintenance, operations, and infrastructure rehabilitation in areas affected by the conflict.
On foreign relations, the minister said securing international support during wartime remains difficult, stressing that alliances are built around shared interests. He added that strengthening state resources and financing the war effort remain key priorities, describing the economic pressure facing Sudan as part of efforts to weaken the country’s financial capacity.
The minister noted that the conflict has forced the government to reduce public sector salaries significantly as resources are redirected toward military and security needs. He also said the return of government operations to Khartoum required major investments to restore water, electricity, and other essential services.
Sudan’s economy continues to suffer from the effects of war, rising defence spending, increased imports, and declining exports. Recent trade data showed a widening imbalance, with exports estimated at around $2.64 billion compared with imports of approximately $6.49 billion, leaving the country with a trade deficit of nearly $3.86 billion.

title: UN Warns Operation Shujaa Has Failed to Eliminate ADF Threat Despite Years of Joint Offensives
excerpt: Beni, July 5, 2026 - Nearly five years after the launch of Operation Shujaa, the joint military campaign by the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda against armed groups in eastern DRC, a United Nations assessment highlights persistent challenges, including troop…
title_en: UN Warns Operation Shujaa Has Failed to Eliminate ADF Threat Despite Years of Joint Offensives
excerpt_en: Beni, July 5, 2026 - Nearly five years after the launch of Operation Shujaa, the joint military campaign by the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda against armed groups in eastern DRC, a United Nations assessment highlights persistent challenges, including troop…
body_en:
Beni, July 5, 2026 - Nearly five years after the launch of Operation Shujaa, the joint military campaign by the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda against armed groups in eastern DRC, a United Nations assessment highlights persistent challenges, including troop shortages, operational constraints, and the continued expansion of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) threat.
The operation, launched in 2021 by the FARDC and the Uganda People’s Defence Forces (UPDF), was designed primarily to dismantle ADF networks operating in North Kivu and Ituri provinces. However, a recent assessment indicates that while several military operations have disrupted the group’s activities, they have not succeeded in eliminating its senior leadership.
The report notes that new offensives were conducted in February 2026 against ADF positions in Mambasa and Irumu territories, including an operation targeting the group’s command structures. Although weapons, explosives, and military equipment were seized, the main ADF leaders reportedly managed to escape.
According to the assessment, military pressure has contributed to the geographical dispersal of the ADF, forcing fighters deeper into remote forest areas northeast of Mambasa. However, this displacement has also expanded the group’s operational reach and increased risks for civilian populations.
The UN experts identified several factors limiting the effectiveness of Operation Shujaa, including intelligence gaps, coordination difficulties, and insufficient resources. They also noted that FARDC operations against the AFC/M23 rebellion have reduced the availability of troops for operations against the ADF.
Facing these constraints, the Congolese army has increasingly relied on cooperation with Wazalendo armed groups operating in several areas. These include local armed factions involved in operations against ADF positions, particularly around Manguredjipa in Lubero territory and other strategic locations.
The report also refers to the reported death of ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, known as Difenda or Defender, following clashes with Shujaa forces in March 2026. However, UN experts indicated that they were unable to independently verify the information.
The assessment comes amid continued deadly attacks against civilians attributed to the ADF, worsening the humanitarian situation in parts of North Kivu and Ituri. Communities in Beni, Mambasa, and surrounding areas continue to face insecurity despite the presence of joint Congolese and Ugandan forces.
The persistent violence has fueled displacement and increased frustration among local populations, with some residents expressing concerns over the ability of authorities to provide effective protection.
In response to the ongoing crisis, the UN has repeatedly called for an end to attacks against civilians and urged all armed actors to respect international humanitarian law.
The continuation of Operation Shujaa follows a revised cooperation framework between Kinshasa and Kampala, signed in 2025, which expanded joint operations against the ADF and other armed groups threatening security in eastern DRC.
Under the updated arrangement, FARDC and UPDF forces were expected to strengthen intelligence cooperation, expand operations into additional areas such as Mambasa territory, and support security efforts along key transport routes, including the Kasindi-Beni-Butembo corridor.
Despite these renewed efforts, the situation remains fragile. The ADF continues to represent one of the most serious security threats in eastern DRC, demonstrating resilience despite sustained military pressure and regional cooperation.

title: Rwandans Abroad Mark 32nd Liberation Day with Focus on Development and International Partnerships
excerpt: MOSCOW/BEIJING, July 5, 2026 - Rwandan communities in Russia, Belarus, and China joined celebrations of the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda's Liberation Day, highlighting the country's post-1994 progress, national unity, and growing international partnerships. In Moscow, more than…
title_en: Rwandans Abroad Mark 32nd Liberation Day with Focus on Development and International Partnerships
excerpt_en: MOSCOW/BEIJING, July 5, 2026 - Rwandan communities in Russia, Belarus, and China joined celebrations of the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda's Liberation Day, highlighting the country's post-1994 progress, national unity, and growing international partnerships. In Moscow, more than…
body_en:
MOSCOW/BEIJING, July 5, 2026 - Rwandan communities in Russia, Belarus, and China joined celebrations of the 32nd anniversary of Rwanda's Liberation Day, highlighting the country's post-1994 progress, national unity, and growing international partnerships.
In Moscow, more than 350 guests, including diplomats, government officials, military representatives, and members of the Rwandan diaspora, attended a ceremony organized by the Rwandan Embassy. The event emphasized Rwanda's development since the end of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and the country's commitment to expanding cooperation with Russia in areas such as healthcare, education, nuclear energy, and defense. Embassy officials also encouraged Rwandan students studying abroad to acquire scientific and technological skills that can contribute to Rwanda's future development.
Meanwhile, in Beijing, diplomats and friends of Rwanda gathered to commemorate Liberation Day while celebrating the growing relationship between Rwanda and China ahead of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries. The event highlighted Rwanda's economic transformation over the past three decades and reaffirmed the importance of continued nation-building, resilience, and sustainable development.
Chinese officials reaffirmed their country's commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with Rwanda, citing expanding collaboration in trade, infrastructure, healthcare, and education. The celebrations in both capitals also paid tribute to those who lost their lives during the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and reflected on Rwanda's continued efforts to promote peace, security, and economic growth under the theme, "Rwanda's Journey Continues."

title: Djibouti and Algeria Explore New Energy and Mining Cooperation Opportunities
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti and Algeria are seeking to strengthen cooperation in strategic sectors including energy, hydrocarbons, mining, and technical expertise, as officials from both countries discuss new avenues for partnership and economic development. The…
title_en: Djibouti and Algeria Explore New Energy and Mining Cooperation Opportunities
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti and Algeria are seeking to strengthen cooperation in strategic sectors including energy, hydrocarbons, mining, and technical expertise, as officials from both countries discuss new avenues for partnership and economic development. The…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti and Algeria are seeking to strengthen cooperation in strategic sectors including energy, hydrocarbons, mining, and technical expertise, as officials from both countries discuss new avenues for partnership and economic development.
The Minister of Energy in charge of Natural Resources, Dr. Djama Mohamed Hassan, held talks with Algeria’s Ambassador to Djibouti, Dr. Mohamed Nacer Bessaklia, during a meeting focused on expanding bilateral cooperation and identifying areas of mutual interest.
Discussions centered on opportunities to enhance collaboration in hydrocarbons, mineral resources, and the exchange of technical knowledge, sectors considered essential for strengthening economic growth and diversifying national development strategies.
During the meeting, the Djiboutian minister highlighted the historic and fraternal ties between the two countries, reaffirming Djibouti’s commitment to deepening cooperation with Algeria. He stressed the importance of developing stronger partnerships in oil and gas, mining, capacity building, and knowledge sharing.
The Algerian ambassador welcomed the longstanding friendship between Algiers and Djibouti and expressed his country’s willingness to support Djibouti’s efforts to develop its energy and mining industries.
The discussions also explored potential cooperation in professional training, technical assistance, and the implementation of joint projects aimed at improving energy security and promoting economic diversification.
The meeting was attended by senior officials from Djibouti’s energy sector, including the Secretary General of the Ministry of Energy, Mohamed Kileh Wais, the Director General of the Djibouti International Hydrocarbons Company (SIHD), Dabar Adaweh Ladieh, as well as technical advisors Mahdi Waberi Hassan and Abass Aden Atteyeh.
The discussions mark another step in strengthening Djibouti-Algeria relations and highlight the growing importance of energy cooperation as a driver of sustainable development, industrial growth, and closer ties between the two countries.

title: Djibouti Youth Volunteers Complete 18-Month Campaign Against Gender-Based Violence
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 5, 2026 - The Taalo Saan Association has concluded an 18-month initiative aimed at empowering young people to fight gender-based violence and promote equality through community awareness and youth-led action. The closing ceremony of the project, titled…
title_en: Djibouti Youth Volunteers Complete 18-Month Campaign Against Gender-Based Violence
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 5, 2026 - The Taalo Saan Association has concluded an 18-month initiative aimed at empowering young people to fight gender-based violence and promote equality through community awareness and youth-led action. The closing ceremony of the project, titled…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 5, 2026 - The Taalo Saan Association has concluded an 18-month initiative aimed at empowering young people to fight gender-based violence and promote equality through community awareness and youth-led action.
The closing ceremony of the project, titled “Youth as Agents of Change in the Fight Against Gender-Based Violence,” brought together government officials, international partners, community representatives, and youth volunteers who participated in awareness campaigns across Djibouti City and inland regions.
The initiative trained and mobilized young volunteers through Community Development Centers (CDCs), schools, and community spaces to raise awareness about violence against women and girls, gender equality, and the growing risks associated with cyberbullying.
The ceremony was attended by Minister Delegate for Digital Economy and Innovation Safia Mohamed Ali Gadileh, President of the Taalo Saan Association Zahra Ali Cheik, European Union Ambassador to Djibouti and IGAD Denisa-Elena Ionete, representatives from the World Health Organization, local mayors, and project volunteers.
The event featured a theatrical performance, a retrospective presentation of project activities, and the presentation of Youth Awards recognizing the dedication and commitment of volunteers. Certificates and distinctions were also awarded to participants for their contribution to advancing equality and combating gender-based violence.
Speaking during the ceremony, Taalo Saan Association President Zahra Ali Cheik highlighted the challenges and achievements of the initiative, describing months of fieldwork, community engagement, and outreach efforts carried out by young volunteers.
She expressed appreciation to the European Union for its support, as well as to government institutions, partners, and host communities involved in the project. She particularly praised the commitment of young participants, describing them as the driving force behind the campaign.
European Union Ambassador Denisa-Elena Ionete highlighted the importance of placing young people at the center of social change, noting that providing youth with opportunities, resources, and platforms allows them to become active contributors to addressing major societal challenges.
The Director of Youth Social Integration and Volunteering at the Ministry of Youth and Culture, Roukiya Hassan, emphasized that the project reached both urban and rural communities, raising awareness among young people, women, and community leaders on issues including female genital mutilation, domestic violence, and cyberbullying.
Closing the ceremony, Minister Delegate Safia Mohamed Ali Gadileh stressed the importance of collective action in preventing violence, including forms occurring in digital spaces, and promoting a more inclusive society. She reaffirmed that violence has no place in Djibouti’s society and called for continued efforts to protect rights and strengthen equality.
The completion of the Taalo Saan project marks another step in engaging youth as leaders of social transformation. Through training, awareness, and community involvement, the young volunteers have emerged as important actors in preventing gender-based violence and promoting a culture of respect and inclusion.

Certificates and distinctions were also awarded to participants for their contribution to advancing equality and combating gender-based violence.
Speaking during the ceremony, Taalo Saan Association President Zahra Ali Cheik highlighted the challenges and achievements of the initiative, describing months of fieldwork, community engagement, and outreach efforts carried out by young volunteers.
She expressed appreciation to the European Union for its support, as well as to government institutions, partners, and host communities involved in the project. She particularly praised the commitment of young participants, describing them as the driving force behind the campaign.
European Union Ambassador Denisa-Elena Ionete highlighted the importance of placing young people at the center of social change, noting that providing youth with opportunities, resources, and platforms allows them to become active contributors to addressing major societal challenges.
The Director of Youth Social Integration and Volunteering at the Ministry of Youth and Culture, Roukiya Hassan, emphasized that the project reached both urban and rural communities, raising awareness among young people, women, and community leaders on issues including female genital mutilation, domestic violence, and cyberbullying.
Closing the ceremony, Minister Delegate Safia Mohamed Ali Gadileh stressed the importance of collective action in preventing violence, including forms occurring in digital spaces, and promoting a more inclusive society. She reaffirmed that violence has no place in Djibouti’s society and called for continued efforts to protect rights and strengthen equality.
The completion of the Taalo Saan project marks another step in engaging youth as leaders of social transformation. Through training, awareness, and community involvement, the young volunteers have emerged as important actors in preventing gender-based violence and promoting a culture of respect and inclusion.

title: Djibouti Strengthens African Economic Integration Through High-Level AU Talks
excerpt: Addis Ababa, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti reaffirmed its commitment to African economic integration as Minister of Trade and Tourism Orbis Elaf Orbis held high-level discussions with the Chairperson of the African Union Commission following his participation in the 18th Council of…
title_en: Djibouti Strengthens African Economic Integration Through High-Level AU Talks
excerpt_en: Addis Ababa, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti reaffirmed its commitment to African economic integration as Minister of Trade and Tourism Orbis Elaf Orbis held high-level discussions with the Chairperson of the African Union Commission following his participation in the 18th Council of…
body_en:
Addis Ababa, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti reaffirmed its commitment to African economic integration as Minister of Trade and Tourism Orbis Elaf Orbis held high-level discussions with the Chairperson of the African Union Commission following his participation in the 18th Council of Ministers of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).
The meeting focused on the outcomes of the ministerial session held in Abuja, Nigeria, where African ministers reviewed progress on the implementation of the AfCFTA, one of the African Union's flagship initiatives aimed at expanding intra-African trade and accelerating the continent's economic integration.
During the discussions, Minister Orbis presented Djibouti's perspectives on advancing the agreement and highlighted the opportunities the AfCFTA offers member states, including improved market access, stronger regional value chains, increased investment, and enhanced trade competitiveness.
The talks also addressed the implementation of the African Union's Agenda 2063, with particular emphasis on aligning Djibouti's national development priorities with continental objectives. Key areas of cooperation included trade facilitation, infrastructure development, industrialization, economic transformation, and employment creation.
For Djibouti, which continues to position itself as a strategic logistics and commercial gateway linking Africa, the Middle East, and global markets, the AfCFTA represents a major opportunity to deepen regional economic integration while diversifying its economy and expanding commercial partnerships across the continent.
On the sidelines of the Abuja ministerial meeting, the Djiboutian minister also met with the Secretary-General of the AfCFTA to discuss Djibouti's strategic priorities and explore ways to maximize the country's participation in what is expected to become one of the world's largest integrated free trade markets.
The discussions concluded with a renewed commitment to strengthen cooperation between Djibouti and the African Union in support of the effective implementation of the AfCFTA. Both sides emphasized the importance of continental economic integration as a catalyst for sustainable growth, investment, job creation, and long-term prosperity across Africa.
The high-level engagements underscore Djibouti's continued support for the African Union's integration agenda and its determination to play an active role in advancing the continent's major economic initiatives.

title: Djibouti Government Sets Results-Driven Agenda with Operational Reform Roadmaps
excerpt: Djibouti City, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti's government has stepped up efforts to accelerate the implementation of its national development priorities, with Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed calling for concrete, measurable, and fully financed action plans to transform…
title_en: Djibouti Government Sets Results-Driven Agenda with Operational Reform Roadmaps
excerpt_en: Djibouti City, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti's government has stepped up efforts to accelerate the implementation of its national development priorities, with Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed calling for concrete, measurable, and fully financed action plans to transform…
body_en:
Djibouti City, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti's government has stepped up efforts to accelerate the implementation of its national development priorities, with Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed calling for concrete, measurable, and fully financed action plans to transform policy objectives into tangible results for citizens.
During a high-level progress meeting on the government's strategic framework, the Prime Minister brought together lead ministers to assess the implementation of key national priorities and emphasized the need to move beyond broad policy commitments toward operational execution.
He instructed ministries to develop detailed roadmaps supported by measurable targets, implementation timelines, financing plans, and monitoring mechanisms. Each priority action is expected to include a baseline assessment, objectives to be achieved within the next 12 months, immediate actions for the first three months, identified funding sources, and solutions to anticipated implementation challenges.
The discussions covered several strategic sectors considered essential to the country's long-term development, including economic growth and diversification, public and private investment, external financing, the revitalization of public-private dialogue, sustainable management of national resources, and the energy transition.
Participants also reviewed policies aimed at strengthening human capital, promoting social cohesion, supporting balanced regional development, improving public governance, enhancing administrative performance, and reinforcing accountability across government institutions.
The Prime Minister stressed the importance of greater coordination among ministries, urging government departments to adopt a cross-sectoral approach rather than working independently. Particular attention was given to improving collaboration on employment, energy, regional development, and performance monitoring to ensure greater consistency in public policy implementation.
As part of the reform process, ministerial teams have been tasked with preparing a consolidated government strategy by July 31, 2026. The document will harmonize existing national frameworks, including Vision Djibouti 2035 and the ADEEG National Development Plan 2025-2030, into a unified roadmap designed to guide public action and mobilize financial resources.
The final report is expected to outline short- and medium-term priorities, budget requirements, financing opportunities, performance indicators, and monitoring and evaluation mechanisms. It will also establish clearer institutional coordination through designated focal points and strengthened government communication.
The initiative reflects the government's broader objective of reinforcing a culture of performance and accountability by ensuring that national development strategies produce measurable improvements in economic growth, public services, and the daily lives of the Djiboutian population.

title: Darfur Displacement Camps Face Growing Humanitarian Crisis as War Continues
excerpt: TAWILA, July 5, 2026 - Humanitarian conditions in displacement camps across Darfur are deteriorating rapidly as the prolonged conflict continues to overwhelm basic services and limit access to vital assistance, raising concerns over the survival of millions of displaced…
title_en: Darfur Displacement Camps Face Growing Humanitarian Crisis as War Continues
excerpt_en: TAWILA, July 5, 2026 - Humanitarian conditions in displacement camps across Darfur are deteriorating rapidly as the prolonged conflict continues to overwhelm basic services and limit access to vital assistance, raising concerns over the survival of millions of displaced…
body_en:
TAWILA, July 5, 2026 - Humanitarian conditions in displacement camps across Darfur are deteriorating rapidly as the prolonged conflict continues to overwhelm basic services and limit access to vital assistance, raising concerns over the survival of millions of displaced people.
Displaced communities are facing severe shortages of food, clean water, and medical care, while the collapse of infrastructure and public services has placed additional pressure on already vulnerable populations. The health sector has been among the hardest hit, with many medical facilities no longer operating due to shortages of medicines, supplies, and personnel.
Women and children are bearing the greatest impact of the worsening crisis, with reports of increased malnutrition, psychological distress, and gender-based violence among displaced populations.
Health risks are also rising as infectious diseases, including malaria, measles, and watery diarrhoea, spread in overcrowded camps with limited sanitation facilities. The arrival of the rainy season has further increased fears of disease outbreaks as water and hygiene services remain severely inadequate.
The economic crisis has deepened the humanitarian emergency, with rising prices of essential goods and continued depreciation of the Sudanese pound making survival increasingly difficult for displaced families.
Humanitarian actors have called for urgent international action to increase food and medical assistance, restore healthcare services, and ensure that aid reaches affected communities without political restrictions.
They also urged the warring parties to end hostilities, warning that continued fighting could further worsen the suffering of millions of displaced people across Darfur, Kordofan, and the Blue Nile region.

title: UN Report Says FDLR Fighters Integrated into Wazalendo Coalition in Eastern DRC
excerpt: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 5, 2026 — A United Nations panel of experts has reported that cooperation between the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and the Wazalendo coalition has deepened in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with FDLR fighters now…
title_en: UN Report Says FDLR Fighters Integrated into Wazalendo Coalition in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 5, 2026 — A United Nations panel of experts has reported that cooperation between the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and the Wazalendo coalition has deepened in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with FDLR fighters now…
body_en:
KINSHASA, DR Congo, July 5, 2026 — A United Nations panel of experts has reported that cooperation between the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and the Wazalendo coalition has deepened in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with FDLR fighters now embedded within several Wazalendo armed groups operating in North Kivu Province.
According to the report, the collaboration extends across Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale, Lubero, and Beni territories, where Wazalendo factions have conducted military operations independently and alongside the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC), particularly against AFC/M23 positions. The report states that some Wazalendo fighters have received specialized military training and have benefited from drone-supported operations.
The UN experts said FDLR combatants have been integrated into several Wazalendo groups, particularly those sharing anti-Tutsi ideology, including CMC/FDP, FDDP, and APCLS. The report argues that this cooperation has strengthened the FDLR while allowing it to evade international efforts calling for its dismantlement under the June 2025 Washington peace agreement.
The report further alleges that senior Congolese military officials were aware of the FDLR's presence within Wazalendo formations and that cooperation included intelligence sharing, logistical support, and weapons transfers. It also describes three regional Wazalendo coalitions operating across North Kivu and identifies two of them as hosting FDLR fighters. Additionally, the experts cite evidence of arms deliveries and continued coordination between FARDC officers and senior FDLR commanders, despite international commitments to dismantle the armed group.

title: RSF Attacks in North Darfur Trigger Civilian Deaths and New Refugee Exodus
excerpt: TINE, July 5, 2026 - Fresh attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on villages near Tine in North Darfur have killed civilians, injured dozens, and forced thousands of residents to flee toward neighboring Chad, according to local accounts. The attacks targeted six villages…
title_en: RSF Attacks in North Darfur Trigger Civilian Deaths and New Refugee Exodus
excerpt_en: TINE, July 5, 2026 - Fresh attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on villages near Tine in North Darfur have killed civilians, injured dozens, and forced thousands of residents to flee toward neighboring Chad, according to local accounts. The attacks targeted six villages…
body_en:
TINE, July 5, 2026 - Fresh attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on villages near Tine in North Darfur have killed civilians, injured dozens, and forced thousands of residents to flee toward neighboring Chad, according to local accounts.
The attacks targeted six villages along the route between Ambara locality and Tine, following recent battlefield advances by the Joint Force, an alliance of armed movements fighting alongside the Sudanese army. The coalition had recently taken control of several strategic areas in North and West Darfur after clashes with RSF forces.
Survivors said a large RSF force launched attacks on the villages, causing widespread destruction, including the burning of homes and markets, the destruction of water sources, and the looting of livestock. The resulting shortages of food and clean water pushed many families to leave their communities and cross toward Chad on foot.
The affected villages include Qarboura, Oruwa, Um Marahik, Kourbia, Abu Leiha, and Ana Baji, areas largely inhabited by the Zaghawa community.
Residents reported significant civilian casualties, although the exact number remains unclear. The attacks have intensified fears of further displacement in a region already heavily affected by years of conflict and humanitarian crises.
The latest violence follows a pattern of previous attacks in parts of North Darfur, where villages have been destroyed and communities displaced amid accusations of ethnic targeting and reprisals linked to local alliances in the wider conflict.
The RSF has previously accused residents in these areas of supporting the Joint Force, while humanitarian organizations have repeatedly warned of the impact of continued fighting on civilians across Darfur.

title: IGAD and South Sudan Reaffirm Commitment to Peace and Regional Cooperation
excerpt: JUBA, July 5, 2026 - The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the Government of South Sudan have renewed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in support of peace, stability, and sustainable development as the country continues its political…
title_en: IGAD and South Sudan Reaffirm Commitment to Peace and Regional Cooperation
excerpt_en: JUBA, July 5, 2026 - The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the Government of South Sudan have renewed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in support of peace, stability, and sustainable development as the country continues its political…
body_en:
JUBA, July 5, 2026 - The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the Government of South Sudan have renewed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in support of peace, stability, and sustainable development as the country continues its political transition.
The commitment was reaffirmed during a meeting in Juba between IGAD Special Envoy to South Sudan, Ambassador Moussa Djama Ali, and South Sudan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, James Pitia Morgan.
The discussions focused on ongoing initiatives, recent commitments, and efforts aimed at consolidating peace and strengthening state institutions in South Sudan.
Minister James Pitia Morgan praised IGAD’s continued contribution to South Sudan’s development and peacebuilding efforts, highlighting the regional organization’s role in mediation, political dialogue, and support for peace processes since the country gained independence in 2011.
For its part, IGAD reiterated its determination to continue working closely with the South Sudanese government and other stakeholders to advance common objectives related to peace, security, governance, and development.
The organization emphasized the importance of maintaining support for South Sudan’s transition process and preserving the progress achieved toward long-term stability in Africa’s youngest nation.
During the meeting, Minister Morgan also expressed support for Ambassador Moussa Djama Ali’s efforts and diplomatic engagement as he prepares to continue his mission from Addis Ababa, marking a new phase in his contribution to regional peace and cooperation.
The meeting highlighted IGAD’s continued role as a key partner in accompanying South Sudan through its political, economic, and security challenges while supporting efforts to build lasting peace and stronger institutions.

title: Djiboutian Scientific Talent Honored During International Alumni Day
excerpt: Djibouti City, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti celebrated scientific excellence and academic achievement during the fourth edition of International Alumni Day for French Higher Education, an event that highlighted the accomplishments of Djiboutian graduates trained in France and…
title_en: Djiboutian Scientific Talent Honored During International Alumni Day
excerpt_en: Djibouti City, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti celebrated scientific excellence and academic achievement during the fourth edition of International Alumni Day for French Higher Education, an event that highlighted the accomplishments of Djiboutian graduates trained in France and…
body_en:
Djibouti City, July 5, 2026 - Djibouti celebrated scientific excellence and academic achievement during the fourth edition of International Alumni Day for French Higher Education, an event that highlighted the accomplishments of Djiboutian graduates trained in France and their growing contribution to research, innovation, and national development.
Held at the French Institute of Djibouti, the gathering brought together students, researchers, professionals, and alumni under the theme "Scientific Talents: Discover, Innovate, Undertake." The event provided a platform for dialogue between experienced scientists and aspiring students while showcasing the professional and entrepreneurial achievements of former graduates of French universities.
Organizers described the initiative as an opportunity to make scientific careers more accessible and to encourage exchanges between academia and society. Beyond celebrating individual success stories, the event also promoted networking, mentorship, and international collaboration among alumni and future graduates.
Djibouti continues to encourage the return and professional integration of graduates educated abroad, viewing them as important contributors to the country's economic, scientific, and technological development. Their expertise is increasingly recognized as a valuable asset in supporting innovation and strengthening national institutions.
Academic cooperation between Djibouti and France also remained at the center of the discussions. More than 900 Djiboutian students are currently pursuing higher education in France with academic support services, reflecting the sustained educational partnership between the two countries. Long-standing collaborations between the University of Djibouti and several French universities continue to expand opportunities for research, student mobility, and academic exchange.
Speakers emphasized that Djiboutian graduates trained in France play an important role beyond academia, contributing to entrepreneurship, public service, and scientific research while serving as ambassadors of knowledge and innovation within their communities.
The event also highlighted the growth of the international alumni community of French higher education, which now connects more than 530,000 members and 5,500 partner organizations across 137 countries, creating a global network that facilitates professional cooperation and knowledge sharing.
One of the day's highlights was a panel discussion featuring young scientists, researchers, and entrepreneurs who shared their academic journeys, professional experiences, and the challenges they overcame to build successful careers. Their testimonies offered practical guidance and inspiration to students considering higher education opportunities in France.
The discussions continued through information sessions and direct exchanges between alumni and prospective students, strengthening mentorship opportunities and encouraging new academic and professional partnerships.
The celebration concluded with a reception that provided participants with an informal setting to continue networking, marking the occasion as both a tribute to academic excellence and a symbol of the enduring educational and cultural ties between Djibouti and France.

excerpt: LUSAKA, Zambia, July 5, 2026 - The Zambian government has described Rwanda's transformation since the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi as a source of inspiration and an important lesson for Africa, praising the country's progress in rebuilding its economy and strengthening…
title_en: Zambia Hails Rwanda's Development as Model for Africa
excerpt_en: LUSAKA, Zambia, July 5, 2026 - The Zambian government has described Rwanda's transformation since the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi as a source of inspiration and an important lesson for Africa, praising the country's progress in rebuilding its economy and strengthening…
body_en:
LUSAKA, Zambia, July 5, 2026 - The Zambian government has described Rwanda's transformation since the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi as a source of inspiration and an important lesson for Africa, praising the country's progress in rebuilding its economy and strengthening national unity.
The remarks were made during celebrations marking Rwanda's 32nd Liberation Day in Lusaka, where more than 500 guests, including government officials, diplomats, members of the Rwandan community, and friends of Rwanda, gathered for the occasion.

title: More Than 60 Suspects Arrested in Security Crackdown in Ngoma District
excerpt: NGOMA, Rwanda, July 5, 2026 - Rwandan police have arrested more than 60 people during security operations in Ngoma District targeting suspected criminals involved in violent crime, illegal mining, drug trafficking, and other activities linked to public insecurity. The…
title_en: More Than 60 Suspects Arrested in Security Crackdown in Ngoma District
excerpt_en: NGOMA, Rwanda, July 5, 2026 - Rwandan police have arrested more than 60 people during security operations in Ngoma District targeting suspected criminals involved in violent crime, illegal mining, drug trafficking, and other activities linked to public insecurity. The…
body_en:
NGOMA, Rwanda, July 5, 2026 - Rwandan police have arrested more than 60 people during security operations in Ngoma District targeting suspected criminals involved in violent crime, illegal mining, drug trafficking, and other activities linked to public insecurity.
The coordinated operations were carried out on July 3 in Kibungo and Rukumberi sectors with the support of local residents. In Kibungo Sector, dozens of suspects were arrested in Mahango, Gahima, Karenge, and Cyasemakamba cells on allegations including violent crime, theft, and the sale of marijuana. Additional arrests were made in connection with other suspected criminal activities.
In Rukumberi Sector, police arrested 27 suspects in Gituza and Ntovi cells, including individuals accused of illegal mineral trading, robbery, trafficking illicit alcohol known as kanyanga, and possession or use of marijuana. Authorities also reported seizing 133 kilograms of cigarettes during the operation.
Police said the crackdown followed complaints from residents about rising insecurity and emphasized that operations against criminal networks would continue. Authorities also urged the public to cooperate with law enforcement by reporting criminal activities and avoiding involvement in illegal mining, drug abuse, and the trade of illicit alcohol.

title: Sudan Peace Talks Face Calls to Prioritize Ending War Before Political Settlements
excerpt: ADDIS ABABA, July 5, 2026 - Ahead of the planned Addis Ababa talks, growing debate is emerging over the direction of Sudan’s peace process, with calls for international and regional mediators to prioritize ending the war and addressing the humanitarian crisis before advancing…
title_en: Sudan Peace Talks Face Calls to Prioritize Ending War Before Political Settlements
excerpt_en: ADDIS ABABA, July 5, 2026 - Ahead of the planned Addis Ababa talks, growing debate is emerging over the direction of Sudan’s peace process, with calls for international and regional mediators to prioritize ending the war and addressing the humanitarian crisis before advancing…
body_en:
ADDIS ABABA, July 5, 2026 - Ahead of the planned Addis Ababa talks, growing debate is emerging over the direction of Sudan’s peace process, with calls for international and regional mediators to prioritize ending the war and addressing the humanitarian crisis before advancing political arrangements.
Critics of the current approach argue that negotiations risk becoming disconnected from the realities facing civilians if they proceed without a firm commitment from the warring parties to halt hostilities. They warn that political processes conducted alongside ongoing fighting could unintentionally provide legitimacy to armed actors while failing to address the immediate suffering of the population.
The planned meeting in Addis Ababa, scheduled for late July, is expected to focus on establishing a preparatory framework for broader political dialogue. However, opponents argue that any political process must first be tied to a humanitarian ceasefire, protection of civilians, and concrete steps toward ending military confrontations across the country.
Sudan’s conflict continues to intensify in several strategic areas, including the Kordofan region and parts of Darfur, where civilians remain exposed to violence, displacement, and severe shortages of essential services. Humanitarian organizations have repeatedly warned that millions of people require urgent assistance as infrastructure collapses and access to aid remains limited.
Some political actors have raised concerns that the current format of negotiations could create space for former ruling elites and Islamist factions to regain influence without addressing the causes of Sudan’s political instability. They argue that any future settlement should prevent the return of authoritarian structures and focus on building a civilian-led democratic system.
Supporters of a revised approach say previous international mediation efforts in other conflict zones demonstrate the risks of prolonged negotiations without effective mechanisms to stop fighting. They emphasize that humanitarian protection, food assistance, and civilian safety should come before political power-sharing discussions.
The debate comes as Sudan’s war continues to reshape the country’s political landscape, with competing armed groups, regional interests, and civilian movements seeking influence over the future direction of the state.
Calls are growing for a comprehensive peace framework that combines an immediate end to hostilities, humanitarian access, accountability measures, and long-term reforms aimed at addressing the root causes of Sudan’s repeated cycles of conflict.

title: Russia Raises Alarm Over Drone Warfare and Alleged Foreign Mercenary Presence
excerpt: New York, July 4, 2026 - Russia has expressed concern over the changing nature of the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly the growing use of armed drones and reports of foreign fighters allegedly involved in training and drone operations. Speaking…
title_en: Russia Raises Alarm Over Drone Warfare and Alleged Foreign Mercenary Presence
excerpt_en: New York, July 4, 2026 - Russia has expressed concern over the changing nature of the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly the growing use of armed drones and reports of foreign fighters allegedly involved in training and drone operations. Speaking…
body_en:
New York, July 4, 2026 - Russia has expressed concern over the changing nature of the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly the growing use of armed drones and reports of foreign fighters allegedly involved in training and drone operations.
Speaking during a United Nations Security Council briefing on the security situation in eastern DRC, Russia’s representative to the UN, Anna Evstigneeva, warned that the transformation of military tactics is increasing risks for civilians, humanitarian workers, and international personnel operating in conflict zones.
According to the Russian diplomat, the widespread use of combat drones has significantly altered the dynamics of the conflict, with attacks increasingly threatening civilian populations and aid operations.
Evstigneeva referred specifically to a drone strike in Goma on March 11 that resulted in the death of a UNICEF staff member. She also raised concerns over reports that foreign mercenaries with battlefield experience from Ukraine were allegedly being recruited as instructors and drone operators in the eastern DRC conflict.
Beyond drone warfare, Russia also highlighted the threat posed by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), describing the armed group as a major security concern due to its alleged links with international extremist networks.
Moscow called for stronger regional and international cooperation to address the threat posed by the ADF, emphasizing the need for coordinated action involving countries in the Great Lakes region and international partners.
The Russian position comes as insecurity continues to affect eastern DRC despite ongoing diplomatic initiatives, including the Washington Agreement and the Doha peace process. Tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali remain unresolved, with both sides maintaining different interpretations of the commitments made under the peace frameworks.
Negotiations between the Congolese government and AFC/M23 under the Doha process have also struggled to achieve significant progress, with disagreements persisting over key political and security issues. Recent diplomatic efforts have failed to produce the expected breakthroughs, while broader international crises have further slowed mediation efforts.
As fighting continues, regional and international actors are increasing calls for all parties to respect peace commitments. However, the gap between diplomatic agreements and developments on the ground remains a major obstacle to achieving a lasting resolution to the conflict in eastern DRC.

title: Gen. Karusisi Urges Youth to Safeguard Rwanda’s Liberation Gains
excerpt: Nyagatare, July 4, 2026 - The Commander of the Rwanda Defence Force’s 5th Division, Maj. Gen. Ruki Karusisi, has called on young Rwandans to preserve the achievements of the country’s liberation, saying the peace and stability enjoyed today were secured through the sacrifices…
title_en: Gen. Karusisi Urges Youth to Safeguard Rwanda’s Liberation Gains
excerpt_en: Nyagatare, July 4, 2026 - The Commander of the Rwanda Defence Force’s 5th Division, Maj. Gen. Ruki Karusisi, has called on young Rwandans to preserve the achievements of the country’s liberation, saying the peace and stability enjoyed today were secured through the sacrifices…
body_en:
Nyagatare, July 4, 2026 - The Commander of the Rwanda Defence Force’s 5th Division, Maj. Gen. Ruki Karusisi, has called on young Rwandans to preserve the achievements of the country’s liberation, saying the peace and stability enjoyed today were secured through the sacrifices of many heroes.
He made the remarks on July 3 during a 23-kilometre Liberation Walk attended by more than 4,500 residents, youth and local leaders from across the Eastern Province. The march began at Nyagatare Stadium and ended at Gasantimetero in Tabagwe Sector, a site associated with President Paul Kagame during the liberation struggle.
Addressing participants, Maj. Gen. Karusisi described Liberation Day as a reminder of the courage, patriotism and determination that shaped Rwanda’s history. He said many Rwandans were forced into exile after being denied the right to live in their homeland and, after repeated unsuccessful attempts to return peacefully, launched the liberation struggle on October 1, 1990.
He recalled that the Rwanda Patriotic Army campaign was led by President Kagame, who now serves as Commander-in-Chief of the Rwanda Defence Force. He added that during the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, in which more than one million people were killed, the international community failed to stop the massacres, while the liberation forces ended the genocide on July 4, 1994.
Maj. Gen. Karusisi said Rwanda's achievements extended beyond ending the war, pointing to national reconstruction, reconciliation, institution building and socio-economic development as key milestones that followed the liberation. He described today's Rwanda as a stable, secure and forward-looking nation built through visionary leadership and the collective efforts of its citizens.
He urged Rwandans, particularly the youth, to honour the sacrifices of those who fought for the country's freedom by protecting peace, respecting the law, embracing innovation and contributing solutions that advance national development.
Eastern Province Governor Pudence Rubingisa also addressed the gathering, encouraging young people to draw inspiration from the heroes of the liberation struggle and to safeguard the progress achieved through their sacrifices.

title: Sudan Reaffirms El Obeid's Defense, Calls for International Pressure on RSF Supporters
excerpt: GENEVA, July 4, 2026 - Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem declared that the city of El Obeid would remain under government control, while calling for increased international action to halt external support for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as fighting intensifies…
title_en: Sudan Reaffirms El Obeid's Defense, Calls for International Pressure on RSF Supporters
excerpt_en: GENEVA, July 4, 2026 - Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem declared that the city of El Obeid would remain under government control, while calling for increased international action to halt external support for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as fighting intensifies…
body_en:
GENEVA, July 4, 2026 - Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem declared that the city of El Obeid would remain under government control, while calling for increased international action to halt external support for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) as fighting intensifies around the strategic North Kordofan capital.
Addressing an urgent session of the United Nations Human Rights Council, Salem described the siege of El Obeid as a critical challenge to Sudan's stability and urged the international community to take stronger measures to stop the flow of advanced weapons reaching the RSF.
The foreign minister accused the United Arab Emirates (UAE) of providing military support to the paramilitary group, including weapons, drones, and logistical assistance. The UAE has previously denied allegations of supporting the RSF.
Salem also called for the RSF to be formally designated as a terrorist organization, arguing that its actions against civilians and public infrastructure meet internationally recognized definitions of terrorism.
On the sidelines of the Human Rights Council session, the Sudanese foreign minister met with UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk and senior UN officials to present the government's position on the conflict and discuss the worsening humanitarian situation in Sudan.
During the meetings, Salem reiterated Sudan's willingness to cooperate with United Nations human rights mechanisms and ongoing international diplomatic initiatives aimed at ending the conflict. He emphasized, however, that any future peace process should be consistent with the government's political roadmap presented to the United Nations in March 2025.
According to the Sudanese government, the proposed roadmap envisions a negotiated settlement based on the dismantling of the RSF, the collection of its weapons, and the relocation of its fighters to designated assembly areas as part of a broader security arrangement.
As military operations continue around El Obeid, the city remains one of the most strategically significant frontlines in Sudan's three-year conflict, with mounting humanitarian concerns for hundreds of thousands of civilians affected by the fighting.

title: Equal Citizenship Seen as Key to Sudan’s Lasting Stability
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Building a stable and peaceful Sudan will require addressing the country's longstanding identity crisis through equal citizenship, inclusive governance, and stronger national institutions, according to a political analysis examining the roots of…
title_en: Equal Citizenship Seen as Key to Sudan’s Lasting Stability
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Building a stable and peaceful Sudan will require addressing the country's longstanding identity crisis through equal citizenship, inclusive governance, and stronger national institutions, according to a political analysis examining the roots of…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Building a stable and peaceful Sudan will require addressing the country's longstanding identity crisis through equal citizenship, inclusive governance, and stronger national institutions, according to a political analysis examining the roots of Sudan's recurring conflicts.
The analysis argues that ethnic divisions and ideological rivalries have remained the primary drivers of political instability since independence, shaping military coups, armed rebellions, and competition for state power. It contends that whenever ethnicity or ideology becomes the basis for political authority, national cohesion weakens and the risk of violent conflict increases.
Despite decades of political transition and armed conflict, successive governments are said to have failed to establish a governance system that guarantees equal citizenship and fair participation for all communities. As a result, many Sudanese continue to identify more closely with their tribal or ethnic groups than with the state, reflecting limited confidence in national institutions.
With more than 300 ethnic groups across the country, Sudan continues to face challenges in balancing cultural diversity with national unity. The analysis notes that unequal access to political representation, economic opportunities, and public institutions has contributed to persistent grievances and varying perceptions of citizenship among different communities.
Three broad forms of identity-related conflict are highlighted. The first stems from ideological competition among political movements seeking to shape the state according to their respective visions. The second centers on demands for greater political inclusion, equitable power-sharing, and recognition of Sudan's cultural diversity. The third involves conflicts driven by ethnic domination, territorial control, and demographic change, which the analysis describes as posing the greatest threat to long-term stability.
According to the analysis, many of Sudan's major conflicts have been presented as political struggles while being deeply influenced by ethnic or ideological divisions. It argues that the war that began in April 2023 has brought these underlying tensions into sharper focus, with identity becoming an increasingly significant factor in the conflict.
The paper also compares the current conflict with previous periods of violence, noting both similarities and differences in the nature of identity-based violence and the objectives of armed actors. It argues that the current war has intensified concerns over ethnic violence, displacement, and demographic change in several regions of the country.
The analysis concludes that sustainable peace in Sudan will depend on building a state founded on equal citizenship, the rule of law, and inclusive political participation. It argues that resolving the country's identity crisis through gradual institutional reform and national reconciliation will be essential to preventing future conflicts and strengthening long-term stability.

title: Uganda Reaffirms Recognition of Sudan’s Military-Led Government
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Uganda has reaffirmed its recognition of Sudan's military-led administration as the country's sole legitimate government, rejecting the establishment of any parallel governing authority and expressing support for Sudan's sovereignty and territorial…
title_en: Uganda Reaffirms Recognition of Sudan’s Military-Led Government
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Uganda has reaffirmed its recognition of Sudan's military-led administration as the country's sole legitimate government, rejecting the establishment of any parallel governing authority and expressing support for Sudan's sovereignty and territorial…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Uganda has reaffirmed its recognition of Sudan's military-led administration as the country's sole legitimate government, rejecting the establishment of any parallel governing authority and expressing support for Sudan's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
The position was conveyed during a visit to Khartoum by Joseph Ocwet, Director of Uganda's External Intelligence Organisation and special envoy of President Yoweri Museveni, who delivered official messages from the Ugandan leader to Sudanese authorities.
During his visit, Ocwet held separate meetings with Sovereign Council Chairman Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Prime Minister Kamel Idris, and Sovereign Council Deputy Chairman Malik Agar to discuss the ongoing conflict and bilateral relations.
Uganda reiterated its opposition to any attempts to create alternative governing structures in Sudan, describing the country's military-led administration as the only legitimate authority.
Sudanese officials used the meetings to brief the Ugandan delegation on the impact of the conflict, including damage to critical infrastructure and the government's ongoing political and peace initiatives aimed at restoring stability.
The discussions also focused on regional cooperation, with Sudanese officials emphasizing the importance of African-led solutions to conflicts on the continent and calling for closer coordination between Khartoum and Kampala in addressing regional security challenges.
According to Sudanese officials, the Ugandan envoy indicated that President Museveni intends to place the Sudan crisis among the priorities of his new presidential term, underscoring Uganda's continued engagement in regional efforts to support peace and stability.

NYARUGURU, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - More than 33,700 people across Rwanda received free medical treatment through a nationwide outreach program organized by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and the Rwanda National Police as part of activities marking the country's 32nd Liberation Day.
Health services were provided at several hospitals, including Munini, Byumba, Kirehe, and Gihundwe. A total of 33,722 patients were treated, with 1,004 undergoing surgical procedures and 3,369 receiving free medication. In Nyaruguru District alone, more than 8,400 people received medical care, including over 200 patients treated for eye conditions.
Military medical officials said the initiative brought together specialists from major referral and military hospitals, allowing advanced healthcare services to reach communities across all provinces. The program was presented as part of broader efforts to improve public health and support national development.
Health Minister Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana praised the initiative, saying it reflects the continued commitment to improving citizens' well-being beyond the achievements of the country's liberation. He also called on the public to support efforts to address social challenges, including teenage pregnancy, substance abuse, and domestic conflicts.
The medical campaign formed part of a three-month nationwide civil-military outreach program launched in March 2026, which also included the construction of homes, schools, and bridges, tree planting, the provision of clean water, and livestock distribution to support community development.

title: RPF Marks Liberation Day with Focus on Unity, Self-Reliance and Youth Leadership

title_en: RPF Marks Liberation Day with Focus on Unity, Self-Reliance and Youth Leadership
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - Rwanda's 32nd Liberation Day was marked by renewed emphasis on national unity, self-reliance, and inclusive governance, with the ruling RPF-Inkotanyi highlighting the country's transformation since the end of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.…
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - Rwanda's 32nd Liberation Day was marked by renewed emphasis on national unity, self-reliance, and inclusive governance, with the ruling RPF-Inkotanyi highlighting the country's transformation since the end of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
The anniversary underscored the RPF's view that liberation extends beyond military victory to encompass reconciliation, institution-building, economic development, and citizen participation. The party argued that its governance model has sought to replace decades of division, discrimination, and authoritarian rule with policies centered on national cohesion and equal opportunities.
The RPF also stressed the importance of empowering citizens through education, justice, and political inclusion, while promoting gender equality and youth leadership as key pillars of Rwanda's long-term development. It maintained that reducing poverty and expanding public participation remain essential to sustaining the country's progress.
Looking ahead, the party called on Rwanda's younger generation to continue the country's transformation by embracing innovation, responsibility, and patriotism. It said the ongoing mission is to strengthen Rwanda's self-reliance and preserve the gains achieved in peace, security, freedom, and sustainable development.
