title: Sudan Withdraws Small Banknotes as Inflation Weakens Pound’s Value
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has announced the withdrawal of small-denomination banknotes from circulation, giving citizens a three-month period to deposit the affected currencies into commercial bank accounts as inflation continues to erode the purchasing…
title_en: Sudan Withdraws Small Banknotes as Inflation Weakens Pound’s Value
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has announced the withdrawal of small-denomination banknotes from circulation, giving citizens a three-month period to deposit the affected currencies into commercial bank accounts as inflation continues to erode the purchasing…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has announced the withdrawal of small-denomination banknotes from circulation, giving citizens a three-month period to deposit the affected currencies into commercial bank accounts as inflation continues to erode the purchasing power of the Sudanese pound.
The measure targets 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, and 50-pound notes, which have become increasingly insignificant in everyday transactions due to rising prices and the depreciation of the national currency.
The withdrawal process will run until July 30, 2026, after which the affected banknotes will lose their legal tender status and will no longer be accepted for settling financial obligations.
Until the deadline, the notes will remain valid but can only be exchanged through deposits into bank accounts at their face value. Direct cash exchanges between individuals and banks will not be permitted.
The Central Bank said special measures will apply in areas affected by severe insecurity and disruptions to banking operations, allowing authorities to assess each situation and protect citizens’ rights to recover the value of their withdrawn currency.
The decision comes amid Sudan’s deepening economic crisis, marked by high inflation, currency depreciation, and the impact of ongoing conflict on financial services.
Meanwhile, a separate currency exchange program involving 500- and 1,000-pound notes has already been completed in Khartoum, Al Jazirah, and White Nile states, while the process remains delayed in conflict-affected areas where banking activities have been disrupted.

title_en: Rwandan Prime Minister Calls for Continued Vigilance in Safeguarding National Security
excerpt_en: BIGOGWE, Nyabihu District, July 4, 2026 - Rwandan Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva has called on citizens to remain vigilant and continue working with security institutions to preserve the country's peace and stability, saying national security requires the active…
body_en:
BIGOGWE, Nyabihu District, July 4, 2026 - Rwandan Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva has called on citizens to remain vigilant and continue working with security institutions to preserve the country's peace and stability, saying national security requires the active participation of all Rwandans.
Speaking at the close of a three-month civil-military outreach program in Bigogwe Sector as part of the 32nd Liberation Day celebrations, the Prime Minister praised the Rwanda Patriotic Army (RPA) for ending the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and acknowledged the sacrifices made by its soldiers and veterans in securing the country.
He said security goes beyond the absence of armed conflict, emphasizing that it also means protecting the country's peace, unity, and development. He urged citizens to uphold national values, strengthen social cohesion, and avoid complacency in safeguarding the gains achieved over the past three decades.
The annual outreach program, organized under the theme of collaboration between the population, the Rwanda Defence Force, and the Rwanda National Police, included the construction of homes, bridges, and classrooms, as well as the provision of boats, medical services, and access to clean water for communities across the country.

title: Sudan Orders South Sudanese Refugees to Update Registration for Aid Access
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudanese authorities have instructed South Sudanese refugees living in Khartoum State to update their personal information under a new registration system, warning that failure to comply could affect access to humanitarian assistance and essential…
title_en: Sudan Orders South Sudanese Refugees to Update Registration for Aid Access
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudanese authorities have instructed South Sudanese refugees living in Khartoum State to update their personal information under a new registration system, warning that failure to comply could affect access to humanitarian assistance and essential…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudanese authorities have instructed South Sudanese refugees living in Khartoum State to update their personal information under a new registration system, warning that failure to comply could affect access to humanitarian assistance and essential services.
The Commission for Refugees said the data update and renewal of identity documents are mandatory measures aimed at ensuring refugees can continue receiving support from humanitarian organizations while maintaining their legal status in Sudan.
Sudan currently hosts hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees, making them the largest refugee population in the country. Many refugees have been displaced by years of conflict and instability in the region.
Authorities said the new registration process will introduce a foreign national identification number system designed to improve documentation and strengthen protection mechanisms for refugees under Sudan’s asylum regulations.
Refugees in Khartoum State have been directed to designated registration centres and camps, particularly in White Nile State, which hosts the country’s largest concentration of South Sudanese refugees due to its proximity to the border with South Sudan.
The registration campaign follows recent efforts by Khartoum State authorities to relocate some refugee communities to organized camps, amid security concerns and allegations that some foreign nationals may have become involved in the ongoing conflict.
Officials said maintaining updated registration records is essential for ensuring access to services, humanitarian assistance, and legal residency protections.
Humanitarian agencies estimate that a significant number of South Sudanese refugees in Sudan remain without official registration, while many others live outside formal refugee camps, creating additional challenges for aid delivery and protection efforts.

title_en: Gatsibo Rice Farmers Invest Over Rwf3.1 Billion in Community Development Projects
excerpt_en: GATSIBO, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - A rice farmers' cooperative in Gatsibo District has invested more than Rwf3.1 billion in community development projects, including a hotel, a farmers' supply store, healthcare services, and social welfare programs, as Rwanda marked the 32nd…
body_en:
GATSIBO, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - A rice farmers' cooperative in Gatsibo District has invested more than Rwf3.1 billion in community development projects, including a hotel, a farmers' supply store, healthcare services, and social welfare programs, as Rwanda marked the 32nd anniversary of Liberation Day.
The investments were highlighted during Liberation Day celebrations, which also featured the inauguration of new facilities developed by the Coproriz Ntende cooperative, including a building valued at Rwf450 million and a farmers' store worth more than Rwf200 million.
According to the cooperative, the investments extend beyond agriculture to include poultry farming, education support for members' children, development loans, daycare centers near rice fields, a pharmacy, and retirement assistance for elderly farmers. Cooperative members said the initiatives have improved access to affordable farm inputs, medicines, housing, and financial services, contributing to higher living standards.
Officials praised the cooperative as a model of farmer-led economic development and encouraged other cooperatives to adopt similar approaches to reducing poverty and creating sustainable income opportunities. Founded in 2003, Coproriz Ntende now has more than 3,700 members cultivating approximately 900 hectares of rice across Gatsibo and neighboring Kayonza districts.

title: Twirwaneho Seizes Strategic Point-Zéro in South Kivu Offensive
excerpt: MINEMBWE, South Kivu, July 4, 2026 - The armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho announced on Saturday that it had captured the strategic Point-Zéro area and several surrounding localities following a military offensive against the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Burundian…
title_en: Twirwaneho Seizes Strategic Point-Zéro in South Kivu Offensive
excerpt_en: MINEMBWE, South Kivu, July 4, 2026 - The armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho announced on Saturday that it had captured the strategic Point-Zéro area and several surrounding localities following a military offensive against the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Burundian…
body_en:
MINEMBWE, South Kivu, July 4, 2026 - The armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho announced on Saturday that it had captured the strategic Point-Zéro area and several surrounding localities following a military offensive against the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Burundian forces in South Kivu Province.
The group said its fighters took control of Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi, and Rubemba by 8:35 a.m. local time after clashes that targeted positions held by the Congolese army, Burundian troops, FDLR fighters, and Wazalendo militias. It claimed the operation marked a significant battlefield victory and indicated that military advances could continue toward other areas in Fizi Territory.
The capture of Point-Zéro follows Twirwaneho's seizure of Mikenke and Bilalombili on July 1, further expanding its control around Minembwe Commune. The latest gains strengthen the group's presence in a region that has witnessed intense fighting in recent months.
Point-Zéro is considered a strategic military position because it sits atop the Fizi mountain range and controls road networks linking Uvira, Minembwe, Mikenke, Fizi, and Baraka. Control of the area provides a tactical advantage for military operations across southern South Kivu.
The group has previously accused government forces of using Point-Zéro as a staging ground for planned offensives against Minembwe and neighboring Banyamulenge-populated areas. Although Twirwaneho briefly captured the position in January 2026, it later lost control after counteroffensives involving drones and Congolese special forces. The latest operation marks the group's return to one of the most strategically important positions in the region.

title: Tito Rutaremara Recounts Origins of Rwanda's Gacaca Courts
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - Tito Rutaremara, Director General of Rwanda's National Advisory Board of Experts, has described how the idea of using Gacaca courts emerged as a response to the overwhelming number of suspects accused of participating in the 1994 Genocide…
title_en: Tito Rutaremara Recounts Origins of Rwanda's Gacaca Courts
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - Tito Rutaremara, Director General of Rwanda's National Advisory Board of Experts, has described how the idea of using Gacaca courts emerged as a response to the overwhelming number of suspects accused of participating in the 1994 Genocide…
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda, July 4, 2026 - Tito Rutaremara, Director General of Rwanda's National Advisory Board of Experts, has described how the idea of using Gacaca courts emerged as a response to the overwhelming number of suspects accused of participating in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
Rutaremara said the proposal took shape after he was tasked with investigating the planning and execution of the genocide and identifying a practical way to prosecute the large number of suspects. According to him, the scale of participation in the genocide made it clear that the conventional judicial system alone would not be capable of handling the caseload within a reasonable period.
He explained that the idea drew inspiration from Rwanda's traditional community-based dispute resolution system. Although the proposal initially faced opposition from legal experts who questioned whether genocide cases could be handled through such a mechanism, further research and national consultations eventually led to its adoption through the National Dialogue Council.
Rwanda's Gacaca courts operated for a decade before closing on June 18, 2012. During that period, they handled approximately 1.9 million genocide-related cases, significantly accelerating the delivery of justice while complementing the country's broader reconciliation process.

title: UN Warns El Obeid Could Face Siege as Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 – United Nations agencies have warned that the Sudanese city of El Obeid faces a growing risk of a major humanitarian catastrophe as escalating attacks, displacement, and restrictions on aid access raise fears of a crisis similar to previous sieges in…
title_en: UN Warns El Obeid Could Face Siege as Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 – United Nations agencies have warned that the Sudanese city of El Obeid faces a growing risk of a major humanitarian catastrophe as escalating attacks, displacement, and restrictions on aid access raise fears of a crisis similar to previous sieges in…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 – United Nations agencies have warned that the Sudanese city of El Obeid faces a growing risk of a major humanitarian catastrophe as escalating attacks, displacement, and restrictions on aid access raise fears of a crisis similar to previous sieges in Darfur.
International officials said the strategic capital of North Kordofan State is facing increasing pressure as fighting intensifies around the city, with civilians suffering from shortages of essential services, including water and electricity.
The humanitarian situation across the Kordofan region has deteriorated sharply in recent months, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced by violence. Aid organizations reported a significant increase in displacement incidents, driven by attacks on communities and worsening insecurity.
An estimated 500,000 people remain trapped in El Obeid, where access to humanitarian assistance has become increasingly difficult. Repeated attacks on civilian infrastructure have disrupted basic services and left many residents struggling to obtain food, water, and medical care.
Humanitarian officials warned that continued inaction could lead to a repeat of the devastating events experienced in other besieged Sudanese cities, where civilians suffered widespread violence and displacement.
Aid agencies also highlighted growing challenges in maintaining relief operations due to declining resources and increased security risks. Emergency supplies, including food and shelter materials, are becoming increasingly limited as humanitarian needs continue to rise.
The warnings come after a humanitarian transport vehicle carrying vital relief supplies was destroyed in a drone strike in White Nile State. The shipment included essential items such as blankets, solar lamps, kitchen equipment, and other materials intended for conflict-affected communities.
Humanitarian officials said the incident reflects a broader pattern of attacks affecting civilians and aid operations across Sudan, calling for stronger protections and guaranteed access for relief workers.
The United Nations has described Sudan as one of the most dangerous environments in the world for humanitarian operations, as aid organizations face increasing difficulties delivering assistance amid ongoing fighting and security threats.

title: Sudan Revokes Fintech License Amid Scrutiny Over Digital Banking Expansion
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has revoked the operating license of Al-Asjad for Smart and Digital Solutions, a local financial technology company, following controversy surrounding its recent launch and questions over its operations and regulatory compliance.…
title_en: Sudan Revokes Fintech License Amid Scrutiny Over Digital Banking Expansion
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has revoked the operating license of Al-Asjad for Smart and Digital Solutions, a local financial technology company, following controversy surrounding its recent launch and questions over its operations and regulatory compliance.…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has revoked the operating license of Al-Asjad for Smart and Digital Solutions, a local financial technology company, following controversy surrounding its recent launch and questions over its operations and regulatory compliance.
The decision comes shortly after the company introduced a new digital platform that attracted significant attention within Sudan’s banking and economic sectors. Concerns were raised over the firm’s technical capabilities, financial strength, and alleged external connections, prompting the central bank to launch a review of its activities.
The company’s launch event had drawn the participation of senior government and banking officials, increasing public interest and debate over the role of newly licensed fintech providers in Sudan’s financial system.
Following the review, the central bank formed a specialized committee to assess the company’s operations and regulatory position. The committee recommended the withdrawal of the firm’s license, leading to the official cancellation decision.
The move follows a broader regulatory tightening by the central bank, which recently instructed commercial banks and licensed financial technology companies to obtain prior approval before entering into new partnerships, operational agreements, or data-sharing arrangements.
Authorities said all fintech operators must comply with strict requirements related to corporate governance, financial stability, cybersecurity, risk management, and customer data protection.
The central bank emphasized that safeguarding financial information remains a priority and that payment service providers must maintain strong security measures, including encryption systems and controlled access to sensitive data.
Sudan has been working to expand its digital payment infrastructure by licensing financial switch operators to improve connectivity between banks, businesses, telecommunications companies, and government payment platforms.
The initiative aims to support electronic payments, enable direct bank transfers, expand point-of-sale services, and provide digital financial solutions to institutions that lack their own payment networks.
Despite these modernization efforts, regulators have stressed that all technology providers operating within the financial sector remain subject to strict oversight to protect the stability and security of the banking system.

KHARTOUM, July 4, 2026 - Sudan’s Central Bank has revoked the operating license of Al-Asjad for Smart and Digital Solutions, a local financial technology company, following controversy surrounding its recent launch and questions over its operations and regulatory compliance.
The decision comes shortly after the company introduced a new digital platform that attracted significant attention within Sudan’s banking and economic sectors. Concerns were raised over the firm’s technical capabilities, financial strength, and alleged external connections, prompting the central bank to launch a review of its activities.
The company’s launch event had drawn the participation of senior government and banking officials, increasing public interest and debate over the role of newly licensed fintech providers in Sudan’s financial system.
Following the review, the central bank formed a specialized committee to assess the company’s operations and regulatory position. The committee recommended the withdrawal of the firm’s license, leading to the official cancellation decision.
The move follows a broader regulatory tightening by the central bank, which recently instructed commercial banks and licensed financial technology companies to obtain prior approval before entering into new partnerships, operational agreements, or data-sharing arrangements.
Authorities said all fintech operators must comply with strict requirements related to corporate governance, financial stability, cybersecurity, risk management, and customer data protection.
The central bank emphasized that safeguarding financial information remains a priority and that payment service providers must maintain strong security measures, including encryption systems and controlled access to sensitive data.
Sudan has been working to expand its digital payment infrastructure by licensing financial switch operators to improve connectivity between banks, businesses, telecommunications companies, and government payment platforms.
The initiative aims to support electronic payments, enable direct bank transfers, expand point-of-sale services, and provide digital financial solutions to institutions that lack their own payment networks.
Despite these modernization efforts, regulators have stressed that all technology providers operating within the financial sector remain subject to strict oversight to protect the stability and security of the banking system.

title: UN Human Rights Chief Calls for Urgent Action to Prevent Atrocities in Sudan
excerpt: GENEVA, July 3, 2026 - United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has urged the UN Security Council to take immediate action to prevent further atrocities in Sudan, warning that the besieged city of El Obeid faces a rapidly deteriorating humanitarian and…
title_en: UN Human Rights Chief Calls for Urgent Action to Prevent Atrocities in Sudan
excerpt_en: GENEVA, July 3, 2026 - United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has urged the UN Security Council to take immediate action to prevent further atrocities in Sudan, warning that the besieged city of El Obeid faces a rapidly deteriorating humanitarian and…
body_en:
GENEVA, July 3, 2026 - United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has urged the UN Security Council to take immediate action to prevent further atrocities in Sudan, warning that the besieged city of El Obeid faces a rapidly deteriorating humanitarian and human rights crisis.
Addressing an urgent session of the UN Human Rights Council on Friday, Türk said the situation in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan State, had reached a critical stage after months of escalating violence and siege-like conditions. He called on the Security Council to fulfill its responsibility to protect civilians and prevent large-scale violations of international humanitarian law.
The High Commissioner also renewed calls for greater restraint in the use of the Security Council's veto during situations involving genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and other mass atrocities, arguing that international mechanisms should be better equipped to respond to such crises.
Türk warned that continued fighting around El Obeid has placed hundreds of thousands of civilians at increasing risk. He noted that repeated drone strikes and other attacks have caused civilian casualties while damaging essential infrastructure and disrupting access to basic services.
According to the UN, dozens of civilians have been killed or injured in drone attacks recorded throughout June, although the actual number of casualties is believed to be significantly higher. The continued violence has heightened fears of a broader humanitarian catastrophe if hostilities intensify further.
The High Commissioner also called for stronger international efforts to curb the flow of weapons into Sudan, urging an expansion of the existing arms embargo beyond Darfur to cover the entire country.
Humanitarian conditions in El Obeid continue to worsen as shortages of clean water, fuel, food, and medical supplies become more severe. Damage to water networks, markets, schools, fuel stations, and transportation infrastructure has further limited access to essential services, while communication disruptions have complicated relief efforts.
With the rainy season underway, aid agencies have also warned of an increased risk of waterborne diseases, including cholera, as overcrowded communities and displaced populations face deteriorating sanitation and limited access to safe drinking water.
Türk called for an immediate humanitarian pause to allow the delivery of life-saving assistance and to reduce the suffering of civilians caught in the conflict.

title: AFC/M23 Reinforces Positions Around Pinga Amid Rising Security Concerns
excerpt: Walikale, July 3, 2026 - Tensions are rising around the strategic town of Pinga, in Walikale territory, North Kivu, following reports of new AFC/M23 troop movements and reinforcements along several access routes in the area. According to local sources, AFC/M23 fighters…
title_en: AFC/M23 Reinforces Positions Around Pinga Amid Rising Security Concerns
excerpt_en: Walikale, July 3, 2026 - Tensions are rising around the strategic town of Pinga, in Walikale territory, North Kivu, following reports of new AFC/M23 troop movements and reinforcements along several access routes in the area. According to local sources, AFC/M23 fighters…
body_en:
Walikale, July 3, 2026 - Tensions are rising around the strategic town of Pinga, in Walikale territory, North Kivu, following reports of new AFC/M23 troop movements and reinforcements along several access routes in the area.
According to local sources, AFC/M23 fighters strengthened their positions on Thursday, July 2, after receiving additional personnel and ammunition through multiple routes connecting Walikale and neighboring areas.
The reported movements involved the Malemo-Mindjendje axis along the Mpety-Kalembe road, the Rusamambu-Chanjikiro route, the Bukumbirwa-Misambo-Maruho corridor in Walikale territory, and the Bulende-Bukonde route from Masisi territory.
Local sources indicate that these reinforcements could be linked to preparations for a possible offensive aimed at capturing Pinga, a strategic town that has remained a key objective for the armed movement.
Traditional authorities from the Kisimba group have called on security forces to increase vigilance and strengthen defensive measures to prevent any advance toward the town. They also urged residents to cooperate with security services by reporting suspicious movements and activities.
Despite the reported troop movements, the security situation in Pinga remains under the control of government forces. However, the broader environment remains tense, with continued military deployments and movements reported in several parts of Walikale territory.
The developments add to growing concerns over renewed fighting in North Kivu, where strategic positions and supply routes remain at the center of competition between armed groups and government forces.

title: Gen. Nkubito Rebukes Mugesera’s Past Remarks, Highlights Rwanda’s Progress
excerpt: Ngororero, July 3, 2026 - Commander of the Rwanda Defence Force’s 3rd Division, Maj. Gen. Eugene Nkubito, has criticised past remarks made by Dr. Léon Mugesera, saying the former politician should witness Rwanda’s transformation before describing former Inkotanyi fighters as…
title_en: Gen. Nkubito Rebukes Mugesera’s Past Remarks, Highlights Rwanda’s Progress
excerpt_en: Ngororero, July 3, 2026 - Commander of the Rwanda Defence Force’s 3rd Division, Maj. Gen. Eugene Nkubito, has criticised past remarks made by Dr. Léon Mugesera, saying the former politician should witness Rwanda’s transformation before describing former Inkotanyi fighters as…
body_en:
Ngororero, July 3, 2026 - Commander of the Rwanda Defence Force’s 3rd Division, Maj. Gen. Eugene Nkubito, has criticised past remarks made by Dr. Léon Mugesera, saying the former politician should witness Rwanda’s transformation before describing former Inkotanyi fighters as “fools.”
Speaking on July 2 during a ceremony in Kabaya Sector, Ngororero District, where members of the Western Province Private Sector Federation donated cows to 10 families of former soldiers disabled during the liberation struggle, Gen. Nkubito said Mugesera’s statements remained disturbing because of the contempt they expressed toward those who fought to liberate the country.
Referring to Mugesera’s controversial 1992 speech delivered in Kabaya, Gen. Nkubito said he wished the former politician could return and see the development achieved since then, including improved infrastructure, better public services and the well-being of citizens. He said the achievements demonstrated that those who fought for Rwanda’s liberation had fulfilled their mission and disproved the insults directed at them.
Gen. Nkubito also paid tribute to former soldiers who sustained disabilities during the liberation struggle, saying their sacrifices were recognised by all Rwandans. He thanked the Western Province business community for supporting the veterans’ families, describing the donations as a gesture of appreciation for their contribution to the country's liberation.
During the event, the private sector federation donated 10 cows worth a total of Rwf9.685 million to families of former liberation fighters living with disabilities in Ngororero District.
On November 22, 1992, Dr. Léon Mugesera delivered a speech at an MRND political rally in Kabaya that later became widely known for its inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

title: AFC/M23 Accuses FDLR of Killing Woman and Five Children in Rutshuru
excerpt: Rutshuru, July 3, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) of killing a woman and her five children during an overnight attack in Rutshuru Territory, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. According to AFC/M23…
title_en: AFC/M23 Accuses FDLR of Killing Woman and Five Children in Rutshuru
excerpt_en: Rutshuru, July 3, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) of killing a woman and her five children during an overnight attack in Rutshuru Territory, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. According to AFC/M23…
body_en:
Rutshuru, July 3, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) of killing a woman and her five children during an overnight attack in Rutshuru Territory, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
According to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the attack occurred on the night of July 2 in the Kabizo/Butare area of Bwito Chiefdom. He said the armed group targeted the family of a local leader identified as Rugamba, killing his wife, Tuombe Maniragaba, and their five children: Sifiwe Rugamba, Dorika Rugamba, Emery Rugamba, Mariam Rugamba and Divine Rugamba.
Kanyuka alleged that the FDLR continues to carry out attacks against Congolese civilians with the support of the Congolese government, adding that AFC/M23 would continue military operations against the group.
The allegations come amid renewed scrutiny of the FDLR's activities following a report by United Nations experts released in late June 2026, which stated that the armed group remains active in several parts of North Kivu and continues to cooperate with elements of the Congolese army and Wazalendo militias.
The reported cooperation has drawn attention because it is inconsistent with commitments made under the peace agreement signed in Washington in June 2025, under which the Democratic Republic of the Congo agreed to dismantle the FDLR within 90 days. The reported killings have not been independently verified, and Congolese authorities had not publicly commented on the incident at the time of publication.

title: UN Envoy and Darfur Rebel Leader Discuss Peace Efforts in Nairobi
excerpt: NAIROBI, July 3, 2026 - United Nations Secretary-General's Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, met with Sudan Liberation Movement-Abdel Wahid (SLM-AW) leader Abdel Wahid Mohamed Nur in Nairobi on Thursday to discuss the humanitarian crisis in Darfur and prospects for an…
title_en: UN Envoy and Darfur Rebel Leader Discuss Peace Efforts in Nairobi
excerpt_en: NAIROBI, July 3, 2026 - United Nations Secretary-General's Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, met with Sudan Liberation Movement-Abdel Wahid (SLM-AW) leader Abdel Wahid Mohamed Nur in Nairobi on Thursday to discuss the humanitarian crisis in Darfur and prospects for an…
body_en:
NAIROBI, July 3, 2026 - United Nations Secretary-General's Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, met with Sudan Liberation Movement-Abdel Wahid (SLM-AW) leader Abdel Wahid Mohamed Nur in Nairobi on Thursday to discuss the humanitarian crisis in Darfur and prospects for an inclusive political process to end Sudan's conflict.
The meeting follows the rebel movement's decision not to endorse a political framework proposed by several armed groups and political coalitions in June. The SLM-AW has maintained that any future political process must clearly exclude former ruling party figures, Islamist groups, and actors opposed to civilian rule.
During the talks, both sides examined possible pathways toward a comprehensive political transition capable of addressing the underlying causes of Sudan's prolonged instability. The rebel movement stressed that any future settlement should involve broad national participation while ensuring an inclusive civilian-led transition.
The discussions also focused on the worsening humanitarian situation in Darfur, where millions of civilians continue to face displacement and limited access to essential services. Representatives of the movement highlighted the deteriorating conditions in conflict-affected areas, citing growing shortages of food, medicine, clean water, and shelter.
Particular attention was given to the situation in Jebel Marra and parts of North Darfur, including Tawila locality, where hundreds of thousands of internally displaced people remain in need of humanitarian assistance.
The SLM-AW also called for unrestricted humanitarian access to conflict-affected regions, including Darfur, Kordofan, and Blue Nile, warning that continued obstacles to aid delivery are worsening the humanitarian crisis. The movement urged regional and international partners to press Sudan's warring parties to agree to a humanitarian truce as a first step toward a lasting nationwide ceasefire.
For his part, Haavisto reaffirmed ongoing international efforts to coordinate diplomatic initiatives and strengthen humanitarian support, particularly as the approaching rainy season threatens to further complicate aid operations and increase the vulnerability of displaced populations.

title: Jeannette Kagame Hosts Central African Republic’s First Lady to Showcase Imbuto Foundation Programmes
excerpt: Kigali, July 3, 2026 - Rwanda’s First Lady, Jeannette Kagame, on Thursday welcomed Central African Republic First Lady Brigitte Touadéra for discussions focused on the work of the Imbuto Foundation and its contribution to improving the well-being of communities through…
title_en: Jeannette Kagame Hosts Central African Republic’s First Lady to Showcase Imbuto Foundation Programmes
excerpt_en: Kigali, July 3, 2026 - Rwanda’s First Lady, Jeannette Kagame, on Thursday welcomed Central African Republic First Lady Brigitte Touadéra for discussions focused on the work of the Imbuto Foundation and its contribution to improving the well-being of communities through…
body_en:
Kigali, July 3, 2026 - Rwanda’s First Lady, Jeannette Kagame, on Thursday welcomed Central African Republic First Lady Brigitte Touadéra for discussions focused on the work of the Imbuto Foundation and its contribution to improving the well-being of communities through health, education and youth empowerment programmes.
The meeting highlighted the Foundation’s achievements since its establishment in 2001, with Mrs. Kagame outlining its role in complementing national development efforts by promoting access to quality education, strengthening healthcare initiatives and empowering women and young people.
Among its flagship initiatives is the Inkubito y'Icyeza programme, launched in 2005 to reward top-performing girls in national examinations marking the transition from primary to secondary education. Between 2005 and 2025, the programme recognised more than 7,600 students for their academic excellence.
The Foundation also runs the Edified Generation programme, which supports secondary school students by covering tuition fees and providing essential learning materials to help them complete their education.
In addition, the Imbuto Foundation has expanded support for vulnerable families through childcare initiatives. Over the past two years, it has assisted more than 5,000 childcare centres serving families participating in Rwanda's Vision 2020 Umurenge Programme (VUP) across all 30 districts.
The visit provided an opportunity for the two First Ladies to exchange views on initiatives aimed at improving social welfare and promoting inclusive development through community-based programmes.

title: UN Report Contradicts FDLR’s Peace Claims in Letter to United States
excerpt: Kigali, July 3, 2026 - A letter sent by the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) to the United States, presenting the armed group as a partner for peace in the Great Lakes region, has been contradicted by findings contained in a United Nations report on the…
title_en: UN Report Contradicts FDLR’s Peace Claims in Letter to United States
excerpt_en: Kigali, July 3, 2026 - A letter sent by the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) to the United States, presenting the armed group as a partner for peace in the Great Lakes region, has been contradicted by findings contained in a United Nations report on the…
body_en:
Kigali, July 3, 2026 - A letter sent by the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) to the United States, presenting the armed group as a partner for peace in the Great Lakes region, has been contradicted by findings contained in a United Nations report on the conflict in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The letter, dated July 2, 2025 and signed by FDLR leader Victor Byiringiro, also known as Gaston Iyamuremye, was included in the report of the UN Group of Experts on the DRC. In the document, the FDLR expresses support for the Washington Peace Agreement signed by Rwanda and the DRC on June 27, 2025, and describes itself as a movement committed to restoring lasting peace and protecting Rwandan refugees living in eastern Congo.
However, the UN report presents a different picture, describing the FDLR as a structured armed group that remains actively involved in the conflict in eastern DRC. According to the report, the organisation continues to operate through three main factions-FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-FPP-and remains under international sanctions because of its military activities.
The letter also claims that the FDLR is neither a terrorist nor a genocidal organisation and has never posed a threat to Rwanda. Those assertions contrast with the group's documented history, including attacks carried out in northwestern Rwanda and the involvement of its founders in the planning and execution of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
The report states that FDLR fighters continue to operate in several territories of North Kivu, including Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale. It also cites information indicating that the group's elite unit, known as CRAP, claims to have fighters positioned on the outskirts of Goma and others who have infiltrated the city.
According to the UN findings, a secret meeting held on April 7, 2026 in Pinga, Walikale, brought together senior officers of the Congolese armed forces and FDLR leaders, where both sides reportedly agreed to maintain their cooperation despite the signing of the Washington peace agreement.
The report estimates the FDLR's fighting force at around 3,500 members in 2025, while the group itself claims to command about 10,000 fighters and says its elite unit has more than 20,000 members.
Rwandan authorities have consistently described the FDLR as one of the country's principal security threats, arguing that beyond its military capacity, the group's continued promotion of genocidal ideology remains a major concern. The dismantling of the FDLR has been a key provision of regional peace initiatives, including the Washington agreement, as well as several United Nations Security Council resolutions calling on the DRC to disarm the group and facilitate the voluntary return of its members.
The contrast between the FDLR's message to the United States and the findings presented in the UN report has raised fresh questions over the group's portrayal of itself as a peace actor while remaining actively engaged in armed operations in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The dismantling of the FDLR has been a key provision of regional peace initiatives, including the Washington agreement, as well as several United Nations Security Council resolutions calling on the DRC to disarm the group and facilitate the voluntary return of its members.
The contrast between the FDLR's message to the United States and the findings presented in the UN report has raised fresh questions over the group's portrayal of itself as a peace actor while remaining actively engaged in armed operations in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Burundi’s Ndayishimiye Intervenes as Congolese Opposition Delays Anti-Tshisekedi Protests
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo's main opposition coalition, C64, has postponed planned protests demanding President Félix Tshisekedi’s resignation after accepting an invitation from Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye for talks on the…
title_en: Burundi’s Ndayishimiye Intervenes as Congolese Opposition Delays Anti-Tshisekedi Protests
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo's main opposition coalition, C64, has postponed planned protests demanding President Félix Tshisekedi’s resignation after accepting an invitation from Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye for talks on the…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo's main opposition coalition, C64, has postponed planned protests demanding President Félix Tshisekedi’s resignation after accepting an invitation from Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye for talks on the country's political and security crisis.
The coalition, which brings together leading opposition figures including Martin Fayulu, Jean-Marc Kabund, Moïse Katumbi, Augustin Matata Ponyo and Delly Sesanga, announced on July 3 that it would attend an urgent meeting convened by Ndayishimiye in his capacity as Chairperson of the African Union. The discussions are expected to focus on security, political and institutional challenges facing the DRC.
According to sources in Kinshasa, Ndayishimiye, a close ally of President Tshisekedi, had encouraged dialogue between the government and opposition over the controversial plan to amend the Congolese Constitution, an initiative that has sparked growing political tensions.
The opposition had been preparing a major demonstration outside the Presidential Palace on July 8 to demand Tshisekedi's resignation, accusing him of attempting to undermine the Constitution. The planned protest followed earlier demonstrations on June 12 outside the National Assembly, where opposition supporters said they were dispersed by police and members of the ruling UDPS party's youth wing, Forces du Progrès.
The government has rejected the opposition's campaign. Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo recently suspended public demonstrations in Kinshasa, citing measures to prevent the spread of Ebola. Opposition leaders, however, argued that the decision was politically motivated, noting that Ebola cases have been concentrated in eastern provinces far from the capital.
Just a day before the postponement, Martin Fayulu had renewed calls for nationwide protests, urging Congolese citizens to demand Tshisekedi's resignation over what he described as attempts to violate the Constitution.
Following an emergency meeting on July 3, C64 leaders agreed to postpone the demonstrations until July 22 to allow time for discussions with Ndayishimiye. They said they intended to use the talks to express concerns over the country's political direction and to defend constitutional order, while maintaining that their campaign against constitutional changes would continue if their demands were not met.

title: Rwanda Introduces Random Anti-Doping Tests for Football Players from 2026/27 Season
excerpt: Kigali, July 3, 2026 - Football players in Rwanda will undergo random health checks from the 2026/27 season as part of new measures introduced by the Rwanda Football Association (FERWAFA) to combat the use of prohibited substances and illegal performance-enhancing drugs in…
title_en: Rwanda Introduces Random Anti-Doping Tests for Football Players from 2026/27 Season
excerpt_en: Kigali, July 3, 2026 - Football players in Rwanda will undergo random health checks from the 2026/27 season as part of new measures introduced by the Rwanda Football Association (FERWAFA) to combat the use of prohibited substances and illegal performance-enhancing drugs in…
body_en:
Kigali, July 3, 2026 - Football players in Rwanda will undergo random health checks from the 2026/27 season as part of new measures introduced by the Rwanda Football Association (FERWAFA) to combat the use of prohibited substances and illegal performance-enhancing drugs in sports.
The decision was taken during a FERWAFA Executive Committee meeting held on July 1, 2026, where officials approved several reforms aimed at improving competition standards and protecting athletes’ health. The anti-doping programme will involve random testing of players to prevent doping practices and promote fair competition.
FERWAFA also approved new registration fees for controlled competitions for the 2026/27 and 2027/28 seasons. Clubs in the BK Pro League will pay Rwf2 million, while registration for the Second Division Championship, Third Division Championship, Women’s Super League and Bagabo Peace Cup will cost Rwf500,000. Women’s Second Division competitions and the Bagore Peace Cup will require Rwf200,000, while women’s regional competitions will cost Rwf100,000.
The football governing body also announced plans to update its logo, competition branding, trophies and national team uniforms across all categories through a creative competition involving local talents.
The move comes as Rwanda continues efforts to strengthen its anti-doping system. Although the country has signed the UNESCO Convention on the Fight against Doping in Sport, a fully operational national anti-doping body has not yet been established. A previous study by the Rwanda Olympic Committee’s Medical and Anti-Doping Commission showed that many sports stakeholders receive doping information mainly through the media, with 97.1% saying they were familiar with the topic, although only 15.9% expressed strong confidence in their knowledge.
Currently, Rwanda sends doping samples to foreign laboratories, mainly in South Africa and Spain, due to the absence of a national testing facility. Officials have said the process is costly, with one test estimated to cost around $600, or more than Rwf870,000.
Sports authorities have proposed the creation of a National Anti-Doping Organisation (NADO), an independent institution that would oversee testing, education, regulations and legal matters related to doping. Establishing such a body would also help Rwanda meet international requirements and reduce reliance on foreign laboratories.
With the introduction of random testing in football and ongoing efforts to build stronger anti-doping structures, Rwanda aims to improve the integrity of its sports competitions and protect the health of athletes.

title: MONUSCO Ready to Support Ceasefire Monitoring Missions, Says James Swan
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 - The United Nations Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO) has reaffirmed its readiness to support ceasefire monitoring operations in eastern DRC as diplomatic efforts continue to end the conflict between government forces…
title_en: MONUSCO Ready to Support Ceasefire Monitoring Missions, Says James Swan
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 - The United Nations Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO) has reaffirmed its readiness to support ceasefire monitoring operations in eastern DRC as diplomatic efforts continue to end the conflict between government forces…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 - The United Nations Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO) has reaffirmed its readiness to support ceasefire monitoring operations in eastern DRC as diplomatic efforts continue to end the conflict between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion.
James Swan, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Head of MONUSCO, announced the mission’s preparedness following a meeting on Thursday, July 2, with Guy Kabombo, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence and Veterans Affairs.
The discussions focused on MONUSCO’s role in supporting peace initiatives, particularly the Washington Agreement and the Doha Process, as well as strengthening the operational capacity of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), a regional mechanism tasked with monitoring security commitments.
James Swan said MONUSCO had received a mandate to assist ceasefire verification efforts and was working closely with Congolese authorities to ensure effective implementation. He stressed that the mission was prepared to provide logistical support and security assistance once the locations for verification missions are officially identified.
“MONUSCO is ready to support missions at the identified sites for ceasefire monitoring,” Swan said, adding that planning activities were already underway to facilitate the deployment of verification teams.
The announcement comes amid growing international pressure for the rapid deployment of ceasefire monitoring mechanisms following discussions within the framework of the Washington Agreement. Kinshasa and Kigali have committed to supporting the deployment of the EJVM+ and strengthening verification processes aimed at ensuring compliance with peace commitments.
During the meeting, MONUSCO also reviewed its broader cooperation with the Congolese government and the FARDC. James Swan highlighted the importance of coordination in protecting civilians, supporting disarmament and reintegration programs for armed groups, and assisting security sector reforms.
MONUSCO currently maintains thousands of peacekeepers in the country and continues operations, particularly in areas affected by armed violence in northern North Kivu and Ituri.
The mission’s renewed commitment comes as diplomatic initiatives face significant challenges amid persistent insecurity in eastern DRC. The success of ceasefire monitoring efforts will depend on the cooperation of all parties involved and the creation of conditions allowing verification teams to operate safely on the ground.

title: Kamuli Man Arrested After Allegedly Severing Wife’s Arm in Domestic Violence Attack
excerpt: Kamuli, Uganda, July 3, 2026 - A 50-year-old man has been arrested in Kamuli District after allegedly attacking his wife with a machete, severing one of her arms during a domestic dispute before reportedly attempting to take his own life by ingesting poison. The incident…
title_en: Kamuli Man Arrested After Allegedly Severing Wife’s Arm in Domestic Violence Attack
excerpt_en: Kamuli, Uganda, July 3, 2026 - A 50-year-old man has been arrested in Kamuli District after allegedly attacking his wife with a machete, severing one of her arms during a domestic dispute before reportedly attempting to take his own life by ingesting poison. The incident…
body_en:
Kamuli, Uganda, July 3, 2026 - A 50-year-old man has been arrested in Kamuli District after allegedly attacking his wife with a machete, severing one of her arms during a domestic dispute before reportedly attempting to take his own life by ingesting poison.
The incident occurred in the early hours of July 2 in Kadholwe Zone, Kasolwe Parish, Kagumba Sub-county. The victim, a 40-year-old woman, sustained life-threatening injuries after being assaulted while reportedly leaving the couple's home following a domestic disagreement.
Preliminary investigations indicate that the suspect allegedly ordered his wife to leave the residence before attacking her with a machete, severing her left hand at the wrist and inflicting additional injuries. The victim raised an alarm, prompting nearby residents to intervene and arrange her transfer for emergency medical treatment.
Following the attack, authorities launched a search operation and later found the suspect unconscious after he allegedly consumed poison in an apparent suicide attempt. He was taken to Kamuli General Hospital, where he remains under police guard while receiving treatment.
Authorities said the suspect is expected to face attempted murder charges once he is declared medically fit.
The case has renewed concerns over the persistence of domestic and gender-based violence in Kamuli District, where authorities say several serious incidents have been recorded in recent years. Investigations into the attack remain ongoing.

title: UN Report Details Alleged Rwandan Command Structure Behind AFC/M23 Operations
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 - A new report by the United Nations Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of Congo has highlighted what it describes as a structured chain of command linking the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) to the operations of the Congo River Alliance/AFC-M23…
title_en: UN Report Details Alleged Rwandan Command Structure Behind AFC/M23 Operations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 - A new report by the United Nations Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of Congo has highlighted what it describes as a structured chain of command linking the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) to the operations of the Congo River Alliance/AFC-M23…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 3, 2026 - A new report by the United Nations Group of Experts on the Democratic Republic of Congo has highlighted what it describes as a structured chain of command linking the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) to the operations of the Congo River Alliance/AFC-M23 movement in eastern DRC.
The assessment examines the military coordination and operational links between the RDF and AFC/M23, which continues to control significant areas of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict.
According to the report, Rwanda’s leadership appointed senior military figures to oversee security and defence matters connected to the conflict. Retired General James Kabarebe was appointed as senior defence and security adviser in December 2025, while Brigadier General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama was later named his deputy in January 2026.
The document states that Nyirabutama played a role in managing communication channels with AFC/M23, while James Kabarebe allegedly acted as a key intermediary between Rwandan authorities, AFC/M23 leaders, and former Congolese President Joseph Kabila. The report mentions frequent meetings held in Gisenyi as part of these contacts.
The UN experts describe an operational structure in which senior RDF officials in Kigali maintained links with commanders on the ground. The report identifies General Vincent Nyakarundi, Chief of Staff of the RDF army, as having overseen operations in eastern DRC.
The assessment further indicates that elements of Rwanda’s 3rd and 4th Divisions were involved in the regional military deployment. The 3rd Division was reportedly active mainly in North Kivu under Major General Eugene Nkubito, while the 4th Division operated primarily in South Kivu before being redeployed to Mozambique at the end of 2025. Special forces units were also reportedly involved in frontline operations.
According to the report, former AFC/M23 recruits interviewed by UN experts described the presence of RDF personnel, including specialized units, during high-risk military operations.
The experts further state that the Rwandan authorities allegedly influenced AFC/M23’s strategic decisions, including which territories to capture, hold, or withdraw from, suggesting a high level of operational coordination between the two actors.
The report also indicates that UN experts formally requested explanations from the Rwandan government regarding alleged support to AFC/M23 but had not received a response at the time of publication.
The allegations involving former President Joseph Kabila and his political allies remain strongly contested. Kabila’s camp has repeatedly rejected accusations of links with AFC/M23 and Rwanda, describing the legal proceedings against him as politically motivated and aimed at weakening his political influence.
The publication of the UN report comes as diplomatic efforts under the Washington Agreement and the Doha peace process continue to face major obstacles. Despite international mediation efforts, tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali remain high, with disagreements persisting over the interpretation and implementation of commitments.
Negotiations between the Congolese government and AFC/M23 have yet to achieve a breakthrough, while security conditions on the ground continue to deteriorate. Regional and international actors continue to call on all parties to respect their commitments, but the gap between diplomatic agreements and developments on the battlefield remains a major challenge for peace efforts in eastern DRC.

title: Red Cross Expands Emergency Aid in El Obeid as Conflict Threatens Civilian Lives
excerpt: EL OBEID, July 3, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has increased humanitarian assistance in El Obeid and surrounding areas of North Kordofan as rising tensions and the threat of a major offensive place hundreds of thousands of civilians at risk.…
title_en: Red Cross Expands Emergency Aid in El Obeid as Conflict Threatens Civilian Lives
excerpt_en: EL OBEID, July 3, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has increased humanitarian assistance in El Obeid and surrounding areas of North Kordofan as rising tensions and the threat of a major offensive place hundreds of thousands of civilians at risk.…
body_en:
EL OBEID, July 3, 2026 - The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has increased humanitarian assistance in El Obeid and surrounding areas of North Kordofan as rising tensions and the threat of a major offensive place hundreds of thousands of civilians at risk.
Humanitarian teams have provided assistance to approximately 42,000 people, including displaced families and vulnerable communities affected by the ongoing conflict. The support includes food distributions, emergency healthcare assistance, and nutritional programs aimed at preventing further deterioration among the most vulnerable groups.
El Obeid is currently hosting around 105,000 internally displaced people, including tens of thousands living in overcrowded displacement camps. Aid organizations warn that many families are reaching the limits of their ability to cope due to unemployment, rising living costs, and limited humanitarian funding.
Food assistance has been delivered to displaced households and vulnerable residents, while nutritional supplements are being provided to thousands of children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding mothers facing increased risks of malnutrition.
The humanitarian situation has worsened as continued fighting disrupts essential services. Residents have faced months of displacement, uncertainty, electricity interruptions, and growing difficulties accessing basic needs.
The city has become a major focus of concern as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) continue to increase military pressure around El Obeid, with reports of attacks affecting power facilities and fuel infrastructure.
A possible escalation of fighting threatens not only the city's population but also surrounding communities, given El Obeid’s strategic role as a major commercial and transport hub connecting central Sudan with Kordofan and western Darfur.
To prepare for potential casualties, emergency medical teams have strengthened healthcare capacity in cooperation with local partners. Hundreds of people suffering weapon-related injuries have received treatment at El Obeid Teaching Hospital since the beginning of the year, placing additional pressure on medical facilities.
Humanitarian organizations have delivered surgical supplies, emergency medical equipment, and disease-control materials to support hospitals and respond to potential outbreaks, including waterborne diseases.
Efforts are also underway to improve access to clean water through the rehabilitation of existing wells and the construction of new water points benefiting thousands of displaced families.
Humanitarian officials have called on all parties to the conflict to protect civilians and avoid targeting essential infrastructure, including hospitals, water systems, and electricity networks, warning that damage to these services could significantly increase civilian suffering.

title: Sudan Central Bank Tightens Oversight of Fintech Partnerships
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 3, 2026 - The Central Bank of Sudan has introduced stricter regulations requiring all banks and licensed financial technology (fintech) companies to obtain prior approval before entering into partnerships, technical integrations, operational agreements, or…
title_en: Sudan Central Bank Tightens Oversight of Fintech Partnerships
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 3, 2026 - The Central Bank of Sudan has introduced stricter regulations requiring all banks and licensed financial technology (fintech) companies to obtain prior approval before entering into partnerships, technical integrations, operational agreements, or…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 3, 2026 - The Central Bank of Sudan has introduced stricter regulations requiring all banks and licensed financial technology (fintech) companies to obtain prior approval before entering into partnerships, technical integrations, operational agreements, or data-sharing arrangements.
The new directive comes as Sudan's financial sector continues its transition toward digital banking and electronic payment systems, amid growing scrutiny over the governance, security, and transparency of fintech operations.
Under the new rules, all licensed banks, payment service providers, and financial switch operators must receive written authorization from the central bank before implementing any contractual or technical collaboration involving financial services or customer data.
The central bank said the measure is intended to strengthen oversight of the country's payment ecosystem and ensure that all licensed entities comply with strict standards on corporate governance, financial stability, risk management, cybersecurity, business continuity, and data protection.
Authorities emphasized that safeguarding customer information and preserving financial confidentiality remain key regulatory priorities. Financial institutions and technology providers are expected to apply robust encryption, access controls, and data governance measures to ensure that customer information is processed only within legally authorized limits.
The regulator said the licensing of multiple technology providers is part of a broader strategy to promote innovation, increase competition, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen the resilience of Sudan's digital financial infrastructure. However, it stressed that licensing alone does not authorize a company to provide services directly to banks without additional regulatory approval.
The Central Bank reaffirmed that it remains the sole authority responsible for regulating and supervising the national payment system, while licensed companies operate within a framework established by the regulator.
Officials said the ongoing modernization of Sudan's payment infrastructure is designed to expand access to digital financial services, promote financial inclusion, and enhance the stability of the country's banking sector in line with international standards.
In recent months, the central bank has licensed several national companies to operate as financial switch providers. The initiative aims to strengthen electronic payment services, support banks without their own switching infrastructure, facilitate retail banking services, improve connectivity between automated teller machines (ATMs) and payment terminals, and integrate telecommunications companies, utility providers, and government revenue collection agencies into the national payment system.
The modernization effort is also expected to enhance interoperability between banks and fintech firms, paving the way for broader adoption of innovative digital financial services across Sudan.

title: Sudan Seeks International Backing for Peace Plan Amid Rising Security Concerns
excerpt: GENEVA, July 2, 2026 - Sudan's Foreign Minister, Mohieddin Salem, held a series of high-level meetings in Geneva on Wednesday to present the government's roadmap for peace and reconstruction while highlighting growing security challenges, particularly the escalating violence…
title_en: Sudan Seeks International Backing for Peace Plan Amid Rising Security Concerns
excerpt_en: GENEVA, July 2, 2026 - Sudan's Foreign Minister, Mohieddin Salem, held a series of high-level meetings in Geneva on Wednesday to present the government's roadmap for peace and reconstruction while highlighting growing security challenges, particularly the escalating violence…
body_en:
GENEVA, July 2, 2026 - Sudan's Foreign Minister, Mohieddin Salem, held a series of high-level meetings in Geneva on Wednesday to present the government's roadmap for peace and reconstruction while highlighting growing security challenges, particularly the escalating violence in El Obeid.
During discussions with senior international officials, Salem outlined Sudan's transition plan, emphasizing post-conflict reconstruction, the protection of human rights, and measures aimed at facilitating the return of millions of displaced citizens.
The diplomatic visit marks the second senior Sudanese mission to Geneva this year as the government continues efforts to secure international support for rebuilding the country after more than three years of conflict.
In talks with representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the foreign minister expressed concern over continued drone attacks targeting civilians and critical infrastructure in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan State. The city remains under mounting pressure as fighting intensifies, threatening hundreds of thousands of residents and internally displaced people while raising fears of disrupted humanitarian access to the wider Kordofan and Darfur regions.
Salem also reiterated Sudan's willingness to cooperate on prisoner exchanges, noting ongoing international mediation efforts and raising concerns over thousands of detainees reportedly being held in Darfur.
During a separate meeting with the Director General of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), discussions focused on shifting from emergency humanitarian assistance toward early recovery and reconstruction programs in areas now under government control.
According to official figures presented during the meetings, approximately 3.66 million people have returned to their homes following improvements in security across parts of Khartoum, Gezira, Sennar, White Nile, and North Kordofan. The government said the number includes more than 775,000 Sudanese who have returned from neighboring countries.
Authorities also reported a decline in the number of internally displaced people, which has fallen to an estimated 8.8 million from a peak of 11.58 million recorded in January 2025. Despite the progress, humanitarian needs remain significant as large parts of the country continue to experience insecurity and limited access to essential services.

title: Sudanese Army Downs Long-Range Drone as Fighting Intensifies in White Nile
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 2, 2026 - The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announced on Thursday that they had intercepted and destroyed a long-range drone operated by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) over Tendalti in White Nile State, amid escalating hostilities in central Sudan. According to…
title_en: Sudanese Army Downs Long-Range Drone as Fighting Intensifies in White Nile
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 2, 2026 - The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announced on Thursday that they had intercepted and destroyed a long-range drone operated by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) over Tendalti in White Nile State, amid escalating hostilities in central Sudan. According to…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 2, 2026 - The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announced on Thursday that they had intercepted and destroyed a long-range drone operated by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) over Tendalti in White Nile State, amid escalating hostilities in central Sudan.
According to the military, air defense units shot down what was described as a strategic drone during the morning hours. Authorities later released footage showing the aircraft being intercepted in flight.
The incident comes as the RSF has intensified drone attacks across El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan State, and along the strategic highway linking North Kordofan with White Nile State. Military officials say the recent strikes have also targeted the cities of Kosti and Rabak, damaging fuel stations and other public infrastructure.
The attacks have reportedly resulted in civilian casualties and disrupted essential services, adding to growing humanitarian concerns in the affected areas.
White Nile State Governor Qamar al-Din Mohammed Fadl al-Mawla praised the performance of the army's air defense systems, describing the interception as evidence of the state's preparedness to respond to aerial threats.
The governor reaffirmed his administration's support for the Sudanese military and allied forces, stating that security operations would continue until government control is restored across all contested areas.

title: Fragile Calm Returns to Bulende After AFC/M23 and Wazalendo Clashes
excerpt: Goma, July 2, 2026 - A fragile calm has returned to Bulende, in the Bashali Mokoto area of Masisi territory, North Kivu province, following armed clashes between AFC/M23 fighters and Wazalendo groups. The fighting erupted on Wednesday, July 1, when AFC/M23 elements attempted…
title_en: Fragile Calm Returns to Bulende After AFC/M23 and Wazalendo Clashes
excerpt_en: Goma, July 2, 2026 - A fragile calm has returned to Bulende, in the Bashali Mokoto area of Masisi territory, North Kivu province, following armed clashes between AFC/M23 fighters and Wazalendo groups. The fighting erupted on Wednesday, July 1, when AFC/M23 elements attempted…
body_en:
Goma, July 2, 2026 - A fragile calm has returned to Bulende, in the Bashali Mokoto area of Masisi territory, North Kivu province, following armed clashes between AFC/M23 fighters and Wazalendo groups.
The fighting erupted on Wednesday, July 1, when AFC/M23 elements attempted to advance toward Bukonde, a strategic area located on the border between Bashali Mokoto in Masisi and Kisimba in Walikale territory. The reported objective was to bypass positions held around Mindjendje and continue progress toward Mpety.
The advance was met with resistance from Wazalendo fighters stationed in Bulende. According to local security sources, the armed group succeeded in pushing back the AFC/M23 forces, forcing them to withdraw toward Malemo, where they had previously established positions.
The clashes reportedly involved heavy and light weapons, causing panic among residents in nearby villages. Several local sources also reported the use of drones by AFC/M23 forces against Wazalendo positions, although the extent of damage and the number of casualties remain unclear.
While no major fighting was reported on Thursday, July 2, security conditions in the area remain uncertain. Residents continue to face heightened concerns as armed groups maintain positions in the surrounding areas and tensions persist across Masisi territory.

title: Djibouti's National Assembly Marks International Day of Parliamentarism with Call for Stronger Democratic Governance
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - The President of Djibouti's National Assembly, Dileita Mohamed Dileita, has reaffirmed the importance of parliamentary institutions in strengthening democracy, promoting good governance, and advancing national development as the country marked…
title_en: Djibouti's National Assembly Marks International Day of Parliamentarism with Call for Stronger Democratic Governance
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - The President of Djibouti's National Assembly, Dileita Mohamed Dileita, has reaffirmed the importance of parliamentary institutions in strengthening democracy, promoting good governance, and advancing national development as the country marked…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - The President of Djibouti's National Assembly, Dileita Mohamed Dileita, has reaffirmed the importance of parliamentary institutions in strengthening democracy, promoting good governance, and advancing national development as the country marked the International Day of Parliamentarism.
In a message issued to commemorate the annual observance, Dileita praised parliamentarians for their continued commitment to the rule of law, democratic governance, peace, and the country's socioeconomic progress.
He emphasized that parliaments play a central role in representing citizens, overseeing government action, and adopting legislation that shapes national life. He also highlighted the importance of maintaining parliamentary institutions that remain responsive to public expectations while supporting the country's ongoing economic and social transformation.
The National Assembly president reiterated his commitment to building a strong, responsible, and transparent parliament capable of addressing citizens' concerns and reinforcing democratic institutions.
He also underscored the growing importance of parliamentary diplomacy, describing cooperation between legislative bodies as a valuable tool for strengthening international partnerships, encouraging dialogue, and promoting peace and sustainable development.
Dileita extended his congratulations to parliamentarians and all individuals working to strengthen democratic institutions, recognizing their contribution to advancing democratic values and improving governance in Djibouti.
Observed annually on June 30, the International Day of Parliamentarism recognizes the essential role of parliaments in fostering inclusive, representative, and resilient societies. Through its commemorative message, Djibouti's National Assembly reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening the rule of law, democratic governance, and public service while supporting the aspirations of the Djiboutian people.
