title: Djiboutian Diaspora in Belgium Celebrates Independence with Unity, Cultural Pride and Community Recognition
excerpt: BRUSSELS, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti's diaspora in Belgium commemorated the 49th anniversary of the country's independence with a series of events celebrating national unity, cultural heritage, sporting excellence, and the achievements of Djiboutians living abroad, while looking…
title_en: Djiboutian Diaspora in Belgium Celebrates Independence with Unity, Cultural Pride and Community Recognition
excerpt_en: BRUSSELS, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti's diaspora in Belgium commemorated the 49th anniversary of the country's independence with a series of events celebrating national unity, cultural heritage, sporting excellence, and the achievements of Djiboutians living abroad, while looking…
body_en:
BRUSSELS, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti's diaspora in Belgium commemorated the 49th anniversary of the country's independence with a series of events celebrating national unity, cultural heritage, sporting excellence, and the achievements of Djiboutians living abroad, while looking ahead to the nation's golden jubilee in 2027.
The celebrations, organized by Djibouti's embassy in Belgium, the European Union, and the Benelux countries, brought together nearly 1,200 members of the Djiboutian community from Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and neighboring countries for a patriotic gathering in Brussels.
The anniversary events united multiple generations of the diaspora, with families, young people, and elders participating in cultural performances, patriotic ceremonies, and community activities that highlighted their continued ties to their homeland.
Addressing the gathering, Ambassador Aden Mohamed Dileita paid tribute to those who contributed to Djibouti's independence in 1977 and reflected on the country's progress over the past 49 years. He emphasized the importance of preserving national unity and encouraged members of the diaspora to continue promoting the values of solidarity, tolerance, and social cohesion as Djibouti prepares to celebrate the 50th anniversary of its independence next year.
The ambassador also praised the diaspora for serving as ambassadors of Djibouti abroad through their professional achievements and contributions to their host societies.
The celebrations featured cultural performances by Djiboutian artists, showcasing the country's musical heritage and strengthening cultural ties among community members. Organizers noted that the event also brought together participants from diverse political backgrounds, describing the broad participation as a symbol of national reconciliation and unity.
A major highlight of the celebrations was the inaugural Diaspora Excellence Awards, which recognized Djiboutians living in Belgium for outstanding achievements in professional, academic, entrepreneurial, technological, medical, and community leadership fields.
The awards honored individuals whose careers and civic engagement have contributed both to Belgian society and to Djibouti's international image. Three categories of recognition-Merit Awards, Encouragement Awards, and Honorary Awards-were presented during the ceremony.
Officials said the initiative aims not only to celebrate individual accomplishments but also to encourage greater involvement of the diaspora in Djibouti's development through knowledge transfer, mentoring, innovation, and support for younger generations. Organizers indicated that the awards could become an annual event.
The independence celebrations concluded with the third edition of the Djiboutian Independence Football Tournament, held in Aalst and bringing together teams from Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg.
The competition attracted young players, former footballers, families, and supporters, with organizers promoting sport as a platform for strengthening unity, discipline, and social cohesion within the diaspora. Former national football figures also participated, adding a symbolic dimension to the event.
The tournament ended with a medal ceremony led by Ambassador Aden Mohamed Dileita, who commended the commitment and community spirit demonstrated by young Djiboutians across the Benelux region.
As preparations begin for Djibouti's 50th anniversary of independence in 2027, the events underscored the diaspora's growing role as a source of talent, cultural identity, and national unity. Organizers emphasized that, despite living abroad, Djiboutians remain closely connected through a shared history, common values, and a collective commitment to the country's future.

title: UN Report Links Rubaya Coltan to Organized Smuggling Network Through Rwanda
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 – The exploitation of coltan in the Rubaya mining area of North Kivu intensified significantly in 2025, with production reportedly exceeding previous estimates, according to a United Nations report detailing an organized system of mineral extraction,…
title_en: UN Report Links Rubaya Coltan to Organized Smuggling Network Through Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 – The exploitation of coltan in the Rubaya mining area of North Kivu intensified significantly in 2025, with production reportedly exceeding previous estimates, according to a United Nations report detailing an organized system of mineral extraction,…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 – The exploitation of coltan in the Rubaya mining area of North Kivu intensified significantly in 2025, with production reportedly exceeding previous estimates, according to a United Nations report detailing an organized system of mineral extraction, taxation, and cross-border trade under AFC/M23 control.
The report describes a structured revenue collection mechanism in which taxes are imposed on mineral production, with charges reportedly set at US$4 per kilogram of coltan and US$2 per kilogram of cassiterite. It also outlines a system involving licensed transporters, checkpoints, and financial channels allegedly used to collect revenues generated from the mining sector.
According to the findings, minerals extracted from Rubaya are transported through an organized supply chain before reaching companies based in Kigali, where they are processed and exported to international markets.
The report identifies Rani Mining Ltd. and Kanzamin Limited among the companies that allegedly exported substantial quantities of coltan originating from Rubaya. Customs documentation examined by investigators reportedly indicates that Rani Mining Ltd. exported more than 84 tonnes of coltan, while Kanzamin Limited exported at least 70 tonnes during 2025.
The report also points to a sharp increase in Rwanda's cassiterite exports, which reportedly rose by 58 percent, from 4,859 tonnes to 7,700 tonnes over the course of the year. According to the investigators, the increase is not consistent with Rwanda's reported domestic production levels, raising questions about the origin of the exported minerals.
As part of its investigation, the United Nations Panel of Experts requested clarification from the Rwandan government regarding these findings on April 2, 2026. At the time of the report's publication, no official response had been received.
The findings add to longstanding international concerns over the illicit exploitation of mineral resources in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and the role that cross-border mineral trade may play in financing armed groups and sustaining regional insecurity.

title: Drone Strike Destroys Vital UN Aid Supplies as Sudan Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
excerpt: UNITED NATIONS, July 2, 2026 - A drone strike in Sudan has destroyed 50 tonnes of humanitarian supplies intended for vulnerable communities in South Kordofan, further worsening the challenges facing aid operations in the conflict-hit country. The attack targeted a contracted…
title_en: Drone Strike Destroys Vital UN Aid Supplies as Sudan Humanitarian Crisis Deepens
excerpt_en: UNITED NATIONS, July 2, 2026 - A drone strike in Sudan has destroyed 50 tonnes of humanitarian supplies intended for vulnerable communities in South Kordofan, further worsening the challenges facing aid operations in the conflict-hit country. The attack targeted a contracted…
body_en:
UNITED NATIONS, July 2, 2026 - A drone strike in Sudan has destroyed 50 tonnes of humanitarian supplies intended for vulnerable communities in South Kordofan, further worsening the challenges facing aid operations in the conflict-hit country.
The attack targeted a contracted humanitarian transport truck near Tendelti in White Nile State while it was carrying relief materials destined for Abu Jubeyha. The driver survived the incident, but the entire shipment was destroyed.
The destroyed supplies included thousands of blankets, water containers, kitchen equipment, sleeping mats, plastic sheets, and solar lamps, materials intended to support families affected by conflict and displacement.
Humanitarian officials warned that the loss of the shipment would leave thousands of civilians without essential assistance at a time when access to basic services remains severely limited across several regions of Sudan.
The incident occurred amid a wider escalation of violence involving increased drone activity and attacks on civilian areas. Additional drone strikes were reported in Kosti, White Nile State, causing civilian injuries and further damaging already fragile infrastructure.
Despite growing security risks, humanitarian organizations continue efforts to deliver emergency assistance where access remains possible. Recent operations have included the transport of medical supplies, including cholera response materials, to health facilities in South Kordofan to address rising disease outbreaks.
The United Nations has renewed calls on all parties to the conflict to protect civilians, safeguard humanitarian operations, and prevent attacks on essential infrastructure.
International partners have also been urged to increase financial support for relief operations as humanitarian needs continue to grow across Sudan.

The incident occurred amid a wider escalation of violence involving increased drone activity and attacks on civilian areas. Additional drone strikes were reported in Kosti, White Nile State, causing civilian injuries and further damaging already fragile infrastructure.
Despite growing security risks, humanitarian organizations continue efforts to deliver emergency assistance where access remains possible. Recent operations have included the transport of medical supplies, including cholera response materials, to health facilities in South Kordofan to address rising disease outbreaks.
The United Nations has renewed calls on all parties to the conflict to protect civilians, safeguard humanitarian operations, and prevent attacks on essential infrastructure.
International partners have also been urged to increase financial support for relief operations as humanitarian needs continue to grow across Sudan.

title: Rwanda Cuts Under-Five Mortality by Nearly 82% in 25 Years
excerpt: Kigali, July 2, 2026 - Rwanda has achieved a major milestone in child survival, reducing the under-five mortality rate by nearly 82% over the past 25 years, reflecting sustained improvements in maternal and child healthcare across the country. In 2000, 196 out of every 1,000…
title_en: Rwanda Cuts Under-Five Mortality by Nearly 82% in 25 Years
excerpt_en: Kigali, July 2, 2026 - Rwanda has achieved a major milestone in child survival, reducing the under-five mortality rate by nearly 82% over the past 25 years, reflecting sustained improvements in maternal and child healthcare across the country. In 2000, 196 out of every 1,000…
body_en:
Kigali, July 2, 2026 - Rwanda has achieved a major milestone in child survival, reducing the under-five mortality rate by nearly 82% over the past 25 years, reflecting sustained improvements in maternal and child healthcare across the country.
In 2000, 196 out of every 1,000 children born alive died before reaching their fifth birthday. By 2005, the figure had dropped to 152, before falling sharply to 76 in 2010.
The downward trend continued in subsequent years, reaching 50 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2014-2015, 45 in 2019-2020, and 36 per 1,000 live births by 2025.
Overall, the country has reduced under-five mortality by 160 deaths per 1,000 live births since 2000, representing an 81.6% decline.
The most dramatic improvement occurred between 2005 and 2010, when the mortality rate was cut in half, dropping from 152 to 76 deaths per 1,000 live births.
Despite the significant gains, the figures indicate that challenges remain, with 36 children out of every 1,000 live births still dying before the age of five, underscoring the need for continued investment in maternal and child health services.
The progress has been driven by a range of health sector reforms, including the expansion of skilled birth attendance, increased numbers of trained midwives, and improved access to quality healthcare services.
One of the most notable achievements has been the rise in hospital deliveries. The proportion of women giving birth in health facilities increased from just 25% in 1992 to 98% in 2025, marking a dramatic shift toward safer childbirth.
Hospital deliveries rose steadily over the years, climbing from 27% in 2000 to 39% in 2005, 69% in 2010, 91% in 2014-2015, 94% in 2019-2020, and 98% in 2025.
As a result, only 2% of births now take place outside health facilities, a development that has contributed significantly to reducing both maternal and newborn deaths.
The country's sustained progress has positioned Rwanda among the leading performers in East Africa in improving child survival, with expanded access to maternal healthcare playing a central role in saving the lives of mothers and children alike.

title: Nakawa Officials Arrested Over Alleged Mismanagement of Emyoga Funds
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, July 2, 2026 - Authorities have ordered the arrest of two leaders of the Nakawa Market Vegetable Emyoga SACCO over allegations of mismanaging more than Shs6 million allocated under the government's Emyoga programme. The arrests target the SACCO chairperson,…
title_en: Nakawa Officials Arrested Over Alleged Mismanagement of Emyoga Funds
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, July 2, 2026 - Authorities have ordered the arrest of two leaders of the Nakawa Market Vegetable Emyoga SACCO over allegations of mismanaging more than Shs6 million allocated under the government's Emyoga programme. The arrests target the SACCO chairperson,…
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, July 2, 2026 - Authorities have ordered the arrest of two leaders of the Nakawa Market Vegetable Emyoga SACCO over allegations of mismanaging more than Shs6 million allocated under the government's Emyoga programme.
The arrests target the SACCO chairperson, Denis Muliisi, and the secretary, identified only as Kasoma, following complaints from market traders who accused the leadership of failing to account for funds intended to support members through the government initiative.
The allegations emerged during a meeting convened to address concerns raised by SACCO members. The organisation's treasurer accused the chairperson of managing the SACCO independently, making financial decisions without consulting other leaders, and exercising sole control over members' funds.
Authorities subsequently demanded an explanation for the whereabouts of the reportedly missing funds. In response, Muliisi denied misappropriating the money but stated he was willing to reimburse the amount to protect the credibility of the Emyoga programme. He also attributed any administrative shortcomings to his limited educational background.
Several SACCO members further alleged that funds had been distributed to beneficiaries in ways that did not comply with the programme's operational guidelines.
Following the meeting, police were instructed to arrest Muliisi and Kasoma to facilitate investigations into the management of the SACCO's finances. Authorities warned that any leaders found to have mismanaged public funds allocated under government programmes would face legal action.
The two officials have denied the allegations, arguing that the accusations are part of an internal leadership dispute aimed at undermining their positions. Investigations are ongoing.

title: IGAD and South Sudan Step Up Preparations for December 2026 General Elections
excerpt: JUBA, July 2, 2026 - The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the Government of South Sudan have intensified consultations on the implementation of the country's peace agreement and preparations for the general elections scheduled for December 2026. The…
title_en: IGAD and South Sudan Step Up Preparations for December 2026 General Elections
excerpt_en: JUBA, July 2, 2026 - The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the Government of South Sudan have intensified consultations on the implementation of the country's peace agreement and preparations for the general elections scheduled for December 2026. The…
body_en:
JUBA, July 2, 2026 - The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the Government of South Sudan have intensified consultations on the implementation of the country's peace agreement and preparations for the general elections scheduled for December 2026.
The discussions took place during a meeting in Juba between IGAD Special Envoy to South Sudan, Ambassador Moussa Djama Ali, and South Sudanese Vice President Hussein Abdelbagi Akol, as the country moves closer to what is expected to be a landmark electoral process.
The two officials reviewed progress in implementing the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement, the status of electoral preparations, political dialogue among the transitional parties, and arrangements for concluding the country's transitional period.
Vice President Hussein Abdelbagi Akol reaffirmed his government's commitment to fully implementing the peace agreement and creating the conditions necessary for free, fair, peaceful, and credible elections later this year. He also commended IGAD for its sustained support since the signing of the peace accord, describing the regional bloc as a key partner in South Sudan's efforts to consolidate peace and stability.
Ambassador Moussa Djama Ali reiterated IGAD's commitment to supporting South Sudan throughout the transition, emphasizing the organization's continued engagement in promoting political dialogue, national reconciliation, and cooperation among the parties to the peace process.
The consultations come as South Sudan prepares for what is expected to be its first general elections since gaining independence in 2011, a milestone widely regarded as critical to advancing democratic governance and securing long-term peace and stability.
Both sides emphasized the importance of maintaining momentum in implementing the peace agreement to ensure a credible electoral process and support a peaceful political transition. The meeting underscored IGAD's continued role in accompanying South Sudan as it seeks to conclude its transitional period and strengthen democratic institutions ahead of the December polls.

title: Djibouti Inaugurates First Hydroelectric Plant to Advance Green Energy Transition
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti has taken a major step toward sustainable energy development with the inauguration of the “Hydroforce” hydroelectric power plant at PK20, a pioneering project designed to support the energy transition of the water sector and promote…
title_en: Djibouti Inaugurates First Hydroelectric Plant to Advance Green Energy Transition
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti has taken a major step toward sustainable energy development with the inauguration of the “Hydroforce” hydroelectric power plant at PK20, a pioneering project designed to support the energy transition of the water sector and promote…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti has taken a major step toward sustainable energy development with the inauguration of the “Hydroforce” hydroelectric power plant at PK20, a pioneering project designed to support the energy transition of the water sector and promote renewable energy-based industrial innovation.
The facility was inaugurated by the Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries, Livestock and Marine Resources, Radwan Abdillahi Bahdon, in the presence of French Ambassador Jérôme Bresson, the Director General of the National Office for Water and Sanitation (ONEAD), Mohamed Fouad, representatives of development partners, and several technical and financial stakeholders.
Developed by French company SOC, a subsidiary of the NGE Group, with support from PAM-Saint Gobain for the supply of pipes and equipment, the project benefited from partial financing through a grant from the French Treasury under the FASEP program.
The Hydroforce plant relies on an innovative technology that recovers hydraulic pressure from water transported from the Ethiopian highlands. This energy is used to operate a turbine connected to a generator capable of producing 200 kVA of continuous power, equivalent to approximately 160 kWh.
Thanks to this system, the PK20 facility has achieved energy self-sufficiency through renewable electricity generated continuously, reducing dependence on external energy sources and supporting more sustainable water management operations.
Beyond electricity production, the project is expected to become the foundation for a broader “100% Green” technology hub focused on innovation, industrial development, and the production of high-value-added goods and services based on renewable energy.
Among the first planned initiatives are a sodium chloride production unit, aimed at reducing dependence on imported products used in drinking water treatment, and a laboratory dedicated to producing ultra-purified water for healthcare facilities.
The project has also strengthened technical cooperation between ONEAD and SOC, with both partners planning a skills-transfer program to train national technicians in the design, construction, and maintenance of hydraulic infrastructure.
The inauguration of Hydroforce represents a significant milestone in Djibouti’s efforts to modernize its infrastructure, expand renewable energy solutions, and promote a sustainable development model driven by innovation, technology transfer, and environmental responsibility.

title: AFC/M23 Pursues Territorial Expansion and Political Recognition, UN Report Says
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 — The AFC/M23 armed movement continues to pursue its political and military ambitions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the conflict and restoring stability in the region. According to a new…
title_en: AFC/M23 Pursues Territorial Expansion and Political Recognition, UN Report Says
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 — The AFC/M23 armed movement continues to pursue its political and military ambitions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the conflict and restoring stability in the region. According to a new…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 2, 2026 — The AFC/M23 armed movement continues to pursue its political and military ambitions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the conflict and restoring stability in the region.
According to a new assessment by the United Nations Group of Experts on the DRC, the movement, which controls significant areas of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, is seeking to strengthen its territorial influence, establish parallel governance structures, and obtain official recognition through political negotiations.
The report indicates that the group’s long-term objective remains the removal of the Congolese government, while also considering the creation of an autonomous entity in eastern DRC as an alternative scenario. The movement has reportedly promoted the idea of a “Federal Republic of Congo” for territories under its control, accompanied by the establishment of its own security and defense structures.
The experts note that AFC/M23 leaders have shifted their position on the future of their fighters, moving away from previous calls for integration into the Congolese armed forces (FARDC). Instead, the group is reportedly seeking to form and lead the armed forces of a future federal entity.
The report also highlights the increasing use of narratives related to the protection of Tutsi, Banyamulenge, and Hema communities from alleged ethnic violence as part of the movement’s public justification for its military actions and political demands.
Despite international calls for the withdrawal of foreign forces and the cessation of external support to armed groups, the UN assessment states that AFC/M23 has continued expanding its areas of influence. The movement has reportedly intensified military operations with ambitions to extend its control toward strategic locations, including Walikale, Kisangani, Kalemie, and Beni.
The experts further indicate that since the launch of the Doha peace process in 2025, the territory controlled by AFC/M23 has significantly increased, raising concerns over the effectiveness of diplomatic initiatives and existing security commitments.
The publication of the report comes as regional and international mediation efforts continue to face major challenges. The implementation of agreements supported by international partners remains difficult amid persistent disagreements between Kinshasa and Kigali over security issues and political commitments.
Meanwhile, negotiations between the Congolese government and AFC/M23 under the Doha framework have yet to resolve key points of disagreement. Recent diplomatic meetings, including talks aimed at revitalizing the process, have failed to produce major breakthroughs, while worsening international crises have further slowed efforts to achieve a lasting settlement.

title: Ugandan Police Dismantle Suspected Counterfeit Currency Ring, Seize Alleged $9 Million in Fake Notes
excerpt: Lira, Uganda, July 2, 2026 – Ugandan authorities have arrested four suspects following the seizure of United States dollar notes with a purported face value of USD 9 million during an intelligence-led operation targeting a suspected counterfeit currency network in Lira City.…
title_en: Ugandan Police Dismantle Suspected Counterfeit Currency Ring, Seize Alleged $9 Million in Fake Notes
excerpt_en: Lira, Uganda, July 2, 2026 – Ugandan authorities have arrested four suspects following the seizure of United States dollar notes with a purported face value of USD 9 million during an intelligence-led operation targeting a suspected counterfeit currency network in Lira City.…
body_en:
Lira, Uganda, July 2, 2026 – Ugandan authorities have arrested four suspects following the seizure of United States dollar notes with a purported face value of USD 9 million during an intelligence-led operation targeting a suspected counterfeit currency network in Lira City.
The operation was conducted in Ireda Shamba Cell, Lira City East Division, after investigators received information that counterfeit currency and related materials were being stored at a private residence. A lawful search of the property led to the discovery of a safe believed to contain the suspected counterfeit notes.
During the operation, officers recovered approximately 100 bundles of USD 100 notes suspected to be counterfeit, along with several motor vehicle logbooks and additional United States dollar notes in various denominations.
Preliminary investigations indicate that the safe had been delivered to the residence by one of the suspects, who is already facing separate allegations of obtaining money by false pretences. Authorities also believe the suspects may have been involved in similar activities over an extended period, with possible links to associates operating in Soroti City.
The recovered currency has been secured as evidence and will undergo forensic examination to determine its authenticity. Investigators are working to establish the full extent of the suspected network and identify any additional individuals connected to the operation.
Authorities said investigations remain ongoing and that further arrests are expected as efforts continue to dismantle the alleged counterfeit currency network.

title: Djibouti Receives International Messages of Support as Leaders Celebrate Independence Anniversary
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh has received a series of congratulatory messages from international leaders and heads of regional organizations on the occasion of Djibouti’s 49th anniversary of independence, with partners praising the country’s…
title_en: Djibouti Receives International Messages of Support as Leaders Celebrate Independence Anniversary
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh has received a series of congratulatory messages from international leaders and heads of regional organizations on the occasion of Djibouti’s 49th anniversary of independence, with partners praising the country’s…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh has received a series of congratulatory messages from international leaders and heads of regional organizations on the occasion of Djibouti’s 49th anniversary of independence, with partners praising the country’s stability, development efforts, and growing role on the regional and international stage.
Among the latest messages was one from King Felipe VI of Spain, who conveyed his warm congratulations to President Guelleh, as well as to the Government and people of Djibouti. The Spanish monarch expressed his wishes for the President’s personal well-being and for continued peace and prosperity for the Djiboutian people.
President Guelleh also received greetings from Benin’s President Romuald Wadagni, who highlighted the importance of strengthening friendship and cooperation between the two countries. He expressed his willingness to continue working with Djibouti’s leadership to deepen bilateral relations for the benefit of both nations.
Similar messages were sent by other international leaders, including Sierra Leone’s President Julius Maada Bio and Malawi’s President Arthur Peter Mutharika, who extended their wishes for success and prosperity to President Guelleh and the Djiboutian population on the 49th anniversary of national independence.
The President of Poland, Karol Nawrocki, also conveyed his congratulations while highlighting Djibouti’s growing importance as a strategic logistics and commercial hub in the Horn of Africa.
Beyond individual states, regional and international institutions also expressed their support for Djibouti’s development trajectory. The Chairperson of the African Union Commission, Mahamoud Ali Youssouf, sent his congratulations on behalf of the continental organization and praised Djibouti’s progress, stability, and strengthened position in regional and global affairs.
He emphasized the importance of maintaining and deepening the partnership between Djibouti and the African Union, while expressing hopes for continued cooperation and stronger ties between the two institutions.
These messages reflect the continued recognition of Djibouti’s role as a stable partner in the Horn of Africa and acknowledge the country’s efforts in promoting development, regional cooperation, and international engagement nearly five decades after gaining independence.

excerpt: ADOYLA, Tadjourah Region, July 2, 2026 - Environmental preservation is gaining momentum in Adoyla, where residents are increasingly engaging in community-driven initiatives aimed at improving sanitation, reducing waste, and protecting natural resources. Led by the Diffou…
title_en: Adoyla Mobilizes Residents in Tadjourah to Strengthen Environmental Protection Efforts
excerpt_en: ADOYLA, Tadjourah Region, July 2, 2026 - Environmental preservation is gaining momentum in Adoyla, where residents are increasingly engaging in community-driven initiatives aimed at improving sanitation, reducing waste, and protecting natural resources. Led by the Diffou…
body_en:
ADOYLA, Tadjourah Region, July 2, 2026 - Environmental preservation is gaining momentum in Adoyla, where residents are increasingly engaging in community-driven initiatives aimed at improving sanitation, reducing waste, and protecting natural resources.
Led by the Diffou Association, a recent awareness campaign brought together residents from several neighborhoods to promote environmentally responsible practices and encourage greater community participation in sustainable development efforts.
The initiative focused on direct engagement with local communities, with association members visiting households and public areas to discuss environmental challenges affecting the town. Through dialogue sessions and neighborhood meetings, volunteers highlighted the importance of maintaining clean public spaces, managing household waste responsibly, protecting vegetation, and using natural resources sustainably.

title_en: Suspected ADF Collaborators Arrested and Presented to Provincial Authorities

body_en:
Isiro, July 2, 2026 - A group of individuals suspected of supporting the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) has been arrested in Suka na Mboka, Watsa territory, and presented to the provincial authorities in Haut-Uele.
Major General François Mukalay Ngoy, commander of the Uele operational sector, presented the suspects on Tuesday, June 30, in Isiro before the provincial government. The group included two women, a member of the Pygmy community, individuals of Arab origin, and children.
According to military authorities, the suspects are accused of providing logistical assistance and intelligence support to ADF fighters operating in the area. Their arrest follows ongoing security operations aimed at dismantling armed group networks and preventing their expansion in the region.
The provincial authorities praised the efforts of the FARDC and the cooperation of local communities in Watsa territory. The governor highlighted the importance of continued collaboration between civilians and security forces in combating armed groups.
The provincial executive called on residents to remain vigilant and immediately report any suspicious activities to security services. Authorities stressed that community cooperation remains essential for preventing attacks and enabling rapid responses to security threats.
Major General François Mukalay Ngoy also expressed appreciation for the support provided by national and provincial authorities, while encouraging continued collaboration with the population to strengthen operations against armed groups in Haut-Uele.

title: Djibouti Concludes National Refugee Week with Renewed Focus on Inclusion and Long-Term Solutions
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti has concluded the second edition of National Refugee Week with a renewed commitment to strengthening refugee protection, promoting social cohesion, and advancing durable solutions to the challenges posed by forced displacement. Held from…
title_en: Djibouti Concludes National Refugee Week with Renewed Focus on Inclusion and Long-Term Solutions
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti has concluded the second edition of National Refugee Week with a renewed commitment to strengthening refugee protection, promoting social cohesion, and advancing durable solutions to the challenges posed by forced displacement. Held from…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 2, 2026 - Djibouti has concluded the second edition of National Refugee Week with a renewed commitment to strengthening refugee protection, promoting social cohesion, and advancing durable solutions to the challenges posed by forced displacement.
Held from June 20 to 25, the week-long event brought together government institutions, development partners, humanitarian organizations, refugee representatives, community leaders, and host communities to discuss strategies for improving inclusion and fostering peaceful coexistence.
Participants focused on strengthening dialogue between refugees and host populations while addressing the humanitarian, economic, and social challenges associated with displacement. The discussions emphasized the importance of coordinated action to build resilient communities and expand opportunities for displaced people.
Many of the activities were conducted under the Refugee and Host Community Inclusion Project (PIRB), implemented with support from the World Bank in partnership with the Urban Rehabilitation and Social Housing Agency (ARULOS). The initiative promotes an integrated approach combining refugee protection, economic inclusion, skills development, and community empowerment.
Youth engagement and innovation featured prominently throughout the program. Working with the Center for Technology and Innovation for Development (CTID), organizers introduced activities designed to equip young refugees and members of host communities with practical skills for the digital age.
In Holl-Holl, community dialogue sessions encouraged greater understanding and trust between refugees and local residents, while technology and science workshops in Ali-Addeh introduced young participants to innovation and digital skills, highlighting education and creativity as important tools for social integration and long-term resilience.
During the closing ceremony, the president of the Association of Refugees in Djibouti expressed appreciation for the country's longstanding commitment to hosting refugees, recognizing the support provided by national authorities and local communities over several decades.
He also highlighted the significance of Djibouti's 2017 refugee legislation, noting that it expanded refugees' access to education, healthcare, employment opportunities, and broader participation in the country's economic and social life.
The Executive Secretary of the National Office for Assistance to Refugees and Disaster Victims (ONARS) stressed that growing humanitarian crises, armed conflicts, climate change, and declining international funding have increased the need for stronger partnerships and sustained international support.
He called for greater investment in youth development, vocational training, entrepreneurship, and skills-building initiatives, describing them as essential for strengthening refugee self-reliance and enhancing the resilience of host communities.
Officials also acknowledged the contributions of humanitarian and development partners, including UNHCR, the World Bank, ARULOS, and CTID, whose support helped facilitate the event.
The week concluded with participants endorsing a Charter of Peaceful Coexistence, which will serve as a roadmap for future efforts to promote peace, inclusion, and social cohesion. The initiative reaffirmed Djibouti's commitment to addressing forced displacement through policies centered on solidarity, shared responsibility, innovation, and sustainable human development while reinforcing its reputation as a regional model for refugee protection and inclusion.

title: Djibouti and UNHCR Appeal for Increased International Support as Refugee Funding Declines
excerpt: ADDIS ABABA, July 1, 2026 - The Government of Djibouti and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) have intensified efforts to secure international funding for refugee assistance, launching a high-level advocacy mission in Addis Ababa amid a worsening global…
title_en: Djibouti and UNHCR Appeal for Increased International Support as Refugee Funding Declines
excerpt_en: ADDIS ABABA, July 1, 2026 - The Government of Djibouti and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) have intensified efforts to secure international funding for refugee assistance, launching a high-level advocacy mission in Addis Ababa amid a worsening global…
body_en:
ADDIS ABABA, July 1, 2026 - The Government of Djibouti and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) have intensified efforts to secure international funding for refugee assistance, launching a high-level advocacy mission in Addis Ababa amid a worsening global humanitarian financing crisis.
The mission sought to engage diplomatic missions and development partners accredited to Djibouti but based in Ethiopia's capital, highlighting the growing impact of declining humanitarian funding on refugee protection and assistance programs in Djibouti.
Led by the Secretary General of Djibouti's Ministry of the Interior, Souleiman Moumin Robleh, the delegation included UNHCR Representative in Djibouti Sandrine Dominique Desamours and the Deputy Executive Secretary of the National Office for Assistance to Refugees and Disaster Victims (ONARS), Houssein Mohamed Chardi.
During the visit, the delegation held consultations with ambassadors representing Canada, Finland, Sweden, Spain, Switzerland, and Indonesia, presenting an overview of Djibouti's humanitarian situation, the consequences of shrinking international assistance, and the country's most urgent funding needs.
Officials also met with the African Union Commission's Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs at the African Union headquarters to discuss regional displacement challenges and the need for stronger international cooperation.
The advocacy mission builds on a funding appeal launched in August 2025 to mobilize additional resources for refugee protection, humanitarian assistance, social inclusion, and support for host communities.
Djiboutian officials emphasized that the country remains one of the Horn of Africa's most stable states despite ongoing regional conflicts and humanitarian emergencies. Djibouti currently hosts nearly 35,000 refugees, equivalent to approximately 3.5 percent of its population, while also providing humanitarian assistance to more than 500,000 vulnerable migrants transiting through the country each year.
The delegation warned that funding shortages are already affecting critical refugee services. Essential protection activities-including the registration of new asylum seekers, renewal of refugee identity documents, and issuance of travel documents-have been significantly disrupted, increasing the vulnerability of displaced populations and limiting their access to essential services.
Officials cautioned that continued financial constraints could undermine years of progress achieved in refugee protection and inclusion.
Diplomatic representatives welcomed Djibouti's longstanding commitment to hosting refugees and acknowledged the country's efforts to integrate displaced populations into national education, healthcare, and labor market systems. They also recognized Djibouti's role as a key regional actor in responding to forced displacement across the Horn of Africa.
Through the mission, Djibouti and UNHCR renewed their appeal for stronger international solidarity, calling for increased financial support to sustain life-saving services, protect refugee rights, and continue supporting both displaced populations and the communities hosting them.
Conclusion
The first half of July 2026 highlights Djibouti’s continued pursuit of a comprehensive national transformation strategy, combining ambitious domestic reforms with stronger international engagement. At the national level, the government has reinforced its development agenda through the implementation of the 2025-2030 National Development Plan (PND-ADEEG) and the strengthening of its institutional framework, including new measures to promote transparency and combat corruption. These reforms, alongside initiatives supporting digital inclusion, youth entrepreneurship, skills development, and environmental resilience, reflect a broader shift toward a results-oriented governance model focused on sustainable and inclusive growth.
Internationally, Djibouti continues to leverage its strategic geographic position to expand economic partnerships and reinforce its role as a regional hub for trade, logistics, and connectivity. From securing major development cooperation frameworks with partners such as the Islamic Development Bank and China, to advancing the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and promoting renewable energy solutions through projects such as the Hydroforce initiative, the country is converting its strategic assets into opportunities for economic diversification and long-term development. At the same time, Djibouti’s growing contribution to African peace mediation efforts and its progressive approach to refugee integration continue to strengthen its image as a reliable partner and a pillar of stability in the Horn of Africa.
Nevertheless, significant challenges remain. Funding constraints affecting refugee assistance programs, highlighted by both national authorities and international humanitarian actors, risk placing additional pressure on essential services and local capacities. The achievement of Djibouti’s ambitious development objectives, including the targeted 8.6 percent annual economic growth rate, will depend on the effective implementation of ministerial action plans, improved coordination across institutions, stronger private sector participation, and sustained support from international partners.
As Djibouti enters the second half of 2026, the country’s ability to transform strategic ambitions into measurable outcomes will be the decisive factor in determining whether its current momentum translates into lasting economic resilience, social inclusion, and regional influence.
By Jeff Buleli

title: UN Report Highlights Continued Rwandan Military Presence Supporting AFC/M23 Operations
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 — The security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains highly volatile as a United Nations assessment points to the continued presence and operational support of Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) alongside the AFC/M23 armed movement. The…
title_en: UN Report Highlights Continued Rwandan Military Presence Supporting AFC/M23 Operations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 — The security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains highly volatile as a United Nations assessment points to the continued presence and operational support of Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) alongside the AFC/M23 armed movement. The…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 — The security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains highly volatile as a United Nations assessment points to the continued presence and operational support of Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) alongside the AFC/M23 armed movement.
The report indicates that the AFC/M23 rebellion, which maintains control over significant areas of North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, continues to benefit from military assistance that has contributed to strengthening its positions and expanding its operational capabilities across the conflict zone.
According to the assessment, thousands of RDF troops remain deployed in eastern DRC, with estimates placing their presence between 8,000 and 10,000 personnel in South Kivu and between 6,000 and 8,000 in North Kivu since late 2025. The report notes that no major withdrawal has been observed, with subsequent movements mainly involving troop rotations and reinforcements.
The document further highlights the use of advanced military capabilities, including drones, electronic warfare systems, specialized units, and other sophisticated equipment. UN experts also report that RDF elements have provided operational support to AFC/M23 forces, including assistance in offensive operations and the creation of strategic corridors.
The assessment raises concerns over RDF activities in areas where no presence of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) had been reported, including parts of Uvira territory. This development has intensified debate over Kigali’s justification that its military actions are primarily aimed at addressing security threats linked to armed groups hostile to Rwanda.
The report also describes close coordination between RDF personnel and AFC/M23 fighters, including the integration of some Rwandan units into mixed formations. It further alleges that some RDF elements adopted M23 uniforms and conducted movements mainly at night to reduce the risk of identification.
The findings come amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to end the conflict in eastern DRC. Despite the signing of agreements and mediation initiatives, including the Washington framework and the Doha peace process, tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali remain unresolved.
Negotiations between the Congolese government and the Congo River Alliance, which includes AFC/M23, have struggled to achieve significant progress, with disagreements persisting over key security and political issues. The lack of concrete advances has added to concerns as fighting continues and the humanitarian situation deteriorates across affected provinces.

title: Cholera Outbreak Spreads Across Kordofan as Health System Faces Shortages
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 - A growing cholera outbreak in Sudan’s West and North Kordofan states has infected hundreds of people and caused more than 100 deaths, as health authorities and volunteers struggle to respond amid severe shortages of medical supplies. Health officials…
title_en: Cholera Outbreak Spreads Across Kordofan as Health System Faces Shortages
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 - A growing cholera outbreak in Sudan’s West and North Kordofan states has infected hundreds of people and caused more than 100 deaths, as health authorities and volunteers struggle to respond amid severe shortages of medical supplies. Health officials…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 - A growing cholera outbreak in Sudan’s West and North Kordofan states has infected hundreds of people and caused more than 100 deaths, as health authorities and volunteers struggle to respond amid severe shortages of medical supplies.
Health officials reported 911 confirmed cholera cases and 127 fatalities across the two states, with the Al-Mazroub area in North Kordofan emerging as one of the main centres of the outbreak. The area recorded around 300 infections and 16 deaths within three weeks after the disease spread from neighbouring West Kordofan.
The Ministry of Health has established isolation and rehydration centres in affected areas and activated emergency response mechanisms to monitor the spread of the disease and coordinate medical interventions.
However, volunteers working in North and West Kordofan have warned that shortages of essential medicines and treatment supplies are threatening efforts to contain the outbreak, particularly in conflict-affected areas where access to healthcare remains limited.
Health authorities and humanitarian partners have increased efforts to provide medical assistance, strengthen disease monitoring, and improve access to clean water and sanitation services to slow transmission.
The health situation is further complicated by displacement and damaged infrastructure linked to the ongoing conflict, which has weakened public health systems and increased the risk of disease outbreaks.
Authorities are also maintaining preventive measures against other health threats, including border screening and temperature checks for travelers as part of preparations against potential Ebola risks.
Health officials said efforts are underway to expand emergency treatment capacity, including the completion of a specialized Ebola isolation facility and improvements to national laboratory capabilities.
Despite these measures, the availability of essential epidemic medicines, intravenous fluids, and other medical supplies remains uneven across Sudan’s states.
Meanwhile, health authorities announced that a polio reference laboratory in Red Sea State has resumed operations after rehabilitation support, allowing Sudan to conduct polio testing domestically and strengthen its disease surveillance capacity.

title: Djibouti Strengthens Anti-Corruption Drive, Adopts 2025-2030 Development Plan and Approves Key Judicial Appointments
excerpt: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 1, 2026 - Djibouti's government has approved a series of major legislative, institutional, and development measures aimed at strengthening governance, accelerating economic transformation, reinforcing the judiciary, and expanding public infrastructure…
title_en: Djibouti Strengthens Anti-Corruption Drive, Adopts 2025-2030 Development Plan and Approves Key Judicial Appointments
excerpt_en: DJIBOUTI CITY, July 1, 2026 - Djibouti's government has approved a series of major legislative, institutional, and development measures aimed at strengthening governance, accelerating economic transformation, reinforcing the judiciary, and expanding public infrastructure…
body_en:
DJIBOUTI CITY, July 1, 2026 - Djibouti's government has approved a series of major legislative, institutional, and development measures aimed at strengthening governance, accelerating economic transformation, reinforcing the judiciary, and expanding public infrastructure during the latest session of the Council of Ministers chaired by President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh.
One of the session's flagship decisions was the approval of a draft law to strengthen the prevention and fight against corruption and related offenses. The proposed legislation aligns Djibouti's legal framework with international anti-corruption standards, including the United Nations Convention against Corruption, while responding to recommendations stemming from the country's ongoing Financial Action Task Force (FATF) assessment process.
The legislation expands anti-corruption measures across public institutions, private companies, trade unions, and civil society organizations. It also broadens asset declaration requirements, introduces stronger transparency and internal control obligations, consolidates corruption-related offenses under a unified legal framework, and reinforces investigative and enforcement mechanisms.
The draft law further enhances the authority of the National Independent Commission for the Prevention and Fight Against Corruption by expanding its oversight powers, particularly regarding asset declarations and administrative sanctions, while improving its governance through fixed six-year mandates and staggered membership renewal.

title: Port Sudan Records Strong June Performance Amid War-Time Economic Pressure
excerpt: PORT SUDAN, July 1, 2026 - Port Sudan’s Southern Port recorded significant activity in June, handling more than 26,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) and receiving 30 vessels, as the country’s main maritime gateway continues to support trade during the ongoing conflict.…
title_en: Port Sudan Records Strong June Performance Amid War-Time Economic Pressure
excerpt_en: PORT SUDAN, July 1, 2026 - Port Sudan’s Southern Port recorded significant activity in June, handling more than 26,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) and receiving 30 vessels, as the country’s main maritime gateway continues to support trade during the ongoing conflict.…
body_en:
PORT SUDAN, July 1, 2026 - Port Sudan’s Southern Port recorded significant activity in June, handling more than 26,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) and receiving 30 vessels, as the country’s main maritime gateway continues to support trade during the ongoing conflict.
The container terminal welcomed 15 container ships and 15 other vessels during the month, reflecting continued efforts to maintain the flow of imports and exports despite economic and logistical challenges caused by the war.
According to port authorities, imported containers reached 8,157 units, equivalent to 13,615 TEUs, representing slightly more than half of the total monthly traffic. Export activity accounted for 7,436 containers, including loaded and empty units, representing 12,404 TEUs.
Overall, the port handled 15,593 containers during June, corresponding to 26,019 TEUs, as operators worked to improve efficiency and strengthen Sudan’s international trade connections.
The performance comes amid recent operational improvements at Port Sudan, including the arrival of larger container vessels and the resumption of transhipment services aimed at expanding cargo storage and regional redistribution operations.
The port remains a critical economic lifeline for Sudan, providing the country with access to global markets and supporting the movement of essential goods during a period of severe economic disruption.
Despite recent progress, authorities acknowledge that the facility still faces structural limitations, including the need for expanded storage capacity and deeper berths to accommodate larger vessels and compete with international maritime hubs.
Port Sudan currently operates with limited berth capacity and storage space compared with global standards, creating pressure for future investment and infrastructure expansion.

title: UN Report Identifies AFC/M23 as Leading Perpetrator of Rights Abuses in Eastern Provinces
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 - The latest assessment on the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has placed the AFC/M23 armed movement at the center of the most serious reported violations of international humanitarian law committed in the region. The United…
title_en: UN Report Identifies AFC/M23 as Leading Perpetrator of Rights Abuses in Eastern Provinces
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 - The latest assessment on the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has placed the AFC/M23 armed movement at the center of the most serious reported violations of international humanitarian law committed in the region. The United…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 - The latest assessment on the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has placed the AFC/M23 armed movement at the center of the most serious reported violations of international humanitarian law committed in the region.
The United Nations’ final report released in June 2026 highlights that the group is responsible for the largest share of documented abuses among non-state armed actors operating in eastern DRC. The findings point to a pattern of violence marked by alleged systematic killings, the destruction of villages, and the burning of local livelihoods, particularly in the Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms of Rutshuru territory.
The report also highlights severe humanitarian consequences in areas affected by the conflict, including Minembwe, where restrictions on movement and access have left parts of the Banyamulenge community facing difficulties in obtaining essential goods and services.
Sexual violence remains one of the most alarming dimensions of the crisis. The report describes conflict-related abuses against women and girls as reaching unprecedented levels since 2024, with the AFC/M23 identified as the main perpetrator among the actors involved.
At the same time, the assessment points to serious violations committed by state forces, identifying the FARDC as the principal state actor responsible for abuses. The findings underline the complexity of the conflict, involving multiple armed actors and competing narratives, beyond a single interpretation centered solely on external aggression.
As fighting continues in eastern DRC, the allegations of widespread abuses add further pressure on national and international efforts aimed at protecting civilians, ensuring accountability, and finding a lasting political solution to the crisis.

title: Sudan and Turkey Launch Reconstruction Partnership as War Damage Mounts
excerpt: ANKARA, July 1, 2026 - Sudan and Turkey have agreed to establish a framework for reconstruction cooperation aimed at rebuilding damaged infrastructure and supporting economic recovery after more than three years of war. The agreement between the contractors' associations of…
title_en: Sudan and Turkey Launch Reconstruction Partnership as War Damage Mounts
excerpt_en: ANKARA, July 1, 2026 - Sudan and Turkey have agreed to establish a framework for reconstruction cooperation aimed at rebuilding damaged infrastructure and supporting economic recovery after more than three years of war. The agreement between the contractors' associations of…
body_en:
ANKARA, July 1, 2026 - Sudan and Turkey have agreed to establish a framework for reconstruction cooperation aimed at rebuilding damaged infrastructure and supporting economic recovery after more than three years of war.
The agreement between the contractors' associations of both countries includes the implementation of pilot infrastructure projects designed to support Sudan's reconstruction efforts and create a foundation for broader investment partnerships.
Sudanese authorities estimate that rebuilding the country's infrastructure will require hundreds of billions of dollars, with major reconstruction needs identified in Khartoum and other states affected by the conflict. International organizations are also conducting assessments to determine the full scale of the damage and recovery requirements.
During meetings in Ankara, a Sudanese delegation led by Malik Ali Dongla held discussions with Turkish construction representatives on infrastructure rehabilitation, investment opportunities, and mechanisms to support post-war recovery.
The two sides explored possible financing options involving international financial institutions, including development banks, as well as alternative arrangements linking reconstruction projects with Sudan's natural resources and agricultural production.
As an initial step, the partners agreed to launch a pilot project that will serve as a model for future cooperation. A joint committee will oversee implementation, focusing on transparency, quality control, and compliance with agreed standards.
Turkish construction companies also committed to sharing technical expertise and supporting the training of Sudanese professionals through capacity-building programs aimed at strengthening local skills in the construction sector.
Sudanese officials said the partnership reflects efforts to attract foreign investment and create conditions for economic recovery, while emphasizing the need for a secure and stable environment for international businesses.
The conflict that began in April 2023 has caused extensive damage to Sudan's infrastructure, economy, and public services. Economic assessments indicate a sharp contraction in national output, widespread loss of livelihoods, and severe pressure on the country's financial system.

title: UN Experts Estimate Hundreds of Millions of Dollars in Ituri Gold Smuggled Through Uganda
excerpt: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 – Hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of gold extracted from Ituri Province is being illegally smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, primarily through Uganda, according to recent findings highlighting the scale of illicit mineral trade in…
title_en: UN Experts Estimate Hundreds of Millions of Dollars in Ituri Gold Smuggled Through Uganda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 – Hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of gold extracted from Ituri Province is being illegally smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, primarily through Uganda, according to recent findings highlighting the scale of illicit mineral trade in…
body_en:
Kinshasa, July 1, 2026 – Hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of gold extracted from Ituri Province is being illegally smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, primarily through Uganda, according to recent findings highlighting the scale of illicit mineral trade in the country's northeast.
The assessment estimates that gold production from a mining site between Mabanga and Nizi generated between US$300 million and US$800 million between March 2024 and March 2026. A second mining site near Yedi is reported to have produced more than two tonnes of gold since the beginning of 2025.
Despite this significant level of production, officially declared gold exports from Ituri totaled only 559 kilograms in 2025, revealing a substantial gap between estimated output and recorded exports.
The findings indicate that much of the undeclared gold is believed to be smuggled into neighboring Uganda. In 2025, Uganda recorded a historic 62 tonnes of gold exports valued at approximately US$6.4 billion, representing a 30 percent increase in export volume compared with the previous year. Analysts believe that a significant share of this increase is linked to gold originating from eastern DRC.
The report also highlights the rapid expansion of cyanide leaching operations used to process mining tailings in Djugu Territory. The practice is prohibited under Congolese law because of its environmental and safety risks, yet hundreds of tailings ponds have reportedly been established across the area.
Some of these mining sites are said to be under the influence of local armed groups, which allegedly impose taxes on mining activities, allowing them to generate revenue from the illicit exploitation of mineral resources.
The findings underscore the continuing challenges facing the DRC in regulating its mining sector, combating mineral smuggling, and preventing armed groups from financing their activities through the illegal exploitation of natural resources.

title: Sudan Central Bank Injects Foreign Currency to Stabilize Exchange Market
excerpt: KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 - Sudan's central bank has injected 400 million United Arab Emirates dirhams into commercial banks as part of emergency measures aimed at supporting import financing and slowing the rapid depreciation of the national currency. The intervention comes as…
title_en: Sudan Central Bank Injects Foreign Currency to Stabilize Exchange Market
excerpt_en: KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 - Sudan's central bank has injected 400 million United Arab Emirates dirhams into commercial banks as part of emergency measures aimed at supporting import financing and slowing the rapid depreciation of the national currency. The intervention comes as…
body_en:
KHARTOUM, July 1, 2026 - Sudan's central bank has injected 400 million United Arab Emirates dirhams into commercial banks as part of emergency measures aimed at supporting import financing and slowing the rapid depreciation of the national currency.
The intervention comes as Sudan's pound continues to face intense pressure against major foreign currencies, contributing to sharp increases in the prices of essential goods and services across the country.
The currency crisis prompted Prime Minister Kamel Idris to lead a high-level government meeting in Khartoum to review exchange rate policies, efforts to combat illegal currency trading, and measures against gold smuggling activities.
Central bank officials said the foreign currency injection began on June 23 and was designed to provide importers with access to official financing channels while reducing pressure on the informal exchange market.
Authorities reported that the measure helped lower the official exchange rate of the UAE dirham in some banking transactions, allowing importers to meet essential financial requirements. Commercial banks were instructed to strengthen compliance procedures, register import activities through the “Baladna” electronic platform, and follow trade regulations aimed at limiting capital flight.
Despite the central bank’s intervention, activity in the parallel market remained largely unchanged, with traders reporting continued demand for foreign currencies and gold.
Market rates showed the UAE dirham trading at around 1,417 Sudanese pounds, while the US dollar reached approximately 5,100 pounds. The price of gold remained high, with a gram trading around 580,000 Sudanese pounds.
The government is expected to continue monitoring exchange markets as it attempts to restore stability in the financial sector amid the broader economic impact of Sudan's ongoing conflict.
